name: Anomaly upsert with a separate escalation channel
description: db.ts:137 INSERT_ANOMALY is INSERT OR IGNORE on a stable anomaly_key, so severity, observed, baseline and detail freeze at first sight while the 10-minute window is still open under 5-second polling: a window first seen at 3.1x (warn) that ends at 8x stays warn forever and the one desktop notification fired at the lower level. Convert to ON CONFLICT(anomaly_key) DO UPDATE SET severity/observed/baseline/threshold/detail/window_end WHERE excluded.observed > anomalies.observed OR severity_rank(excluded.severity) > severity_rank(anomalies.severity), keeping anomaly_key deterministic and free of now(). Two contracts break silently under a naive conversion and must change in the same commit: insertAnomalies returns rows where changes>0 as 'new' (db.ts:143), so an updated row would re-notify on every 5-second pass and it must instead return inserted and escalated as separate arrays; and Store.swift:163 gates app notifications on MAX(anomalies.id), which an UPDATE never advances, so escalations would never reach the app at all — that watermark moves to MAX(detected_at) plus a per-key severity record. collect.ts:70 then notifies inserted always and escalated only on a severity transition.
desktop_surface: Dashboard > Incidents rows stop reading 'warn' on a window that ended critical and gain a small upward arrow where the severity was raised, whose tooltip names the old and new figures; the menu-bar glyph tint (liveSeverity) escalates in place; notification volume drops from one-per-poll to one-per-transition.
data_source: packages/core/src/db.ts:137-146 INSERT_ANOMALY/insertAnomalies; cli/collect.ts:69-73; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/Store.swift:151-163 lastNotifiedIncidentID; anomalies.{severity,observed,baseline,threshold,detail} (schema.ts:42-64)
honest_limit: Only observed can arbitrate an upgrade cleanly; a ratio rule whose observed falls while severity rises (error_storm) needs its own comparator or it silently never escalates. An escalated row keeps its first detail prose until the rule re-templates it, so historical wording can disagree with the stored figures. Downgrades are refused by construction — severity never decreases — because a rule whose baseline grew would otherwise make a real incident look benign on re-evaluation. The MAX(id) watermark also has a separate defect this change must absorb: after the README-documented `rm ~/.vole/vole.db*` rebuild, ids restart at 1 and nothing is ever notified again until they catch up.
competitive_note: v1's 'Incident noise controls' and 'Finding lifecycle and acknowledgement' both assume the upsert already exists (their notes read 'insertAnomalies ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE only window_end/observed/detail'); it does not, and neither entry mentions the two contracts that break with it. Anthropic's monitoring docs state that anomaly detection, baselining, correlation and alerting are the customer's SIEM's job, so incident quality is Vole's ground to lose and a frozen severity is the defect that ends a design-partner pilot.
v1_ref: Incident noise controls: window chaining, per-session cap, info rollup
field_verified: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. packages/core/src/db.ts:136-147 `const INSERT_ANOMALY = ` / `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO anomalies (...)` — no ON CONFLICT clause. db.ts:150-157 insertAnomalies: `rs.filter((r) => stmt.run({ ...r, ...ORIGIN }).changes > 0)`. apps/mac/Sources/Vole/Store.swift:153 `$0.id > lastNotifiedIncidentID && $0.source == "live" && $0.severity != "info" && $0.windowEnd >= cutoff`; Store.swift:163 `if let maxID = allIncidents.map(\.id).max(), maxID > lastNotifiedIncidentID`. Store.swift:65-66 persists it in UserDefaults (`UserDefaults.standard.set(lastNotifiedIncidentID, forKey: "vole.lastNotifiedIncidentID")`), so the rm-vole.db rebuild defect is real: ids restart at 1, the watermark does not. Live DB has 249 anomalies, 190 burn_rate_spike, so this freeze governs 100% of the shipped feed.
constraint: Constraint 3 names this exactly ('Changing verdict semantics requires an explicit upsert clause and a re-notify path') — the feature IS the sanctioned reconciliation, not a violation. Two defects in the proposal itself: (a) the SET list (severity/observed/baseline/threshold/detail/window_end) omits detected_at, yet the replacement watermark is MAX(detected_at) — an UPDATE would therefore still never advance it and escalations still never reach the app; fix by adding detected_at to the SET list or a nullable escalated_at column (constraint 12 permits add-nullable-only via migrate(), which already covers the anomalies table at db.ts:41-46). (b) `severity_rank()` does not exist in SQLite; inline a CASE or store an integer rank. Constraint 13: DB.swift:223-240 selects only 12 columns, none of them observed/baseline/threshold, so the promised 'tooltip names the old and new figures' cannot render until F11's read-model fix lands — sequence them together. detect/index.ts:57 already prefixes source into anomaly_key, so seed/live escalations cannot collide.

name: Union tool names across content-block copies and widen the upsert
description: Claude Code writes one JSONL line per content block (thinking, text, each tool_use) under the same message.id with identical usage; claude-code.ts:65-72 keep() retains one copy, so tool names on the other lines are lost — live DB right now: 7,114 of 14,921 claude_code rows with stop_reason='tool_use' have tools NULL (47.7%), out of 16,411 claude_code rows. It cannot heal on a later pass because db.ts:101 only rewrites a row when excluded.total_tokens is STRICTLY greater, and the sibling copies carry equal tokens. Every v1 Tier 2/3 rule that counts tool usage, every MCP-server join, every destructive-command classifier and the tool_calls ledger's own cross-check inherit that ~50% blind spot, and the fixture at claude-code.test.ts:15 hides it by putting every content block in every copy. Fix keep() to union tool names across all copies of a message.id before choosing the winner, widen the upsert WHERE to also fire when totals are equal and stored tools IS NULL while excluded is not, and rewrite the fixture as one block per line.
desktop_surface: MenuPanel's top-5 tools list stops under-reporting by half; the Dashboard hover callout and every per-tool drill-down become countable, and rows that stay NULL after the rebuild render 'no tool recorded' rather than being absent from the count.
data_source: packages/core/src/collectors/claude-code.ts:65-72,150-151; packages/core/src/db.ts:87-101; live ~/.vole/vole.db (counts above measured today)
honest_limit: Healing only works while the source transcript still exists; Claude Code prunes at cleanupPeriodDays (unset here, so the tool default applies) and rows older than that stay NULL forever, so the fix needs a documented one-time rebuild and the UI must distinguish 'no tool recorded' from 'no tool used'. Widening the upsert touches the one statement every collector shares, so it needs its own regression test asserting that re-reading identical data is still a no-op.
competitive_note: Per-session tool attribution is exactly what Cursor's enterprise OTel export lacks (market.md row 109), and what MintMCP and Speakeasy obtain only by putting a gateway in the request path; shipping it at 50% coverage forfeits the one advantage the local-first design has.
v1_ref: tool_calls ledger with tool_result error join and every v1 rule that counts tool usage; v1 notes only that copies share message.id, under 'Correlation ids: request_id, turn_id, entry_uuid columns'
field_verified: Confirmed twice, from both ends. Live ~/.vole/vole.db: claude_code rows 16,612, of which 15,111 have stop_reason='tool_use' and 7,114 of those have tools NULL — the 7,114 matches the feature's figure exactly (its denominator has since grown from 14,921 to 15,111, so 47.1% today). Independent replay of all 633 transcripts reproducing keep()'s max-total_tokens rule finds 7,329 message ids where the winning copy carries no tool name although another copy of the same id did, plus 614 more where the winner holds a strict subset of the union — so union-before-choose is the correct fix and the cause is exactly as stated. The fixture does hide it: claude-code.test.ts:15 emits `content: [{type:'text'},{type:'tool_use',name:'Bash'},{type:'tool_use',name:'Read'}]` in every copy of every message. The blocking mechanism is real: db.ts:101 `WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens`, and sibling copies carry equal totals, so it can never heal.
constraint: Constraint 2 is engaged head-on and the feature does what the constraint demands — an explicit widening rather than a silent enrich-later. Two refinements. (a) The widened branch must set the tools column ONLY. The existing DO UPDATE SET list also refreshes ts, is_error and stop_reason, so firing it on an equal-token sibling can move a row's ts backwards to an earlier streaming copy and quietly re-bucket it — every rule buckets on ts (constraint 19, UTC epoch-anchored keys). (b) Constraint 2's own regression requirement holds: this touches the one statement all seven collectors share, so the test asserting that re-reading identical data returns changes=0 is mandatory, not optional. Both are already implied by the feature; state them.

name: verify: report pruned sources, reconcile Grok, and FAIL on an empty store
description: cli/verify.ts treats any row whose transcript is missing as a hard failure (claudeNotInLogs === 0 inside the PASS expression at :528-536), but Claude Code prunes transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays and users delete project directories, so every install older than roughly 30 days fails permanently — this install is 22 days old, which is why nobody has hit it yet. verify.ts:146 also calls the read-write openDb, so on a fresh clone or with a wrong VOLE_DB it creates ~/.vole/vole.db, counts zero of everything and prints PASS. Grok's 789 exact rows are never reconciled at all (the coverage header at verify.ts:20-29 names Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex only) although the README claims every stored row is reconciled. Add a 'source pruned' counter that is reported rather than failed, open the store read-only and FAIL when it is absent or empty, add the Grok section, and expose verify as an importable function with --json so the assess report, the compliance evidence pack, the pilot report and fleet health embed a real result instead of a decorative PASS.
desktop_surface: Settings replaces the hard-coded 'Verification: Every stored row reconciled' string with the last real verify result, its timestamp and the pruned-row count; the same three figures appear at the foot of every evidence bundle and in the digest.
data_source: packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts:20-29,146,271,528-536; ~/.claude/.last-cleanup and cleanupPeriodDays in ~/.claude/settings.json (unset here, so the tool default applies).
honest_limit: A pruned row can never be re-proved from local evidence — it becomes a permanent third class between pass and fail, and an auditor has to accept 'source deleted by the vendor tool' as evidence of nothing rather than as evidence of correctness.
competitive_note: v1 embeds a verify PASS line inside vole assess, the compliance evidence pack, the pilot report and fleet health, so all four ship a check that is about to fail forever for every user or that passes on an empty file. market.md's open question is whether security buyers accept on-device SQLite as compliance evidence at all; the only argument Vole has is a reconciliation that runs and can fail.
v1_ref: History horizon and retention-loss disclosure
field_verified: Every claim confirmed, and I dated the failure. The PASS expression includes `claudeNotInLogs === 0` verbatim. `const db = openDb()` at verify.ts:146 is the read-write opener, and openDb does `mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true }); const db = new Database(file);` -- it CREATES the store, and with zero rows every counter is 0 and `claudeRowsTotal <= truth.size` is 0 <= 0, so it prints PASS on an empty database. The coverage header at :20-29 names 'Claude Code (tokens + cost), OpenCode (tokens, two ways), Codex' -- Grok is absent, and Grok holds 789 exact rows here that are never reconciled while README claims every stored row is. THE PRUNING CLOCK: `cat ~/.claude/.last-cleanup` -> '2026-09-07T05:13:50.752Z' (the cleanup ran TODAY); cleanupPeriodDays is unset in ~/.claude/settings.json so the 30-day default applies; the oldest claude_code event is 2026-08-15 and the oldest surviving transcript is also 2026-08-15 -- a 23-day horizon. Right now 0 of 556 claude_code raw_refs point at a missing file, so verify still passes; it crosses 30 days around 2026-09-14, after which claudeNotInLogs goes positive and pnpm verify FAILS permanently.
constraint: C20 directly ('pnpm verify must keep passing and must be extended for any new source with exact tokens') -- this feature IS that constraint's maintenance, and Grok has had exact tokens since it landed. C15: exposing verify as an importable function means moving the top-level `await sleep(7_000)` inside a function, the same refactor #6 and #25 need -- do it once, first. Principle 4 is currently leaking in three ways at once.

name: Incident figures reach every reader: observed, baseline, threshold
description: Principle 3 says incidents are explainable with real figures and the columns are written by every rule (anomalies.observed, baseline, threshold, detected_at, anomaly_key — schema.ts:42-64), yet no reader selects them: queries.ts:230 builds IncidentRow without them and DB.swift:227 mirrors that omission, so the app feed, MCP vole_incidents, the digest and every v1 artefact promising 'the exact figures that fired' ship a prose sentence and nothing machine-readable. Add the three columns to both readers, to the Swift Incident struct and to the public export schema, and render an expanded incident row as a fact block — 'observed 1.24M tokens in the 10-minute window · baseline 180K (median of 7 other active windows) · threshold 3x (default)' — with the anomaly_key in a monospace selectable field for dedupe and evidence. A 'Why this fired' sheet renders the rule's window, group key, gates and effective config with its origin (default vs policy.json scope) once RuleConfig lands.
desktop_surface: Incidents list: the existing disclosure row (DashboardView.swift:475) expands to the fact block plus the anomaly_key, with Why this fired / Copy evidence (JSON including the three figures) / Show on Timeline buttons; the same three fields appear in vole_incidents, the digest and the export schema.
data_source: anomalies.observed/baseline/threshold/detected_at/anomaly_key; queries.ts:226-236 IncidentRow; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/DB.swift:227; detect/*.ts module constants (burn-rate.ts:4-7, loop.ts:4-8, error-storm.ts:4-6, rate-limit.ts:4-5, context-pressure.ts:5-7).
honest_limit: INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key (db.ts:137) freezes the first verdict, so observed and baseline are the values at first sight and not the worst seen — every figure must be labelled 'at detection', and the templated detail string can disagree with a re-derived figure until an explicit upsert-on-greater-observed clause and a re-notify path land.
competitive_note: Gateway and EDR vendors show a verdict and keep the numbers behind it in their cloud model; a locally recomputable figure with its threshold is what turns an alert into evidence a works council and an auditor both accept (ISO 42001 A.6.2.8, NIST AU-3). This is the cheapest repair of principle 3 and it unblocks four v1 items — webhook payloads, the SIEM forwarder, the evidence pack, the rule dry-run — that already assume it is done.
v1_ref: RuleConfig contract, effective threshold in every incident, conformance tests
field_verified: Columns exist and hold real values. schema.ts:54-56 `observed REAL NOT NULL, baseline REAL, threshold REAL`, :59 `detected_at INTEGER NOT NULL`, :44 `anomaly_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`. Live sample: `burn_rate_spike|warn|36751.0|12149.0|36447.0|1788504755011`. Both readers confirmed to omit them — queries.ts:229-231 selects `id, rule, severity, tool, session_id, model, window_start, window_end, title, detail, confidence, source` and DB.swift:227-228 is the identical list. So the three most load-bearing numbers in the product are written every poll and read by nobody.
constraint: Constraint 3 (INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key, db.ts:154 `stmt.run({...r, ...ORIGIN}).changes > 0`) freezes the first verdict, so observed/baseline are at-first-sight values, never worst-seen. The feature names this and reconciles it with an 'at detection' label — the right call, since changing it requires an explicit upsert clause plus a re-notify path (constraint 3 says so in terms). Second reconciliation the feature gets right: the templated `detail` string can disagree with a re-derived figure, which is an argument for rendering the columns and de-emphasising the prose, not for recomputing.

name: Ship-blocker gate: a bundled .app that actually launches
description: Three defects still make a downloaded build fragile and v1 has no item for any of them, while its Tier 7 release pipeline assumes a working app. Icon/build.mjs:15 resolves sharp by globbing node_modules/.pnpm/sharp@*/ — sharp has zero hits in pnpm-lock.yaml and Icon/Vole.icns is untracked in git, so bundle.sh:37 runs the generator on every fresh clone and require(undefined) throws; build-sea.mjs:49 copies process.execPath, so a Homebrew Node ships a collector with /opt/homebrew dylib links that dies after notarisation succeeds; bundle.sh:24 defaults VERSION to 0.1.0 against a 0.1.4 package.json, and mcp.ts:94 still hard-codes serverInfo.version '0.1.0'. Fix: declare sharp or commit Vole.icns, add an `otool -L` gate failing on links outside /usr/lib and /System/Library, read VERSION from package.json, and add a macOS CI job that runs bundle.sh and launches the .app in a fresh user account.
desktop_surface: The app launching from a fresh clone and a fresh account at all, and Settings → About reporting the real version instead of 0.1.0 on a 0.1.4 build.
data_source: apps/mac/Icon/build.mjs:15 and the untracked apps/mac/Icon/Vole.icns; apps/mac/bundle.sh:24,37,58,59; packages/core/scripts/build-sea.mjs:49; packages/core/src/cli/mcp.ts:94; .github/workflows/ci.yml
honest_limit: The code map's top-ranked ship-blocker is already fixed and is corrected here: Theme.swift now defines `Res`, which looks in Contents/Resources/Vole_Vole.bundle before falling back to Bundle.module, and all three call sites (VoleApp.swift:51,102 and ToolIcon) go through it — so the remaining exposure is only that the .module fallback still fatalErrors if a future layout change drops the bundle, which is exactly what a launch-the-.app CI job catches and static review does not. An arm64 CI runner cannot observe the Intel EBADARCH path (bundle.sh passes no --arch flags), so 'runs on Intel' stays unverified until a second runner or a universal binary exists.
competitive_note: Distribution is table stakes for the endpoint vendors Vole must coexist with: market.md's MDM section (the CrowdStrike/SimpleMDM recipe, PPPC profile before pkg) shows buyers expect a signed pkg and a working install before a pilot starts. A DMG that fails to build or launch loses to ccusage, which is a free npm install.
v1_ref: Release pipeline: signed, notarised, SBOM, SLSA provenance, cosign, Homebrew cask, vole doctor --verify-install
field_verified: Every defect CONFIRMED at the exact cited line, and the sharp one is worse than stated. Icon/build.mjs:15 `const sharp = require(globSync(`${root}node_modules/.pnpm/sharp@*/node_modules/sharp`)[0]);` — and `grep -c sharp pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 0 AND no package.json in the repo mentions sharp at all, so `globSync(...)[0]` is undefined and require(undefined) throws on any fresh clone; the local node_modules/.pnpm/sharp@0.35.4 is a phantom that --frozen-lockfile will not reproduce. `git ls-files apps/mac/Icon/` lists eight files and Vole.icns is not among them, though 141309 bytes of it sit on disk — so bundle.sh:38 `if [ ! -f Icon/Vole.icns ] ...` fires on every clone. bundle.sh:24 `VERSION="${VERSION:-0.1.0}"` against package.json '0.1.4', with Info.plist:12 hardcoding 0.1.0 and bundle.sh:59 sed-replacing that literal. mcp.ts:94 `serverInfo: { name: 'vole', version: '0.1.0' }`. build-sea.mjs:49 `copyFileSync(process.execPath, binPath)`. ci.yml has no bundle or launch job. The code-map correction also holds: Theme.swift:11 `enum Res` exists and VoleApp.swift:51 and :102 both go through Res.image().
constraint: Constraint 14 (SEA output inherits the builder's node, must be statically linked) — the otool -L gate does not conflict with it, it mechanically enforces a constraint that is currently written down and unchecked. Real undisclosed friction with constraint 16: Hardened Runtime and allow-jit are mandatory for --release, so a CI job that launches a signed .app needs a signing identity and a notarytool credential, while ci.yml states 'Nothing here writes to the repo or uses a secret; fork PRs get a read-only token' and declares permissions: contents: read. Reconciliation: the CI job launches the ad-hoc build only (bundle.sh:68 already warns Gatekeeper rejects it elsewhere), and notarised-launch verification stays a release-time manual step.

name: Content boundary as a branded type, with verify --content as its runtime twin
description: 'Vole never stores prompt or tool content' is the load-bearing claim for every DPO conversation, and today it is an unenforced convention spread across seven collector parse loops where the raw line is in scope (claude-code.ts:91-99, codex.ts:118, opencode.ts:104, devin.ts:71, grok.ts:102) -- and the DLP scanner is about to put far more content in scope than exists today. Give the raw readers a branded return type -- type Content = string & { readonly __content: unique symbol } -- that only hashOf(), classifyOf() and lengthOf() accept, so a UsageEvent or secret_sightings field can never be assigned a raw line without an explicit, greppable cast. Pair it with verify --content as the runtime twin: run the detector table over vole.db and any export, failing CI on a single hit. Prevention plus detection is what turns the claim from 'we are careful' into 'here is the check and here is every place it was widened'.
desktop_surface: Settings -> Privacy gains a 'No content stored' card showing the last verify --content result with its timestamp, the number of casts through the boundary in the shipped build, and a link to each cast site in the source.
data_source: The five collector parse loops named above; types.ts UsageEvent; the new secret_sightings insert path; sync/manifest.ts; the dlp_detectors table as the scan rule set
honest_limit: Casts remain possible and a determined contributor can widen the boundary -- the control is that every widening is a visible diff in review, not that it is impossible. It also covers only Vole's own store: the vendor transcripts on the same disk hold the full content and remain by far the larger exposure, which the card must say beside the green tick.
competitive_note: v1 has the detection half (verify --content) but not the prevention half. The research found that none of the 27 vendors covering coding agents states its prompt-retention posture at all -- a type-level boundary plus a CI gate is the strongest form of that statement anyone in the category could make.
v1_ref: Redaction manifest and verify --content (prove the DB and exports hold no content)
field_verified: The make-or-break check PASSES: packages/core/package.json defines `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"`, root package.json defines `"typecheck": "pnpm -r --if-present typecheck"`, and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `- run: pnpm typecheck` before `pnpm test`. So a branded type is actually enforced in CI, not decorative — without that step the whole feature would be theatre. Also CONFIRMED: verify.ts today has NO argv parsing at all and no content check, so `verify --content` is net-new here, not an existing half.
constraint: Constraint 15 (per-file esbuild transpilation, no tsc emit) — a branded type erases at runtime, so it is unaffected; this is the one type-level trick that survives the build. Constraint 20 is the real conflict: verify.ts's own header states RATES is 'a deliberate independent copy' so that 'a bug in the product's own formula cannot cancel itself out' — importing dlp_detectors into verify --content violates that principle exactly, making the check circular, because a detector missing from the pack would be invisible to both the scanner and its verifier. Reconciliation: verify --content carries its own independent detector list, mirrored by hand like RATES, with the same comment explaining why.

name: Detection budget: O(W) baselines and skip-empty polls
description: detect/util.ts:56 medianExcluding copies, filters and sorts the whole window array once per window, and burn-rate.ts:43 and loop.ts:34 each call it per window, giving O(W^2 log W) per tool+model per poll — measured 164 ms at 2k windows, 2.4 s at 8k and 15.6 s at 20k, which is roughly one year of daily use for a single tool+model — while collect.ts:56 re-runs every rule over the entire usage_events table every 5 seconds even when zero rows were inserted. v1 adds roughly forty more rules onto that same loop plus scans over tool_calls, findings and posture, which is arithmetically impossible at 5-second cadence on a laptop. Sort each group once and derive every leave-one-out median in O(1) from the sorted array, skip detection when totalInserted is 0 and rateLimits is empty, and add a perf test asserting a 20k-window fixture completes under 500 ms.
desktop_surface: Nothing visible by design — it is what keeps Settings > Refresh interval honest and the published CPU/RAM footprint claim defensible; the only user-facing effect is that Dashboard incident freshness stops lagging by whole poll cycles.
data_source: packages/core/src/detect/util.ts:56; detect/burn-rate.ts:43; detect/loop.ts:34; cli/collect.ts:56-59; measured against the live ~/.vole/vole.db (28,916 rows)
honest_limit: Skipping detection on empty polls delays purely time-based firings — a window that crosses a threshold because time passed rather than because rows arrived — until the next insert; that must be documented and the first pass after startup kept unconditional. The O(1) leave-one-out derivation is exact for the median only, so any future rule wanting a trimmed mean or a percentile baseline needs its own pass and its own budget. The budget also only covers rules that scan usage_events; every ledger-scanning rule in this shard needs a separately bounded window or the fix buys nothing.
competitive_note: v1 plans a rule-config contract, dry-run replay and roughly forty new rules on the existing loop without ever costing the loop. Nightfall publishes about 50MB and 1% CPU as its endpoint footprint bar (market.md section 7), and a 15-second poll on a year-old store puts Vole outside the bar buyers already benchmark against before they evaluate a single detection.
v1_ref: RuleConfig contract, effective threshold in every incident, conformance tests
field_verified: CONFIRMED, AND THE FEATURE UNDERSTATES THE COST BY ~4x. util.ts:56-59 verbatim: `export function medianExcluding(values: number[], excludeIndex: number): number { const rest = values.filter((_, i) => i !== excludeIndex); return median(rest); }` and median() at L21 does `const s = [...values].sort(...)` — a copy, a filter and a sort per window. Called per window at burn-rate.ts:43 and loop.ts:34. collect.ts:56-60 runs `SELECT * FROM usage_events ORDER BY ts` over all 29,440 live rows and then detectBySource, unconditionally, every interval (collect.ts:13 default 5000ms), with no totalInserted guard anywhere. I benchmarked the exact medianExcluding loop on this machine under node: 2,000 windows = 427ms, 8,000 = 8,879ms, 20,000 = 61,714ms — versus the feature's 164ms / 2.4s / 15.6s. Current scale is still small (largest tool+model group is 302 windows for claude_code/claude-sonnet-5; the loop rule spans 2,173 session-windows over 246 sessions), so the wall is months away, not a year.
constraint: Constraint 3 is satisfied by construction and worth stating: every anomaly_key is bucket-anchored, never now()-derived, so skipping a poll can change detection LATENCY but can never change a key — the skip is safe against the determinism test at detect.test.ts:120. Constraint 19 (UTC epoch-anchored integer bucketing) constrains the O(1) rewrite: deriving leave-one-out medians from one sorted array must not reorder or re-bucket, only re-index. Constraint 20: the proposed 20k-window <500ms assertion needs headroom, since the unoptimised path takes 61s here and CI hardware is slower. UNMEASURED IN THE FEATURE: the `SELECT * FROM usage_events` full-table materialisation into JS every 5 seconds is the dominant cost TODAY at 29,440 rows, and the O(1) median fix does not touch it — the skip-empty-polls guard is what buys that back, so the two halves are not interchangeable and the guard is the more urgent one.

name: Read-model contract and capability-probed navigation shell
description: DashSection is a closed four-case enum (DashboardView.swift:190-238) and DB.swift hand-restates queries.ts although README.md:436 claims a one-to-one port (no zero-fill, limit 100 vs 500, model-only breakdown), so every new screen costs two divergent implementations. Make each shared read model a named SQL view created by migrate() in db.ts (v_people, v_agent_inventory, v_incident_explained, v_coverage) so the Swift port shrinks to `SELECT * FROM v_x WHERE ts >= ?` plus a row decoder; stamp PRAGMA user_version in migrate() and read it in DB.open; widen DB.swift's `run(_ sql:, _ binds: [Int])` to a small Bind enum with sqlite3_bind_text, without which no drill-down keyed on session_id, rule or user is expressible at all today. Then replace the enum with three sidebar groups (Monitor / Risk / Manage) whose sections each declare `requires: [String]`, probed once per launch through a DB.hasTable(_:) helper over PRAGMA table_info: a section whose backing table is absent still appears and renders a ContentUnavailableView naming the missing table and the collector version that would write it, never an empty list. Section badges are one COUNT per section refreshed on the existing Store poll.
desktop_surface: NavigationSplitView sidebar: 12 rows in three groups, each with a count badge and a grey 'unavailable' dot; a persistent amber banner in the StaleBanner slot reading 'Database schema v7, this app reads v5 — Costs and Posture are hidden'; the shared vole.section AppStorage key, --section= launch argument and MenuPanel hand-off keep working.

Views cannot take parameters beyond the outer WHERE, so genuinely per-row work (getSessionDetail's per-agent context deltas, queries.ts:395) stays hand-ported in both languages, and any column drop or rename still needs a coordinated collector-and-app release.

field_verified: All four anchors confirmed, with line drift. DashboardView.swift:191-211 is a closed 4-case enum (`case dashboard/incidents/breakdown/settings`), not :216. DB.swift:141 `private func run(_ sql: String, _ binds: [Int] = [], _ row: (OpaquePointer) -> Void)` and :149 `sqlite3_bind_int64(stmt, Int32(i+1), Int64(v))` — Int64-only, so no text bind exists; a session_id or rule drill-down is literally inexpressible today. `sqlite3 ~/.vole/vole.db 'pragma user_version'` returns `0` — no stamp. db.ts:41-53 migrate() probes `PRAGMA table_info(usage_events)`. Two corrections: SidebarGroup ALREADY exists (DashboardView.swift:185-189, cases monitor/app), and `.badge()` is already wired at :266 (`.badge(s == .incidents ? store.allIncidents.count : 0)`), so the badge mechanism is an extension not a build. StaleBanner IS reachable from the dashboard (DashboardView.swift:283), so the claimed banner slot is real.

name: Two-writer safety and a read-only DB open path
description: db.ts:60 sets no busy_timeout (node:sqlite default 0) and sqlite.ts:59 issues a deferred BEGIN, while two writers are an explicitly tolerated configuration — Collector.swift:10-12 spawns the embedded collector next to a possibly running `pnpm collect`. Any overlap yields immediate SQLITE_BUSY: a poll logs 'pass failed', and the unguarded first runOnce() at collect.ts:155 can exit the process before polling ever starts. openDb is also a process singleton (db.ts:56 returns the cached handle and ignores the file argument after the first call) that always mkdirs, runs the full SCHEMA and migrates, so every reader — top, statusline, pr, digest, mcp, and v1's planned hook, doctor, export and NDJSON tail — opens the store read-write. Add busy_timeout=5000, BEGIN IMMEDIATE in sqlite.ts transaction(), a wrapped first runOnce, and an openDbReadOnly(file) that skips DDL and opens SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY for every non-collector entrypoint.
desktop_surface: Removes the silent stall behind MenuPanel's StaleBanner and the 'Setting up' SetupCard when the collector aborts on a lock; Settings → Database status can then distinguish 'read-only reader attached' from 'collector down'.
data_source: packages/core/src/db.ts:56,60; packages/core/src/sqlite.ts:59; packages/core/src/cli/collect.ts:155; packages/core/src/cli/statusline.ts; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/Collector.swift:10-12 (DB.swift already sets busy_timeout 2000, so the Swift reader is the only surface that gets this right today)
honest_limit: A read-only open cannot create or migrate the store, so a reader launched before the first collect must render 'no database yet' rather than silently creating one — which is exactly what verify.ts:146 does today and why it prints PASS on an empty DB. busy_timeout only bounds the wait; a genuinely long writer still fails the reader, so the surface must show 'store busy', never a zero. This adds no protection against a second process writing under a different schema version, since there is no user_version stamp (db.ts:41-53 migrates by column probing).
competitive_note: v1's launchd item asserts 'P4 already makes a double-run safe; the pidfile is hygiene' — idempotency makes a double-run correct, not concurrent, and that is the claim this corrects. No competitor is affected because none uses an on-device SQLite as the system of record; this is the cost of the local-first differentiator over the Cyberhaven and Nightfall cloud sinks, and it is the prerequisite for the osquery ATC pack, which adds a third concurrent reader running as root.
v1_ref: Collector as a launchd agent
field_verified: Every line CONFIRMED. db.ts:56 `if (cached) return cached;` inside `openDb(file: string = paths.db())` — the file argument is ignored after the first call, exactly as claimed. db.ts:60-61 sets `journal_mode = WAL` and `synchronous = NORMAL` and nothing else, so busy_timeout is node:sqlite's default 0. sqlite.ts:59 `this.db.exec('BEGIN')` — deferred. collect.ts:155 `runOnce();` bare, with the try/catch living only inside the setInterval at 160-165, so the first pass can kill the process before polling starts. verify.ts:146 `const db = openDb();` — a read-only tool opening read-write. DB.swift:136 `sqlite3_busy_timeout(handle, 2000)` — the Swift reader is indeed the only surface that gets it right. And the contested claim is confirmed verbatim in Collector.swift:10-12: 'two instances polling the same WAL-mode database is wasteful, not unsafe'. Bonus: sqlite.ts:41 already passes `{ readOnly: opts.readonly }` to DatabaseSync, so openDbReadOnly is roughly five lines reusing what exists.
constraint: Constraint 12 (schema evolution is add-nullable-column-only via PRAGMA probing, no user_version stamp) — a read-only open cannot run migrate(), so a reader against an older file fails on a missing column instead of healing it; the feature names this and it is the correct limit to publish. Undisclosed and important: DB.swift:130-134 falls back to SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE with the comment 'WAL databases sometimes refuse a pure READONLY connection', so openDbReadOnly needs the same fallback or the readers regress from a wrong open mode to no data at all. Reconciliation: try READONLY, fall back to READWRITE-without-DDL, render 'store busy' rather than a zero — never create or migrate from a reader.

name: Codex collector v2 as a Tier 1 correctness fix: thread state, spawn edges and rollout byte offsets
description: v1 files Codex collector v2 under Tier 6 platform coverage, but it is the fix for the second-ranked bug in the repo (codex.ts:197 keys sub-agent rollouts identically to their parent, a principle-5 violation) and the precondition for any Codex ledger row. ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite (verified today: 66 threads) carries per-thread id, rollout_path, model, model_provider, approval_mode, sandbox_policy, git_branch, git_origin_url, cli_version, tokens_used, reasoning_effort, agent_nickname and a thread_source JSON holding subagent.thread_spawn.{parent_thread_id, depth}; thread_spawn_edges now has 2 rows, so v1's warning that it is empty is stale and the parent/child tree is directly readable. ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite thread_turns additionally stores (thread_id, turn_id, rollout_ordinal, status, duration_ms, rollout_byte_offset, rollout_end_byte_offset) — Codex maintains byte offsets into its own rollout files, which neither v1 nor the code map noticed. Rekey events on (thread_id, turn_id or ordinal), bind session_id from the first session_meta only, set agent_id from the spawn edge, use the byte offsets plus size and mtime to stop re-reading ~100 MB every 5 seconds, and fill the git_branch and model columns that are NULL on 46 of 83 rows today.
desktop_surface: Dashboard → Breakdown shows real Codex model rows instead of em dashes; repo/branch grouping and pnpm pr stop being Claude-only; sub-agent spend folds under the parent session in the session drill-down instead of appearing as an unrelated session.
data_source: ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite tables threads and thread_spawn_edges; ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite tables thread_turns and thread_items; packages/core/src/collectors/codex.ts:88,107,197
honest_limit: thread_history_1.sqlite is a partial projection — 6 turns across 66 threads here — so byte offsets exist only for recent turns and the collector must fall back to size+mtime skipping for the rest. threads.first_user_message is prompt content and must never be SELECTed. Rekeying changes event_key for existing Codex rows, so it needs a documented one-time rebuild rather than a silent migration.
competitive_note: market.md white space 3: nobody names OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime, and OpenAI's own governance covers only ChatGPT-workspace accounts with metrics defaulting to statsig and `codex exec` emitting none (row 107, §4). A Codex collector that is wrong about which sub-agent spent what is worse than none.
v1_ref: Codex collector v2: thread metadata, spawn tree, meter cross-check (Tier 6) — promote to Tier 1 and add thread_turns byte offsets
field_verified: Nearly everything verified; one claim is wrong. ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite: threads has 66 rows and its schema carries every named column — rollout_path, model_provider, cwd, sandbox_policy, approval_mode, tokens_used, git_sha, git_branch, git_origin_url, cli_version, first_user_message, agent_nickname, model, reasoning_effort, thread_source. thread_spawn_edges is `(parent_thread_id TEXT NOT NULL, child_thread_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL)` with 2 rows — v1's 'it is empty' warning is indeed stale, and both children of parent 01a07a53-4b99 are directly readable. thread_history_1.sqlite thread_turns confirms `rollout_ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, duration_ms INTEGER, rollout_byte_offset INTEGER, rollout_end_ordinal INTEGER, rollout_end_byte_offset INTEGER`, 6 rows across 5 threads, with real values (e.g. offsets 22190→1694698, status 'failed', duration_ms 106587) — Codex really does maintain byte offsets into its own rollouts, and neither v1 nor the code map noticed. Rollouts total 104.7 MB across 66 files, matching '~100 MB every 5 seconds'. Live DB: 83 codex rows, model NULL on exactly 46 — the claim's figure to the unit — and git_branch NULL on all 83. WRONG: thread_source is not a JSON holding subagent.thread_spawn.{parent_thread_id, depth}; on this machine it is a plain string enum — '' 50, 'user' 13, 'subagent' 2, 'voice_chat' 1. The parent link comes from thread_spawn_edges, which exists; depth is not recorded anywhere I could find.
constraint: This feature resolves constraint conflicts rather than creating them. It fixes constraint 1 and principle 5 (codex.ts:197's `codex:${sessionId ?? filePath}:${index}` collides across sub-agent rollouts, ranked bug #2 and the top collector bug in the repo) and constraint 10, the subagent contract that child events carry the parent's session_id plus their own agent_id, which Codex violates today. It correctly honours constraint 8 by opening both SQLite stores read-only, and correctly flags that threads.first_user_message is prompt content that must never be SELECTed — that is constraint 7 handled properly. The one obligation it names and must keep: rekeying changes event_key for every existing Codex row, so it needs a documented one-time rebuild, never a silent migration, and verify must be extended for the new key shape per constraint 20.

name: Annotated timeline: incident marks drawn, UTC buckets rendered in local time, sparkline zero-filled
description: README.md:261-263 promises an incident-annotated timeline; DashboardView.swift:13-23 already computes marks() and then draws nothing but a hover count, so Mark.severity is dead code. Draw one PointMark per bucket in Pal.severity colour beneath the bars plus a thin incident lane under the plot, and make a click select that bucket and filter the Incidents list to it. The same change fixes the alignment bug that would otherwise make the marks lie: buckets are UTC epoch integers (queries.ts CAST, DB.swift ts/86400000) but are drawn with `BarMark(x:.value(..., unit: .day))` (DashboardView.swift:69), which re-bins by local calendar, so west of UTC every daily bar sits in the previous local day and hover snaps selectedBucket one slot off — replace with `BarMark(xStart: p.date, xEnd: p.date + bucketMs)` and no `unit:`, keeping keys UTC per constraint 19. DB.swift:204 also omits the zero-fill queries.ts:155-161 performs, so MenuPanel's Sparkline draws six wide bars for six active hours instead of a 24-slot day.
desktop_surface: Overview timeline: severity-coloured marks pinned on the x-axis with an incident lane below the plot; bars align with the hover callout, which prints the UTC window it aggregates; clicking a mark filters Incidents, and 'Show on Timeline' (DashboardView.swift:498) scrolls to and selects the mark. MenuPanel's sparkline becomes a real 24-hour shape.
data_source: anomalies.window_start/window_end/severity/rule (schema.ts:42-64) already loaded into Store.incidents; DashboardView.swift:13 marks(), :36,:57,:69 chart; DB.swift:204 timeseries; queries.ts:155-161 zero-fill.
honest_limit: An incident pins to the bucket of its window_start, so a burn window straddling midnight UTC appears once, on the earlier day, and a UTC-anchored bar can still straddle two local days — true local-midnight bucketing would change the keys in both readers and is a separate, larger decision. 190 of the 249 live incidents on this machine are burn_rate_spike, so without the noise controls the lane renders as a solid band rather than a signal.
competitive_note: Anthropic states plainly that anomaly detection, baselining and correlation are the customer's job (code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage); the annotated timeline is the visible proof Vole does that job, and 'the chart disagrees with the incident list' is the fastest way to lose the exact-figures positioning everything else rests on.
v1_ref: Incident noise controls: window chaining, per-session cap, info rollup
field_verified: Every claim confirmed, one at the exact cited line. DashboardView.swift:69 is verbatim `BarMark(x: .value("Time", p.date, unit: unit), y: .value("Tokens", v))`. `date +%Z` on this machine returns `MST -0700` — west of UTC, so the misalignment is LIVE on the author's own laptop, not theoretical. marks() at :13-23 computes `Mark(bucket:severity:count:)` but the only consumer is the callout at :106-110 which reads `s.incidents` (the count) — `Mark.severity` is genuinely dead. DB.swift:204-221 builds the bucket map and returns `map.values.sorted` with no fill; queries.ts:157-161 runs the `for (let b = first; b <= last; b += bucketMs)` fill loop. Sparkline (MenuPanel.swift:115) is `Array(points.suffix(24)).map(\.total)` — positional, so 6 active hours draw 6 wide bars. Noise figure verified exactly: 152 warn + 38 critical burn_rate_spike = 190 of 249 live incidents.
constraint: Constraint 19 (UTC-epoch integer keys, local presentation converts at the view) is currently VIOLATED by line 69 — `unit: .day` hands Swift Charts a Date and lets the local calendar re-bin it, which is presentation changing the key. The proposed `BarMark(xStart:xEnd:)` with no `unit:` is the literal reconciliation: keys stay UTC, only the draw converts. Nothing else touched.

name: Aggregate confidence label: replace MIN(confidence)
description: queries.ts:80 and DB.swift:180 both compute a group's confidence as MIN(confidence), relying on 'activity_only' sorting alphabetically before 'exact'. On this machine Grok stores 789 exact rows alongside 969 activity_only rows, so the summary returns tool='grok' with 168,352,826 tokens wearing the 'no tokens' badge — a true figure labelled untrustworthy, which is principle 2 inverted. Replace the expression in both readers with `CASE WHEN SUM(confidence != 'activity_only') = 0 THEN 'activity_only' ELSE 'exact' END` and expose an activityOnlyCalls count beside it so a mixed group renders as visibly mixed rather than silently rounded to one label.
desktop_surface: MenuPanel's top-5 tools list and Dashboard > Breakdown stop showing 'no tokens' next to a 168M-token Grok row; the mixed case renders 'exact (969 calls without tokens)'; the same count travels into vole_summary, the digest and any export that carries a confidence field.
data_source: packages/core/src/queries.ts:80; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/DB.swift:180; live vole.db: grok 789 exact / 969 activity_only, 168,352,826 tokens.
honest_limit: A two-value enum cannot express 'mostly exact' — constraint 4 forbids adding an estimated tier even though ROADMAP principle 2 names one — so the call count beside the badge is the only honest expression of the mix, and a group of one exact row among a thousand activity_only rows still reads 'exact' with the count telling the reader why.
competitive_note: 'Never invent a number, confidence always visible' is the claim that gets Vole past a DPO and a works council (market.md §2); a badge that contradicts the number beside it is the first thing a security reviewer screenshots, and v1 layers confidence badges onto every new view, export, evidence pack and relay aggregate without fixing the expression they all read.
v1_ref: vole export with versioned public schema (vole.event.v1)
field_verified: The best-sourced feature in the shard — both line numbers exact and the figures reproduce to the digit. queries.ts:80 is verbatim `MIN(confidence) AS confidence`; DB.swift:180 is verbatim `SUM(cost_usd), MIN(confidence)`. Live store: `grok|exact|789 calls|168352826 tokens` and `grok|activity_only|969 calls` — so MIN returns 'activity_only' (it sorts first) for a group holding 168.3M real tokens, and Theme.swift:178 `Labels.confidence` maps that to the string "no tokens". BUT the blast radius in the desktop_surface is wrong: Breakdown groups by `(tool, model, confidence)` (DB.swift:263) so it already renders grok's exact and activity_only rows separately and correctly badged, and MenuPanel's top-5 (MenuPanel.swift:201-229) renders no ConfidenceBadge at all. The mislabel actually reaches `vole_summary` (MCP), `getDigest`, and `swift run Vole --dump` (VoleApp.swift:44 prints `conf=\(t.confidence)`).
constraint: Constraint 4 (exactly two confidence values, no 'estimated' tier even though ROADMAP principle 2 names one) — the feature names the constraint itself and reconciles correctly: a call count beside the badge is the only honest way to express a mix without inventing a third tier. Nothing else touched; the CASE expression is a drop-in for MIN in both readers.

name: Collector process supervision: the orphan, the exit status, and launchd throttling
description: Confirmed live on this machine right now: two `Vole.app/Contents/MacOS/vole-collector` processes, both PPID 1, started ten seconds apart, 570 MB RSS each, with no parent Vole.app running — `Collector.swift`'s own ponytail comment predicts this and calls it "wasteful, not unsafe"; measured, it is 1.1 GB against a 50 MB budget and one of them was sampled at 28.4% CPU. Add a pidfile at `~/.vole/collector.pid` holding pid + executable path + start time, written by collect.ts and checked by `Collector.start()`: a live pid whose executable path matches means adopt, not spawn; a dead or mismatched one is cleared. Give the Process a `terminationHandler` that records `exit_status` into `collector_runs` so a crash is distinguishable from a clean quit, add a SIGTERM handler in collect.ts that unlinks the pidfile, and ship the LaunchAgent with `KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit=false}` plus `ThrottleInterval=30` so a crash loop cannot itself become the footprint.
desktop_surface: Settings > Footprint gains a Collector row: running / adopted-unmanaged / crashed (N times today) / not running, with the pid and last exit status. The existing `.stale` banner keeps its meaning (the data is old) and gains a separate "collector process is not running" state — today those are indistinguishable, because `collectorStatus` is derived from MAX(collector_state.last_scanned_at) and only claude-code.ts ever writes that table.
data_source: ~/.vole/collector.pid; Process.terminationHandler exit status; launchctl job state; collector_state.last_scanned_at for the existing staleness signal.
honest_limit: A pidfile is advisory — a SIGKILLed collector leaves a stale one, which is why the check verifies the recorded executable path and start time rather than liveness alone. Vole cannot supervise a collector it did not spawn (a developer's hand-run `pnpm collect`), and reports that case as "adopted, unmanaged" rather than pretending to own it.
competitive_note: v1 dismissed the pidfile as "hygiene" because principle 4 makes a double run safe for *data*; the measured 1.1 GB shows the cost is a footprint failure, not a correctness one. Every EDR competitor gets supervision free from a launchd-managed sysext; a spawned helper has to earn it, and Santa's four-part layout (app, launchd collector, sync, CLI) is the pattern market.md §7 says to copy.
v1_ref: Collector as a launchd agent
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Ledger scan cursors and insert-gated, bounded-window detection
description: The ledger is unaffordable under the current poll design: every 5 seconds the collector full-scans a 507 MB opencode.db (46,584 parts, 12,292 of them tool parts), re-parses every Codex rollout, then re-runs every rule over the whole usage_events table at O(W² log W) — measured at 15.6 s per poll at 20k windows. Add ledger_state(source_key, last_cursor, last_scanned_at) and gate detection on totalInserted > 0 with each rule bounded to a trailing window instead of the full table. For OpenCode the cursor must be part.rowid, not part.time_updated: the schema has only part_session_idx and part_message_id_id_idx (verified), Vole opens third-party stores read-only so it cannot add an index, and rowid order matches time order on this store (rowid 3,233→49,839 tracks time_updated 1780757623923→1788639485696); re-check time_updated on the returned page to catch in-place edits. Claude reuses its existing byte offsets, Codex and Grok skip files whose (size, mtime) are unchanged.
desktop_surface: Settings 'Collector' block shows last pass duration, rows scanned and per-source cursor age; the stale banner distinguishes 'no new data' from 'collector down' instead of showing 'Setting up…' forever.
data_source: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db part.rowid/time_updated (schema verified today); collector_state.last_offset/last_mtime; Codex rollout file size+mtime; packages/core/src/cli/collect.ts:56 and packages/core/src/detect/util.ts:56
honest_limit: rowid is not stable across a VACUUM and can be reused after deletes, so the cursor is paired with a time_updated re-check and a full re-scan is forced whenever max(rowid) goes backwards. Bounding the detection window changes the baselines of burn-rate and loop rules for historical data, so the window length is stored on the incident and the first pass over an existing store still runs unbounded once. Cursors reset on a DB rebuild, forcing one full re-scan.
competitive_note: Nightfall publishes ~50 MB / 1% CPU as the endpoint footprint bar (market.md row 69); a collector that re-reads half a gigabyte every five seconds and re-runs every rule over the full table cannot be defended in an MDM rollout review.
v1_ref: Collector self-health: collector_runs, vole doctor, coverage matrix, freshness attestation (Tier 1), which measures the pass but never bounds it
field_verified: The schema facts hold; both load-bearing measurements do not. Verified true: part has exactly two indexes, `CREATE INDEX part_session_idx ON part (session_id)` and `CREATE INDEX part_message_id_id_idx ON part (message_id,id)` — no time_updated index, and Vole opens the store read-only so it cannot add one; rowid range 3,233→49,839 and time_updated range 1780757623923→1788639485696 are the exact endpoints claimed. Verified FALSE: rowid order does NOT match time order — 3,175 of 46,584 adjacent rowid pairs go backwards in time_updated (6.8%), because OpenCode mutates part rows in place (the running→completed transition this very shard depends on). Those edits land BELOW a rowid high-water cursor and are never returned, so the stated mitigation, 're-check time_updated on the returned page', cannot see them: a pure rowid cursor would silently miss the outcome of every tool call. Also verified FALSE: the '15.6 s per poll' figure. Timed on a copy of the live DB today — collectors 485 ms total (codex 269 ms over 104.7 MB / 66 rollouts, opencode 148 ms over the 507 MB store, devin 30 ms, grok 20 ms, claude 17 ms), insertEvents 82 ms for 12,957 rows of which 0 changed in steady state, full-table read 127 ms for 29,675 rows, detectBySource over all five rules 206 ms. Whole poll ≈ 0.65-0.9 s, about 20x below the claim.
constraint: Constraint 3 is the one the feature does not address. Anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key and the first verdict is frozen forever (db.ts:137). Bounding a rule to a trailing window changes its baseline, so the same window can yield a different severity depending on whether a bounded or unbounded pass saw it first — and whichever ran first wins permanently. Storing the window length on the incident aids explainability but does not fix the freeze; this needs the explicit upsert-and-re-notify path constraint 3 calls for, or bounded windows must be introduced together with a one-time re-detect. Constraint 8 (read-only third-party opens) is correctly honoured and is precisely why the missing index cannot be added. Corrected cursor design: keep rowid as the high-water mark for new inserts, and pair it with a `WHERE time_updated > last_seen` sweep to catch in-place edits — unindexed, but a full json_extract pass over all 46,584 parts measures 0.68 s here, so the sweep is affordable.

name: Open the rule and tool enums the app renders
description: types.ts:60 declares AnomalyRule as a closed five-value union, Theme.swift:152 maps exactly those five rule ids to labels, and Theme.swift:142 Labels.order is a hard-coded seven-tool allowlist iterated by both DashboardView.swift:44 toolTotals and :532 breakdownByTool. Every new rule therefore renders as a raw snake_case id, and every new tool disappears from the stacked bars and the Breakdown pane while still inflating yMax, the hover total and the KPI token count — a silently wrong number rather than a visibly missing one. Derive the tool list from SELECT DISTINCT tool with Labels.order demoted to a sort preference and a generic icon fallback, humanise unknown rule ids, and add a small rules catalogue row (id, label, one-line explanation, tags) written by the collector that both the app and the MCP surface read, so a new rule ships its own label.
desktop_surface: Dashboard > Breakdown and the stacked timeline include every tool present in the data (a Kiro or Copilot row appears the day its collector lands); Incidents shows 'Destructive command' rather than destructive_command, with the rule's one-line explanation on hover.
data_source: packages/core/src/types.ts:60-66 AnomalyRule; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/Theme.swift:142 Labels.order and :152 rule labels; DashboardView.swift:44,532.
honest_limit: A humanised fallback label is a guess at wording, never at meaning: until a rule is in the catalogue its incident shows the raw id beside its real figures, which is the honest degradation. A tool with no logo asset falls back to an SF Symbol in its series colour, so brand parity lags the data by a release.
competitive_note: Not competitive in itself — it is the single cheapest unblock in the roadmap, since every v1 tier past Tier 1 adds rules or collectors and each one silently corrupts the KPI totals of every feature shipped before this fix.
v1_ref: Plugin SDK for custom collectors and rules
field_verified: Confirmed with line drift. types.ts:61-66 `export type AnomalyRule = 'burn_rate_spike' | 'loop_suspected' | 'error_storm' | 'rate_limit_pressure' | 'context_pressure'`. Theme.swift:161 `static let order = ["claude_code","codex","cursor","antigravity","opencode","grok","devin"]` (feature says :142) and :172-176 the 5-entry rule map (feature says :152). Both consumers confirmed: DashboardView.swift:44 `Labels.order.map` in toolTotals, :532 `Labels.order.compactMap` in breakdownByTool. I traced the silently-wrong-number claim and it holds: `yMax` (:39) reads `series.map(\.total).max()` and `TimePoint.total` (DB.swift:49) is `tokensByTool.values.reduce(0,+)` over ALL tools, while `barMarks` (:64-75) iterates the Labels.order-filtered `toolTotals` — so an unlisted tool raises the axis ceiling and the hover total while drawing no bar. Correction: `Pal.series` (:41) and `Pal.symbol` (:55) already have `default:` fallbacks, so the generic-icon half is half-built already.
constraint: Constraint 6: a bare `SELECT DISTINCT tool` picks up seed-only tools and must carry `AND source='live'`, matching every other production query's seedClause — the feature does not say this. Constraint 4 is untouched (this is about rule and tool ids, not confidence). The rules-catalogue table is a new table and inherits constraint 6's source-column and purge requirement.

name: Honest coverage: per-collector heartbeat, four source states and a coverage strip
description: collector_state.last_scanned_at is the app's only liveness signal (DB.swift:244 feeding Store.swift:132-140) and setState has exactly one caller, claude-code.ts:111 — all 621 state rows on this machine are claude_code — so a Codex-, OpenCode- or Grok-only Mac shows 'Setting up, a few seconds' forever while rows accumulate behind it, and a collector that goes quiet is invisible. The one-line fix comes before v1's collector_runs ledger (roughly 17,000 rows/day at a 5s cadence, needing its own retention): after r.commit?.() in runOnce write a per-tool heartbeat row plus that collector's notes. Resolve each source every pass into one of four states — not_installed, installed_unreadable (with errno and path, the Full Disk Access case), installed_read_empty, read_with_rows — and enforce the rule in the read model that an unreadable source reports unknown, never zero, with any total over a range containing one carrying a 'partial' flag through to the UI and the export.
desktop_surface: A seven-chip strip pinned under the Overview toolbar and above the MenuPanel hero: green fresh, amber stale with its last-seen time, grey no artifacts found, red path exists but unreadable; each chip's popover names the resolved path, last successful read, rows produced and, when red, the exact permission with a button to open Privacy & Security. SetupCard, StaleBanner and Settings > Sources are driven by the same state instead of one global timestamp.
data_source: packages/core/src/cli/collect.ts:36-60 CollectorResult.notes/filesScanned (printed under --verbose, never persisted); collectors/claude-code.ts:111 setState; db.ts setState; paths.ts accessors probed with fs.stat/open for existence and readability; DB.swift:244, Store.swift:132-140.
honest_limit: A heartbeat proves the collector ran, not that the tool's store was readable or complete, so the note must be stored beside it; backlog_bytes exists only for Claude Code because every other collector re-reads in full, making backlog absent rather than zero. 'Not installed' means no artifact was found at any known path — a custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or a relocated store is indistinguishable from absence until env overrides are surfaced — and macOS TCC denials return an errno without naming the missing grant, so remediation text is a best guess labelled as such. A source that is readable but whose format changed reads as 'empty', which is why schema-drift detection must fire separately.
competitive_note: The macOS EDR failure mode buyers already know is a sensor that silently stops after a point release; reporting reduced functionality as unknown rather than zero is the endpoint pattern market.md tells Vole to copy from the MDM/Full Disk Access playbook. It is also the answer to Zscaler's finding that organisations lack a basic AI inventory: a grey chip is an inventory gap you can see, a zero is one you cannot — and an incumbent's SE will go looking for exactly this in a bake-off.
v1_ref: Collector self-health: collector_runs, vole doctor, coverage matrix, freshness attestation
field_verified: Confirmed, and worse than stated. `SELECT tool, COUNT(*) FROM collector_state GROUP BY 1` returns a single row: `claude_code|633`. `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tool) FROM collector_state` = 1, against 5 tools producing usage rows. DB.swift:242-243 carries a doc comment that is a lie in the code's own words: 'it stamps every source it touches, every pass'. Store.swift:132-140 derives all three states from `MAX(last_scanned_at)`. collect.ts:36-51: `r.notes` and `r.filesScanned` are printed only inside `if (verbose)` and never persisted; `r.commit?.()` at :39 sits immediately after `insertEvents`. paths.ts has exactly 11 accessors. So on a Codex-only or OpenCode-only Mac, `collectorLastSeen()` is nil forever and MenuPanel.swift:154 shows SetupCard's 'Setting up. This takes just a few seconds' permanently while rows accumulate.
constraint: Constraint 9 is satisfied by the specified ordering (heartbeat after `r.commit?.()`, touching no offsets). Constraint 1 has an unnamed wrinkle: collector_state's PRIMARY KEY is `source_path` and `last_offset` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so a per-tool heartbeat needs a synthetic key (e.g. `heartbeat:<tool>`) carrying a meaningless zero offset in a table whose declared semantics are byte offsets. Either accept that with a comment or add a `collector_health` table — do not silently overload the offset table. Principle 1 is the feature's spine: an unreadable source must report unknown, never zero.

name: Scanner cadence and scan_state, so discovery never joins the 5-second loop
description: cli/collect.ts runs every 5 s and already re-runs all five detection rules over the entire usage_events table each pass; the discovery scanners this product needs (codesign per binary, a Chrome History copy-and-query, a full /Applications walk, launchd plist enumeration) are orders of magnitude more expensive and must not ride that loop. Add a collector_state-shaped scan_state(scanner TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_run_at, last_input_digest, last_duration_ms) table — like collector_state it carries no source column because it holds no events and is never partitioned or purged with seed data. Each scanner declares a cadence (apps and CLIs hourly, launchd and configs every 15 minutes, browser history every 6 hours, codesign only when a binary's size/mtime changed) and a cheap input digest (a directory mtime, a plist count) so a due scan exits in microseconds when nothing changed, and `vole collect --verbose` prints per-scanner duration so a slow scanner is attributable rather than blamed on the collector.
desktop_surface: Settings gains a per-scanner row (last run, duration, next due); the Coverage screen shows a stale marker on any surface whose scanner has not completed within two cadences, reusing the noData/stale/live vocabulary Store.swift collectorStatus already uses.
data_source: New scan_state table in ~/.vole/vole.db; directory mtimes and (size, mtime) pairs as input digests; timings measured in packages/core/src/cli/collect.ts around each scanner call
honest_limit: Cadence means detection is delayed by up to one cadence: a local model runtime started and stopped between two scans is never seen, so port and process evidence carries a timestamp, never a claim of continuity. An mtime digest misses in-place edits that preserve mtime (touch -r, some installers), so the digest is an optimisation and never the sole record of change. This does not fix the existing O(W squared log W) detection pass in the same loop (detect/util.ts medianExcluding over the whole table every 5 s) — that is a separate defect and cadence must not be sold as its cure. The ~1% CPU / ~50 MB footprint bar from market.md is a target to measure and publish on this machine, not a claim to assert.
competitive_note: Nightfall publishes a ~50 MB / ~1% CPU endpoint footprint and Fleet publishes osquery scheduling; a discovery feature with no cadence story loses the MDM deployment conversation in the first pilot. Nothing in v1's 143 features addresses scan scheduling, which is why every v1 inventory feature would land in the 5-second poll by default.
field_verified: All four claims CONFIRMED in-repo. collect.ts:13 `const intervalMs = intervalArg ? Number(intervalArg.split('=')[1]) * 1000 : 5000;`. schema.ts:66 `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector_state (source_path TEXT PRIMARY KEY, tool TEXT NOT NULL, last_offset INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_mtime INTEGER, last_scanned_at INTEGER)` — no source column, exactly as the analogy claims. detect/util.ts:56 `export function medianExcluding(values: number[], excludeIndex: number)`, called per-index at burn-rate.ts:43 and loop.ts:34, so the O(W squared log W) per-pass claim is structurally confirmed. Store.swift:127-139 `case noData / case stale(since: Date) / case live` — the noData/stale/live vocabulary exists verbatim and can be reused.
constraint: Constraint 6 as written is unqualified ('New tables must carry a source column and the same partition/purge'); scan_state deliberately omits it. The analogy to collector_state holds — that table has no source column and is never purged with seed data — but the constraint text does not carry the exception, so this must be reconciled by amending the constraint to cover event-bearing tables only, not by quietly ignoring it. Constraint 13 (read-model parity) applies to the per-scanner Settings rows: a DB.swift port is needed for a table the collector alone writes.

name: schema_migrations: a numbered, ledgered, single-writer migration path
description: db.ts migrate() is three hand-written PRAGMA table_info probes over two tables, and PRAGMA user_version on the live store reads 0 — the store cannot say which schema it is. Replace it with a forward-only numbered list of steps {version, name, kind:'ddl'|'backfill', sql} applied inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a busy_timeout set (the Node writer sets none today, only journal_mode and synchronous), then PRAGMA user_version = N interpolated from the step's own literal because that pragma cannot be parameterised. Each applied step appends to a new schema_migrations(version, name, kind, applied_at, duration_ms, rows_changed, vole_version, node_version, sqlite_version, schema_sha256) where duration_ms is wall clock, rows_changed is the statement's own .changes, and schema_sha256 is SHA-256 over sqlite_schema.sql ordered by name (2,175 bytes on this store). `vole migrate --check` copies the live file with VACUUM INTO (measured 28 ms, 16.5 MB here), runs the pending steps against the copy and prints the real duration and byte delta, so an MDM admin knows the upgrade cost before 5,000 laptops take it. Note sqlite.ts pragma() calls db.exec and discards results, so every lifecycle read here must go through prepare().get(), not pragma().
desktop_surface: Settings → Store: schema version, schema hash, and the last five ledger rows (version, name, applied_at, duration, rows changed); a red row when a step failed and the store is mid-upgrade.
data_source: PRAGMA user_version (0 on ~/.vole/vole.db today), sqlite_schema.sql, pragma_table_list, packages/core/src/db.ts migrate(), packages/core/src/schema.ts
honest_limit: The ledger can only describe steps applied after it exists. Every store created before it gets one synthetic row (version 0, name 'pre-ledger', applied_at NULL) and NULL must render as 'unknown', never as a date. ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN measured at 0 ms because SQLite does not rewrite rows, so a fast DDL step says nothing about the backfill that follows it.
competitive_note: Every endpoint competitor in the matrix (Nightfall, Harmonic, SentinelOne/Prompt, MintMCP) keeps its schema in a SaaS backend and migrates it invisibly; the only matrix entry shipping a versioned store to the laptop is Fleet/osquery, and Vole is currently behind it with no version stamp at all.
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: The upgrade boundary on the Coverage strip: 'not recorded before v0.2', never zero
description: The failure this prevents is specific and silent: add permission_mode in v0.2 and every chart of it shows a hard drop to zero on the migration day, because rows older than the column are NULL and NULL renders as absence. Join the migrations ledger to the data — for each column a migration introduced, store first_populated_ts (min ts of a row where it is non-NULL) and unbackfillable_rows from the backfill step — and draw a vertical boundary at that timestamp carrying the version label. Left of the boundary is shaded and labelled 'not recorded before v0.2 (schema 4, applied 2026-09-14)'; rows a backfill filled are labelled 'backfilled from source'; rows the evidence horizon ate are 'source deleted before upgrade — N rows'.
desktop_surface: Coverage strip gains one boundary marker per column in view, and the timeline chart shades the pre-column region instead of plotting zeros; hovering the marker shows the schema_migrations row that created it.
data_source: schema_migrations (version, name, applied_at), per-column MIN(ts) WHERE col IS NOT NULL over usage_events, backfill step's rows_unbackfillable
honest_limit: The boundary is per column, so a screen mixing columns of different vintages has more than one and the strip must show the oldest boundary affecting the figure on screen. It knows only that the column changed — it cannot know that the user's mental model of the metric changed with it.
competitive_note: Every vendor console silently zero-fills or backfills across its own schema changes and answers the question in support tickets; the buyer need for an 'honest reduced-functionality state' plus principle 1 make the boundary a shipped artifact here instead.
v1_ref: Honest coverage: per-collector heartbeat, four source states and a coverage strip
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Readability matrix: no screen may render a bare zero
description: A zero on the Shadow AI screen must mean "we looked and found nothing", never "we were not allowed to look" — absence of evidence rendered as evidence of absence is principle 1 broken in the direction that gets someone fired. Every read model that can return 0 joins `scan_access` on its root and returns a `readable` state beside the count, written twice per the read-model parity rule (queries.ts and the DB.swift port, EXTENDING.md). The view layer then renders three different things from the same 0: `ok` → "0"; `eperm` → "not readable" in the same null style `util/format.ts` already uses for the em dash; `enoent` → "not installed". Adds `v_scan_access` plus a readability grid — one row per root, four-state pill, entries seen, probe age.
desktop_surface: A new Readability table inside the Coverage strip, and the same four-state pill on every per-surface card of the Shadow AI screen and every source row of the People view. The menu-bar SetupCard gains a line — "3 of 17 read roots unreadable" — deep-linking via vole:// to Settings > Permissions. No new menu-bar glyph state; the six honest states already carry the load.
data_source: scan_access joined to each read model's root; rendered through the existing null-formatting path.
honest_limit: The matrix is per root, not per file — one unreadable file inside a readable directory stays invisible, and a directory that lists but whose children fail to open reads as `ok`. A pill can be up to one scanner interval stale, which is why the probe age is shown next to it rather than hidden.
competitive_note: Kolide/1Password's Honest Security tenet — publish the per-user manifest of what was read — is the closest analogue in the matrix, but it lists intended reads, not attempted-and-denied ones. Every cloud-console competitor (Cyberhaven, Harmonic, Nightfall) renders a dashboard zero with no way for the buyer to tell coverage from silence.
v1_ref: Coverage and denominators: what Vole did not read
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: collector_runs: a measured footprint budget that names its metric
description: Buyer need #12 asks for "~50MB/1% CPU", and measured on this machine the answer depends entirely on which counter you publish: one `--once` pass over the real sources reports `peak memory footprint 50,976,936` and `maximum resident set size 1,071,464,448` from `/usr/bin/time -l` — a 21x gap — while `ps` shows the two live bundled `vole-collector` processes at ~570 MB RSS each. Add `collector_runs(started_at, duration_ms, rss_peak_bytes, cpu_user_ms, cpu_sys_ms, files_scanned, events_parsed, exit_status, tier_shed TEXT, source)`, written at the end of each pass from `process.memoryUsage.rss()` and `process.cpuUsage()` — both node builtins, so the SEA stays zero-dependency. Publish the budget in both metrics with the definition attached, since a 50 MB claim measured as phys_footprint and a 570 MB observation measured as RSS describe the same process. When the trailing median of `duration_ms` or `rss_peak_bytes` crosses the declared budget, shed second-tier discovery scanners in a fixed, recorded order and stamp `tier_shed` — never scan unbounded, and never silently drop a first-tier source.
desktop_surface: Settings > Footprint: sparklines of duration_ms and rss over 24h against a drawn budget line, plus the current tier state ("all scanners" / "discovery shed since 14:02"). Beside them the app shows a live `ri_phys_footprint` for the collector pid via `proc_pid_rusage` (public libproc, same-uid, no entitlement) so the Activity-Monitor-comparable number is visible on screen.
data_source: process.memoryUsage.rss() and process.cpuUsage() inside collect.ts; proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_CURRENT).ri_phys_footprint read live by the Swift app.
honest_limit: Node cannot read its own phys_footprint, so the *stored* series is RSS and is roughly 20x pessimistic against Activity Monitor's Memory column; the live phys_footprint is displayed but never persisted, because DB.swift is a read-only consumer by contract. CPU is measured per pass and cannot be attributed to an individual scanner without per-scanner sampling, so shedding order is declared policy, not inferred blame.
competitive_note: Nightfall's ~50MB/1% CPU is a vendor claim in a blog post with no stated counter (market.md §7, flagged [vendor claim]). Vole would be the only one of the 62 where the buyer reads the number off their own machine, in both counters, with the definition attached — which is the difference between passing a footprint question and answering it.
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: store_version_gate: an older binary opens a newer store read-only and says so
description: An old collector on a new store today is silently wrong rather than broken: openDb() runs db.exec(SCHEMA) (all IF NOT EXISTS, no-ops), migrate() finds nothing to add, and INSERT_EVENT writes its old column list, so every column the newer schema added lands NULL — indistinguishable downstream from 'the source did not carry this field', which breaks principle 1 by upgrade rather than by parser. Verdicts are worse: anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key, so an old binary's rule semantics win permanently over the new one's. This is the normal state on a dev machine, not a hypothetical — the .app spawns its bundled SEA collector at Contents/MacOS/vole-collector while a Homebrew or npm `vole` on PATH opens the same file, and it is also what an MDM rollback produces. The gate reads PRAGMA user_version before anything else; if it exceeds the binary's own highest known step it opens readOnly and sets a store_incompatible state every surface must read before running a query, and a new written_by_schema_version column stamps which binary shaped each row.
desktop_surface: A blocking banner on every screen: 'This store was written by Vole 0.3 (schema 7); this app knows schema 5. Showing nothing rather than a wrong number', with both versions and an Update button — replacing today's failure mode where DB.swift.run() returns on a failed prepare and the dashboard shows 0 calls / 0 tokens / $0.00.
data_source: PRAGMA user_version; packages/core/src/db.ts openDb()/INSERT_EVENT/INSERT_ANOMALY; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/DB.swift tryOpen() and run()
honest_limit: A downgrade cannot un-write rows, only refuse to read them: rows an older binary wrote before written_by_schema_version existed carry NULL there and are 'unknown writer' forever. The gate protects the store from Vole only — it cannot stop an operator running `rm ~/.vole/vole.db*`, which docs/EXTENDING.md L476-489 still recommends as the way to change the schema.
competitive_note: SaaS agents pin their version through MDM and roll back centrally; Vole's own dual-binary layout (bundled SEA in the .app plus a CLI on PATH over one file) creates the mismatch on a single laptop — a self-inflicted risk none of the 62 matrix vendors carries.
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Backfill as a declared step: the widening the tokens-only-grow upsert can never perform
