description: The upsert rewrites a stored row only when excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens, and its SET list never touches model, session_id, project, git_branch, agent_id, raw_ref, confidence or source — so a column added today stays NULL on every existing row forever unless something explicitly UPDATEs it. The only precedent is repriceUnpriced(), which is unbounded, full-table and runs inside the 5-second poll. Add kind:'backfill' to the F1 ledger: a select naming the still-NULL rows, rows_per_pass, and a resumable cursor column (last ts completed), applied oldest-first so the rows nearest the evidence horizon fill before their source disappears; each pass appends rows_backfilled and rows_unbackfillable to its ledger row. Bounding is not optional: 5,000 rows backfilled in 8 ms here, but the poll loop already spends 53 ms re-reading SELECT * FROM usage_events ORDER BY ts (29,978 rows) every 5 seconds, and an unbounded UPDATE over a year of tool_calls would hold the write lock past the app's 2-second busy_timeout, at which point DB.swift.run() logs to stderr, returns, and the dashboard renders Summary.empty as zeros.
desktop_surface: Settings → Store → Backfill: per pending column, rows filled / rows remaining / rows unbackfillable, with the pass cursor date and 'paused — collector busy' when a pass yields.
data_source: packages/core/src/db.ts INSERT_EVENT upsert WHERE clause and repriceUnpriced(); usage_events.raw_ref; ~/.claude/.last-cleanup (dated 2026-09-07 on this machine); cleanupPeriodDays
honest_limit: The backfill's ceiling is the evidence horizon and must be printed with it: a row whose raw_ref file the tool's own cleanup has already deleted can never be filled from anything, so it is counted as unbackfillable and rendered 'not recorded', never 0. repriceUnpriced must be converted into a step of this kind or it remains the one unbounded backfill in the codebase.
competitive_note: No competitor hits this because none keeps a local store whose upsert rule blocks enrichment; the gateways (LiteLLM, Kong, Bifrost) re-shape at the proxy and simply never have the rows the proxy did not see.
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Read-model parity check in CI
description: VoleApp.swift already has a headless --dump that prints a summary, incident count, bucket count and breakdown count from DB.swift. Turn it into `--dump --json` emitting every shared view's rows, add `vole query --json <view>` on the TypeScript side, and have the macOS CI job run both against one fixture database and diff them. This is the only mechanism that keeps a hand-written Swift port honest as tables multiply, and it would have caught the three parity bugs the code map already found: no zero-fill in DB.swift's timeseries, a 100-row incident cap in DB.swift against 500 in queries.ts, and breakdown by model only.
desktop_surface: No user-visible surface by design; failures appear in CI, and at runtime the existing schema-version banner is what a user sees when the app and collector disagree.
data_source: apps/mac/Sources/Vole/VoleApp.swift --dump branch; packages/core/src/queries.ts read models; the shared v_* views; .github/workflows/ci.yml macOS job, which today runs swift build only.
honest_limit: It compares numbers for the manifest views on a fixture database: it cannot catch a rendering bug, a chart binning bug (the UTC-vs-local issue lives in the view layer, not the query), or drift in the bespoke screens that stay hand-ported. It only runs on macOS runners, so a Linux-only CI pass proves nothing about the app. And a fixture DB proves parity for the shapes the fixture contains — a NULL pattern nobody thought to seed still diverges silently.
competitive_note: Vole's own Settings pane already claims 'Verification: Every stored row reconciled' while pnpm verify never reconciles Grok. A product whose entire pitch is 'never invent a number' has to be able to prove its two readers agree on the numbers, and no competitor makes a claim strong enough to have to keep.
field_verified: Mostly confirmed, one source invented. VoleApp.swift:39-48 is real: `if CommandLine.arguments.contains("--dump")` prints db ok/path, 24h calls/tokens/cost/sessions, per-tool lines, then `incidents(7d)=… buckets(24h)=… breakdown=…`. .github/workflows/ci.yml's app job is exactly two steps — checkout and `swift build --package-path apps/mac` — so nothing today runs the app's queries. The three parity bugs are real: queries.ts:155-161 zero-fills the timeseries and DB.swift's port does not; DB.swift:223 is `func anomalies(_ r: DateRange, limit: Int = 100)` against queries.ts:230's `limit = 500`; DB.swift:250 breakdown() hard-codes `GROUP BY tool, model, confidence` with no by-parameter. FALSE: 'the shared v_* views' — there are no views. sqlite_master over the live DB returns three tables and zero views, and schema.ts contains no CREATE VIEW.
constraint: Constraint 13 is the reason it exists — every query written twice or the app cannot show it — so this is enforcement, not conflict. The honest limit to add: constraint 12 says there is no user_version stamp shared by the two readers, so a fixture DB proves parity of results but not of schema expectations, and DB.swift assumes the newest columns are present.

name: ai_surfaces registry (the shadow-AI spine)
description: One table `ai_surfaces(surface_key UNIQUE, kind, vendor, name, identifier, version, path, evidence_kind, state, first_seen, last_seen, scanner, confidence, source)` that every scanner in this category writes through, mirroring `db.ts:insertEvents`: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(surface_key) DO UPDATE SET last_seen=max(...), version=coalesce(excluded.version, version)`. `kind` is app|cli|extension|runtime|gateway|browser_host|config_dir|mcp_client|residue|store; `surface_key` is `<scanner>:<identifier>` and must never embed an mtime — that is the `antigravity.ts:63` anti-precedent, not a template. `evidence_kind` (file_present|identifier_read|process_listening|log_line|history_row) records how we know; `state` is exactly one of {configured_and_observed, configured_never_observed, artifact_present_no_collector, catalog_only_absent} and is the anti-overclaim device — 'artifact_present_no_collector' is a coverage confession printed in the product, not a hidden TODO. `confidence` keeps the two-value enum ('exact' = identifier read verbatim from a vendor-written file, 'activity_only' = presence only), the table carries `source` and is partitioned/purged with the seed rows like every other table.
desktop_surface: New Dashboard sidebar section 'AI Surfaces'. Header line: 'N surfaces found · M produce exact rows · K activity-only · J present but unparsed', each number clicking through to the filtered grid. Grid rows: icon, name, kind chip, vendor, version, first seen, last seen, scanner, state, sorted first_seen desc so the newest thing on the machine is on top. Row click opens a drill-down with the literal evidence path and evidence_kind. Also the first section of `vole doctor` and of the `vole assess` report.
data_source: Written by every scanner in this category; table lives in ~/.vole/vole.db beside usage_events. Needs `getAiSurfaces` in queries.ts and a matching DB.swift read port (read-model parity constraint); schema added via migrate()'s add-nullable-column-only path.
honest_limit: A surface row proves an artifact exists on disk, a socket was listening at a moment, or a log line was written — never that a human used the tool, and never a token or a dollar. first_seen is the first Vole scan that saw it, not the install date, and the column must be labelled 'first seen by Vole'. A state of configured_never_observed collapses four different truths ('never used', 'used before Vole was installed', 'writes nothing parseable', 'transcripts already deleted by the tool's own cleanup') and the UI must not render it as 'unused'. Surfaces under other OS user accounts are invisible without Full Disk Access and often root.
competitive_note: Fleet/osquery ships an 'AI coding assistants' inventory pack at $7/host with undocumented depth and no per-surface first-seen; CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian (2026-09-01) advertises shadow-agent inventory on macOS but requires the Falcon sensor. Snyk agent-scan discovers agent config files one-shot and free but never joins config to observed usage — that join is only possible because the same process reads both the config and the transcripts. Zscaler's own AI Access material concedes 47% of enterprises have no agent inventory at all.
field_verified: Table absent, upsert pattern real. `sqlite3 ~/.vole/vole.db .tables` -> `anomalies  collector_state  usage_events` (three tables only). db.ts:87-101 is the described monotone upsert; db.ts:41-53 migrate() probes ONLY `['usage_events','anomalies']`; purgeSeed (db.ts:228-232) is hard-coded: `DELETE FROM usage_events WHERE source='seed'` / `DELETE FROM anomalies WHERE source='seed'`. DB.swift exposes exactly 5 readers (summary/timeseries/anomalies/collectorLastSeen/breakdown). FALSIFIED SURFACE CLAIM: `vole doctor` and `vole assess` do not exist — packages/core/src/cli/ = collect, digest, mcp, pr, seed, statusline, top, verify, and package.json has no `bin` field at all.
constraint: Constraint 6 (seed/live partition): 'purged with the seed rows like every other table' is not free — purgeSeed names two tables literally and must be extended. Constraint 12 (add-nullable-column-only migrate, no user_version, DB.swift assumes newest columns): a new table via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in SCHEMA is fine, but an older shipped Vole.app SELECTing a table it does not know must be guarded by a table-exists probe in DB.swift or it errors. Constraint 13: +1 queries.ts read model AND +1 DB.swift port. DUPLICATE RISK, the real conflict: roadmap-v1 L95 already defines `posture_inventory(kind, name, version, path, first/last_seen)` and L124 `posture_snapshots` keyed on (kind, identity, sha256) with first/last_seen. Reconciliation: ai_surfaces must BE that table (extended with evidence_kind + the 4-value state enum, which are genuinely new), not a third parallel registry. Rename the v1 entries rather than shipping both.

name: Unsanctioned-agent rule against an admin allowlist
description: A pure rule that fires warn when an ai_surfaces row's surface_key is absent from allowed_surfaces (a list of globs) in the admin-owned policy file — /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json merged over ~/.vole/policy.json, the same override precedence pricing.json already uses. anomaly_key is 'unsanctioned:' + surface_key + ':' + policy_sha256, so re-evaluating after a policy change produces a new, explainable incident instead of being swallowed by INSERT OR IGNORE. observed = 1, threshold = 0, baseline NULL, and the detail quotes both the evidence path and the literal policy clause that failed. The AI Surfaces grid status chip reads the same policy, so the two views cannot disagree.
desktop_surface: Incident feed row 'Unsanctioned agent: com.electron.ollama — not in allowed_surfaces (policy 3f9a…)'; a sanctioned/unsanctioned chip on every row of the AI Surfaces grid, replaced by a 'no policy loaded' strip when the file is absent.
data_source: ai_surfaces rows; allowed_surfaces in /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json and ~/.vole/policy.json.
honest_limit: With no policy file present the rule is inert and must stay inert — 'unsanctioned' is a company decision, not a technical fact, and shipping a default allowlist would make Vole's opinion look like evidence. It cannot prove the tool was used with company data, only that its artifacts exist on this Mac.
competitive_note: Extends v1's policy file with the surface-allowlist clause it never defines (v1 lists allowed models/providers/hosts/MCP pins but no agent surfaces). CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian offers agent allow/deny but only inside a Falcon deployment.
v1_ref: Policy-as-code file with local enforcement, drift report and vole_policy check
field_verified: NEITHER policy file exists: `ls -la '/Library/Application Support/Vole'` -> 'No such file or directory'; `ls -la ~/.vole/` -> only vole.db, vole.db-shm, vole.db-wal. THE PRECEDENT CLAIM IS INVERTED: pricing.ts loadPricing() merges `paths.pricingOverride()` (= `process.env.VOLE_PRICING ?? join(home(),'.vole','pricing.json')`) ON TOP of the shipped builtin -- the USER wins over the shipped file. There is no /Library layer anywhere in the codebase. An admin-over-user precedence is a new inversion, not 'the same override precedence pricing.json already uses'. Also `const P = loadPricing();` runs ONCE at module import, so a policy loader copied from it never reloads and policy_sha256 would be frozen for the life of the 5s daemon.
constraint: C14 (SEA: no runtime file reads except pricing override and sources) -- a second runtime read path. pricing override is the precedent so it is declarable, but it must be declared, not assumed. C3 is respected and well designed: policy_sha256 in the key is deterministic and carries no now(), so a policy edit produces a new explainable incident rather than being swallowed.

name: Shadow AI screen
description: One sidebar destination that makes the whole shadow-AI lens legible in ten seconds: a headline count ('14 AI surfaces on this Mac — 9 sanctioned, 3 unsanctioned, 2 unknown'), the AI Surfaces grid with kind and status chips, a 'New this week' strip driven by first_seen, the local-runtime and gateway cards (the two that mean an admin should act today), the browser Web AI panel and the coverage footer pinned beneath so an empty result can never be read as 'clean'. It needs getAiSurfaces(range, includeSeed) in queries.ts and its DB.swift twin, since under the read-model parity constraint an unported query cannot be shown at all.
desktop_surface: A 'Shadow AI' section in the Monitor group of the sidebar; row click opens a drill-down sheet with evidence_kind, the literal path, first and last seen, and any incidents keyed to that surface; the count also feeds the menu panel's security strip.
data_source: ai_surfaces rows via a new queries.ts getAiSurfaces plus a DB.swift port; anomalies rows for new_ai_surface / unsanctioned_agent / ai_gateway_persistent / local_model_server_exposed / ai_binary_unsigned.
honest_limit: The status chips are only as good as the policy file behind them: with no policy every surface is 'Unknown' and the headline must say so rather than defaulting to sanctioned or unsanctioned. Counts are per-machine and the screen must not imply a fleet. Two shipped bugs block it: Bundle.module fatalErrors in every packaged .app (VoleApp.swift:51) so the icons the grid needs crash the bundle, and the UTC/local bucket offset (DashboardView.swift:69) misaligns any first-seen chart.
competitive_note: Every competitor with shadow-agent inventory (CrowdStrike, Cyberhaven, Harmonic, Forcepoint) renders it in a cloud console the employee never sees. A local screen the employee can open themselves is what makes the works-council and CNIL story defensible, and it is the one UI no SaaS competitor can copy without shipping an endpoint app.
v1_ref: Shadow agent surface: Claude Desktop scratch sessions and non-engineering accounts
field_verified: Backing data absent, and one of the two claimed blockers is stale. `.tables` on ~/.vole/vole.db returns exactly `anomalies collector_state usage_events` — no ai_surfaces. No getAiSurfaces in queries.ts. The five named rules cannot exist: types.ts:61-66 is a closed five-value union. BLOCKER (a) IS ALREADY FIXED: the feature says 'Bundle.module fatalErrors in every packaged .app (VoleApp.swift:51)', but VoleApp.swift:51 calls `Res.image("AppIcon")`, and Res.bundle (Theme.swift:12-16) resolves `Bundle.main.resourceURL?.appendingPathComponent("Vole_Vole.bundle")` FIRST and only falls back to `.module`; bundle.sh:59 is `cp -R "$(dirname "$BIN")/Vole_Vole.bundle" "$APP/Contents/Resources/"` — exactly where Res looks. The code-map's bug #1 is out of date; icons do not crash a bundled app. BLOCKER (b) is real: DashboardView.swift:69 uses `unit:` and this machine is `MST -0700`.
constraint: Constraint 6: a new ai_surfaces table must carry a `source` column, be partitioned in detection and be covered by purgeSeed — the feature's `includeSeed` parameter shows awareness but the table spec must say it. Constraint 1: a surface row keyed on path+mtime would repeat antigravity.ts:63's mistake (a new row per observed mtime), which constraint 1 explicitly calls out as 'not a precedent' — first_seen/last_seen columns on a stable identity key instead. Constraint 13: two readers.

name: model_routes: resolving the local gateway's alias map, and the two rules it exposes
description: Read the config file the gateway job's own ProgramArguments names (--config <path> for LiteLLM; also ~/.config/litellm/*.yaml, Claude Code Router's config, ~/.continue/config.json, ~/.aider.conf.yml) and extract the routing map only: model_list[].model_name -> litellm_params.model, the api_base host and scheme, and the presence (never the value) of api_key. Adds model_routes(surface_id, alias, upstream_model, upstream_host, upstream_scheme, key_present, config_path, first_seen, source) plus a read-time view v_events_route that left-joins usage_events.model to model_routes.alias - the stored model column is never rewritten, both because the upsert refuses to touch it and because the row is a faithful record of what the agent logged. Two rules follow: sanctioned_name_unsanctioned_upstream (an alias carrying a vendor route name maps to a third-party api_base) and plaintext_model_transport (upstream_scheme='http', or the host is a bare IP literal). On this machine ~/.config/litellm/claude-gemini.yaml maps claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5 to openai/qwen3.8-27b-heretic at http://89.169.113.254:8081/v1 and claude-mythos-5 to a second bare IP over plaintext HTTP, which means the Anthropic model names already sitting in usage_events are, for those sessions, false.
desktop_surface: A 'Route' chip beside every model name in Breakdown, Sessions and Leak Ledger whenever v_events_route resolves an alias - 'claude-sonnet-5 -> qwen3.8-27b-heretic @ 89.169.113.254 (http)' - with a red transport badge on plaintext or bare-IP upstreams. The 'No-log AI' section gains a 'Where your prompts actually went' card listing alias, upstream, transport and config path.
data_source: ~/.config/litellm/*.yaml (model_list[].model_name, litellm_params.model, api_base, api_key presence), Claude Code Router config, ~/.continue/config.json, ~/.aider.conf.yml; the --config path taken from the launchd job's ProgramArguments
honest_limit: The map is what the config says, not what the proxy did: a running gateway may hold an older config in memory, route by wildcard, or fall back per request, and Vole never sees a request. It cannot confirm that a single prompt crossed that host, only that the local configuration would have sent it there. It resolves only aliases appearing verbatim in the model column, so a hex-hashed alias resolves only when the same string appears in the config, and rows for sessions predating the config's first_seen must render unresolved rather than assumed.
competitive_note: Portkey and Helicone see this traffic only because they are the gateway; a homegrown LiteLLM instance is monitored by nobody, and LiteLLM's own matrix row reads 'routed agents only, metadata-only default'. Every console vendor shows the alias the client sent and none can show the upstream it resolved to.
v1_ref: Rerouted-model detector straight from the model column, with CCR hex decode
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: languageModelStats: exact tokens per extension per model, counted by the editor itself
description: The brief's stated honest limit — 'installed is not proof it ran' — is dissolved by a file VS Code already writes. In the Settings Sync global-state blob, key languageModelStats.<model> carries value {"extensions":[{"extensionId":"GitHub.copilot-chat","requestCount":6,"tokenCount":66383,"participants":[]}]} and key languageModelAccess.<model> carries the list of extension ids GRANTED that model. Both verified present here for claude-3.5-sonnet. These are cumulative monotonic counters, which is exactly the shape db.ts's upsert wants: ide_model_usage keyed (root, extension_id, model) with total_tokens and request_count rewritten only when the counter STRICTLY grows, matching the existing WHERE clause rather than fighting it. The dated sync/globalState/<UTC>.json backups turn the cumulative counter into per-interval deltas with real timestamps. This converts an inventory row into a usage row with confidence='exact' and lifts the extension's ai_surfaces evidence-ladder label from 'installed' to 'observed, with figures'. languageModelAccess additionally answers a question no console can: which extension was granted access to which model, i.e. the grant that preceded the burn.
desktop_surface: Costs screen gains an 'IDE extensions' block listing (extension, model, requests, tokens) with an em dash in the cost column and the unpriced-rows count beside the total; the People view shows IDE-extension tokens as a separate, explicitly unpriced bar so it can never be silently added to a dollar figure.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/globalState/lastSyncglobalState.json and its dated siblings — storage['languageModelStats.<model>'].value and storage['languageModelAccess.<model>'].value; same keys readable live from ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb ItemTable when sync is off
honest_limit: tokenCount is a single undifferentiated total with no input/output/cache-read/cache-write split, so cost is NOT computable — input_tokens, output_tokens and cost_usd are NULL and computeCost is never called; every aggregate carries these rows in its unpriced count and the UI renders an em dash, never $0.00. The counter is keyed by model id as the editor names it and carries no session id, no cwd and no timestamp of its own, so it cannot be attributed to a repository or joined to a session tree — only to (extension, model) over the interval between two dated backups. It counts only models flowing through the editor's own vscode.lm broker; an extension that calls a provider's HTTPS API directly is not counted here at all. A counter that resets on profile change looks like a decrease and is recorded as counter_reset with the observation dropped, never as negative usage.
competitive_note: market.md: Copilot's own metrics ship AI credits, not tokens, are disabled by default and lag ~2 days; Cursor gives per-event tokens for Cursor only; JetBrains Console gives credits; Amazon Q gives acceptance rates with no tokens. This is an exact token count for a competitor's extension, read from the editor's disk, with zero network — precisely the 'out-of-path, exact, prompt-free' intersection market.md says nobody occupies.
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Per-workspace activation: which repositories each IDE agent actually opened in
description: This is the answer to 'installed, never observed running', and it comes with a repo list. Each editor keeps <App Support>/<Editor>/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/ with workspace.json naming the folder URI and state.vscdb whose ItemTable holds the keys extensions wrote in THAT workspace. Measured on this machine: 76 workspaces; GitHub.copilot-chat state in 74 of them; workbench.view.extension.claude-sidebar-secondary.state in 73; memento/interactive-session-view-copilot in 70; chat.terminalSessions in 19; and terminalChat.toolSessionMappings in 17, whose value is a list of [chat_session_uuid, integer] pairs — a per-session TOOL-CALL COUNT sitting in a per-repo database (one workspace here holds four sessions with 20, 21, 23 and 33). ide_extension_activation rows are keyed (root, workspace_hash, extension_key) with the folder URI resolved to a path, joined to the existing repository dimension so an IDE agent's reach lands in the same scope_drift and shadow_account_on_corporate_repo machinery as the CLI agents. The tool-count pairs feed the tool_ledger as source-native rows with status_source='ide_workspace_state' and duration_kind=NULL — counts without shapes, declared as such.
desktop_surface: Selecting an extension on the Shadow AI screen opens a reach panel: the list of repositories it activated in, each with the state.vscdb mtime as its 'not after' date, corporate/personal classification from policy, and a jump into the Blast Radius screen; workspaces whose folder no longer exists render with a 'folder missing' chip.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/{workspace.json,state.vscdb} — workspace.json.folder (e.g. file://<redacted-local-path>), ItemTable keys 'GitHub.copilot-chat', 'workbench.view.extension.claude-sidebar-secondary.state', 'memento/interactive-session-view-copilot', 'chat.terminalSessions', 'terminalChat.toolSessionMappings', 'chat.customModes.claude-code'; same layout under Cursor/User, Kiro/User and Antigravity IDE/User
honest_limit: Workspace state proves a view container was materialized in that workspace — the extension activated — not that a prompt was sent or a token spent; only the terminalChat.toolSessionMappings rows carry a count, and that count is of tool sessions the terminal chat mapped, not of every tool call. ItemTable has no per-key timestamp, so the only clock is the database file's mtime and every activation date is 'not after <mtime>' with confidence='activity_only' and every token field NULL. workspaceStorage is never garbage-collected, so a row can outlive both the extension and the folder; folder-missing rows are shown, never silently dropped. The DB must be opened read-only through node:sqlite while the editor may hold it open in WAL mode, so a busy read is recorded as scan_skipped for that workspace and counted in the coverage denominator rather than reported as zero activations.
competitive_note: code-map.md line 131 records ~/.cursor state.vscdb as a store the current collectors explicitly ignore. Cursor's own OTel export has 'no per-session tool attribution'; Copilot's audit log has no repository dimension for local chat; no vendor in the matrix maps an IDE agent to the specific repositories it was activated in, which is the join every insider-risk buyer asks for first.
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: agent_home_roots: editor roots and profiles as a resolved dimension, by marker not by name list
description: paths.ts resolves exactly one home and no editor roots at all. Add a resolver that readdirs ~/Library/Application Support and keeps every directory where User/globalStorage/storage.json exists — a marker test, so a fork nobody has heard of still resolves. On this machine that yields exactly 4 (Code, Cursor, Kiro, 'Antigravity IDE') and correctly rejects 2 lookalikes ('ZCode', 'Antigravity', no marker). Each root's storage.json also yields userDataProfiles[] ({location:'builtin/agents', name:'Agents', useDefaultFlags:{extensions,mcp,languageModels}}) and profileAssociations.workspaces (folder URI to profile id), so every extension store path is built as root x profile x extension-id and User/profiles/builtin/agents/globalStorage/<ext> is scanned, not only User/globalStorage/<ext>. Adds agent_home_roots(root_id, product_dir, profile_id, profile_name, store_path, marker_mtime, device_id_hash, readable, first_seen, last_seen, source); paths.ts gains editorRoots() and every existing single-home resolver is left untouched.
desktop_surface: A Roots band on Posture and a term on the Coverage strip: '4 editor roots, 5 profiles, 3 readable' with the unreadable ones named; root and profile become filter chips on Shadow AI and People so a session can be traced to the editor install it ran in.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/*/User/globalStorage/storage.json (marker; keys userDataProfiles, profileAssociations.workspaces, telemetry.devDeviceId/machineId/sqmId), ~/Library/Application Support/*/User/profiles/<id>/globalStorage/
honest_limit: A root launched with --user-data-dir elsewhere, a portable install, or a profile folder deleted while still listed in storage.json leaves no marker and is invisible. The figure is roots Vole could see and must always print with that denominator, never as 'all editors'. telemetry.devDeviceId is the editor's own id, useful only as a join key; it is not a machine identity and must not replace IOPlatformUUID.
competitive_note: The covered census is the CLI-home axis (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME); this is the editor axis and the profile axis, which nothing covers. Snyk Agent Scan and Cisco's free MCP scanners enumerate tools by name from a fixed list; Nightfall and Cyberhaven both list 'VS Code' as one product; JetBrains Console sees only JetBrains IDEs. None resolve per-profile globalStorage, where a second extension set legitimately hides.
v1_ref: Multi-root agent-home census (paths.ts resolves exactly one home)
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: os_intelligence: the AI wired into macOS, and the MDM key that was supposed to stop it
description: Nobody proposed OS-level AI, even though it is MDM-controlled and defaults-readable — and it is the only AI surface on a seat that never opens a terminal. Read the plists directly: com.apple.generativepartnerservicesettings -> AllLLMUISettings.<partner>.{enablementCount, unavailable} (verified here: com.apple.openai.chatgpt = {enablementCount 0, unavailable 1}) and gatMigrationComplete2; com.apple.CloudSubscriptionFeatures.optIn -> {opted_out_buddy, opted_change_os_version "26.4.0"}; com.apple.appleintelligencereporting -> uploadTaskBookmark; the on-device model asset at /System/Library/AssetsV2/com_apple_MobileAsset_UAF_FM_GenerativeModels (verified present, i.e. the foundation model is downloaded); and the managed side, /Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.apple.applicationaccess.plist -> _isAppleIntelligenceRestricted (verified 0, not restricted) with /Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/complete.plist naming the mcx_user_com.apple.applicationaccess_<uuid> payload that set it. Adds ai_surfaces rows kind='os_intelligence' — one per partner plus one for the on-device model — each carrying managed_by = the MCX source string or NULL. Rules: os_ai_partner_enabled (a third-party model wired into the OS with unavailable != 1) and os_ai_unrestricted (generative models available on a device in managed mode where no com.apple.applicationaccess payload sets the restriction — the control exists and is not applied, which is a posture gap the buyer can close the same afternoon).
desktop_surface: Posture screen gains an OS band showing per-partner enablement, the on-device model asset state, and the MDM payload that governs it (or 'no payload applied'); the Shadow AI screen shows the OS row for seats that run no agent at all, on the evidence ladder's bottom rung.
data_source: defaults domains as plists: com.apple.generativepartnerservicesettings (AllLLMUISettings.<partner>.{enablementCount,unavailable}, gatMigrationComplete2), com.apple.CloudSubscriptionFeatures.optIn, com.apple.appleintelligencereporting; /System/Library/AssetsV2/com_apple_MobileAsset_UAF_FM_GenerativeModels; /Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.apple.applicationaccess.plist and complete.plist
honest_limit: These keys record enablement and availability, never prompts: Apple writes no per-request record any user-space reader can see, so tokens, cost and content are structurally NULL forever and the row can never be misread as spend. unavailable: 1 may mean region, account tier or hardware and Vole does not guess which — it reports the flag. Key names have shifted across macOS releases, so they are pinned to a declared, versioned content-pack entry and an unrecognised OS version reports 'not profiled', not 'disabled'.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix reports OS-level AI posture. Jamf and Kandji can SET the com.apple.applicationaccess restriction but do not report the resulting on-device state next to AI usage, which is the join that makes 'the control exists and is not applied' actionable.
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: AI gateway persistence inventory (LaunchAgents and LaunchDaemons)
description: Parse every plist under `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents` and `/Library/LaunchDaemons` for `Label`, `ProgramArguments`, `RunAtLoad`, `KeepAlive` and the Std*Path log targets, then match argv basenames against a gateway catalog (litellm, claude-code-router/ccr, bifrost, portkey, helicone, openllm, vllm, ollama, lmstudio, jan, mitmproxy). Each hit writes an `ai_surfaces` row kind=gateway plus rule `ai_gateway_persistent`. Verified on this endpoint: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.litellm.plist` runs `<redacted-local-path> --config <redacted-local-path> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4010` with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive both true, beside `com.example.gemini-proxy-for-claude.plist` and `com.local.gemini-gateway-for-claude.plist` (and a matching `~/Library/Application Support/GeminiGatewayForClaude`). A boot-started, self-restarting proxy that re-labels Claude Code traffic as Gemini is the single most consequential thing on this machine and Vole records none of it today.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces grid, kind chip 'Gateway': Label, port from argv, and RunAtLoad/KeepAlive as two flags. An amber incident `ai_gateway_persistent` quoting the literal ProgramArguments line. A cross-link on the model Breakdown reads 'a local gateway was resident during this range — model names may not reflect the provider actually called'.
data_source: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist, /Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons: Label, ProgramArguments, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath.
honest_limit: A loaded LaunchAgent proves a process is configured to run, not that any agent was ever pointed at it; binding a gateway to actual traffic needs the route-evidence and rerouted-model features, and where both are absent this row stays informational. The config file named in argv is read for the port and model-alias key names only — API keys inside it are never read or stored. A proxy started from a shell background job, a login item, or a per-project script instead of launchd is missed, and a root-installed daemon may point at a path this user cannot stat.
competitive_note: Roadmap-v1 Tier 6 has a 'gateway hop resolver from claude-code-router's own logs', which only works after a specific router has already written logs; nothing in v1 or in the 62-vendor matrix enumerates launchd persistence for AI infrastructure. LiteLLM's own docs are a routing tutorial, and Bifrost publicly concedes that every agent not pointed at it is shadow AI.
field_verified: The headline plist is verbatim correct. `cat ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.litellm.plist` -> Label `com.example.litellm`; ProgramArguments `<redacted-local-path> --config <redacted-local-path> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4010`; `<key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>`, `<key>KeepAlive</key><true/>`; StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath `<redacted-local-path>`. com.example.gemini-proxy-for-claude.plist and com.local.gemini-gateway-for-claude.plist both present; ~/Library/Application Support/GeminiGatewayForClaude present with bin/, install-state.json, litellm.yaml, run-proxy.sh, uv-python/, uv-tools/. CORRECTIONS: (a) 'port from argv' works for 1 of 3 — com.example.gemini-proxy-for-claude.plist's entire ProgramArguments array is `<redacted-local-path>`: no port, and a basename ('run-claude-multi-proxy.sh') that matches no gateway catalog entry, so basename matching misses 2 of the 3 gateways here. (b) --host 127.0.0.1: the strongest gateway on this machine is loopback-bound. (c) /Library/LaunchAgents holds only com.logi.ghub.plist and /Library/LaunchDaemons only docker x2, logi, nordvpn — both system legs are empty here. (d) litellm is NOT in the lsof LISTEN table on 4010 despite KeepAlive=true: configured, not running, exactly as the honest limit says.
constraint: Constraint 7 (no content, no credentials) is the live risk and the feature handles it correctly by reading the argv config path for the port and alias key names only — <redacted-local-path> is a LiteLLM config and those routinely carry api_key values. Keep that read to key names. No other conflict: plists are XML, no subprocess needed, no new detection state beyond the shared registry.

name: vole assess --wedge: competitor-coverage annex computed on the buyer's own machine
description: Extend the assess report with the three facts a security buyer checks before a pilot, all computed from their machine rather than asserted in a deck: which of their own agent surfaces each incumbent category is documented to cover, read from a shipped, dated data/console_coverage.json with one row per category (endpoint DLP, SASE proxy, agent gateway, LLM observability, vendor console) and a URL plus read date per claim; the local row counts proving the uncovered cells are non-empty; and the `verify --content` result line showing zero content matches in the very database being shown. Output is one markdown and HTML file, ephemeral mode available, no daemon required.
desktop_surface: A dashboard toolbar 'Assess' action that produces the report and reveals it in Finder, with the same annex rendered inline on the Coverage screen so the demo and the document are one artefact.
data_source: usage_events, anomalies, agent_surfaces, posture_apps and coverage_gap rows; shipped data/console_coverage.json with URL and read date per claim; `vole verify --content` output.
honest_limit: Competitor rows are dated readings of public documentation, so each is phrased 'as documented on <date>' and never as 'vendor X cannot' — a vendor may have shipped coverage since, and the annex invites the reader to check. The report describes one laptop; extrapolating to a fleet is the reader's inference and the header says so. Unpriced rows print an em dash with their count (Codex 83/83 and Grok's 969 activity_only rows here), so every dollar figure is partial by a stated amount.
competitive_note: Every competitor's evaluation begins with a demo on the vendor's data; this one begins with the buyer's own machine and needs no account, no rollout and no procurement step — the only motion available to a free MIT tool selling into a market where Cyberhaven, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto arrive through an existing contract, and the cheapest strong artefact the research identifies.
v1_ref: vole assess: retrospective assessment report from history already on disk
field_verified: The local row counts are exact and reproduce to the digit: `codex|exact|83 calls|83 unpriced` (83/83 as claimed) and `grok|activity_only|969` (969 as claimed). Everything else is absent. `data/console_coverage.json` does not exist — git ls-files shows only `packages/core/src/data/pricing.json`. `agent_surfaces`, `posture_apps` and `coverage_gap` do not exist. `vole assess` itself does not exist (v1 Tier 4). And `grep -rn -- '--content' packages/core/src apps README.md docs` returns NOTHING — the `verify --content` result line the report is built around is a flag nobody has written, cited by this feature and by the Privacy Center both.
constraint: Principle 5 handled well: shipping competitor coverage as a DATED STATIC FILE rather than fetching it is the correct reconciliation of 'no scraping, no silent network calls', and the feature says so. Constraint 18 is missed: every dollar figure in the report is 'equivalent API value at Anthropic list rates', not money anyone was billed, and an assessment handed to a CFO must state that on the page or it reads as spend. Separate non-technical risk worth flagging: a shipped file in a public MIT repo asserting what named competitors do not cover is a standing reputational and legal surface — the 'as documented on <date>' phrasing helps only while someone keeps it current.

name: Full Disk Access canary and the launch-context record
description: There is exactly one bit that matters for buyer need #12's "honest reduced-functionality state without FDA", and exactly one honest way to read it: `open('~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db', O_RDONLY)`, which succeeds only under kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles. Confirmed here it returns EPERM (this shell has no FDA) while ~/Desktop, ~/Documents and ~/Downloads read fine — proving FDA and the per-category folder grants are separate axes and that one cannot be inferred from the other. The probe opens the descriptor and immediately closes it: no query is ever issued, so no TCC content is read, and the outcome lands as a `scan_access` row with root='tcc_canary'. Alongside it record `launch_context` derived from ppid/uid/env (app_child | launchagent_gui | launchdaemon_root | terminal), because that value decides the prompt fork admins must be told about: an MDM-pushed PPPC profile is the only silent grant, a LaunchDaemon receives EPERM with no prompt ever, and a user LaunchAgent prompts only when an Aqua session exists.
desktop_surface: Settings > Permissions gains one chip at the top: "Full Disk Access — granted / not granted / not probed", with the launch context beside it and, when not granted, a button opening `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.settings.PrivacySecurity.extension?Privacy_AllFiles` (falling back to the Privacy pane root — the URL scheme is unversioned Apple surface). The menu-bar SetupCard gains a state so "no data" never renders when the true cause is "no access".
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db — open() outcome only, never contents; process.ppid / process.getuid() / XPC_SERVICE_NAME for launch_context.
honest_limit: The canary answers "can this process read FDA-protected files right now", which is not the same question as "the admin granted Vole FDA" — a PPPC profile, a grant inherited from a responsible parent, or a stale grant on a different build can all produce `ok`. Vole cannot read TCC.db's rows to explain the answer, and must not; launch_context is a heuristic from ppid/uid and is labelled as one.
competitive_note: market.md §7 names "reduced-functionality state when FDA missing: report unknown, not zero" as the CrowdStrike/Nightfall deployment pattern; none of the 62 vendors in the matrix ship an inspectable FDA bit to the person running the endpoint, because for sysext-based agents (Jamf, SentinelOne, Santa) the entitlement makes the question moot.
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Evidence-ladder card: a surface with no telemetry that can never be misread as spend
description: One card design shared by every homegrown surface, whose only job is to make an inventory row unmistakably not a usage row. Each surface renders a five-rung evidence ladder - dependency resolved, provider key held, keychain or gateway-config binding, launchd persistence, matched request lines - each rung either lit and clickable through to its path receipt, or greyed with the reason it is dark. Sort order is evidence strength, never spend, because spend does not exist here: the token, cost and session columns are structurally absent from this section rather than rendered as zero, and the section header carries its own denominator, 'N surfaces found by inventory; 0 have token counts'. A card with only rung 1 lit reads 'code that could call a model'; one with rung 5 lit reads 'requests observed on N days'.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen gains a third section, 'No-log AI', beneath the enrolled agents and the detected-but-unsanctioned apps. Each card expands to its ladder, its path receipts and the incidents citing it (provider_key_without_sanctioned_surface, sanctioned_name_unsanctioned_upstream, plaintext_model_transport). Menu-bar security counts include those incidents; menu-bar token and cost figures never include this section.
data_source: ai_surfaces, ai_dependencies, provider_keys, key_residency, model_routes, surface_activity - read models only, no new collection
honest_limit: The ladder shows how much evidence Vole holds, not how much risk exists: five lit rungs on a weekend side project outrank one lit rung on a service handling customer data, and the product has no way to tell those apart. It ranks by evidence, never by exposure, and the card says so in the place where a risk score would otherwise go.
competitive_note: Console-based shadow-AI dashboards render an unknown surface as a row with zeros in the spend columns, which reads as 'costs nothing'; refusing to draw the column is the honest version and the visible half of the NON-GOALS charter.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: site_capabilities: what a chat site was allowed to touch on this machine
description: The existing browser feature stops at hostname visit counts, which cannot distinguish reading a marketing page from handing an AI site the microphone and a directory picker. Chrome records every persistent grant per origin in Default/Preferences -> profile.content_settings.exceptions.* (105 setting kinds present here); join those to the AI origins already registered in ai_surfaces. Verified on this machine: media_stream_mic for https://chatgpt.com:443 = 1 (a standing microphone grant), file_system_access_chooser_data present for https://chatgpt.com:443 (proof the site invoked the File System Access picker), file_system_last_picked_directory storing a real local path for another origin (<redacted-local-path>), durable_storage = 1 for chatgpt.com and claude.ai, notifications = 1 for claude.ai, and permission_actions_history for grok.com carrying AudioCapture.one_time_grant_count = 1. site_engagement.{rawScore,lastEngagementTime} and media_engagement.visits give the browser's own usage measure per AI origin without touching the 125 MB History database. Adds site_capabilities(surface_id, origin_hash, capability, setting_value, granted_at, source_file) and a dlp_egress reason 'browser_capability'; rules ai_site_local_file_reach (an AI origin holds file_system_access_chooser_data or a file_system_last_picked_directory entry), ai_site_capture_grant (persistent mic or camera = 1) and ai_site_clipboard_grant (clipboard = 1). Paths are stored as paths — Vole already stores cwd and file paths — and file contents are never opened.
desktop_surface: Leak Ledger gains a Browser grants section beneath the at-rest findings: one row per (origin, capability) citing the exact content-settings key and the pref file it came from, with the picked directory shown as a path and a jump to the ai_surfaces row for that host.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences -> profile.content_settings.exceptions.{media_stream_mic, media_stream_camera, clipboard, file_system_access_chooser_data, file_system_last_picked_directory, file_system_access_extended_permission, durable_storage, notifications, permission_actions_history, site_engagement, media_engagement}
honest_limit: A grant is authority, not transfer: Vole cannot see whether any file was actually uploaded, and chosen-objects is [] in the live state here, meaning nothing is currently persisted — only that the picker was opened. Chrome prunes these entries on site-data clear, so absence proves nothing. Origins are HMAC-hashed with the existing Keychain key unless they are already a registered ai_surface host. Safari and Firefox store grants in formats Vole has not profiled, so those seats render NULL, never zero.
competitive_note: Cyberhaven and Harmonic reach this class of evidence only by reading full page content through an endpoint sensor plus a browser extension; Vole reads the browser's own grant record and stores no content, which is what makes it survivable in a works-council review.
v1_ref: Browser AI-host visit census (hostname counts only, no extension, no proxy)
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: Rerouted-model detector straight from the model column, with CCR hex decode
description: v1's model-route item hunts config files, CCR backups and api_error bodies; the stored rows already hold the proof. On this machine 2,540 `usage_events` rows carry `tool='claude_code'` with a model id that is not Anthropic's — `qwen3.8-27b-fp8` (1,492 rows, 452M tokens), `glm-5.2` (564), `fable-fusion-27b`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha`, `lfm2.5:latest` — plus 461 rows whose model is `anthropic/claude-ccr-h<hex>`, where the hex after the `h` is claude-code-router's encoding of the true upstream (h7177656e2f… decodes to qwen/qwen3.8-27b-fp8, h6f70656e… to openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha). Ship a first-party model-id list, a pure `canonical(model)` helper that also hex-decodes the ccr form, and rule `agent_model_not_first_party` citing tool, model id, decoded upstream, session, project and token total. This is a query plus a static table, not a config scanner, and it is the highest-value security fact already sitting in the store.
desktop_surface: Breakdown shows a 'not first-party' badge per model row with the decoded upstream printed underneath; Incidents gains one row per session; the menu-bar glyph tints on a critical firing in a repo policy.json marks corporate.
data_source: usage_events.model in ~/.vole/vole.db (counts verified by query); packages/core/src/pricing.ts:75-96 rateFor/contextWindow; data/pricing.json first-party ids; ~/.claude-code-router/app-data/{usage.sqlite, request-logs.sqlite} as corroboration only.
honest_limit: The model string proves which model answered, not which host served it: a self-hosted or proxied Anthropic-compatible endpoint returning `claude-sonnet-5` is indistinguishable from the real thing here, and a NULL model (46 Codex, 789 Grok rows) can never be classified — report those as 'unknown route', never as first-party. The hex decode is claude-code-router's private encoding, so it must be versioned and must degrade to 'undecodable, ccr-shaped' rather than guessing. Cost stays NULL for every one of these rows: 'cost delta at list rates' is not computable because the displaced model is unknown.
competitive_note: Gateways (LiteLLM, Bifrost, Tailscale Aperture) see only the agents they route and admit the rest is shadow AI; Claude Code Analytics never sees these calls because they never reach Anthropic. No vantage point in the 62-vendor matrix can make this detection.
v1_ref: Model-route integrity and allowlist (model_provider_rerouted, model_switch, model_not_allowed)
field_verified: Verified by direct query, numbers slightly off. `SELECT count(*), sum(total_tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE source='live' AND tool='claude_code' AND model IS NOT NULL AND model NOT LIKE 'claude-%' AND model <> '<synthetic>'` -> 2,549 rows / 559,145,144 tokens (feature says 2,540 in one place and 2,661 elsewhere; the 559.1M token figure is exact). Per-model verified: qwen3.8-27b-fp8 1,492 rows / 452,243,584 tokens; glm-5.2 564; fable-fusion-27b 16; qwen/qwen3.8-27b-fp8 6; gemini-3.7-flash 2; openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha 2; lfm2.5:latest 2; qwen3.8-27b-base 2; qwen3.8-27b-heretic 1; qwen3.8-claude:27b 1. CCR-hex verified: 461 rows / 40,718,239 tokens across `anthropic/claude-ccr-h7177656e2f7177656e332e382d3237622d667038` (456) and `anthropic/claude-ccr-h6f70656e726f757465722f737465616c74682f6f782d616c706861` (5); the hex decodes to `qwen/qwen3.8-27b-fp8` and `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha`, and the first decoded value matches `"ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b-fp8"` inside settings.json.ccr-backup-2026-08-23T19-37-59-762Z — independent corroboration from a second artifact.
constraint: None. Pure SELECT plus a static first-party id list plus a pure hex decode — no schema change, no new write path, no poll cost. Constraint 5 honoured (cost stays NULL; 'cost delta at list rates' correctly declared not computable). Two correctness traps to write into the spec: `<synthetic>` (129 rows, 0 tokens) must be excluded explicitly or it reads as 'not first-party', and `claude-fable-5-1` (1,149 rows / 106,751,776 tokens) IS first-party and must be in the shipped list or the rule fires 1,149 false criticals on day one. Overlaps roadmap-v1 L128 (model_provider_rerouted) but genuinely corrects it: v1 hunts config files and api_error bodies; the proof is already in the stored model column.

name: Overview: security-first tile grid with no risk score
description: The dashboard pane leads today with Tokens and Equivalent Cost (DashboardView.swift:388-400), which is the right first screen for a cost monitor and the wrong one for a security buyer. Replace the KPI form with six count tiles, each a plain COUNT or SUM over rows that exist and each a link into its section with the matching filter pre-applied: people monitored on this host, agents detected (n outside policy), open exposure findings, incidents by severity in 24h, posture controls unknown, spend with its unpriced count beside it. There is deliberately no composite risk score — principle 1 forbids inventing a number and a posture score is the most inviting number to invent — and the timeline plus token KPIs move below the fold with the cost figure relocated to Costs.
desktop_surface: Overview: a 3x2 tile grid above the incident-annotated timeline; each tile shows the figure, a one-line 'what this counts' caption ending in 'on this Mac', and a chevron that navigates to the section with its filter applied.
data_source: usage_events (COUNT DISTINCT user/machine, COUNT DISTINCT tool, COUNT cost_usd IS NULL), anomalies severity counts, plus the enterprise tables when the capability probe finds them; all in ~/.vole/vole.db today.
honest_limit: Counts on one laptop are not a fleet posture and the captions must say 'on this Mac' until fleet sync exists. 'Agents detected' counts agents that wrote parseable local artifacts, so a web-chat or hosted-agent user reads as zero, and the user/machine columns are unread by any query today (they are NULL on historical rows), so 'people monitored' is 1 or unknown until identity stamping backfills.
competitive_note: Every AI-security console opens on a risk score; buyers cite IBM's breach data and Gartner's shadow-AI warnings, and the defensible answer is counts with evidence — which is also the only Overview compatible with the works-council prohibition on performance scoring (GDPR Art. 88, EU AI Act Annex III 4(b)).
field_verified: Premise confirmed: DashboardView.swift:372-373 leads with `metricRow("Tokens", ...)` then `metricRow("Equivalent Cost", ...)`, both `prominent: true` (feature cites :388-400, drift 16). Tile data checked against ~/.vole/vole.db: `COUNT(DISTINCT tool) WHERE source='live'` = 5; anomalies severity counts = 249 live; `COUNT(*) WHERE cost_usd IS NULL` = 4,723 of 29,653 (16% unpriced). But only 3 tables exist — `.tables` returns exactly `anomalies collector_state usage_events` — so 'open exposure findings' and 'posture controls unknown' have no backing table and render as unavailable states, not counts. MATERIAL CORRECTION to the honest_limit: it claims user/machine 'are NULL on historical rows'. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM usage_events WHERE user IS NULL` returns **0**; all 29,551 rows carry user='shiva', machine='Marys-MacBook-Pro.local' (db.ts:129 spreads ORIGIN over every insert). They are unread by any query — grep for `machine` in queries.ts and DB.swift returns zero hits — but they are fully populated.
constraint: None, and the feature is the strongest principle-1 statement in the shard: refusing a composite posture score is exactly the number a security dashboard is most tempted to invent. Constraint 5 (aggregates dropping NULLs must expose an unknown count) is satisfied by putting the 4,723 unpriced count beside spend rather than behind it. Watch constraint 6 on the agents tile: `COUNT(DISTINCT tool)` without `AND source='live'` counts seeded tools.

name: scan_access: the attempted read is the only honest observable
description: Every collector today guards with `existsSync(dir)` and on failure emits a note like devin.ts:36 `No Devin data at <dir>` — a sentence that is factually wrong for a permission denial, and that nothing stores or renders (notes only reach `--verbose` stdout). Measured on this machine (macOS 26.6.2): `existsSync('~/Library/Safari')` returns **true** while `readdirSync` on it throws EPERM, and `existsSync('~/Library/Safari/History.db')` returns true while `openSync` throws EPERM — TCC denies at open/readdir and never at stat, so `existsSync` is not a permission oracle and cannot be made into one. Add `scan_access(root TEXT, tool TEXT, probe_ts, result TEXT CHECK(result IN ('ok','eperm','enoent','empty')), entries_seen INTEGER, errno TEXT, launch_context TEXT, build_id TEXT, source TEXT DEFAULT 'live', PRIMARY KEY(root, source))`, written once per scanner-cadence pass by attempting the *real* operation — readdir for a directory, open+close for a file — and classifying `err.code`. `CollectorResult` gains `access: {root, result, entries_seen, errno}[]` so the write stays on the single `db.ts` path and honours the seed/live partition; `entries_seen` is the field that makes `ok` with zero rows different from `eperm`.
desktop_surface: Not a screen of its own — it is the join every other screen needs. Feeds the Coverage strip and the Shadow AI screen (see the Readability matrix feature), and Settings > Permissions lists the raw table: root, four-state pill, entries seen, errno, probe age.
data_source: Attempted readdir/open on each of the 11 roots in paths.ts plus the ~15 discovery roots the shadow-AI spine adds (~/Library/Safari/History.db, other apps' Application Support and Group Containers, ~/Library/Logs/Claude, ~/Desktop, ~/Documents, ~/Downloads); errno from node:fs.
honest_limit: Reports the outcome of one attempt at one instant. It cannot say *why* — user denied, never prompted, profile removed and re-signed binary are indistinguishable from the errno alone — cannot enumerate its own grants, and a root readable at probe time can be denied 200ms later. `empty` is a count of zero entries, never a claim that the tool is unused.
competitive_note: Fleet/osquery's ATC tables read the same TCC-gated paths and return an empty table when denied, with no per-path readability signal; Jamf Protect and SentinelOne sidestep the question entirely with an Endpoint Security sysext (a multi-month Apple entitlement Vole is explicitly not pursuing, per market.md §7). For a file-reading endpoint tool the probe ledger IS the permission story, and no competitor publishes one.
v1_ref: Honest coverage: per-collector heartbeat, four source states and a coverage strip
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Installed AI app census by bundle id and signing Team ID
description: Walk /Applications, /Applications/Utilities, ~/Applications and ~/Downloads (depth 1, *.app only), read `CFBundleIdentifier` / `CFBundleShortVersionString` / `CFBundleExecutable` from `Contents/Info.plist`, read `TeamIdentifier` and the Authority line from a spawned `codesign -dv`, and match against a shipped `data/ai-apps.json` catalog of bundle ids and Team IDs derived from the 22 market profiles. Matching on bundle id and Team ID rather than filename is the entire point, and this machine proves it three times: /Applications/ChatGPT.app is `com.openai.codex` (Team 2DC432GLL2), /Applications/Devin.app is `com.exafunction.windsurf` (Team 83Z2LHX6XW), /Applications/OpenCode.app is `ai.opencode.desktop` — the visible name lies about the vendor in two of four cases. Apps signed by a known AI vendor Team ID but absent from the catalog are surfaced as `ai_vendor_app_unknown_to_catalog` rather than silently dropped: /Applications/Claude Science.app is `com.anthropic.operon` v0.1.43, an Anthropic-signed binary no catalog knows. Writes `ai_surfaces` rows kind=app keyed on (bundle_id, version, team_id), never on mtime.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces grid, kind chip 'App'; the row prints the bundle id under the display name so an admin sees com.openai.codex where Finder says ChatGPT, with the vendor column driven by Team ID. Row click expands the evidence: the plist path, the codesign authority line, and whether any Vole collector produces rows for that bundle. Unrecognised bundle ids are not shown, but are counted in a coverage banner: 'N apps scanned, M in catalog, K signed by an AI vendor but uncatalogued'.
data_source: /Applications/*.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleIdentifier + CFBundleShortVersionString; `codesign -dv` TeamIdentifier/Authority (node:child_process, a node: builtin, so SEA-safe); ~/Library/Application Support/<bundle id> mtime; shipped packages/core/src/data/ai-apps.json.
honest_limit: Presence is not use: an installed app with no data-directory writes proves only that it exists, and nothing here says what was typed into it, which account it used, or what it spent. Only the scanned directories are seen — an app run from a DMG, from ~/Desktop, or a per-project Electron build is missed, as is a browser PWA. An unsigned or ad-hoc-signed build has no Team ID, so the vendor column is NULL, never guessed. All 28 apps here carry XML plists so a regex read works, but a binary plist needs a `plutil -convert xml1 -o -` spawn and degrades to NULL version rather than a guessed one. Catalog matching means a brand-new AI app is invisible until the catalog ships an entry: the honest framing is 'known AI apps', never 'all AI apps'.
competitive_note: Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI discovers AI usage only as a domain-wildcard list of browser-visited sites and sees no installed app at all; LayerX/Akamai, Island and Menlo are browser-shaped and share that blind spot. CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian and Cyberhaven's ES sensor enumerate agent processes but need a kernel/ES sensor and an EDR contract — this is the same inventory fact from an unprivileged plist+codesign read, which is why it can ship in a free MIT binary. No LLM-observability vendor (Datadog, Langfuse, Helicone, Portkey) can see an app that never routed through their SDK.
field_verified: Every named identity confirmed verbatim. `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleIdentifier'` + `codesign -dv`: ChatGPT.app -> `com.openai.codex` v26.901.51231, TeamIdentifier=2DC432GLL2; Devin.app -> `com.exafunction.windsurf` v3.8.20, Team=83Z2LHX6XW; OpenCode.app -> `ai.opencode.desktop` v1.18.29, Team=5NZ4Q7NXJ4 (the feature omits this one); 'Claude Science.app' -> `com.anthropic.operon` v0.1.43, Team=Q6L2SF6YDW — the SAME team as Claude.app (`com.anthropic.claudefordesktop` v1.46388.4), so the Team-ID-to-vendor join demonstrably surfaces an uncatalogued Anthropic binary. FALSIFIED: 'All 28 apps here carry XML plists so a regex read works' — /Applications holds 27 .app bundles and `file` reports 7 as 'Apple binary property list': Xcode.app, TestFlight.app, VLC.app, Developer.app and the three Creator Studio apps. ~/Downloads has zero .app; ~/Applications has 'Claude Code URL Handler.app'.
constraint: Constraint 14 (SEA: node: builtins only): node:child_process is a builtin so `codesign`/`plutil` spawns are legal — but the binary-plist finding makes the subprocess mandatory rather than a degradation path, and Xcode.app being binary matters because feature 11 depends on reading Xcode preferences. Second conflict is cost, not policy: cli/collect.ts runs every 5 s (code-map §1) and code-map bug 8 already shows the poll loop is O(W^2 log W); one `codesign -dv` spawn per app per pass is unacceptable. Reconciliation: run this scanner on its own cadence (hourly / on-demand) with its own collector_state offset, never inside the 5 s usage pass.

name: Menu bar as the security surface: six honest states and two security counts
description: MenuBarLabel (VoleApp.swift:95-130) has two states — glyph tinted by liveSeverity and a token count — and MenuPanel.swift:150-240 shows tokens, cost, a sparkline and the top five tools with no incident or posture information whatsoever, which makes the always-visible surface the product's biggest unused asset. Define six states the deployment actually has: not-consented (collector held), collector down (Store.CollectorStatus.stale), degraded (a source unreadable / Full Disk Access missing), quiet, active incident (warn/critical), and action pending (a confirm-to-act request waiting), each with a distinct SF Symbol variant, an accessibility label and a one-line status strip naming its single next action. Add two counts above the fold, each a count of rows with evidence behind it and each opening the dashboard on the section that explains it: unsanctioned or unknown AI surfaces seen on this host, and sessions whose account could not be proven corporate. Both render an em dash rather than 0 when the underlying inventory has never run, and the glyph tint keeps its existing severity source so the new counts never silently change what the icon means.
desktop_surface: Menu bar: glyph plus optional figure with a distinct variant per state. MenuPanel: a status strip above the hero card naming the state and its action (Grant access, Restart collector, Review request, Open Incidents), then a two-tile security strip between the hero figures and the tool list, each tile preserving the selected range on click.
data_source: Store.collectorStatus (Store.swift:132-140), Store.liveSeverity, ~/.vole/consent.json presence, per-source readability probe over paths.ts; posture_apps / agent_surfaces / account_class columns and policy.json sanctioned lists when present; existing Store.summary for the range.
honest_limit: The menu bar carries an icon and a few characters, so the state is a summary and the panel is where the reason lives; the counts are of what Vole observed on this one host in the selected range, not a fleet position, and there is deliberately no composite score. 'Unsanctioned' is entirely a function of a list an admin supplied — with an empty policy every surface reads 'unknown', which is the honest default rather than a clean zero — and 'degraded' cannot distinguish a missing permission from a tool the user never installed until the source-state model records both.
competitive_note: EDR and DLP sensors are deliberately invisible to the employee; Kolide's employee-visible endpoint agent is the precedent that made device trust acceptable to workforces, and a monitor a works council must approve should be visible on purpose. The developer keeps a free local cost tool and the security team gets its two numbers from the same install — the dual surface Cyberhaven, Zscaler and CrowdStrike cannot offer because their endpoint components never land voluntarily.
field_verified: Premise confirmed, data sources largely not. MenuBarLabel (VoleApp.swift:96-127) has exactly the two states claimed: glyph tinted by `store.liveSeverity` at :117-118 and a tokens/cost/EmptyView switch at :119-126. MenuPanel body (:148-168) branches on collectorStatus into SetupCard / StaleBanner+hero+tools / hero+tools, and neither `hero` (:180-199) nor `tools` (:201-229) references incidents or posture — confirmed, zero security information on the always-visible surface. But: `~/.vole/consent.json` DOES NOT EXIST (`ls` fails) and `grep -rn consent packages/core/src apps/mac/Sources` returns nothing — there is no consent concept anywhere in the product. `posture_apps`, `agent_surfaces`, `account_class` and `policy.json` likewise do not exist; `.tables` is `anomalies collector_state usage_events`. Of the six proposed states, three are computable today (collector down = Store.CollectorStatus.stale, quiet, active incident = liveSeverity); of the two counts, zero are.
constraint: No violation — and the em-dash-not-zero rule for an inventory that never ran is a correct principle-1 application, as is refusing a composite score. One design risk the feature does anticipate: keeping the glyph tint on its existing severity source while adding counts, so the icon's meaning does not silently change. Unnamed: 'degraded' depends entirely on feature 7's four-state source model, so this cannot ship a truthful degraded state before that does.

name: pnpm verify --surfaces: the firewall between inventory and usage
description: A verify section that asserts the invariants this entire gap depends on, and fails the run when one breaks. (a) No row in ai_dependencies, provider_keys, key_residency, model_routes, surface_activity or history_sightings shares an event_key prefix with, or has ever produced, a usage_events row - the cross-reference count must be zero. (b) Every surface_activity counter is monotone against its stored predecessor and every scan cursor is <= the current file size, so a rotated log resets instead of double-counting. (c) Every inventory row's cited path either still exists or carries stale_since, and both counts are printed. (d) A canary pass runs the shipped DLP detector pack against the inventory tables themselves; any value-shaped string found in a name-only column fails the run. (e) The section prints its own denominators - consented roots walked, manifests parsed, plists parsed, logs tailed - so a passing run never reads as a coverage claim.
desktop_surface: Settings -> Verification replaces the hard-coded 'Every stored row reconciled' string with the last run's real per-section results including the surfaces section and its five assertion outcomes; a failed assertion renders as a red row naming the offending table and column.
data_source: the inventory tables themselves, their scan cursors, and the shipped DLP detector pack
honest_limit: Verify proves the inventory never contaminated usage and never stored a value; it cannot prove the inventory is complete. A homegrown surface with no manifest, no plist, no key name and no history line passes every assertion by being absent, which is why the section reports what it walked rather than what it covered.
competitive_note: No competitor ships a self-check that can fail its own build for inventing a number; this is the machine-checkable form of the claim the sales collateral makes against prompt-storing incumbents.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: AI CLI and package-manager inventory (PATH, npm global, pipx, Caskroom)
description: Agents installed by a package manager have no .app bundle and often no dot-directory until first run, so they are invisible to both the app census and the store prober. List (never execute) the entries of `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`, `~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules`, `~/.local/pipx/venvs` and `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom`, match basenames against the catalog, and write `ai_surfaces` rows kind=cli with the install root as evidence and an 'installed via' class (npm/pipx/brew/manual). Where the manager records a version — `<pkg>/package.json` version, the pipx venv metadata — read it; otherwise NULL. On this machine `~/.local/bin` alone is a whole shadow stack Vole knows nothing about: `litellm`, `litellm-proxy`, `litellm-gemini`, `litellm-azure`, `claude-provider`, `claude-science`, `cua-driver`, `hermes`, `hermes-acp`, `hermes-agent`, `graphify-mcp`, `mako`, `muse`, `unsloth`, plus the `~/.local/pipx/venvs/litellm` that the persistent LaunchAgent actually executes.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces rows kind=CLI grouped by install root, with the 'installed via' chip and the version where readable, and a 'never launched' marker when no matching dot-directory, store or log exists — separating 'installed' from 'has run' explicitly rather than implying use.
data_source: Directory listings of ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules, ~/.local/pipx/venvs, /opt/homebrew/Caskroom; <pkg>/package.json `version` for npm entries.
honest_limit: This is filename matching against a catalog: a locally built or renamed binary (`~/bin/x`) is invisible, and a name collision produces a false positive that only the evidence path lets an admin dismiss. The npm-global leg is often empty and is here — `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules` contains only `npm` on this machine, so the feature must not be pitched on it. Directories outside the user's PATH, and installs under another OS user, are not scanned. Presence on disk is never use.
competitive_note: Fleet/osquery can enumerate packages but has no AI catalog behind it; the SASE and browser vendors see none of this. Nothing in v1 inventories package-manager installs — its 'Agent runtime inventory (agent SBOM)' reads versions from transcripts of agents already collected, which by definition excludes anything never collected.
field_verified: ~/.local/bin verbatim: claude, claude-provider, claude-science, cua-driver, graphify, graphify-mcp, hermes, hermes-acp, hermes-agent, lite, litellm, litellm-azure, litellm-gemini, litellm-proxy, mako, muse, muse-bin-0.1.0-R708.1, node, npm, npx, unsloth, yt-dlp (the feature omits graphify, lite and muse-bin-0.1.0-R708.1). ~/.local/pipx/venvs = {litellm, yt-dlp} — the litellm venv is the exact binary the com.example.litellm LaunchAgent executes. CORRECTION, in the feature's favour: 'the npm-global leg is often empty and is here' is FALSE. /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules holds only `npm` (that leg IS empty), but ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules holds @anthropic-ai, @deepseek-ai, @musistudio and mako-security — and @musistudio is claude-code-router's own npm scope, so the npm leg independently proves the gateway install that features 6 and 7 detect by two other routes. /opt/homebrew/Caskroom holds only `fontforge-app`: the Caskroom leg is empty here.
constraint: None. Directory listings only, never execute — no subprocess, no network, no schema pressure beyond the shared registry (constraint 6: source column + purge). Reading `<pkg>/package.json` version for the npm leg is a read of a vendor-written manifest, not content, so constraint 7 is clear. Worth stating in the honest limit: `~/.local/bin/claude` and `node`/`npm`/`npx` sitting in the same directory mean the 'installed via' class is inferred from the install root, not proven — a manually symlinked binary reads as manual.

name: Notification coalescing, auditable per-rule mute and quiet hours
description: Store.notifyFreshIncidents (Store.swift:151-176) posts one notification per new warn/critical incident behind a 15-minute freshness gate and a monotonic id high-water mark. At the real rate on this machine — 249 live incidents, 190 of them burn_rate_spike — that is a spam generator and the fastest route to the user quitting the app, which makes shadow AI invisible again. Coalesce by (rule, session) inside a window into one notification with an 'and N more' body, add quiet hours and a per-rule mute, and make a mute write an auditable info-severity suppression row rather than silently dropping, so an auditor can see what was hidden and by whom.
desktop_surface: Grouped notifications; an Incidents toolbar 'Notifications' popover listing each rule with its 24h fire count, a mute toggle and quiet-hours pickers; muted rules stay visible in the Incidents list behind a 'muted' chip rather than disappearing.
data_source: Store.swift:151 notifyFreshIncidents and the vole.lastNotifiedIncidentID UserDefaults key; anomalies.anomaly_key/rule/session_id/severity/window_end; collect.ts:16,72 freshness gate.
honest_limit: Coalescing hides the individual arrival time of the merged incidents in the notification banner even though the rows keep it; and because verdicts are frozen at first sight by INSERT OR IGNORE (db.ts:137), a warn that later becomes critical never re-notifies until the anomaly upsert and a re-notify path land. A mute is per-machine and user-writable, so it proves nothing against the seat owner.
competitive_note: Netskope's benchmark of 223 GenAI policy violations per organisation per month sets the volume expectation; any endpoint product that posts one alert per violation gets muted at the OS level, and v1's noise controls act on the collector side only — the notification path is a second, independent amplifier that nothing in v1 addresses.
v1_ref: Incident noise controls: window chaining, per-session cap, info rollup
field_verified: Confirmed. Store.swift:145-166 posts one UNNotificationRequest per fresh incident in a `for incident in fresh.sorted` loop; the gate at :151-154 is `$0.id > lastNotifiedIncidentID && $0.source == "live" && $0.severity != "info" && $0.windowEnd >= cutoff` with a 15-minute cutoff; the high-water key `vole.lastNotifiedIncidentID` is at :65. Rate confirmed: 190 of 249 live incidents are burn_rate_spike. One overstatement: the feature reads as if 249 historical incidents would fire at once — they cannot, because the 15-minute freshness filter suppresses them and Store.swift:62-64 documents exactly that. The real exposure is forward-looking bursts of a rule that produces 76% of all firings.
constraint: DIRECT CONFLICT the feature does not name. It proposes that a mute 'write an auditable info-severity suppression row'. Constraint 13 states DB.swift must stay a read-only consumer (READONLY open, no writes), and db.ts insertEvents/insertAnomalies are the single write path. I confirmed DB.swift performs no writes (READONLY at :129 with a READWRITE fallback at :131 used only to open). Reconciliation: the mute is a preference the COLLECTOR reads — ~/.vole/policy.json, consistent with paths.ts:21's pricing-override pattern — and the collector writes the suppression row; or the audit row is dropped and the mute stays a per-machine UI preference, which the feature's own honest_limit already concedes 'proves nothing against the seat owner'. Do not let the app write.

name: coverage_degraded: a root that was readable and stopped being
description: The dangerous failure is not "never had access" — that is loud on day one — it is a root that was readable for six months and silently stopped, which is what a re-signed build, a removed PPPC profile or a macOS upgrade produces. `scan_access` therefore keeps `last_ok_ts`, `last_ok_entries` and `last_result` per root rather than only the current state, and a rule fires on the `ok → eperm` transition only (never `ok → enoent`, since an uninstalled tool is not a degradation). `anomaly_key = 'access:' || root || ':' || build_id || ':' || <UTC day bucket of first denial>` — deterministic, no now(), so the existing INSERT OR IGNORE stays idempotent. The detail carries the figures principle 3 demands: root, last_ok_ts, entries seen at last ok, current errno, and whether `build_identity.cdhash` changed between the two probes — which names the usual cause instead of guessing at it.
desktop_surface: Appears in the existing incident feed with a distinct icon, and pins to the top of Settings > Permissions until resolved. Severity is critical for a first-tier root (a collector's own source path, so real spend is now invisible) and warn for a second-tier discovery root.
data_source: scan_access transition history joined to build_identity.cdhash.
honest_limit: It reports a transition and the two facts that bound the explanation (errno, cdhash change); it cannot distinguish a revoked grant from a re-signed binary from a directory whose mode changed for unrelated reasons.
