A root that was never once readable never fires — a fresh install with no grants is silent by design, which is exactly why the FDA canary exists as a separate, always-present state.
competitive_note: No vendor in the matrix alerts on its own loss of read access; EDR agents with a sysext cannot lose it this way, and osquery/Fleet simply return fewer rows. This is the rule that keeps Vole's zeros trustworthy, and it is only necessary because Vole chose file reads over an Endpoint Security entitlement.
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Ghost-app detector: AI tools that ran here and were then deleted
description: An uninstalled AI app leaves three residues macOS never cleans: `~/Library/Preferences/<bundle-id>.plist`, `~/Library/Application Support/<name>/`, and dangling symlinks in /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin. Set-difference the residue bundle-id set against the installed bundle-id set from the app census and emit `ai_surfaces` rows kind=residue, recording the plist mtime as last_seen (the last preference write). The set-difference must be over bundle ids, never app names, and this machine shows exactly why: `~/Library/Preferences/com.exafunction.windsurf.plist` looks orphaned by name because there is no Windsurf.app, but /Applications/Devin.app carries that bundle id — a name-based residue rule fires a false positive here. The verified true positive is Ollama: `/usr/local/bin/ollama` is a dangling symlink into `/Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama`, the app is gone, and `~/.ollama` (logs, models, id_ed25519, plaintext history) plus `~/Library/Application Support/Ollama` and `~/Library/Preferences/com.electron.ollama.plist` all remain. Renamed or quarantined support directories are recorded verbatim as their own residue rows (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p.empty-20260811-234028` here).
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces grid, kind chip 'Residue', struck-through app icon, caption 'ran here, no longer installed'; the drill-down lists every residue path found so a responder can confirm or clean them, with the dangling symlink target shown literally.
data_source: ~/Library/Preferences/*.plist filenames (bundle ids); ~/Library/Application Support/ directory names; readlink on dangling symlinks under /usr/local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin; joined against the installed-app bundle-id set.
honest_limit: A preference plist proves the app launched at least once under this user; it does not prove what was done with it, and mtime is the last preference write, not the last use. Residue cannot distinguish 'evaluated for ten minutes' from 'used daily for a year' — the row says presence only. A user who ran a clean uninstaller (AppCleaner, `brew uninstall --zap`) leaves nothing and is invisible, so absence of residue is never evidence of absence of use. And the bundle-id join is load-bearing: without it, an app that was renamed by its own vendor between releases reads as a ghost.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix reports removed-app residue. Network proxies (Netskope, Zscaler, Cato) see nothing after uninstall; EDR and MDM inventories (Jamf, Kolide, Fleet, CrowdStrike) list what is installed now. This is the only signal that survives an employee tidying up before an audit.
field_verified: Every residue confirmed. `ls -la /usr/local/bin/ollama` -> `lrwxr-xr-x root wheel Jul 25 08:31 /usr/local/bin/ollama -> /Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama` with /Applications/Ollama.app ABSENT (verified dangling). ~/.ollama survives with `history`, `id_ed25519`, `id_ed25519.pub`, `config.json`, `logs/`, `models/`, `backup/`. ~/Library/Preferences/com.electron.ollama.plist and ~/Library/Application Support/Ollama both present. ~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p.empty-20260811-234028 present verbatim. The named false-positive is real: ~/Library/Preferences/com.exafunction.windsurf.plist exists with no Windsurf.app, while /Applications/Devin.app carries exactly that bundle id — a name-based rule fires here, a bundle-id rule does not. NEW residue the feature misses: com.openai.sky.CUAService.plist + ~/Library/Application Support/CuaDriver + ~/.local/bin/cua-driver (an OpenAI computer-use cluster).
constraint: Constraint 6/7: the residue rows land in the shared registry so they need the source column and the purgeSeed extension from feature 1; a residue path is a path, not content, so constraint 7 is satisfied. New correctness caveat, not a constraint: `com.electron.ollama` is a GENERIC Electron bundle id — its siblings here are com.electron.dockerdesktop and com.electron.wispr-flow — so 'bundle id, never name' is not a vendor key for Electron apps; the catalog must match the exact id and the vendor column stays NULL, never inferred from the com.electron.* prefix.

name: Deleted agent sessions, proved by the stores that outlived them
description: Three independent local records here name sessions that no longer exist. ~/.kiro/session-index/<hash>.jsonl holds {'op':'remove','sessionPath':'<hash>/sess_<uuid>','at':<ms>} while that session directory is now empty. Code/User/globalStorage/agent-host.db metadata holds sessionTombstone:claude:/<uuid> rows alongside 104 live sessions(session_uri, provider, start_time, external=1, registration_source='discovery', modified_time) — VS Code discovering and hosting Claude Code's own sessions, which is also a double-count hazard the collector must dedupe on the uuid. v1's Kiro plan polls session-index as a change feed and rules that remove ops must not delete rows, but a session created and removed between two polls — this one lived 20 minutes — leaves no session.json, so there is no row to keep. Adds session_tombstones(tool, root_id, session_ref, removed_at, evidence_path, had_row, reconstructable_from, source) and the rule session_removed_without_row: observed = removals in the window, baseline = rows Vole holds for that tool, threshold = 0. reconstructable_from points at the launch log that still carries the deleted session's model, executions and approvals — sess_6d62ec4e is present in full in ~/.kiro/logs/20260816T000221318/kiro.log after its removal.
desktop_surface: Coverage strip gains a Deleted column per tool; each entry either jumps to the surviving evidence or states plainly that no evidence remains, so a zero there is never read as 'nothing happened'.
data_source: ~/.kiro/session-index/<hash>.jsonl (op add|remove, sessionPath, at); <editor root>/User/globalStorage/agent-host.db metadata rows sessionTombstone:* and sessionRegistryBackfilled:*; ~/.kiro/logs/<stamp>/kiro.log
honest_limit: A deletion is not misconduct — it is what 'clear chat' does in the vendor's own UI. The record proves only that a session existed and stopped existing, never why, and never its content. If both the store and the launch log are gone the tombstone is the last artifact and Vole must report the session as unreconstructable rather than infer anything about it. sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli proves a provider was registered whose earlier sessions were only backfilled, so start_time for those is a backfill artefact, not an observation.
competitive_note: Vole's own handicap list already concedes that local evidence is deleted after 30 days; nothing in the 62-vendor matrix detects a deleted agent session, because a cloud sensor sees the traffic and never the store. This is the one signal that distinguishes 'this employee did nothing' from 'this employee's sessions are gone'.
v1_ref: Kiro collector (activity_only with autonomy flags)
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: Model-route rewrite evidence: rejected key labels, config backups, env names
description: Three cheap reads that establish whether an agent's traffic was redirected, without ever reading a secret value, ordered here by how much they actually deliver. (a) `~/.claude.json` `customApiKeyResponses.{approved,rejected}` stores the short label of every custom API key the user was prompted about — live here as `rejected: ["not-needed", "sk-litellm-local"]`, naming the local gateway by label. (b) Enumerate `~/.claude/settings.json.ccr-backup-*`, `.ccr-original`, `.bak-pre-ccr` by filename alone: four such files exist here and their names are dated proof that claude-code-router rewrote the settings file on 2026-08-23, plus `~/.claude-code-router/global-profile-takeover.json` and `gateway-proxy-preload.cjs`. (c) Grep ~/.zshrc, ~/.zshenv, ~/.zprofile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, ~/.config/fish/config.fish for `export <NAME>=` where NAME matches ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL|OPENAI_BASE_URL|OLLAMA_HOST|CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT|*_API_KEY, storing the variable NAME and the value's hostname only, never the value. All three feed `ai_surfaces` evidence rows and rule `model_route_rewritten`.
desktop_surface: A 'Routing' card inside each agent's AI Surfaces drill-down: custom-key labels offered with their approved/rejected verdict, a dated timeline of config-backup filenames, and the env var names set with their value hostname — each leg rendering 'none found' rather than an empty card.
data_source: ~/.claude.json customApiKeyResponses.approved/rejected; ~/.claude/settings.json.ccr-* filenames and mtimes; ~/.claude-code-router/{global-profile-takeover.json, gateway-proxy-preload.cjs}; shell rc files (variable NAMES + value hostname only); ~/.codex/config.toml model_providers.*.base_url host.
honest_limit: Leg (c) is the weakest and must not be sold as the mechanism: the rc scan returns zero matching exports on this machine even though a gateway demonstrably rewrote the config, because the redirection lived in settings.json and launchd, not in a shell profile. A shell rc export is in any case a snapshot of the current file, never of what was exported in a past session, so it can never be stamped onto historical usage_events rows — the card is labelled 'as of this scan'. Variables set inside a wrapper script, direnv, or a terminal profile are unobservable. `customApiKeyResponses` records that a key was offered and how the human answered, not that it was used: a rejected key proves the gateway exists and proves no traffic.
competitive_note: Extends v1's model-route integrity and Tier 6 'Provider endpoint snapshots', neither of which names customApiKeyResponses, the ccr backup filenames, or the shell rc files. Anthropic's Compliance API explicitly excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry and personal-account sessions, so a rerouted Claude Code session is invisible in the vendor console by design.
v1_ref: Model-route integrity and allowlist (model_provider_rerouted, model_switch, model_not_allowed)
field_verified: Leg (a) verbatim: ~/.claude.json `customApiKeyResponses` = {"approved": [], "rejected": ["not-needed", "sk-litellm-local"]}. Leg (b) verbatim: settings.json.bak-pre-ccr, settings.json.ccr-backup-2026-08-23T19-32-15-375Z, settings.json.ccr-backup-2026-08-23T19-37-59-762Z, settings.json.ccr-original (four, all dated 2026-08-23), plus settings.json.reset-backup-2026-08-29T06-40-00Z and ~/.claude/.claude.json.ccr-original-missing; ~/.claude-code-router/{global-profile-takeover.json, gateway-proxy-preload.cjs, config.sqlite} all present. Leg (c) confirmed WORTHLESS as the feature admits: grep for export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL|OPENAI_BASE_URL|OLLAMA_HOST|CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT|*_API_KEY|CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|CODEX_HOME across ~/.zshrc ~/.zshenv ~/.zprofile ~/.bashrc ~/.profile ~/.config/fish/config.fish returns ZERO matches. FALSIFIED leg: ~/.codex/config.toml has NO [model_providers] section and no base_url anywhere — the named field does not exist here; the file carries `model = "gpt-6-astra"`, model_reasoning_effort, marketplaces and a `notify` hook into 'Codex Computer Use.app'.
constraint: Constraint 7 (the DB holds no credentials) is a live hazard the feature under-states. The ccr backup it enumerates by filename contains, inside, `"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:3456"` immediately followed by `"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-ccr-g2Wv-93-..."` — a live bearer token in plaintext. This feature is safe because it reads filenames only, but it must say so loudly since feature 18 opens the same file for env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Reconciliation: one shared settings-layer reader that selects keys by name from an allowlist and never retains the parsed object; the auth token becomes a DLP finding (a fingerprint), never a stored value. Also drop or re-source the Codex model_providers leg.

name: Permission preflight in the app, and proof the grant reached the collector
description: `apps/mac/Info.plist` carries zero usage-description keys, so every TCC prompt Vole will ever raise shows a bare system string with no stated purpose — the worst possible first impression for a tool asking a developer for their whole disk, and a works-council problem downstream. Add `NSDesktopFolderUsageDescription`, `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription`, `NSDownloadsFolderUsageDescription` and `NSSystemAdministrationUsageDescription` carrying the same purpose sentences the Privacy Center already publishes, then run a first-run preflight in the **app** — which is guaranteed a UI session even as an LSUIElement agent — attempting one read per category so prompts arrive in a deliberate order with context on screen, rather than at 3am from a background helper the user cannot see. Both processes then probe the same roots and both write `scan_access` rows tagged with `launch_context`: the collector's row is the empirical proof that TCC responsibility actually transferred to the spawned child, which today is an untested assumption — and one that matters, since the collector orphans to PPID 1 the moment the app quits.
desktop_surface: A first-run Permissions sheet listing each root with its purpose sentence and a live four-state pill that flips as the user answers, plus a Re-check button; the same sheet is reachable afterwards from Settings > Permissions, where an "app vs collector" column shows both probes side by side and flags any root where the two disagree. Prompts are never raised silently from the background.
data_source: apps/mac/Info.plist usage-description keys; paired app-side and collector-side scan_access rows distinguished by launch_context.
honest_limit: A preflight can only ask. A denied category stays denied until the user changes it in System Settings; Vole cannot re-prompt, cannot revoke, and cannot tell "Don't Allow" from a dismissed prompt. Under MDM the prompts never appear at all because the PPPC profile pre-answers them, so "granted by profile" can only be inferred from a probe returning ok with no prompt observed — it is labelled as an inference, not a fact.
competitive_note: market.md §7's Kolide/Honest-Security pattern is per-user transparency about what is read; extending it to *who asked and who was answered* is unclaimed. It also closes the gap the round-2 shadow-AI spine opens: ~15 new TCC-gated discovery roots whose denials would otherwise surface as a clean, confident zero.
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Copilot CLI collector: exact tokens from session.shutdown modelMetrics
description: GitHub Copilot CLI writes ~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl, whose session.shutdown event carries modelMetrics per model with input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite and reasoning counts — the same five components usage_events already stores, so rows land confidence='exact' and get a real cost_usd once a rate exists. Key each row copilot:<session-id>:<model> from the shutdown event (never a line index or an mtime — the two existing idempotency violations in codex.ts:197 and antigravity.ts:63 are bugs, not precedents) and read tool.execution events for the tools column. A second presence-only path reads ~/.copilot/config.json firstLaunchAt, ~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log and ~/.copilot/ide/*.lock (ideName, workspaceFolders, pid only) so a Copilot install that has completed no session still appears as a discovered surface rather than as nothing. Verified on this machine: ~/.copilot exists with firstLaunchAt 2026-07-25T16:00:13.753Z, ten process logs (newest 2026-09-07T03:20Z) and three IDE locks, and Vole is entirely blind to all of it.
desktop_surface: Copilot becomes an eighth tool in Theme.swift Labels.order, Pal.series and the breakdown/timeline stacks, with exact tokens and no 'no tokens' badge; its AI Surfaces row shows firstLaunchAt, process-log count, IDE lock workspace and session count, and reads 'present, 0 sessions recorded' when session-state is empty.
data_source: ~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl (session.shutdown.modelMetrics.*, tool.execution); ~/.copilot/config.json firstLaunchAt; ~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log; ~/.copilot/ide/*.lock (ideName, workspaceFolders, pid)
honest_limit: session-state/ does not exist on this machine (only config.json, logs/ and ide/), so the token path is unverified against a real file and must ship behind a per-version fixture with an 'unverified format' chip; presence-without-usage is the correct display, never zero usage. Tokens land only at session.shutdown, so a running or SIGKILLed session contributes nothing and the most recent hour is systematically under-reported — a live session must never render as zero. ~/.copilot/ide/*.lock carries an 'Authorization: Nonce <uuid>' header and a unix socket path: read ideName/workspaceFolders/pid only and never the header, matching the existing rule for ide/*.lock authToken. GitHub treats the events schema as internal and syncs sessions to github.com, so the local file is neither documented nor authoritative.
competitive_note: Corrects v1's Copilot collector, which routes through VS Code chatSessions and concludes total_tokens must be NULL because that source has no per-request input total; the CLI's modelMetrics carries all five components, and v1's own note that '~/.copilot/logs holds lifecycle lines only' is true but describes the wrong file. ccusage already reads this file, which is independent confirmation the fields exist. GitHub's usage-metrics API lags ~2 days and never shows local prompts, and market.md lists hosted Copilot cloud as a surface nobody sees locally.
v1_ref: GitHub Copilot collector (VS Code agent mode exact output tokens; CLI activity_only)
field_verified: Presence half: CONFIRMED verbatim. ~/.copilot/config.json = {"firstLaunchAt": "2026-07-25T16:00:13.753Z"}. Ten logs/process-*.log, newest containing "2026-09-07T03:20:09.840Z [INFO] Starting graceful shutdown of CLI server". Three ide/*.lock (one zero-byte); populated ones carry exactly {socketPath, scheme, headers:{Authorization:"Nonce 5e992b89-..."}, pid:23716, ideName:"Visual Studio Code", workspaceFolders:["<redacted-local-path>"], isTrusted} — the Authorization-nonce warning is real. Token half: NOT FOUND. ~/.copilot/session-state does not exist; `find ~ -maxdepth 6 \( -path "*copilot*session*" -o -name events.jsonl \)` returns nothing. modelMetrics is unverifiable on this machine. COUNTER-FINDING: v1's source IS verifiable here — 173 files under Code/User/workspaceStorage/*/chatSessions/*.jsonl, of which 41 contain `completionTokens`.
constraint: Constraint 20 (pnpm verify must be extended for any new exact-token source) — unmentioned; a fixture-only source cannot be reconciled by verify, so it must ship activity_only until a real store is seen. Constraint 13 (read-model parity, queries.ts + DB.swift twice) and the fact that DashboardView.swift has exactly four panes (dashboard/incidents/breakdown/settings, line 331-334) — there is no 'AI Surfaces' row to add to; the presence half needs a new table plus a new pane. Reconciliation: ship the token path behind a per-version fixture chipped 'unverified format', write presence to a new posture table (not usage_events — presence is not an event), and gate the exact/verify switch on first reconciliation.

name: foreign_root_transcript: a cwd this filesystem cannot have
description: The cheapest proof that an agent ran somewhere else: classify every recorded working directory against the set of path roots that can exist on this volume. Sources are already parsed today — Claude Code transcript `cwd` (present on all 806 non-assistant lines sampled) and the `~/.claude/projects/<dash-encoded-path>` directory names, `~/.claude.json` `projects` keys (23 here), `~/.claude/history.jsonl` `project`, Codex `session_meta.payload.cwd` and `turn_context.payload.workspace_roots` (a real multi-root array here), OpenCode `session.directory`/`path.root`, and `~/.claude/ide/*.lock` `workspaceFolders` plus its `runningInWindows` flag. Three states, never conflated: `local` (root is /Users, /private, /tmp, /var, /opt, /Volumes, /Applications and the path resolves), `deleted` (root plausible, path gone — 9 of 23 Claude project keys and 4 of 10 Codex cwds here), and `foreign_root` (root is provably impossible on macOS: /workspaces, /home/<u>, /root, /app, /srv, /github/workspace, /builds, /var/lib/jenkins, C:\, \\wsl$\ — 0 here, measured). A `foreign_root` row is a transcript written by an agent on another filesystem that reached this disk only because a home or config dir was bind-mounted, synced or copied; it fires `foreign_root_transcript` with the root prefix as the explanation and links the run to an `execution_contexts` row of kind devcontainer/docker/ci.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen gains a 'Ran elsewhere' section listing foreign-root sessions with their root prefix, tool, first/last seen and the config dir that carried them; a `deleted` count sits beside it in grey so the two are never read as the same thing. The Coverage strip shows '0 foreign-root sessions, measured' when the count is zero — the point of the feature is that the zero is a measurement.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/*/ (dash-encoded cwd) and transcript `cwd`; ~/.claude.json `projects` keys; ~/.claude/history.jsonl `project`; ~/.claude/ide/*.lock `workspaceFolders` + `runningInWindows`; ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl `session_meta.payload.cwd` and `turn_context.payload.workspace_roots`; opencode.db `session.directory`
honest_limit: A foreign root proves the run's filesystem, not the machine or the container: a `~/.claude` copied from a Linux workstation, synced by Dropbox, or restored from a backup looks byte-identical to a live bind mount, and Vole says 'foreign root' for all of them rather than naming a container it cannot see. The far more common case leaves no trace at all — a devcontainer with its own home writes its transcripts inside the container and this detector correctly finds nothing, so zero foreign roots is not zero container runs and the card must say so. Root-prefix classification is a fixed shipped list; an unusual container image root (/opt/project) reads as `local` and is missed.
competitive_note: Snyk agent-scan (raw.githubusercontent.com/snyk/agent-scan) discovers agent configs across 11 tools including OpenCode and Antigravity but never asks whether the paths inside those configs exist on the host it is running on; no vendor in the 62-row matrix reports foreign-root transcripts, because everyone else reads process or network events rather than the agents' own on-disk path records.
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: Gemini CLI collector with prompts-logged-to-disk posture
description: Gemini CLI persists per-project conversations at ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/*.json with token usage and tool executions, plus logs.json and a settings.json whose telemetry.logPrompts defaults to true. Emit one exact row per model turn keyed gemini_cli:<project_hash>:<chat-id>:<turn-index>, taking model, input/output tokens and tool names verbatim, and record telemetry.logPrompts and any telemetry.outfile path as a posture row: a Gemini CLI with logPrompts on is writing full prompt text to a local file plus the vendor's collector, a DLP surface the company almost certainly does not know exists. Vole reads only the Antigravity half of ~/.gemini today and ignores the CLI entirely, so gemini_cli must be added as a distinct Tool literal in types.ts, the collectors REGISTRY, Labels.order and Pal.series — Antigravity and Gemini CLI are two products sharing a directory and must never be summed as one.
desktop_surface: Gemini CLI as a separate tool from Antigravity in the breakdown, timeline and Labels.order; an amber 'prompts logged to disk' chip on its AI Surfaces row when telemetry.logPrompts is true, with the outfile path and the managed-layer path in the drill-down.
data_source: ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/*.json; ~/.gemini/logs.json; ~/.gemini/settings.json telemetry.logPrompts / telemetry.outfile; /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/settings.json (managed layer)
honest_limit: Gemini CLI deletes chats after 30 days, so totals carry that horizon and are never presented as lifetime. On this machine ~/.gemini holds only antigravity/, antigravity-ide/ and config/ — the CLI chats directory does not exist, so this collector produces zero rows here and the correct display is 'not present', never zero usage. The chat JSON schema is undocumented and version-unstable, so a per-version fixture and a schema-drift note are mandatory. Reading logPrompts proves the switch is on, not that any prompt was written: quote the setting and the outfile path, never a count of logged prompts.
competitive_note: v1 covers Antigravity but has no Gemini CLI entry at all, and its vendor-telemetry posture report names Claude OTel, Codex [otel], Grok repo_state.upload and the Cursor crash reporter but not Gemini's logPrompts default — this extends that report with the one vendor whose default ships prompts plus user.email to a collector. Google itself documents that its system settings are 'not a foolproof security boundary' (market.md §7), which makes the local posture read worth more than the vendor pipeline to a privacy-constrained buyer; ccusage does not cover Gemini CLI tokens either.
v1_ref: Vendor telemetry and upload posture report

No tmp/, no chats/, no logs.json, no settings.json. /Library/Application Support/ has no GeminiCli directory (full listing: App Store, Apple, BTServer, CrashReporter, GarageBand, Logi, Logic, Mozilla, ProApps, Script Editor, com.apple.TCC, com.apple.backgroundassets.user, iLifeMediaBrowser). The claim 'Vole reads only the Antigravity half of ~/.gemini' is CONFIRMED in paths.ts: antigravityConversations() and antigravityBrain() both join(home(),'.gemini','antigravity-ide',...) and nothing else touches ~/.gemini. Constraint 3 (confidence has exactly two values) — a posture row must not invent a third badge for 'setting observed'. Constraint 20 (verify extension). name: Agent-home redirect, re-detected every pass (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME)
description: Re-run root enumeration on every scanner-cadence pass instead of once at install, into agent_roots(root_path, tool, first_seen, last_seen, discovered_by). Fire agent_home_moved on either of two exact signals: a live session id from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json whose transcript exists under no known root, or an allowlisted env name resolving to a path outside every known root. For a running agent the environment is directly readable — ps -E -p <pid> returned the full 3.6 KB environment of a same-uid Claude process on this machine, so CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL are obtainable with no hook and no injection; launchctl getenv, the ~/.claude/settings.json env block and shell rc exports cover the persistent form. Only variable names and path-shaped values are stored, and any name matching the credential list is recorded as present-with-shape, never with a value.
desktop_surface: The Shadow AI screen gains a Roots panel listing every agent home with first/last seen, how it was discovered, and a 'moved' badge. The incident card names the old root, the new root or 'unknown', which sessions fell outside it, and the pass that noticed.
data_source: ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json {pid, sessionId, cwd, startedAt, version, entrypoint} (3 live files here); ~/.claude.json projects[].lastSessionId (23 project entries); ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl; ps -E -p <pid> for same-uid processes; launchctl getenv; ~/.claude/settings.json env block; paths.ts VOLE_* overrides re-read per call
honest_limit: ps -E sees only processes alive at that instant and only same-uid ones — an agent that ran under a redirected home and exited between passes leaves only an orphan-session trace, which cannot say where it went. launchctl setenv and rc-file exports are found; a var set inline for one command (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/x claude) is found only if a pass catches the process running. A home on an unreadable volume or another user account is out of reach entirely and must render 'home unknown', never 'no activity'. Reading another process's environment is itself sensitive and belongs behind the scope gate and in the path receipts with the allowlist printed.
competitive_note: EDR sensors (Jamf, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) see the exec and its environment at kernel level and never lose the home, and Vole should say so plainly. But Fleet/osquery's AI inventory tables query fixed paths and would miss a redirected home exactly the way an install-time census does — this closes the same hole without kernel privilege.
gap_area: Evidence integrity when the monitored user is the local admin: gaps, source mutability, store lineage, clock

name: Multi-root agent-home census (paths.ts resolves exactly one home)
description: `paths.ts:24` resolves every source under a single `home()` (`VOLE_HOME_OVERRIDE ?? homedir()`) and hard-codes `~/.claude/projects`, so any agent pointed elsewhere is 100% invisible while the app still reports 'live' — which is worse than reporting nothing. Replace `claudeCodeProjects()` with `claudeCodeProjectRoots(): string[]` and add a general `homes(): {label, path, granted_by}[]` enumerating: the defaults, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `$CODEX_HOME` from the environment and from the shell-rc scan, `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig` and `Agents/XcodeVersions/*/claude/`, any `extra_roots[]` in policy.json, and `/Users/*/.claude` by stat only. Stamp `raw_ref` and `collector_state.source_path` with the root that produced each row, and write an `ai_surfaces` row kind=config_dir per discovered root with `granted_by` (env, well-known path, policy, stat-only) so the coverage claim is auditable. Corroborate per-tool install identity from `~/.codex/installation_id` and `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/installation_id` (36 bytes each).
desktop_surface: Settings → Sources gains a 'Config roots' list: each root, how it was found, whether it is being read, its transcript count and last scan. The AI Surfaces header shows an amber badge when a root was discovered that the collector has never scanned, and the summary carries the line 'Vole is watching 1 of 2 Claude config directories' rather than implying completeness. Discovered-but-unreadable roots show an amber dot reading 'present, not readable'.
data_source: packages/core/src/paths.ts:24; $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, $CODEX_HOME; ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig (verified ABSENT on this machine — the correct output here is a NULL row, not a fabricated one); shell rc assignments; /Users/*/.claude (stat only); collector_state.source_path.
honest_limit: Only roots that are well-known, exported in a scanned rc file, or admin-listed are discoverable: a root set inline for one command (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/x claude`) leaves no trace and is permanently invisible, so this widens coverage without ever proving completeness. Enumerating another POSIX user's home needs Full Disk Access and usually root; without it Vole must print 'other user directories: not readable', never 'no other agents'. Widening the root list changes the denominator of every historical total, so the change is dated in the UI and rows begin at first scan — there is no backfill. The Xcode layout is community-verified rather than vendor-documented and needs a per-version fixture; once the root is added the JSONL format is identical, so the tokens are exact — the gap was addressing, not parsing.
competitive_note: Contradicts an assumption v1 inherits from the code: its Copilot, Kiro and Codex-v2 collectors and its platform-coverage plan all widen sideways while keeping one home per OS, and its agent-version inventory reads versions out of transcripts Vole already collects, so it cannot report the gap either. market-extracts lists honouring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Xcode sessions as an explicit feature implication; no vendor in the matrix names it, because none of them address the endpoint by config directory at all.
v1_ref: Windows and Linux collector distribution / Agent runtime inventory (agent SBOM)
field_verified: Gap confirmed, line number off by ten. paths.ts line 14: `const home = () => process.env.VOLE_HOME_OVERRIDE ?? homedir();` (the feature cites paths.ts:24, which is actually the `claudeCodeProjects: () => process.env.VOLE_CLAUDE_PROJECTS ?? join(home(), '.claude', 'projects')` accessor). Every one of the 11 accessors resolves under that single home(); $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and $CODEX_HOME are honoured NOWHERE in the file. ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant -> 'No such file or directory' (the correct output is a NULL row, exactly as the feature states). Corroborating ids verified: ~/.codex/installation_id is 36 bytes containing `9c0a2575-b5fc-48bc-a40e-def3b7976912`; ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/installation_id is 36 bytes.

It proposes stamping `raw_ref` with the root that produced each row — but the db.ts:87-101 SET list never refreshes raw_ref (or model, session_id, project, git_branch, agent_id, confidence, source), and only fires at all when excluded.total_tokens is STRICTLY greater. So root provenance cannot be back-stamped onto existing rows; it must be correct on FIRST insert, and the feature's own 'no backfill, rows begin at first scan' line is therefore load-bearing, not a nicety. name: BYOK agent collectors: Goose, Amp and Continue
description: Three agents that write exact per-request token ledgers to disk that no vendor console anywhere reports, and that a gateway sees only if the developer happened to point them at one: Goose (~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db, or the macOS Application Support path — messages, tool calls, accumulated tokens per provider/model), Amp (~/.local/share/amp/threads/**/*.json with input/output/cache tokens and credits, plus a managed layer at /Library/Application Support/ampcode/managed-settings.json) and Continue (.continue/dev_data/*.jsonl with tokensGenerated, chatInteraction and toolUsage events). Each follows the existing collector contract: read-only open, stable event_key on the vendor's own id, confidence='exact' only where every token component is present and activity_only otherwise, with commit() called only after insertEvents succeeds.

data_source: ~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db and ~/Library/Application Support/goose/sessions/sessions.db; ~/.local/share/amp/threads/**/*.json; <repo>/.continue/dev_data/*.jsonl; ~/.continue/config.yaml for provider and base URL only
honest_limit: None of the three exists on this machine (all five candidate paths checked and absent), so all three parsers are written from vendor documentation and ccusage's reading and must ship activity_only until pnpm verify reconciles a genuine file, switching to exact per tool. Continue's dev_data lives inside each repo, not under a home directory, which paths.ts cannot express today (one home, eleven fixed paths) — it needs repo discovery, and a cloned checkout can contain another machine's events, so the collector keys on the event id and must not stamp the local user/machine identity on rows it did not observe. Amp reports credits as well as tokens; the two are never mixed into one cost figure.
competitive_note: Market research found no vendor that names OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime; Goose, Amp and Continue extend that list of blind spots. ccusage covers 18 sources for cost alone and is free MIT, which sets the floor: coverage alone is not defensible, coverage plus exact tokens plus behaviour rules on the same rows is. All three are BYOK by design, so vendor consoles report nothing for them by construction and a gateway sees them only by accident.
field_verified: All five candidate paths ABSENT, exactly as the honest limit states: ~/.local/share/goose, ~/Library/Application Support/goose, ~/.config/goose, ~/.local/share/amp and ~/.continue all return 'No such file or directory', and `ls -d <redacted-local-path>*/.continue` returns 'no matches found'. The feature says the Continue collector 'must not stamp the local user/machine identity on rows it did not observe' — that is not a collector-local choice, it is a change to a shared invariant in db.ts, and without it a cloned checkout attributes a colleague's agent usage to this employee in a security product. It also silently pollutes the per-active-host meter's own inputs. Constraint 20 (three new exact sources, three verify extensions). Constraint 18 (Amp credits are a third cost definition beside Anthropic list rates and OpenCode's provider figure) — correctly named by the feature.

name: Second-tier store prober: one module, ten tools
description: Ten more agents leave local stores worth detecting but not worth ten collectors, so ship one prober driven by a table of `(name, glob, id_field, kind)`: Goose `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db` and `~/.local/state/goose/logs/llm_request.*.jsonl`, Amp `~/.local/share/amp/threads/**/*.json`, Continue `.continue/dev_data/*.jsonl`, Cline/Roo `<editor>/User/globalStorage/saoudrizwan.claude-dev/tasks/<id>/`, Zed `~/Library/Application Support/Zed/threads/threads.db`, Kiro `~/.kiro/sessions/<hash>/sess_*/session.json` and `~/.kiro/session-index/<hash>.jsonl`, Copilot `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`, Aider `.aider.chat.history.md` in repo roots already known from `usage_events.project`, LM Studio `~/.lmstudio/conversations`, Jan `~/Library/Application Support/Jan/data/threads`. Each writes an `ai_surfaces` row with store path, file/row count, total bytes, mtime range and state=`artifact_present_no_collector`; only where a stable per-session id exists (Kiro `sess_<uuid>`, Goose session ids, Amp thread ids) does it additionally emit `activity_only` usage rows. Store growth over time is what shows an unsanctioned tool moving from trial to daily use.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces rows kind=cli/extension with a 'store' column reading '3 sessions, 42 MB, last write 2026-08-15'; these tools appear in the Breakdown only once they have produced activity_only rows, always with the existing 'no tokens' badge. The coverage report names each as 'present, not monitored — last activity <mtime>'.
data_source: The ten store paths above. Verified present on this machine: ~/.kiro/sessions (two workspace hashes) with ~/.kiro/session-index/*.jsonl, ~/.copilot/{config.json,ide,logs}, ~/Library/Application Support/{Kiro, Zed?, Devin, Codex, Cursor}. Verified ABSENT: ~/.continue, ~/.config/goose, ~/.local/share/{goose,amp}, ~/.lmstudio — the correct output for those is no row at all.

name: Local model runtime census and the exposed-bind rule
description: Three independent probes for on-device inference, stored as facts with which probe fired, because any one alone lies. (a) Socket sample: one unprivileged `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` per pass, filtered to 11434 (Ollama), 1234 (LM Studio), 1337 (Jan), 4891 (GPT4All), 8000/8080 (vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI) plus any port whose owning process matches the catalog, recording process, pid and bind address. (b) Manifest probe: directory listings only of `~/.ollama/models/manifests/**` (registry/namespace/model/tag path segments are the model inventory), `~/.lmstudio/models`, and the `model` field of `~/Library/Application Support/Jan/data/threads/*/thread.json`. (c) Log probe: `~/.ollama/logs/server*.log` `msg="Listening on"` and the `server config` env map. New table `posture_local_runtimes(source, runtime, model_ref, port, bind_addr, last_request_ts, evidence_kind)` feeding `ai_surfaces` kind=runtime, and rule `local_model_server_exposed` when the bind address is not loopback — real here: every server log records `OLLAMA_HOST:http://0.0.0.0:11434` and `Listening on [::]:11434 (version 0.33.2)`, i.e. an unauthenticated inference endpoint that was reachable from the LAN. Conversation stores are never opened: Jan's thread.json is read for the model id only, `~/.ollama/history` is plaintext and is deliberately not read.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces → 'Local models' card: runtime, port, bind address, models pulled, last observed request, evidence_kind chip saying which of the three probes fired, a red 'exposed' badge on any non-loopback bind, and a permanent 'no tokens recorded — this runtime does not log per-request usage' badge instead of a zero. Drill-down lists model names from the manifest tree, names only.
data_source: `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN`; ~/.ollama/models/manifests/** path segments; ~/.ollama/logs/server-1..5.log; ~/.lmstudio/models; ~/Library/Application Support/Jan/data/threads/*/thread.json.
honest_limit: This machine is the proof that the socket probe alone is worthless: nothing is listening on 11434 right now and the manifests tree is empty (models pruned with the app), yet the server logs show the runtime bound to 0.0.0.0 as recently as 2026-08-30 — so the correct row is evidence_kind=log_line with last_seen from the log, not a live port, and the port evidence must always be stamped 'sampled at <ts>', never read as 'was never used'. lsof without root shows only this user's sockets; a runtime started and stopped between passes is missed; a runtime on a non-default port with an uncatalogued process name is missed entirely. A manifest proves a model was pulled, not that it was ever run. No probe yields tokens: local inference produces no cost row and must render '—', never 0, and never an estimate from model size or duration.
competitive_note: The structural blind spot of every network-shaped competitor: Netskope, Zscaler, Cato/Aim, Palo Alto, Menlo, Island, LiteLLM, Bifrost, Kong, Cloudflare AI Gateway and Tailscale Aperture all sit in a request path that 127.0.0.1:11434 never enters. Harmonic Security lists Ollama coverage but reaches it through an endpoint agent plus full content inspection. Splunk's 2025-12 detection guide reaches the same conclusion from log ports; nobody pairs it with exact per-agent token accounting on the same host.
field_verified: All three probe behaviours confirmed, including the failure mode the feature predicts. `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` runs unprivileged and returns this user's sockets; NOTHING is on 11434. `find ~/.ollama/models/manifests -type f | wc -l` -> 0 (manifests pruned). Log probe is the only one that fires: server logs carry `msg="server config" env="map[... OLLAMA_HOST:http://0.0.0.0:11434 ...]"` and `msg="Listening on [::]:11434 (version 0.33.2)"` dated 2026-08-30. ~/.lmstudio ABSENT; ~/Library/Application Support/Jan ABSENT. NEW, and it breaks the port filter: the only genuinely non-loopback AI-relevant listeners right now are `Python  31440  *:8934 (LISTEN)` (all-interfaces, uncatalogued process name, not in the 11434/1234/1337/4891/8000/8080 set) and `Google  16842  127.0.0.1:9222` — Chrome's CDP port, which is exactly what the observed `Claude_Browser`/`claude-in-chrome` MCP servers drive.
constraint: No principle conflict — the feature already refuses to open ~/.ollama/history and Jan threads beyond the model id, honouring constraint 7. Constraint 5 respected by the permanent 'no tokens recorded' badge. The real problem is design, not policy: filtering lsof to a fixed catalog port list means the one exposed bind on this machine (*:8934) is missed while the headline exposure (11434) is not running. Reconciliation: invert the filter — record every non-loopback listener owned by this user plus every catalog-name match, and let the catalog decide the label, not the visibility. Second: an lsof spawn cannot live in the 5 s poll (same cadence argument as the app census).

name: Ollama activity rows from the runtime's own server log
description: `~/.ollama/logs/server*.log` is a structured logfmt stream (`time= level= source= msg=`) recording model loads and, when `OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS` is true, `[GIN]` request lines. Parse it incrementally with the existing `util/jsonl.ts` byte-offset reader adapted to line-oriented logfmt, and emit `usage_events` rows with `tool='ollama'`, `confidence='activity_only'`, every token field and cost_usd NULL, `model` verbatim from the load line, and `event_key='ollama:<log-file-inode>:<byte-offset>'` so re-reads are idempotent and no poll-time value enters the key. This is the first widening of the `Tool` union to a runtime with no vendor account behind it — usage that generates no invoice anywhere and therefore appears in no vendor console, on any plan.
desktop_surface: Ollama becomes a first-class tool in the existing Breakdown and Timeline with the same 'no tokens' badge Cursor carries today, and a per-model call count inside the AI Surfaces runtime drill-down.
data_source: ~/.ollama/logs/server-1..5.log model-load lines and `[GIN]` request lines; ~/.ollama/models/manifests for the model catalog; collector_state gets its own per-file offset row.
honest_limit: Ollama logs no per-request token counts, so every row is activity_only forever — no cost, no context pressure, no burn-rate or budget rule can ever apply, and the digest must print '—'. Request-level lines exist only when OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS is true, and it is explicitly `false` in every server config block on this machine, so by default the signal is model loads, not conversations: the row count is a floor, never a total. Logs rotate through server-1..server-5 and older activity is simply gone, so the earliest date Vole can claim is the oldest surviving rotation, not first use. verify must be extended to treat ollama as a no-token source, not reconcile it.
competitive_note: ccusage covers 18 agent sources but no local runtime, because there is nothing to bill. No vendor console can show local inference at all — it is the one category where an endpoint-only tool is the sole possible source of truth.
field_verified: PARTLY FALSIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Confirmed: logfmt shape `time=2026-08-30T21:51:01.096-07:00 level=INFO source=routes.go:1951 msg="server config"`; rotation server.log + server-1..5.log; `OLLAMA_DEBUG_LOG_REQUESTS:false` in every config block. FALSIFIED (a): there is no model-load line carrying a model name. The COMPLETE set of distinct `msg=` values across all six logs is: server config / Listening on [::]:11434 / inference compute / discovering available GPUs... / vram-based default context / total blobs: 1534 / total unused blobs removed: 0 / model list cache hydration complete / model recommendations cache sleep scheduled / model recommendations refresh failed / model show cloud cache hydration failed / Ollama cloud disabled: false. Not one names a model, so `model` verbatim from the load line is unobtainable — it stays NULL. FALSIFIED (b) in Vole's favour: `[GIN]` lines DO exist with the debug flag false — 1,303 of them — but only 10 are inference (`POST "/api/generate"`); the other ~1,293 are GET /api/version, /api/status, /api/tags and POST /api/me app polling, and a GIN line carries no model and no tokens. Net honest yield on this machine: 10 activity_only rows, model NULL, over five weeks. ALSO: Vole ALREADY captures Ollama inference with EXACT tokens through OpenCode — `opencode | ollama/hf.co/DavidAU/Qwen3.5-9B-...-GGUF:Q4_K_M | 150 rows | 9,706,745 tokens` and `opencode | ollama/qwen3.8:27b | 18 rows`.
constraint: Constraint 4 (Tool union): types.ts lines 2-9 pin exactly 7 tools; adding 'ollama' touches types.ts, Theme.swift Labels.order (hard-coded 7 tools), the Breakdown ordering, DATA-SOURCES/README, and constraint 20 (verify must be extended for any new source — here as a declared no-token source, which verify.ts:473's NULL-check already models). Constraint 1 (idempotency): `ollama:<inode>:<byte-offset>` is compliant and survives log rotation because rotation renames the file and the inode follows the content — but util/jsonl.ts keys collector_state by PATH, so the offset row must key on inode or every rotation re-reads server.log from 0.

name: execution_contexts: where the work actually ran, and the count Vole could not read
description: One table enumerating every execution context this machine has evidence of, built from five local reads and zero network calls: VS Code/Cursor `User/workspaceStorage/*/workspace.json` (76 entries here, each a single `folder` URI), `User/globalStorage/storage.json` keys `profileAssociations.workspaces`, `backupWorkspaces.folders` and `windowsState`, Cursor's `User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` `ItemTable['history.recentlyOpenedPathsList']`, plus `~/.ssh/config` Host aliases (4 here: b300, fuchsia-lark, air, h200), `~/.docker/config.json` + `~/.docker/contexts/meta`, container-runtime install evidence (docker/colima/limactl/podman/orbctl on PATH, Docker.app/OrbStack.app, `~/Library/Application Support/OrbStack`), and `~/.vscode-server`/`~/.cursor-server` (this machine acting as somebody else's remote host). The URI scheme is the whole discriminator and needs no parsing beyond a prefix match: `file:` is local, `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<host>` / `dev-container+<hex>` / `attached-container+<hex>` / `wsl+<distro>` / `codespaces+<name>` name the context in the URI itself. Adds `execution_contexts(context_id, kind{local|devcontainer|docker|ssh_remote|wsl|codespace|ci|remote_host_role}, label, evidence_path, evidence_kind, first_seen, last_seen, monitored, source)` — `monitored` is 1 only when Vole rows exist carrying that context_id, never inferred — and one derived figure, `contexts_unmonitored`, that must render beside every per-person total. Scanned on the discovery cadence (scan_state), never in the 5-second poll.
desktop_surface: A new Topology card on the Coverage strip: 'N execution contexts seen, M unmonitored'. On the People view every per-person figure gains a subscript reading 'k of this person's n recent workspaces were remote or containerised; Vole read none of them' — and where k is 0 it says '0 of n, measured' rather than staying silent. Drill-down lists each context with its kind, label, evidence path and last_seen, and a per-row 'not monitored' chip that links to COVERAGE-TOPOLOGY.md. Requires the DB.swift read-model port for parity.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor}/User/workspaceStorage/*/workspace.json (`folder`); .../User/globalStorage/storage.json (`profileAssociations.workspaces`, `backupWorkspaces.folders`, `windowsState.lastActiveWindow.folder`); .../User/globalStorage/state.vscdb ItemTable['history.recentlyOpenedPathsList'] (read-only, same pattern as cursor.ts); ~/.ssh/config Host/HostName; ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.docker/contexts/meta/*/meta.json; ~/.vscode-server, ~/.cursor-server; PATH + /Applications probe for docker|colima|limactl|podman|orbctl|tart
honest_limit: A workspace URI proves an editor window, not an agent run — Vole cannot know whether Claude Code or Codex was ever launched in that remote workspace, and it never estimates its tokens. An SSH Host alias proves configuration, not use. A user who never opens VS Code or Cursor contributes zero workspace evidence, so `contexts_unmonitored` can be an undercount and must be labelled as a floor, not a total. Editor storage is per-profile; a second profile is a separate file that must be enumerated or declared unread.
competitive_note: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian (2026-09-01) ships a per-endpoint shadow-agent inventory, but a devcontainer without its own sensor is exactly as dark for Falcon as for Vole and Falcon publishes no such gap number. Cursor's server-side OTel export (cursor.com/docs/enterprise/opentelemetry-export) genuinely does capture Cursor sessions run inside containers — a real competitor advantage Vole must concede in this card rather than paper over.
v1_ref: Coverage and denominators: what Vole did not read
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: ai_extensions census: three readers, because extensions.json is the smallest one
description: The brief's collector reads <root>/extensions/extensions.json and would miss the single most-deployed AI extension on earth. Verified here: GitHub Copilot Chat 0.64.1 lives at /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/package.json as a BUILT-IN and appears in no extensions.json anywhere, yet it has a populated globalStorage and 227 chat turns on disk. So ai_extensions is a UNION of three readers per editor root: (1) <root>/extensions/extensions.json for identifier.id, version, metadata.installedTimestamp, metadata.source, metadata.publisherId, publisherDisplayName, isPreReleaseVersion, pinned, updated, private, targetPlatform; (2) <App>/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/*/package.json for the bundled set, stamped is_builtin=1; (3) <App>/Contents/Resources/app/product.json for the EDITOR's own version, commit, quality, extensionsGallery.serviceUrl (which gallery this fork actually points at), defaultChatAgent.chatExtensionId, copilotVersions.{runtime,sdk} and trustedExtensionAuthAccess (the extensions allowed to silently reuse your GitHub session — github.copilot-chat is on that list here). Rows keyed (root, extension_id, version); editor rows keyed (root, '_editor'). Rules: sideloaded_ai_extension when metadata.source != 'gallery'; unsanctioned_ai_extension against the admin allowlist; known_vulnerable_editor_version against the shipped offline floor, which is what Cursor DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548/9) and MCPoison (CVE-2025-54136) key on — an extension table alone can never fire those. Each row feeds ai_surfaces with an evidence-ladder label of 'installed' until a usage reader lifts it.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen gains an Extensions band grouped by editor root, each root headed by its own version/commit/quality chip and its gallery host; a built-in badge distinguishes bundled from installed; Posture screen gets one row per fork showing editor version against the advisory floor.
data_source: ~/.vscode/extensions/extensions.json (9 rows here), ~/.antigravity-ide/extensions/extensions.json (7 rows), ~/.cursor/extensions/extensions.json and ~/.kiro/extensions/extensions.json (both empty arrays); /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/*/package.json (81 built-ins incl. copilot 0.64.1) and .../app/product.json (version 1.136.1, commit a44adf7f53e0, quality stable)
honest_limit: extensions.json is the installer's record, not proof the extension ever ran; every row starts at 'installed, never observed running' until feature 4 or 7 supplies evidence. Built-ins have no installedTimestamp and no source, so sideload and unsanctioned rules cannot be evaluated on them — those columns are NULL, not 'gallery'. A fork whose .app was moved or is on an external volume yields the user root only, and is_builtin coverage renders as unread rather than zero. An empty extensions.json (Cursor, Kiro here) is indistinguishable from a fork whose extensions live under a profile, so the root is recorded as present-but-empty, never as 'no AI'.
competitive_note: market.md lists 'blind to extension compromises' as an explicit Vole handicap. Snyk agent-scan discovers Cursor/Windsurf/Kiro/Antigravity CONFIGS but not extension versions; Fleet/osquery inventories agents with 'depth undocumented'; JetBrains Console sees in-IDE agents but excludes BYOK. No vendor in the 62-row matrix reads the editor's own product.json to version the IDE itself, which is the only way the two Cursor CVEs are observable.
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Ghost AI extensions: assistants that are gone from disk but not from the editor's memory
description: Uninstalling an extension removes its directory and its extensions.json row; it does not remove the workbench state it contributed. Keys of the shape workbench.view.extension.<viewContainerId>.state.hidden, memento/webviewView.<id>, memento/<viewId> and chatStatusDashboard.contributedCollapsed.<id> persist in global state indefinitely. Verified on this machine: augment-chat, augment-panel, blackbox, blackbox-terminal, blackboxai-dev-ActivityBar and continue all have live keys, and NONE of Augment Code, BlackBox AI or Continue is installed in any editor root today, appears in any extensions.json, or appears anywhere in the sync extension history. Three AI assistants used on this laptop that every other reader in this proposal misses. ghost_ai_extensions rows are keyed (root, view_container_id) with first_seen and last_seen derived from the earliest and latest dated globalState backup containing the key, and a resolved extension_id from a shipped, versioned view-container-id map (a content pack, so it re-scores under content_rev without duplicating incidents). Rule ai_extension_removed_after_use fires when a mapped id is an unsanctioned AI surface with no current install — the shape of 'IT found it and the developer uninstalled it', which is the exact evidence a leaver investigation needs.
desktop_surface: A Ghosts band on the Shadow AI screen, visually distinct from installed rows, each entry showing the view-container id verbatim beside the resolved product name or an explicit 'unmapped container' chip, and the two backup timestamps that bound its existence.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/globalState/*.json (11 dated files here, 115-130 keys each) and ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb ItemTable; same key shapes in each fork's own globalStorage/state.vscdb
honest_limit: A view-container id is not an extension id. Resolution comes from a shipped offline map and an unmapped id renders as 'unmapped container: <id>' — never guessed, never keyword-matched into a vendor name. The key proves a container was contributed, i.e. the extension activated at least once, but proves nothing about whether a prompt was sent or a token spent. The keys carry no timestamps of their own: dates come entirely from which dated backup they appear in, so first_seen is 'not after' and last_seen is 'not before', and with sync off there is one undated observation and the interval collapses to a single point. State from a different machine can roam in via Settings Sync, so a ghost row carries syncData.machineId and is labelled 'this device' only when the machineId matches the one this root has been observed writing.
competitive_note: That feature finds deleted .app bundles; this finds deleted IDE extensions, a population no bundle-id or process scan can reach. Nothing in the 62-vendor matrix looks at persisted workbench state — EDR (Jamf Protect, SentinelOne, Santa) is process-level and sees nothing once the extension host has exited; Fleet/osquery inventories what is installed now.
v1_ref: Ghost-app detector: AI tools that ran here and were then deleted
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Contribution-point classifier: what makes an extension an AI surface, with no name list
description: An allowlist of known AI publishers is obsolete the day it ships. VS Code makes extensions DECLARE their AI surface in package.json contributes, and that declaration is vendor-neutral, machine-readable and already on disk. Read each extension dir's package.json and record, per extension: contributes.languageModelChatProviders (this extension registers a MODEL ROUTE into the editor's chat), contributes.chatParticipants / chatAgents, contributes.languageModelTools and languageModelToolSets (the tools the model gets handed), contributes.mcpServerDefinitionProviders (this extension registers MCP servers programmatically, so they appear in NO mcp config file the existing sweep reads), contributes.chatSessions / chatSkills / chatPromptFiles, capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.supported, extensionKind (a value of ['workspace'] means it executes in the REMOTE host — devcontainer or SSH — outside this machine's monitoring), and len(enabledApiProposals). Verified catches on this machine that no keyword list produces: MermaidChart.vscode-mermaid-chart, a DIAGRAM extension, contributes chatParticipants + languageModelTools; ms-python.vscode-pylance contributes mcpServerDefinitionProviders + chatSkills; Ollama.ollama contributes languageModelChatProviders. ai_extension_capabilities rows join to ai_surfaces so surface_kind is derived from the declaration, and to the MCP registration sweep so a provider-declared server stops looking like a missing config.
desktop_surface: Each Extensions-band row carries capability pills (model-route, chat, tools, mcp-provider, remote-host, untrusted-ok/limited/no); a Shadow AI filter 'declares a model route' lists every extension that can inject a model into chat regardless of publisher; Posture screen flags extensionKind=workspace rows as 'executes off this device'.
data_source: <root>/extensions/<id>-<version>/package.json and <App>/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/*/package.json — fields contributes.{languageModelChatProviders, chatParticipants, chatAgents, languageModelTools, languageModelToolSets, mcpServerDefinitionProviders, chatSessions, chatSkills, chatPromptFiles}, capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.supported, extensionKind, enabledApiProposals
honest_limit: A contribution point is a declaration of intent, not proof of runtime registration, and it only catches PROVIDERS. An extension that merely CONSUMES the API — calls vscode.lm.selectChatModels and ships your buffer to a model — needs no contribution point whatsoever and is invisible to this reader. Partial mitigation within existing rules: a bounded byte scan of the extension's declared main bundle for the literals 'vscode.lm.', 'selectChatModels', 'registerChatModelProvider' and known provider hosts, reusing the dlp_scan_state cursor and byte budget, storing only a match COUNT and the file's sha256 — never a byte of content (measured: mermaid-chart's out/extension.js, 5.4MB, returns 17 hits; Ollama's out/*.js return 0, because its provider path is declarative). Extensions over the byte budget are recorded as scan_skipped with their size, never as clean. A minified bundle can obfuscate these literals, so a zero count is 'not found', never 'does not call the model'.
competitive_note: Every discovery vendor in the matrix works from a curated tool list — Snyk agent-scan names 10 agents, Fleet names 5, Nudge/Obsidian/Reco see SaaS only. A contribution-point classifier is the only mechanism in this market that finds an AI surface inside an extension nobody has ever profiled, which is exactly the population market.md calls 'blind to extension compromises'.
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Model routes chosen inside the sanctioned editor
description: The most interesting model a developer uses is often selected inside an approved IDE, from a picker, and appears in no console anywhere. The editor records every one. From the Settings Sync global-state blob: chatModelRecentlyUsed, chatModelPinned, chatModelVisibility, chatModelPickerPreferences, chat.currentLanguageModel.{panel,editor,terminal,editing-session} (plus the .<agent> and .isDefault variants), and chat.modelConfiguration.panel whose value is a per-model map of reasoningEffort and contextSize. From <App Support>/<Editor>/User/chatLanguageModels.json (present for VS Code and Kiro here): vendor and per-model settings. Verified values on this machine: chatModelRecentlyUsed contains ollama-models/hf.co/DavidAU/Qwen3.5-9B-The-Defiant-Fable-Uncensored-Heretic-NEO-IMATRIX-MAX-MTP-GGUF:Q4_K_M and a second uncensored Qwen build, alongside copilot/kimi-k2.7-code and copilot/claude-sonnet-5 — an uncensored local model and a non-Western frontier model, both selected inside the corporate-sanctioned editor. ide_model_routes rows are keyed (root, provider_prefix, model_id, surface) with an event_key of sha256 over the observed value, so re-reading an unchanged value is idempotent and a changed value appends. The provider prefix ('copilot/', 'ollama-models/') resolves through the existing model-route and cloud-provider-class machinery, and the ollama-models prefix joins straight to the local runtime census: the extension that registered that provider is the languageModelChatProviders declarer from feature 3, so the chain from picker entry to extension to local daemon is complete and evidenced at every hop.
desktop_surface: A Models row on the Shadow AI screen listing every model id ever selected in an IDE, grouped by provider prefix, each with the surface it was selected on, its account class, and a warning chip where the prefix resolves to a local runtime or a provider with no sanctioned surface; drill-down names the extension that registered the provider.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/globalState/lastSyncglobalState.json — storage['chatModelRecentlyUsed'], ['chatModelPinned'], ['chatModelVisibility'], ['chat.modelConfiguration.panel'], ['chat.currentLanguageModel.*']; ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/chatLanguageModels.json and .../profiles/builtin/agents/chatLanguageModels.json; ~/Library/Application Support/Kiro/User/chatLanguageModels.json
honest_limit: A model id in a recently-used list proves selection, not that a request was sent, and carries no timestamp, no count and no repository — the only usage figures for these ids come from feature 4's languageModelStats, and the two lists do not fully overlap, so a selected model with no counter renders as 'selected, usage unread' rather than as zero. The list is capped and rolls over, so it is a recent window whose depth the editor decides, never a complete history; the dated globalState backups bound when an id first appeared but not when it was last used. Provider prefixes are the editor's own naming and a private or self-hosted provider can name itself anything, so an unrecognised prefix resolves to an explicit unknown bucket and is never mapped to a vendor by string similarity. And this reads the picker, not the wire: nothing here proves what host the request reached.
competitive_note: market.md's third white-space point is that no vendor names local or non-mainstream model routes at runtime, and the Anthropic/OpenAI/Copilot/Cursor consoles are each blind to models they do not serve. An uncensored local Qwen selected inside VS Code reaches no console at all: Copilot's metrics count only Copilot models, Ollama has no console, and the gateway vendors (LiteLLM, Portkey, Cloudflare) see only what was routed through them.
v1_ref: Rerouted-model detector straight from the model column, with CCR hex decode
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: browser_extensions: the reach ledger read from Secure Preferences, not the Extensions folder
description: Enumerate Chromium roots (~/Library/Application Support/{Google/Chrome,Chromium,Microsoft Edge,BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser,Arc,Comet,Dia,Vivaldi}), take the profile list from `Local State` -> profile.info_cache keys (only `Default` here), and read each profile's `Secure Preferences` -> extensions.settings.<id>: the cached manifest.{name,version,permissions,host_permissions,content_scripts}, `location` (int enum: 1 INTERNAL, 4 UNPACKED, 5 COMPONENT, 7/9 policy, 10 EXTERNAL_COMPONENT), `path`, `from_webstore`, `was_installed_by_default`, `disable_reasons`, and the three that actually matter — `active_permissions`, `granted_permissions`, `withholding_permissions`. This corrects the brief twice. First, the on-disk manifest is the DECLARED reach only; the granted reach lives in Secure Preferences (AdGuard here: explicit_host `<all_urls>`, withholding_permissions false — full reach actually granted), so the schema carries `declared_reach` and `granted_reach` as separate columns and never conflates them. Second, a folder walk of Extensions/<id>/<ver>/ misses component extensions entirely: Chrome's own `Gemini in Chrome` (id admccjkmockfdflocgggjfgdacdodkdf, location 5, path /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/Frameworks/Google Chrome Framework.framework/Versions/151.0.7922.170/Resources/glic_extension, API permission `glicPrivate`) has no directory under Default/Extensions, so a folder-only census reports zero AI extensions on this machine while Secure Preferences names the browser vendor's own assistant. Fall through to Extensions/<id>/<ver>/manifest.json plus _locales/<default_locale>/messages.json only when the cached manifest is absent — three of six real manifests here carry name `__MSG_name__` and need the locale file, while Secure Preferences already holds the resolved string ("AdGuard AdBlocker"). Adds tables browser_profiles and browser_extensions, projected into ai_surfaces as kind='browser_extension'; rule ai_extension_broad_reach fires when an AI-classified extension's GRANTED reach includes <all_urls> (or http://*/* + https://*/* scriptable_host) together with one of cookies|clipboardRead|nativeMessaging|debugger|webRequest|userScripts and withholding_permissions=false; anomaly_key = browser_ext:<profile_hash>:<ext_id>:<granted_reach_hash>, deterministic and free of now(). Classification follows the contribution-point pattern — AI-privileged API surface (glicPrivate, aiLanguageModel, sidePanel+scripting+all-urls, offscreen) plus reach — with an id list only as a versioned content_packs attribute, never the identity.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen gains a Browser band listing profile, extension, install source (webstore / MDM policy / sideloaded-unpacked / component) and a granted-reach chip; the drill-down shows declared vs granted permission lists side by side with the withheld rows greyed.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/<Chromium root>/Local State (profile.info_cache); <root>/<Profile>/Secure Preferences (extensions.settings.<id>.{manifest,location,path,from_webstore,was_installed_by_default,disable_reasons,active_permissions,granted_permissions,withholding_permissions,first_install_time,last_update_time}); fallback <Profile>/Extensions/<id>/<ver>/manifest.json + _locales/<default_locale>/messages.json
honest_limit: Reach is authority, not exercise — this row can never say the extension ran on a page. Secure Preferences is Chrome's HMAC-protected store; Vole reads it, never validates the MAC and never writes it, and Chrome flushes lazily (schedule_to_flush_to_disk), so state can lag a running browser by minutes. Firefox's Profiles/*/extensions.json has no granted-vs-withheld split, so those rows carry declared_reach with granted_reach NULL. A profile Vole cannot open (no FDA, another user account) is a counted scan_access denial, never a zero.
competitive_note: LayerX/Akamai and Microsoft Purview get browser signal only by installing their own extension through MDM, and Purview's agent discovery is a domain wildcard list of browser sites; Island replaces the browser outright. None of the 62 vendors inventories the other extensions' granted reach from the profile on disk, and CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian's shadow-agent inventory is process- and agent-shaped.
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: browser_assistant: the browser vendor's own AI, with a real last-invoked date
description: The assistant that ships inside the browser is the AI surface a non-engineer actually uses, and it navigates to no domain and installs no extension folder, so both hostname counts and folder walks miss it. Read Default/Preferences -> `glic` {completed_fre 1, onboarding_status 3, pinned_to_tabstrip true, last_invoked_time "13431163951056639"}, in_product_help.new_badge.{Glic,GlicContextMenu,GlicAppMenuNewBadge}.{show_count,used_count} (Glic used_count 1, GlicContextMenu show_count 10), contextual_cueing.zero_state_suggestions.supported_tools (16 entries here including instacart_mcp, zillow_mcp, dropbox, gmail_bard, google_calendar_2, workspace_tool), ntp.compose_button.shown_count (4221), account_values.sync.{ai_subscription_tier 3, glic_rollout_eligibility true}, and Local State -> glic.launcher_enabled. Chrome timestamps are microseconds since 1601-01-01 UTC, so convert with a fixed 11644473600 s offset into the existing UTC-epoch integer bucketing (13431163951056639 -> 2026-08-14T06:52:31Z). Adds an ai_surfaces row kind='browser_assistant' whose last_used_at is populated rather than NULL, plus an assistant_tools child table holding the offered connector list — the browser twin of the offered-tool-surface ledger. Rule browser_assistant_active fires when onboarding is complete, last_invoked_time falls in the window and the surface is absent from the sanctioned policy; rule browser_assistant_connector_offered fires when supported_tools names a third-party connector (*_mcp, dropbox), i.e. the browser assistant has been handed a SaaS reach nobody sanctioned.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen, Browser band: one row per profile showing the assistant name, a real last-used date instead of the word 'installed', the paid AI tier from ai_subscription_tier, and an expandable list of the connectors it was offered.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences (glic, in_product_help.new_badge.Glic*, contextual_cueing.zero_state_suggestions.supported_tools, ntp.compose_button, account_values.sync.ai_subscription_tier, account_values.sync.glic_rollout_eligibility); ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Local State (glic.launcher_enabled)
honest_limit: last_invoked_time is the last time the assistant panel was opened, not a prompt count — the row prints one date and never a call or token figure. used_count is an in-product-help badge counter that saturates and is not usage. supported_tools is what was OFFERED; Chrome writes no record of which connector actually ran. Edge Copilot and Brave Leo write different pref keys and stay NULL until each is profiled (Brave is installed on this machine with no profile written yet), and this row can never be misread as spend because tokens and cost are structurally NULL.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix reads the browser vendor's own assistant. Purview's browser coverage is a domain wildcard list, which by construction cannot see an assistant that never navigates to a domain; Island and Menlo see it only by being the browser.
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: Browser AI-host visit census (hostname counts only, no extension, no proxy)
description: Opt-in and off by default. Open each Chromium-family `History` SQLite read-only (`file:History?immutable=1`, which succeeds while the browser runs; fall back to copying History and History-wal into ~/.vole/tmp so Vole's write scope stays inside ~/.vole) and run one aggregate over `urls`: hostname, `SUM(visit_count)`, `MAX(last_visit_time)` grouped by host, filtered inside the read loop to a shipped `data/ai-hosts.json` allowlist (chatgpt.com, claude.ai, gemini.google.com, perplexity.ai, poe.com, copilot.microsoft.com, huggingface.co, x.ai, mistral.ai, deepseek.com, together.ai, openrouter.ai). Non-allowlisted rows are discarded before anything is written — no URL path, no query string, no title, ever. Stored as `browser_ai_visits(source, browser, host, day_bucket, url_rows, visit_count)` feeding `ai_surfaces` kind=browser_host. Chrome, Brave and Safari History files all exist on this machine, and none of Vole's seven collectors can see a single row of it.
desktop_surface: AI Surfaces → 'Web AI' strip: one row per host with visit count, last-visit date and a 30-day sparkline, plus a per-browser badge showing which profiles were readable. An explicit 'counts only — Vole reads no URL, title or page content' line rendered from the redaction manifest, not hard-coded. Safari renders as a greyed 'requires Full Disk Access' row, never as zero. The disabled state shows the switch and exactly what turning it on would read.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/<profile>/History and the Brave/Edge/Arc/Chromium equivalents, `urls` table columns url, visit_count, last_visit_time; ~/Library/Safari/History.db behind Full Disk Access.
honest_limit: A visit count is an adoption signal and nothing else: it is not a conversation count, not a volume, and not a leak measurement — a ChatGPT tab left open all day counts once, and what was pasted into it is unknowable from here and must be stated as such. Incognito, guest and private profiles write no row. With `immutable=1` the -wal file is ignored, so counts lag to the last checkpoint while the browser runs. Clearing history erases the evidence with no trace. Safari and un-scanned Chrome profiles report 'unknown coverage', never 0. This is the highest-sensitivity read in the product and must stay opt-in, allowlisted and count-only or it fails the works-council test that is the rest of the wedge.
competitive_note: Closes the handicap market.md names explicitly ('blind to non-CLI shadow AI: web chat'). This is the one category the browser vendors genuinely own — Purview DSPM, LayerX/Akamai, Island and Menlo read live browser content and can DLP it, and Netskope/Zscaler get it from inline inspection; both routes see content and need a deployment Vole cannot match. The honest positioning is complementarity: free hostname-level adoption numbers from a file the browser already wrote, with the coverage map saying outright that content inspection needs one of them.
field_verified: Read mechanics and yield both confirmed live. Chrome Default/History = 125,698,048 bytes; Brave Default/History = 294,912; Chromium Default/History = 163,840; `ls ~/Library/Safari/` -> 'Operation not permitted' (the Full Disk Access claim is exact). `sqlite3 "file:.../Chrome/Default/History?immutable=1" "select count(*) from urls"` -> 24,909, succeeding while Chrome is running, exit 0. Real AI yield: claude.ai/new 549 visits, claude.ai/new#settings/general 149, chatgpt.com/ 142, gemini.google.com/app 110, claude.ai/new#settings/usage 91; 727 url rows / 3,395 visits across claude.ai + chatgpt.com + huggingface.co alone. CORRECTION: Chrome's sidecar here is `History-journal` (0 bytes), not `History-wal` — the copy fallback names the wrong file and the '-wal is ignored under immutable=1' caveat must be re-worded for rollback-journal mode. Also note `urls.url` carries path AND fragment (`claude.ai/new#settings/usage`), so host extraction must happen inside the read loop before any write, as specified.
constraint: Constraint 8 (third-party stores opened read-only) satisfied by immutable=1; constraint 8's second half (Vole writes only under ~/.vole) satisfied by the ~/.vole/tmp copy fallback. Principle 5 / constraint 17 (keep it local) is satisfied — no network — but this is the highest-sensitivity read in the product and the works-council argument the rest of the wedge depends on.
