Reconciliation is exactly what the feature states and must be non-negotiable: off by default, allowlist applied inside the read loop, counts only, no URL/title/path/query ever written, and the disabled state must show precisely what enabling would read. One addition: the allowlist must be rendered from the shipped data/ai-hosts.json in the UI, so the user can audit what is matched rather than trusting a claim.

name: Repo-only agents: Aider's footprint and Continue's repo-side dev_data
description: Two agents are structurally invisible to a home-rooted collector: Aider writes nothing under $HOME at all, only .aider.chat.history.md, .aider.input.history, .aider.model.metadata.json and .aider.tags.cache.v*/ in the repo root plus an optional --llm-history-file, and Continue's per-project dev_data JSONL sits at <root>/.continue/dev_data even where the covered BYOK collector reads ~/.continue/config.yaml. The sweep turns those footprints into ai_surfaces rows with discovery='repo_artifact', and for Continue emits surface_activity from a per-file line-count watermark over dev_data event names only (tokensGenerated, chatInteraction, toolUsage, autocomplete) with no bodies read. Principal is attributed as weakly as the evidence allows: the file's owner uid plus the principal on the root's last agent activity, tagged binding_evidence='weak_by_root_colocation', never the session principal. This extends the BYOK collector work rather than repeating it — it supplies the repo-side path that collector cannot reach, and adds the agent that has no home path to reach.
desktop_surface: New rows on the Shadow AI screen carrying a 'found in repo' badge and the root path instead of a home path, with the evidence-ladder card showing 'footprint only, no telemetry' for Aider; the Repos band shows a per-root agent chip.
data_source: <root>/.aider.chat.history.md, .aider.input.history, .aider.model.metadata.json, .aider.tags.cache.v*/ ; <root>/.continue/dev_data/*.jsonl event-name field and line count; <root>/.continue/config.yaml key names and data-destination host only
honest_limit: Both tools are invisible in any root Vole never discovered, so this is a lower bound on a lower bound. Aider records tokens only through opt-in analytics, so every token field and cost_usd stay NULL at confidence activity_only. Zero Aider and zero repo-side Continue artifacts exist anywhere under this $HOME to depth 4, so the shipped figure is honestly '0 found across 58 known roots' and the feature's value is the denominator, not the count.
competitive_note: ccusage covers 18 agent sources and still misses Aider precisely because it has no home artifact. Cyberhaven and Harmonic map process to provider, so an Aider run appears as 'python' with a provider-dependent endpoint; Snyk Agent Scan discovers configs for the named IDE agents only.
v1_ref: BYOK agent collectors: Goose, Amp and Continue
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: VS Code chat request rows: fixing the 'Copilot collector' into an editor chat-store collector
description: Measured on this machine: 173 chatSessions files, 213 MB, 163 requests, 163 unique responseId with zero collisions, 690,680 completionTokens that Vole stores none of. Four corrections to the v1 entry. (a) It walks workspaceStorage/*/chatSessions only; globalStorage/emptyWindowChatSessions/*.jsonl is a second store — 20 files here — holding chats opened with no folder, the rows least likely to carry a project and most likely to be personal use. (b) It is not a Copilot store: modelId is vendor-prefixed and one request here reads 'ollama-models/hf.co/DavidAU/Qwen3.5-9B-...-Uncensored-Heretic-...', so labelling the source 'copilot' invents a vendor; split modelId on the first '/' into provider and model and set tool='vscode_chat'. (c) Key on responseId, verified unique, not requestId. (d) The file is an append-only patch log (kind:0 snapshot, kind:1 set at path k, kind:2 append at path k), so byte offsets in collector_state work exactly as claude-code.ts does — re-reading 213 MB every 5 s does not. Fields taken: responseId, requestId, timestamp, modelId, completionTokens, elapsedMs, timeSpentWaiting, result.timings.{firstProgress,totalElapsed}, agent.{extensionId,extensionVersion,id}, modeInfo, isSystemInitiated (25 here), terminalExecutionId (25 here), editedFileEvents[].
desktop_surface: The People-view rows for every employee who never opens a terminal. The request card shows a real duration (two kinds: totalElapsed and timeSpentWaiting) and an 'agent's own turn' badge for isSystemInitiated. Overview must print an 'output-only rows: N' counter beside every token figure.
data_source: <editor root>/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/chatSessions/<sessionId>.jsonl and <editor root>/User/globalStorage/emptyWindowChatSessions/<id>.jsonl
honest_limit: The store has no input or cache count at all, so rows are confidence='exact' with output_tokens set and input_tokens, cache_*, total_tokens and cost_usd all NULL. TOKEN_FILTER (total_tokens IS NOT NULL) already excludes them from token aggregates, which is correct but silently drops 690,680 real tokens unless the output-only counter is shown. Cost from this source is impossible, forever. completionTokens is the last value set on a patched path, so an interrupted request keeps whatever it had. A chat the user deleted leaves no file.
competitive_note: Market implication 7 assumes VS Code/Kiro/Cline are 'activity-only with a no-tokens badge'; measured here that is wrong for VS Code, and v1 inherited half the error by treating the store as Copilot's. JetBrains Console reports in-IDE credits but excludes BYOK, so the ollama-routed request in this very store is invisible to the one console that would otherwise cover it.
v1_ref: GitHub Copilot collector (VS Code agent mode exact output tokens; CLI activity_only)
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: Cline / Roo / Kilo task collector: one exact row per task from the vendor's own running totals
description: Read state/taskHistory.json under each root x profile x extension-id (saoudrizwan.claude-dev, rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline, kilocode.kilo-code): per task {id, ts, task, tokensIn, tokensOut, cacheWrites, cacheReads, totalCost, size, workspace}. Emit one usage_events row per task, event_key 'cline:<extensionId>:<taskId>' — no line index, no mtime — because those totals only ever grow while a task runs, which is precisely what the monotone upsert at db.ts:87-101 already implements: each poll rewrites the row when total_tokens strictly grows and is a no-op otherwise. That also survives Cline's context-condense, which rewrites api_conversation_history.json and would renumber any index-based key. tasks/<id>/api_conversation_history.json supplies provider and model when the history entry lacks them; task_metadata.json files_in_context[] feeds the file ledger. totalCost is the extension's figure and is stamped cost_basis='vendor_local', never summed into the Anthropic-list-rate total.
desktop_surface: These rows are what People view is missing for the non-terminal employee: surface='extension' with the editor root and profile beside the model. The Costs screen shows them in a separate vendor-figure column with its own subtotal, so a mixed total can never be printed as one number.
data_source: <editor root>/User/[profiles/<id>/]globalStorage/{saoudrizwan.claude-dev,rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline,kilocode.kilo-code}/{state/taskHistory.json, tasks/<id>/{api_conversation_history.json,task_metadata.json,ui_messages.json}}
honest_limit: Not installed on this machine, so the key names come from the vendors' trackers rather than from disk here — the collector must probe and, when the usage keys are absent, emit activity_only with the extension version stamped and every token field NULL, never deriving tokens from message counts. These schemas change per extension version. A BYOK task whose provider block is missing gets model NULL, not a guess. The workspace field is the extension's record of the folder, which may no longer exist.
competitive_note: Cyberhaven's matrix is the only one that names Cline, and only as content passing an endpoint DLP sensor; JetBrains Console explicitly excludes BYOK and provider-account agents, which is exactly what Cline is. No vendor reads Cline's own totalCost, so nobody can show spend for the agent that has no console at all.
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: ai_dependencies: the installed SDK tree, not the declared manifest
description: Under already-consented repo roots, read both the declaration and the resolution and store them as separate bindings: package.json dependencies, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod and Cargo.toml for 'declared'; node_modules/.package-lock.json (packages{} -> version), **/site-packages/*.dist-info directory names, ~/.local/pipx/venvs/*/lib/python*/site-packages/*.dist-info, uv.lock and poetry.lock for 'installed'. Names are matched against a shipped, versioned model-SDK dictionary (openai, anthropic, @anthropic-ai/sdk, @ai-sdk/*, @google/genai, google-genai, langchain*, litellm, ollama, boto3+bedrock-runtime) so the dictionary version is recorded on every row and a dictionary bump is a re-scan, not a silent reinterpretation. Adds ai_dependencies(repo, manifest_path, package, version, binding IN ('declared','installed'), dict_version, first_seen, last_seen, source) and feeds the resolved version into the shipped offline advisory floor table, so an SDK below a CVE floor raises exactly as an agent does. Rows are inventory only: they never produce a usage_events row, and token and cost columns do not exist on this table. On this machine @google/genai is declared in three package.json files but resolves to 2.17.0 in one repo and 2.0.1 in another, and the pipx venv resolves litellm 1.93.0, openai 2.46.0, google_genai 2.16.0 and boto3 1.43.53 - none of which any Vole collector sees.
desktop_surface: Shadow AI screen gains a 'No-log AI' section; inside it a 'Code that calls a model directly' table lists repo, package, installed version (declared version struck through when they differ), first seen and an advisory-floor chip. Row expands to the manifest paths with byte-offset path receipts. The cost column is a structural em dash.
data_source: package.json / requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / go.mod / Cargo.toml; node_modules/.package-lock.json; **/site-packages/*.dist-info; ~/.local/pipx/venvs/*; uv.lock / poetry.lock
honest_limit: A dependency is not a call. It cannot know whether the code ever ran, which key it used, or how many tokens it spent; a vendored copy, a venv-less script or an inline `uv run --with openai` leaves no manifest and stays invisible; roots outside the consented list are never walked and the coverage denominator must say which roots were skipped.
competitive_note: Snyk Agent Scan and Lasso discover agent and MCP *configs*, not SDK dependencies; Fleet/osquery ships generic npm and python package tables with no AI dictionary and no provider binding; Bifrost's own matrix row admits anything not pointed at its gateway is shadow AI.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: launchd-declared log tail: surface_activity for daemons that were never instrumented
description: Parse ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist and /Library/Launch{Agents,Daemons}/*.plist with the plist reader (never launchctl load), and for any job whose ProgramArguments[0] resolves inside an ai_dependencies repo or venv, enrol it in ai_surfaces as surface_class='homegrown', binding_evidence='launchd', carrying RunAtLoad, KeepAlive and StartInterval. Then read the log the job's own operator declared in StandardOutPath / StandardErrorPath, tailed with a byte-offset cursor in scan_state, counting only windows that match a shipped versioned endpoint pattern pack (POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1beta/models/*:generateContent, model=<id>). Adds surface_activity(surface_id, day_utc, pattern_id, pack_version, status_class, count, first_seen, last_seen, source), upserted only when count strictly grows and reset - not double-counted - when the file shrinks under the cursor. No line is ever stored, and no row here becomes a usage_event: tokens and cost stay NULL because the log carries neither. On this machine the three homegrown jobs are all RunAtLoad+KeepAlive, and the litellm job's declared log holds 9 POST /v1/messages lines (2x 200, 7x 400) and 1,769 process restarts that reach nothing today.
desktop_surface: 'No-log AI' section, 'Always-on AI services' card per launchd job: label, program path, run-at-load and keep-alive chips, restart count, and a per-day sparkline of matched request lines split by status class, captioned 'requests observed, tokens unknown'. Clicking a day opens the pattern that matched and the log path receipt.
data_source: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist and /Library/Launch{Agents,Daemons}/*.plist (Label, ProgramArguments, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, StandardOutPath, StandardErrorPath); the file those two keys name
honest_limit: The counter counts log lines that match a pattern, never billed API calls: the operator can point StandardOutPath at /dev/null, rotate on their own schedule, or run the same service under nohup or tmux with no plist at all. A matched line proves the daemon logged a request shape, not that a provider charged for it, so tokens and cost remain NULL forever. Enrolment is only as good as the dependency scan - a job whose program lives outside a known AI repo is never tailed.
competitive_note: The v1 handshake assumed the shadow surface cooperates and registers itself; launchd already holds a registration the operator wrote for their own reasons. Gateways (LiteLLM, Portkey, Bifrost, Helicone) see only what is pointed at them and this machine's gateway is itself unmonitored; CrowdStrike's shadow-agent inventory needs the Falcon sensor at ES level, and no vendor reads a launchd job's own declared stdout path.
v1_ref: Agent registration handshake for SDK apps, CI runners and custom agents
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: First-seen AI surface rule (new_ai_surface)
description: A zero-configuration rule over the ai_surfaces table in the shape detect/*.ts already uses: the first time a surface_key is stored, fire an info anomaly keyed 'surface_first_seen:' + surface_key. The key contains no now(), so the INSERT OR IGNORE at db.ts:137 makes it fire exactly once per surface for the life of the store. observed = 1, threshold = 0, baseline NULL, and the detail quotes the evidence path (the residue file, bundle id or process name that produced the surface row). Firing is suppressed for surfaces discovered during the very first scan, and that suppression is printed on the incident list rather than hidden.
desktop_surface: Incident feed row 'New AI surface: Windsurf (residue) first seen 2026-09-07' with the evidence path; the AI Surfaces grid marks the row with a 'new' dot until acknowledged.
data_source: ai_surfaces rows (surface_key, kind, evidence path, first_seen) produced by the shadow-AI scanners; db.ts insertAnomalies.
honest_limit: A surface that existed before Vole was installed cannot be distinguished from one installed today, which is why first-scan discoveries are suppressed and the suppression disclosed. The rule proves an artifact exists on disk, never that the tool was used, and never that it was used with company data.
competitive_note: v1 has no first-seen rule over surfaces at all: its posture_snapshots diff is a manual 'vole posture diff --since=7d', not an incident. Snyk agent-scan discovers configs one-shot from a CLI with no first-seen memory; Island claims agent/MCP/Bash discovery with an undocumented mechanism.
field_verified: ai_surfaces DOES NOT EXIST. `sqlite3 ~/.vole/vole.db .tables` -> `anomalies  collector_state  usage_events` (three tables, nothing else); no grep hit for ai_surfaces anywhere in packages/core/src. The insert path IS as claimed: db.ts INSERT_ANOMALY reads `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO anomalies (anomaly_key, rule, severity, ...)`. Ollama's bundle id `com.electron.ollama` is real (market-extracts local_artifacts_by_tool, tool 'Ollama', process_or_bundle_id: 'ollama; GUI com.electron.ollama').
constraint: C6 (seed/live never mix): ai_surfaces is a NEW table and the description gives it no `source` column, so `pnpm seed` demo data would fire fake shadow-AI incidents and `purgeSeed` (DELETE WHERE source='seed') would not clean them. Reconcile: source column + the same partition/purge as usage_events. Second: the first-scan suppression needs a durable 'first scan completed' marker and no such row exists -- collector_state is keyed by source_path with 634 claude_code rows and nothing else. Reconcile: one tiny meta row, not now(), so C3 holds.

name: Sanctioned-vs-detected policy join and unsanctioned_surface_first_seen
description: The buyer-facing layer over the registry: join every `ai_surfaces` row against an allowlist in `~/.vole/policy.json` (merged under the admin-owned `/Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json`, following the pricing.json override pattern) to resolve a Sanctioned / Unsanctioned / Undeclared chip, and fire `unsanctioned_surface_first_seen` the first day a surface appears that policy does not declare. Each card states detected (yes/no/artifact-only), sanctioned (yes/no/undeclared), first seen, last seen, sessions, whether tokens are exact or activity-only, and which literal local artifact proved it. The screen's honesty rule is structural: 'not detected' renders grey, never green, and 'undeclared' is a distinct third state from 'unsanctioned' so an incomplete policy never masquerades as an approval.
desktop_surface: Agents & Shadow AI card grid ordered detected-unsanctioned first; card drill-down shows the artifact path with Reveal in Finder, the per-pass heartbeat sparkline from collector_runs, and the sessions list filtered to that surface. Incident feed gains one row per newly detected unsanctioned surface.
data_source: ai_surfaces joined to policy.json allowlist; collector_runs / CollectorResult.notes+filesScanned (collect.ts:36-60) for the heartbeat half; DISTINCT tool FROM usage_events for the observed half.
honest_limit: Sanctioning is only as complete as the policy file: with no allowlist every surface is 'undeclared' and the screen must say so rather than defaulting anything to unsanctioned. Vole sees only agents that leave parseable local artifacts — web chat, ChatGPT desktop, Copilot cloud, Codex cloud and Claude managed agents are invisible, and a tool installed but never run leaves nothing. Cursor and Antigravity have zero rows on this machine, which is 'no artifacts found', not 'never used', and the card must render it that way.
competitive_note: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian shipped shadow-agent inventory on 2026-09-01 and Zscaler reports orgs 'still lack a basic inventory of active AI models', but no vendor names OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime; only Snyk's free agent-scan reads their configs, with no console, no policy join and no history.
v1_ref: Policy-as-code file with local enforcement, drift report and vole_policy check
field_verified: Both policy files verified ABSENT — `ls ~/.vole/policy.json` and `ls '/Library/Application Support/Vole'` both fail (no such file/directory); ~/.vole contains only vole.db, vole.db-shm, vole.db-wal. So the merge layer is entirely net-new, and roadmap-v1 L126 already specifies exactly it: '~/.vole/policy.json merged under an admin-owned /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json (pricing.json override pattern)' — and the pricing.json override pattern is real (pricing.ts:15 `import builtin from './data/pricing.json'`, pricing.ts:43 readFileSync of the override). The honest-limit example is verified: live tool counts are claude_code 16,487 / opencode 10,885 / grok 1,758 / devin 204 / codex 83 — Cursor and Antigravity have ZERO rows, so 'no artifacts found' is the correct render. collect.ts:36-60 CollectorResult.notes+filesScanned exists as the heartbeat source.
constraint: Not a constraint breach but a broken promise in the desktop_surface: the drill-down promises a 'per-pass heartbeat sparkline from collector_runs', and code-map bug 4 establishes that only claude-code.ts:111 ever calls setState — collector_state is written by ONE of seven collectors, so six of seven surfaces would render a blank sparkline that reads as 'not running'. Either fix the heartbeat first or render 'no heartbeat recorded for this collector', never an empty chart. Dependencies: gated on feature 1 (the registry it joins) and on v1 L126 (the policy file it reads), so it cannot ship first. Constraint 5: with no allowlist every surface must render 'undeclared' — the three-state chip and the grey-not-green rule are the correct expression of principle 1 and must be structural, not styling.

name: Provider key-name census and the provider_key_without_sanctioned_surface rule
description: Four name-only reads that never carry a value past the match window: (i) ~/.zshrc, .zshenv, .zprofile, .bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile, ~/.config/fish/config.fish, .envrc and repo .env* - store the variable NAME, the file and a line ordinal for *_API_KEY, *_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_BASE_URL, AZURE_OPENAI_*, GEMINI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_HOST; (ii) launchctl getenv <name> over the same dictionary, recording set/unset and a length only; (iii) security dump-keychain with no -w ever, keeping only the svce and acct blob labels; (iv) any value actually encountered goes solely through the existing DLP fingerprint path, whose provider-classing detector is what binds a key name to a provider. Adds provider_keys(name, holder IN ('rc','envrc','dotenv','launchd_env','keychain'), path_or_service, provider, first_seen, last_seen, source) and the rule provider_key_without_sanctioned_surface, which fires when a provider key is held here and no enrolled agent authenticates to that provider: observed = holder count, baseline = enrolled surfaces for that provider, threshold = 1, key = (provider, holder, path_hash) with no clock component. On this machine the rc files hold nothing - the finding is that the keys live elsewhere: the keychain carries svce com.local.gemini-gateway-for-claude with acct litellm-claude plus acct anthropic and acct openai, and six repo .env files carry GEMINI_API_KEY.
desktop_surface: 'No-log AI' section, 'Provider keys held here' table: provider, key name, holder, first seen, and a chip reading 'an enrolled agent uses this provider' or 'no enrolled surface'. Rows open a path receipt naming the file and byte offset read; there is no value column to hide, because the column does not exist.
data_source: shell rc and env files; .envrc; repo .env*; launchctl getenv; security dump-keychain svce/acct labels
honest_limit: Possession is not use, and this rule fires on possession: it cannot count a call, price one, or prove the key is still valid. security dump-keychain returns only unlocked keychains and may prompt, so an absent row is not an absent key; keys held in a password manager, a cloud secret store or only in a teammate's shell are invisible, as is a variable exported into a running process that no file on disk mentions.
competitive_note: Buyer need #1 names raw API keys and BYOK-in-IDE as the hole every vendor console admits it cannot see; Anthropic's own Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry auth paths, Entra Agent ID sees only IdP-authenticated agents, and JetBrains Console excludes BYOK and provider accounts entirely.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: Console and gateway coverage ledger — what nobody else can see
description: Turn the market wedge into a number the buyer computes on their own laptop. Ship data/console_coverage.json: for each vendor console and gateway shape, the exclusions the vendor itself documents — Anthropic's Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex and personal accounts; Codex governance covers ChatGPT-workspace accounts only; Cursor's OTel export has no per-session tool attribution and no subagent roll-up; Copilot metrics lag about two days and are credits, not tokens — each with the doc URL and the date it was read. Cross-join it with local rows (tool × account_class × provider host) into a new coverage_gap view over existing columns and print a ledger of calls, sessions, exact tokens and list value per cell, with the 'visible to no console you own' cell first. No new collection is required.
desktop_surface: A new top-level Dashboard screen 'Coverage' showing a two-axis matrix (rows = tool, columns = visible to vendor console / gateway / neither), each cell carrying calls and exact tokens, with a footnote per column citing the vendor doc URL and the date it was read, and an Export button that writes the same table into the assessment report.
data_source: usage_events (tool, session_id, tokens, cost_usd, account_class) joined to a shipped data/console_coverage.json; provider host from provider config snapshots where present.
honest_limit: This is a claim about what a vendor's documentation said on a given date, not an observation of the customer's actual console or gateway configuration, so every column is labelled 'as documented <date>' and an admin can override it. It cannot see rows on laptops that never ran Vole, so the 'neither' cell is a floor and never a total. Where account_class is unproven the row lands in an explicit fourth cell rather than being assigned to a side, and a vendor shipping new coverage silently makes the ledger stale until the JSON is updated.
competitive_note: This is the artefact market.md's GTM section names as the wedge — 'coverage report = agents Vole sees minus agents the gateway sees' — and it exists in no roadmap-v1 tier. It is the only sales asset that gets stronger every time a competitor publishes more docs, and it reframes the conversation from 'replace your DLP', which Vole loses against Cyberhaven, Zscaler and CrowdStrike distribution, to 'measure what your DLP cannot reach', which none of them can answer without installing something on the laptop.
field_verified: The join key does not exist. `account_class` is not a column in schema.ts and not in the live DB (three tables, 25 usage_events columns, none named account_class); 'provider host from provider config snapshots' has no table either. What is real is the left side of the cross-join: usage_events has tool, session_id, tokens and cost_usd populated across five tools here (claude_code 16,599, opencode 10,885, grok 1,758, devin 204, codex 83), so a tool x coverage matrix is computable today and a tool x account_class one is not. data/console_coverage.json does not exist. The vendor exclusions themselves come from market.md and are external citations I could not verify without network — which is exactly why the 'as documented <date>' labelling in the honest_limit is load-bearing.
constraint: Constraint 14: data/console_coverage.json is a shipped data file, so like data/pricing.json it must be inlined by esbuild at build time, and the 'admin can override it' path needs the same explicit runtime-read carve-out pricing.ts has — otherwise the SEA either cannot read it or gains a forbidden runtime read. Constraint 5/principle 1: the 'neither' cell is a floor, not a total, and where account_class is unproven the row must land in the explicit fourth cell rather than being assigned — the description already commits to this, and it is the difference between a defensible ledger and a sales number.

name: console_invisible auth-path tag (Bedrock, Vertex, base-URL, router)
description: Claude Code under Bedrock or Vertex is excluded from both the Analytics API and the Compliance API, and a base-URL override or a local router removes the traffic from Anthropic's billing relationship entirely — all three are detectable on disk with no network. Classify each session's `auth_path` from the settings-layer `env.{ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX}` and `apiKeyHelper`, from Codex `session_meta.payload.model_provider` and `turn_context`, from OpenCode `providerID`, and from model-id shape. Every session so classified carries a `console_invisible` tag that flows into the coverage report and, crucially, SUPPRESSES false `vendor_only` gaps rather than raising them — the reconciliation consequence, not just the detection.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation coverage strip: 'K% of observed value used an auth path no vendor console reports (router: 461 calls, Bedrock: 0, base-URL override: 0)'; the same tag appears as a chip on affected sessions in the session list.
data_source: ~/.claude/settings.json and settings.local.json `env`/`apiKeyHelper`; ~/.claude-code-router/{config.sqlite, gateway-proxy-preload.cjs, global-profile-takeover.json} (all present here); usage_events.model values `anthropic/claude-ccr-*`, `glm-5.2`, `qwen3.8-27b-fp8`; ~/.codex/sessions `session_meta.payload.model_provider`.
honest_limit: A settings file records intent at read time, not what a process actually used: an environment variable exported in a shell leaves no trace on disk, so the classification is a lower bound and must be labelled configuration evidence. Vole reads no network traffic and cannot prove where a request went — it can only show that the local configuration and the model string are inconsistent with the vendor's own naming. Today's settings snapshot must never be stamped onto historical rows (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is absent live here but present in two ccr backups).
competitive_note: v1 T3 detects the routing; turning the vendor's own exclusion into a measured percentage that is excluded from the gap arithmetic rather than alerted as shadow spend is new. market.md notes the Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and personal accounts; no vendor turns that exclusion into a number.
v1_ref: Model-route integrity and allowlist (model_provider_rerouted, model_switch, model_not_allowed)
field_verified: The snapshot-vs-history claim is verified in both directions. Live ~/.claude/settings.json has NO `env` block at all — its keys are permissions, enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, effortLevel, remoteControlAtStartup, agentPushNotifEnabled, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt — so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is absent today. It IS present in the backup: settings.json.ccr-backup-2026-08-23T19-37-59-762Z contains `"env": {"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:3456", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-ccr-...", "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b-fp8", ...}` — exactly the 'present in two ccr backups' claim. ~/.claude-code-router/{config.sqlite, gateway-proxy-preload.cjs, global-profile-takeover.json} all present. Codex `session_meta.payload.model_provider` is real (code-map §3.2 lists it among Codex's ignored fields), but ~/.codex/config.toml has no model_providers table, so the config leg is empty here. Router class count: 461 ccr-shaped rows, matching the feature's figure exactly.
constraint: Constraint 5 is breached by the desktop copy, and it is the one thing to fix: 'router: 461 calls, Bedrock: 0, base-URL override: 0' renders 0 for two classes that were never observable — a shell-exported ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL leaves no disk trace, so the honest render is '—' or 'not observed', never 0. Constraint 7: reading env.* out of the ccr backups opens a file whose adjacent key is a live bearer token — select key names from an allowlist, retain the value's host only, never the object. Constraint 2: today's settings snapshot must never be stamped onto historical rows, and the upsert would not let you anyway (raw_ref/confidence are not in the SET list) — so the tag must be computed at read time from the settings-layer timeline, not written onto usage_events.

name: Stable machine identity (IOPlatformUUID) and a hostname history
description: usage_events.machine is os.hostname() (db.ts:19-35) — 'Marys-MacBook-Pro.local' on all 29,293 live rows here. That string contains an employee's first name and changes when DHCP or the network changes, so a fleet keyed on it both leaks a name and splits one laptop's history into several. Resolve a stable id once per install into ~/.vole/identity.json — machine_uuid from `ioreg -rd1 -c IOPlatformExpertDevice` IOPlatformUUID (present here), machine_label from `scutil --get ComputerName`, and the hostname observed at that moment — and add `machines(machine_uuid, hostname, label, first_seen, last_seen)` so a rename appends a row instead of forking the history, joined to usage_events.machine at read time.
desktop_surface: Settings → Identity shows 'This Mac' with the truncated stable id, the current hostname and any earlier hostnames as a small history list, plus a note that neither the hostname nor the label ever leaves the machine.
data_source: ioreg IOPlatformExpertDevice → IOPlatformUUID; scutil --get ComputerName ("Shiva's MacBook Pro" here); existing usage_events.machine values.
honest_limit: Requires one child-process spawn from the SEA collector, which is otherwise spawn-free; on Linux and CI there is no IOPlatformUUID and machine_uuid stays NULL with the hostname as the only key. IOPlatformUUID identifies hardware, not a person — a reimaged or reassigned Mac keeps it. Both the hostname and the ComputerName carry the owner's first name here, so the label is a local convenience only and must be excluded from every export.
competitive_note: v1's identity binding says 'populate the unused user/machine columns from os.userInfo/hostname'; Fleet/osquery and every EDR key on a hardware UUID for exactly this reason (fleetdm.com/endpoint-governance).
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: `ioreg -rd1 -c IOPlatformExpertDevice` returns both IOPlatformUUID and IOPlatformSerialNumber — present. `scutil --get ComputerName` = "Shiva’s MacBook Pro", `--get LocalHostName` = Marys-MacBook-Pro, `hostname` = Marys-MacBook-Pro.local — the first-name leak is confirmed in all three. usage_events: a single (user, machine) pair `('shiva','Marys-MacBook-Pro.local')` across all 29,491 live rows. THE FEATURE'S OWN OBJECTION IS FALSE: cli/collect.ts:1 already has `import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'` and line 145 already spawns (`spawn(argv[0]!, argv.slice(1), {stdio:'ignore', detached:true})` for the Linux notifier). The SEA collector is not spawn-free today, so 'requires one child-process spawn from the otherwise spawn-free collector' overstates the cost.
constraint: C14 (SEA: node: builtins only, no native modules) — child_process is a builtin and is already bundled, so no conflict. C16 (Hardened Runtime + allow-jit) — spawning a system binary needs no additional entitlement. C5 — machine_uuid NULL on Linux/CI with hostname as the only key is the correct NULL-not-zero handling.

name: Seat inventory and seat-value reconciliation from vendor-observed plan fields
description: A per-principal, per-tool inventory of the plan actually observed — Claude `organizationType:'claude_max'` with `organizationRateLimitTier:'default_claude_max_20x'`, `billingType:'stripe_subscription'`, `seatTier`; Codex `chatgpt_plan_type:'team'`; Grok subscription_tier — rendered against a plain `seats_purchased` block in the policy file, producing three named buckets: seats paid for with no usage observed, usage observed on a plan the company never bought (shadow spend), and matches. The same card carries the second half of the seat question: the list-equivalent value Vole computed for that principal against the seat price declared in `~/.vole/units.json`, because Vole must not ship Anthropic's price list — 'Claude Max 20x seat · $1,778.48 list value consumed in 30d · declared seat price $X/mo', with an em dash for the ratio until a price is declared. The ratio is labelled 'list value over declared seat price on a rate-limited plan', never 'savings', and the observed weekly-limit percent is printed beside it as the constraint that bounds the claim.
desktop_surface: A 'Seats' card in the People view listing each tool with observed plan, purchased seats and the three buckets, and a Reconciliation header card with one row per detected plan showing consumed list value, declared seat price, the labelled ratio and the current weekly-limit percent; drill-down opens Breakdown filtered to that tool and principal.
data_source: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{organizationType, organizationRateLimitTier, billingType, seatTier, userRateLimitTier} (all present here); ~/.codex/auth.json id_token chatgpt_plan_type; usage_events cost_usd WHERE cost_basis='anthropic_list'; ~/.vole/policy/identity.json seats_purchased and ~/.vole/units.json seat price.
honest_limit: Absence of usage is not proof a seat is unused — it may mean Vole was never installed on that person's Mac, which is why the bucket is labelled 'no usage observed by Vole', never 'unused'. The plan string is what the client was told at runtime, not the billing record. List-equivalent value is what the same tokens would have cost on the metered API; it is not money anyone paid and must never be summed into a spend total, and only Claude Code rows carry that basis, so the 2,678 unpriced Claude calls and every OpenCode provider-reported row are excluded from the numerator with the exclusion count shown. A Max plan's ceiling is set by quota rather than budget, so the ratio inverts the moment the weekly limit binds. Persist only organizationType/rateLimitTier/billingType/seatTier — never emailAddress, fullName or organizationName from the same object.
competitive_note: v1 hand-enters the plan into plans.json; this reads plan, tier and billing type from fields the vendor itself writes to disk and binds the ratio to the observed weekly-limit percent so the number cannot be quoted out of context. market.md's FinOps need is reconciliation against vendor usage APIs to find shadow spend; JetBrains Console excludes BYOK and provider-account agents and Windsurf/Devin report credits, so no console can produce the shadow-plan bucket.
v1_ref: Contract rate cards, rate_source labelling and seat-price comparison
field_verified: Three of five named Claude fields present, two null. ~/.claude.json oauthAccount: `organizationType 'claude_max'` ✓, `organizationRateLimitTier 'default_claude_max_20x'` ✓, `billingType 'stripe_subscription'` ✓, **`seatTier`: null**, **`userRateLimitTier`: null** — so 'all present here' is not accurate; two of the five render as em dashes. Codex `chatgpt_plan_type: 'team'` verified in the id_token auth claim ✓. The numerator verifies but needs a caveat: claude_code priced rows total **$1,798.52** (feature says $1,778.48 — drift as the DB grew), and the 2,678 excluded unpriced Claude Code calls are **0% Anthropic-named models** (all qwen/glm/ccr-router/synthetic), so the exclusion is not 'calls we could not price' but 'calls that were never Anthropic traffic'. The binding constraint the ratio must be printed beside is live: weekly_scoped 61% on 'Fable', is_active true.
constraint: Principle 5 / constraint 7 (the DB holds no content, and the code map + v1:146 both require persisting only organizationType/rateLimitTier/billingType/seatTier, never emailAddress, fullName or organizationName) — the feature states this correctly, and it matters because all three forbidden fields sit in the same oauthAccount object I just read. Principle 1: 'list value over declared seat price' is a ratio of a computed number to a typed-in number; labelling it as such and printing the weekly-limit percent beside it is the right guard, and 'savings' must never appear. Constraint 18: list-equivalent value is not money anyone paid and must never sum into a spend total.

name: Email and name never stored: domain plus HMAC, enforced by verify --identity
description: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount carries emailAddress, fullName and displayName in cleartext, and they are the most tempting fields in the product. The rule: store HMAC-SHA256(lowercased email) under a per-install key kept in ~/.vole/identity.json (mode 0600) plus the bare domain string, and nothing else — no local part, no name, in any column, export or incident detail. 'pnpm verify --identity' scans every identity column and every export row for an '@'-shaped token or a value matching the local oauthAccount name fields and fails the run on a hit; the redaction manifest gains the matching 'read but never stored' entries.
desktop_surface: Settings → Privacy lists identity fields read beside identity fields stored — 'emailAddress → domain only, address hashed; fullName → read, never stored' — with the last verify --identity result and date beneath.
data_source: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{emailAddress, fullName, displayName}; the new identity columns; sync/manifest.ts; packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts.
honest_limit: A domain alone cannot separate an employee from a contractor, or from a personal account on a custom domain. The HMAC is reversible by anyone holding both the key and a candidate address, so it is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation, and must be described that way to a works council.
competitive_note: v1 says 'never store emailAddress/fullName/tokens' as a warning line with nothing enforcing it and no stated storage form for the address. market.md §2 puts 'proof no prompt text is stored, pseudonymous per-employee rows' at the top of the DPO list; Kolide's Privacy Center is the precedent for showing the manifest rather than asserting it.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: All three fields are in cleartext on this machine right now: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount keys include emailAddress (value begins 'shivaa'), fullName ('Shiva ...'), displayName ('Shiva...'), alongside organizationName and accountUuid, plus top-level userID and machineID. The enforcement target exists but is not callable: packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts has `const db = openDb()` at module scope (:146), `await sleep(7_000)` at :315 (top-level await), and ends `process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1)` -- so `verify --identity` needs the same refactor-to-a-function that #25 and #27 need. sync/manifest.ts does not exist (the whole packages/core/src/sync/ directory is absent; roadmap-v1 L43 proposes it).
constraint: None violated; it reinforces C7 (the DB holds no content). The dependency chain is the real issue: three separate features (#6, #25, #27) each require verify.ts to become importable, so that refactor should be sequenced once and first rather than three times.

name: Privacy Center with live export-payload inspector
description: A sidebar section under Manage rendering four columns generated from the running build rather than from prose. Read: each of the 11 paths in paths.ts resolved against this home with existence, last-scanned time and the env override in force. Stored: every column of usage_events, anomalies, collector_state and any new table, each with its non-NULL rate and one real example value from the viewer's own database via PRAGMA table_info. Never stored: a named list — ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.emailAddress (which really is on this disk), ~/.codex/auth.json, history.jsonl pastedContents, OpenCode's account/credential tables, every transcript content block — each with the file it would have come from. Shared: the redaction manifest, the sink list, and the literal serialized bytes of the ten most recent rows in whichever sink format is selected (OTLP JSON, HEC event, Elastic bulk line, RFC 5424 frame) produced by the exporter's own --dry-run encoder with no sink configured and no network call, beside a column listing the store columns that were dropped and why (dropped by registry / NULL omitted / transformed to HMAC).
desktop_surface: New 'Privacy' section with a lock icon beside Settings, four tabs; the Shared tab carries the sink selector, the rendered payload in a monospaced scroll view with a Copy action, and the dropped-columns list; the same content is available as `vole privacy --json` and as an MCP resource.
data_source: paths.ts accessors; schema.ts DDL plus PRAGMA table_info against the viewer's own ~/.vole/vole.db; collector_state.last_scanned_at; sync/manifest.ts; packages/core/src/export/fields.ts and sinks/*.
honest_limit: 'Never stored' is a claim about Vole's code, backed by `verify --content` over the actual DB — it says nothing about the vendor logs on the same disk, which hold full prompts and, per a self-audit of 59 Claude Code transcripts, live credentials, so the panel must link that out rather than imply the machine is clean. The payload view shows the ten rows this machine happens to have, which is not a proof about every row shape a fleet produces (a project path or branch name on another host may reveal more), and it shows only what the exporter sends, never what the receiving pipeline stores or logs afterwards.
competitive_note: Direct lift of Kolide's Privacy Center, the one precedent in the research for surviving employee scrutiny, extended past v1's panel (which covers only the fourth column and only once sync exists). None of the 62 vendors surveyed lets a buyer see the exact outbound payload from the product UI before purchase, and none of the 27 covering coding agents states its prompt-retention posture per-field on the endpoint.
v1_ref: 'What leaves this machine' panel, vole transparency and the notice-acknowledgement gate
field_verified: Three of four columns verified buildable today; the fourth is not. paths.ts has EXACTLY 11 accessors (db, pricingOverride, claudeCodeProjects, codexSessions, cursorTrackingDb, antigravityConversations, antigravityBrain, opencodeDb, grokUnifiedLog, grokSessionsDir, devinAcpMessages) — the '11 paths' claim is exact, though 2 of them are Vole's own files rather than sources, so the Read column is 9 sources + 2 own. The 'never stored' list is verified against this disk: ~/.claude.json `oauthAccount` really exists and its keys are `['accountUuid','emailAddress','organizationUuid','hasExtraUsageEnabled','billingType',...,'seatTier','organizationRole','organizationName',...]` with emailAddress populated; ~/.codex/auth.json exists (4029 bytes, mode 600). ABSENT: `packages/core/src/export/fields.ts`, `sinks/*` and `sync/manifest.ts` do not exist anywhere in git ls-files, and `grep -rn -- '--content' packages/core/src apps README.md docs` returns NOTHING — the `verify --content` flag the honest_limit leans on has not been built.
constraint: No break, but one under-stated risk. Constraint 7 permits the store to hold cwd paths and project slugs, and the Stored column proposes 'one real example value per column from the viewer's own database' — which means the Privacy Center itself displays the most revealing thing the DB holds (a repo path, a branch name). That is honest and probably correct, but the feature frames it as a fleet-generalisation caveat rather than a here-and-now display decision; give the viewer a redact toggle on that column. Principle 7 is served well: the panel is the natural place to disclose UpdateChecker.swift:27's GET to api.github.com, which README.md:22 and SECURITY.md:13 currently contradict.

name: Deployment mode resolver: personal vs managed
description: One function resolves the install's posture from the presence and completeness of /Library/Managed Preferences/com.launchsafe.vole.plist (only an MDM-installed configuration profile writes there) into install(mode, org_label, profile_hash, resolved_at), and every product default reads it. Personal mode: identity columns NULL, no notices, no audit log, no purpose binding, every content-reading scanner on, retention unlimited, all per-person views available, MCP unrestricted. Managed mode inverts each of those and is the only mode in which identity attribution, per-person views, the access-audit log, purpose binding and pseudonymisation-at-sync activate. `vole privacy --explain` prints the two columns side by side so a developer can see exactly what a company profile would change on their machine, and a conformance test asserts the personal default set enables every collector, rule and view, so enterprise controls can never quietly degrade the free product.
desktop_surface: A small pill beside the range selector in MenuPanel and in the DashboardView title bar reading 'Personal' or 'Managed · <org_label>', opening a new Privacy section; Settings gains a read-only Deployment row showing the declared mode and profile hash.
data_source: /Library/Managed Preferences/com.launchsafe.vole.plist (MDM-only write path); UserDefaults domain com.launchsafe.vole (existing vole.theme/menubar/refresh/loginItem/range/section keys); packages/core/src/paths.ts for the config location
honest_limit: A local admin can hand-write a plist in /Library/Managed Preferences and macOS offers no API to prove a profile was MDM-delivered rather than placed by root, so the UI says 'declared', never 'attested'. A developer on a company laptop stays in personal mode until a profile actually arrives — Vole cannot tell whose laptop it is. The mode changes defaults only; it must never change how a number is computed, or the same rows would mean different things in two modes.
competitive_note: v1 splits editions for licensing (Tier 5 packages/enterprise, ELv2) but never for privacy posture, so there is no artifact that tells a developer what a managed profile changed. Kolide's Privacy Center is the precedent for showing the employee exactly that; Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic ship one posture only — the surveilling one — with no documented developer-owned mode, which is the wedge market.md identifies for works-council and DPO review.
v1_ref: packages/enterprise (ELv2) edge-gated in the same binary, vole licence CLI and entitlement surfacing
field_verified: Domain CONFIRMED: apps/mac/Info.plist:8 `<key>CFBundleIdentifier</key> <string>com.launchsafe.vole</string>`, so com.launchsafe.vole.plist is the correct name. UserDefaults keys CONFIRMED in use (DashboardView.swift settingsPane binds $theme, $launchAtLogin, $menubar, $refreshSeconds; MenuPanel.swift:@AppStorage("vole.menubar")). PATH DEFECT FOUND: the feature names only /Library/Managed Preferences/com.launchsafe.vole.plist, but on this machine the real MDM payloads sit one level down in /Library/Managed Preferences/shiva/ (complete.plist, com.apple.applicationaccess.plist) — the top level holds only the shiva/ directory. A resolver probing the named path alone would report 'personal' on exactly the enrolled configuration this device demonstrates. Also unverified: paths.ts is cited 'for the config location' but exposes only db() and pricingOverride() under ~/.vole — there is no config path today.
constraint: Constraint 6 and 13 both apply to the proposed install(mode, org_label, profile_hash, resolved_at) table — and both are avoidable: nothing needs persisting, so resolve the plist on read in both TS and Swift and delete the table. Constraint 5 (never invent a number) is what the feature's own rule protects — 'the mode changes defaults only; it must never change how a number is computed' — and that rule is correct and must be kept as written, because a mode that altered computation would make identical rows mean different things on two machines.

name: Principal resolution chain and the v_events_principal read-time join
description: Resolve who a row belongs to in a fixed precedence — managed preference (/Library/Managed Preferences, which exists on this Mac) > $VOLE_USER > ~/.vole/identity.json > os.userInfo().username — and record principal_source alongside, so a report can say 'MDM-asserted' rather than 'OS username, unverified'. Because the upsert can never rewrite usage_events.user (db.ts:87-101 excludes it from the SET list), the resolution is a read-time join and not a backfill: a `principals(user, machine_uuid, principal_id, principal_source, valid_from, valid_to)` table plus a `v_events_principal` view that every new per-person query selects from. usage_events.user keeps its original meaning — the origin stamped at observation — while the view answers 'whose is this now', so changing identity.json re-resolves all history immediately without touching a stored row.
desktop_surface: Settings → Identity shows the resolved principal and, in plain words, which of the four sources won; a warning row appears when the winning source is the bare OS username.
data_source: usage_events.user ('shiva' on all 29,293 live rows) and .machine; new ~/.vole/identity.json; VOLE_USER env; the MDM managed-preferences domain.
honest_limit: Nothing local can prove a principal: every source in the chain is an assertion by whoever controls the laptop, and MDM raises the bar but a local admin can still set VOLE_USER. The view also cannot split rows collected before a laptop was reassigned unless valid_from/valid_to were recorded at the time.
competitive_note: v1's Fleet view concedes 'the user column is an OS username, not an SSO principal'; this is the local half of that admission made explicit and configurable before sync exists. Entra Agent ID and Okta for AI Agents only see IdP-authenticated agents, which a subscription-auth CLI is not.
v1_ref: Fleet view with SSO and RBAC
field_verified: usage_events confirmed: `user='shiva'` on all 29,491 live rows, never read by any query (queries.ts and DB.swift both confirmed to omit it). db.ts:87-101 confirmed to exclude `user` from the SET list, so the read-time-join argument is exactly right — a backfill is impossible through collection. FACTUAL CORRECTION ON THE TOP RUNG: `/Library/Managed Preferences/shiva/` does exist (com.apple.applicationaccess.plist, complete.plist, both root-owned) — but `profiles status -type enrollment` reports `Enrolled via DEP: No` and `MDM enrollment: No`. The directory is populated by a local configuration profile, not an MDM server, so its presence does not prove an MDM assertion on the very machine the claim was verified against.
constraint: C2 — the read-time join is the correct and only reconciliation with an upsert that can never rewrite `user`; this is the sharpest structural insight in the shard. C13 (read-model parity) — DB.swift must port v_events_principal or the app renders nothing. UNNAMED: C12 has no user_version scheme, and `CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS` in SCHEMA silently preserves a stale definition forever once the view's SQL changes — the view needs an explicit DROP-then-CREATE guarded by a version marker, which C12's column-probing migration does not cover.

name: Egress inventory, network_calls ledger and a VOLE_NO_EGRESS switch every caller honours
description: Vole ships one undisclosed network call today — UpdateChecker.swift:27 GETs api.github.com/repos/launchsafe/vole/releases on every launch from init(), with no opt-out, while README:22, SECURITY.md:13 and the Settings footer all say nothing leaves the machine — and any reconcile or sync adapter would be the second. Add a declared egress inventory generated from the code (host, path, trigger, purpose, payload, on-by-default), an append-only network_calls(ts, feature, host, path, method, status, bytes_in, bytes_out, rows_written) table written by every call Vole makes, and one hard switch — VOLE_NO_EGRESS=1, the managed preference, or the policy file — that makes the update check and every adapter refuse to run and say so. The app's own claim text is generated from the inventory rather than hand-written, so it cannot drift again.
desktop_surface: Settings → Network: the generated inventory table (two rows today), a master off switch, and a log of the last N calls with host, status and bytes; the About footer's 'Nothing leaves your machine' line is replaced by the live inventory, or by 'No egress' when the switch is on.
data_source: apps/mac/Sources/Vole/UpdateChecker.swift:20-27; any future reconcile or sync adapter; ~/.vole/policy.json and /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json for the managed override.
honest_limit: The inventory covers calls Vole's own code makes; it says nothing about the agents Vole watches, which talk to model APIs constantly, nor about a corporate proxy intercepting either. network_calls lives in a developer-writable SQLite file and is evidence of intent, not a tamper-proof record.
competitive_note: v1 gates the update check behind a preference and lints for new call sites in CI, but adds no per-call ledger, no runtime kill switch and no generated claim text, so the README can drift again the moment a second caller lands; it also covers outbound sync only, not inbound pulls. Kolide's Privacy Center is the pattern and no AI-security vendor publishes one.
v1_ref: Opt-in update check and CI-enforced self-egress allowlist
field_verified: Exhaustively verified -- a grep for URLSession|dataTask|fetch(|node:http|node:https across apps/mac/Sources and packages/core/src returns EXACTLY ONE call site: UpdateChecker.swift:27 `guard let url = URL(string: "https://api.github.com/repos/launchsafe/vole/releases?per_page=1")` reached from `init() { check() }` at :20, with no preference guard. Zero network calls in packages/core. It is contradicted verbatim by SECURITY.md L13: 'There is no server, no account, no telemetry, and no network call this project makes on its own — that's the thing most worth breaking, if it's ever untrue.' and by DashboardView.swift's Settings footer 'Nothing leaves your machine.' and README L22 'Everything runs locally. No scraping, no cloud APIs'.
constraint: C12 (DB.swift must stay a read-only consumer) is a REAL conflict the feature does not name: the only egress today is made by Swift, so a network_calls row for the update check would be a write from the app, breaking read-only parity. Reconcile one of three ways -- move the update check behind the collector, give network_calls its own store outside vole.db, or document an explicit narrow exception. C17 is the constraint this feature enforces. C6: network_calls needs a source-column decision or an explicit exemption.

name: Your-own-rows inspector
description: A tab inside the Privacy Center showing a paginated table of the literal rows keyed to this subject — usage_events, anomalies and any findings — with every column raw, a filter by tool and date, and 'Copy as JSON' / 'Save as JSON' actions. No aggregation, no chart, no interpretation: the persuasive fact in a works-council meeting is not a policy document but a developer scrolling their own record and finding it is model names, token counts and paths. It doubles as the interactive half of the DSAR export, reading the same rows `vole dsar export` writes.
desktop_surface: Privacy section → 'Your record' tab: a plain Table whose column headers match the schema exactly, a row count, and the date of the oldest row held.
data_source: usage_events and anomalies filtered on the subject's user/machine columns (or all rows in personal mode), read through the existing DB.swift sqlite3 C API port.
honest_limit: It shows what Vole holds now — not what an admin exported yesterday, and not rows already removed by retention or prune. On a shared machine it can only show rows whose origin matches this subject, and rows collected before identity stamping keep NULL user/machine and are shown in a separate 'origin unknown' bucket rather than being attributed by guesswork.
competitive_note: No competitor exposes the monitored employee's own record on the endpoint; Cursor and Copilot expose admin analytics only. This is the concrete form of the Honest Security tenet the research names as the Kolide precedent, and it turns a DSAR from a ticket into a scroll.
v1_ref: Data-subject access and erasure: vole dsar export and vole forget
field_verified: One of the few in this shard that is genuinely buildable today with zero new instrumentation. usage_events (25 columns, schema.ts:6-33) and anomalies (18 columns, :42-62) both exist and are populated; DB.swift's sqlite3 C API port is in place. Identity columns are populated, not NULL — 0 rows with `user IS NULL` across 29,551. `vole dsar export` does not exist (v1 Tier 7 item), so the 'interactive half of the DSAR export' currently has no other half.
constraint: Constraint 13: a paginated raw-row reader must be ported to DB.swift, and 'filter by tool' is a TEXT bind — impossible with DB.swift:141's `[Int]` signature, so this has a hard dependency on feature 1's Bind enum that the spec does not name. Constraint 7 is not a conflict but the point: rendering every stored column raw, raw_ref included, is the PROOF that the store holds no content, which is why 'no aggregation, no interpretation' is the right design.

name: Release gate: privacy machinery ships with the MDM kit, not after fleet sync
description: A structural correction to v1's shipping order rather than a new screen. v1 puts every privacy control in Tier 7 gated on the network line, while the MDM pkg and managed preferences land in Tier 5 — so the published order has companies deploying to employee laptops two tiers before the basis record, the Privacy Center and the per-person-view gate exist. Under GDPR the processing that triggers Art. 88 and BetrVG § 87(1) Nr. 6 happens at collection on the endpoint, not at transmission: ArbG Hamburg 24 BVGa 1/24 found no co-determination precisely because the employer held no usage data. Enforce the ordering mechanically — `bundle.sh --release` and CI fail when the redaction manifest module, the consent/basis gate in cli/collect.ts and the Privacy section are absent from the build — and document the managed-mode prerequisite table in PACKAGING.md.
desktop_surface: No new screen; the gate's effect is that a managed build without those three cannot be produced. Settings' Verification row prints the build's privacy-feature attestation line instead of today's hard-coded 'Every stored row reconciled' string in DashboardView.swift.
data_source: apps/mac/bundle.sh (VERSION default and the ad-hoc vs --release signing path); .github/workflows/ci.yml (today: install, typecheck, test, collect:once on ubuntu; swift build on macos)
honest_limit: This is a gate on Vole's own release pipeline only. Nothing stops an organisation building from source with the checks removed and the licence does not prevent it, so the gate makes the shipped artifact defensible, not the codebase tamper-proof. It also asserts nothing about legal sufficiency: it proves three files are in the build, not that a works council was consulted.
competitive_note: The privacy machinery is the wedge against Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic — all in-path, all content-inspecting, none documenting prompt retention (market.md finding 129). Shipping the MDM kit two tiers before that machinery forfeits the differentiator in exactly the pilots it was built to win, and a DPO reviewing the roadmap can read the tier numbers.
v1_ref: MDM / Jamf deployment: signed .pkg and managed preferences
field_verified: Ordering claim MOSTLY confirmed, with one overstatement. Tier headings verified: 'Tier 5 — Hooks, live control and managed deployment [18]' at roadmap-v1.md:181 containing 'MDM / Jamf deployment: signed .pkg and managed preferences' at :205; 'Tier 7 — Opt-in fleet sync ...' at :251 containing the pseudonymisation, per-person-view gate and 'What leaves this machine' items at :257, :260, :263. BUT the redaction manifest is at :43 — Tier 1, not Tier 7 — so 'v1 puts every privacy control in Tier 7' is false for one of the three artifacts the gate demands. Legal sourcing CONFIRMED verbatim at market.md:50: 'ArbG Hamburg 24 BVGa 1/24 found no co-determination only because the employer had no usage data'. CI CONFIRMED: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs install/typecheck/test/collect:once on ubuntu and `swift build --package-path apps/mac` on macos — no bundle.sh, no pkg. DashboardView.swift:696 `LabeledContent("Verification", value: "Every stored row reconciled")` — hardcoded, CONFIRMED.
constraint: No technical constraint conflict; principle 5 is what it defends. The conflict is with the house style: it names no local artifact it reads, no table, no rule and no view, so it is a shipping-order assertion rather than a feature. Reconciliation: demote it to an ordering constraint on the roadmap plus its one shippable line — replace the hardcoded DashboardView.swift:696 string with a real build attestation. Note also that a CI grep for three file paths proves the files are present, not that they work, which the honest limit concedes.

name: Pseudonymise at insert, not at sync
description: db.ts:19-35 origin() stamps os.userInfo().username and os.hostname() onto every row: all 29,293 live rows here read 'shiva' / 'Marys-MacBook-Pro.local', a person's login and first name. In managed mode replace that stamp with a random 128-bit subject_id generated once and held in the macOS Keychain (never in vole.db) plus a device_id from IOPlatformUUID, so the on-device store is already pseudonymous before anything is exported. This corrects roadmap-v1's 'Identity pseudonymisation modes at sync', where user is HMAC-SHA256'd under an org key: over a domain of a few hundred employee logins that HMAC is brute-forceable by anyone holding the key — which is the relay operator — so it is not a control against the party it is meant to constrain. A one-time `vole identity migrate` UPDATE is required because the upsert's SET list never touches user, machine or project and only fires when total_tokens strictly grows, so existing rows can never be healed by re-collection.
desktop_surface: Privacy section → 'Identity' card: subject_id prefix, device_id, the sentence 'your macOS username is not stored', and a 'Migrate existing rows' button showing the count of rows still carrying cleartext (29,293 today).
data_source: db.ts:19-35 origin() and the ORIGIN spread at db.ts:129 and :154; usage_events.user/machine; anomalies.user/machine; IOKit IOPlatformUUID; macOS Keychain (SecItem).
honest_limit: Pseudonymising identity does not de-identify the rows: usage_events.project is an absolute cwd and the overwhelming majority here begin <redacted-local-path>, raw_ref embeds -Users-shiva, and every collector_state primary key is a path under the user's home — those three channels re-identify the subject on their own and need their own treatment. On a single-user laptop the pseudonym is trivially linkable by anyone who can read the disk.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix documents endpoint-side pseudonymisation; LiteLLM's metadata-only spend logs are the closest pattern and still key on a real user id, while Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic identify by corporate account by design.
v1_ref: Identity pseudonymisation modes at sync (cleartext / HMAC-org-key / aggregate-only k)
field_verified: Every claim confirmed. db.ts:19-33 origin() is `userInfo().username` + `hostname()`, ORIGIN const at :35, spread at :129 (events) and :154 (anomalies). All 29,491 live rows carry 'shiva'/'Marys-MacBook-Pro.local'. The three re-identification channels in the honest_limit are confirmed exactly: 27,520 of 29,491 rows have `project LIKE '<redacted-local-path>%'` (1,962 more are empty), raw_ref samples read `<redacted-local-path>`, and all 632 collector_state primary keys are paths like `<redacted-local-path>`. MISSING COST: I grepped both Swift and TS for Keychain/SecItem — zero hits anywhere in the repo, and the collector is a Node SEA with no Keychain binding; reaching SecItem means either a native module (banned by C14) or shelling to /usr/bin/security.
constraint: C2 is the reason the migration must exist and the feature names it correctly — the SET list never touches user/machine and only fires when total_tokens strictly grows, so re-collection can never heal a stored row. UNNAMED: C12 (no user_version) means a half-completed `vole identity migrate` UPDATE across 29,491 rows is undetectable on the next run; it needs its own completion marker. C14 rules out a native Keychain module, so the Keychain must be reached by spawn — feasible (collect.ts:145 already spawns) but it must be stated.

name: Shipped read manifest and per-scanner switches
description: The newer scanners read outside the seven agent stores — browser history, launchd plists, shell rc files, the whole /Applications tree — and a works council or DPO objects to exactly those. Ship packages/core/src/data/scanners.json (beside the existing pricing.json) listing every scanner with the paths it reads, the fields it extracts, the fields it deliberately does not read and a default enabled state; render it verbatim in the app; and gate each scanner on a boolean in ~/.vole/scanners.json merged under the admin-owned policy file. Browser history and shell-rc scanning ship disabled by default because they read personal, non-work artifacts. A disabled scanner's surfaces render as 'not scanned' in the coverage map, never as absent.
desktop_surface: A 'What Vole reads' screen listing each scanner as a row — name, paths, fields stored, fields never read, and a toggle locked with a lock glyph when the managed policy pins it; every AI Surfaces and Leak Ledger panel names the scanners that contributed to it.
data_source: packages/core/src/data/scanners.json (shipped); ~/.vole/scanners.json and /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json for state, following the pricing.json override precedence.
honest_limit: The manifest is a promise the code must keep, so it is only a control with a test that wraps fs reads and fails the build when a scanner touches a path the manifest does not declare — without that test it is documentation. A managed policy can force a scanner on, which is the point for fleet deployment but must be visible to the employee rather than silent. It says nothing about what other software on the machine reads.
competitive_note: Extends v1's manifest from 'what may leave this machine' to 'what is read on this machine', which is the harder question in a GDPR Art. 88 / BetrVG review. Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic store prompt content by design and cannot make the offer at all.
v1_ref: Redaction manifest and verify --content (prove the DB and exports hold no content)
field_verified: The sibling pattern is real and SEA-safe: `packages/core/src/data/pricing.json` exists and pricing.ts does `import builtin from './data/pricing.json'`, i.e. frozen into the bundle at build time -- scanners.json placed beside it inherits that. (The feature's prose says 'packages/core/src/data/scanners.json' which is the correct dir; note feature #10 gets the same path wrong.) scanners.json itself does not exist. Critically, NONE of the scanners it declares exist: no browser-history, launchd-plist, shell-rc or /Applications reader is present in packages/core/src -- the collectors dir holds exactly the seven agent collectors.
constraint: C14 (zero runtime deps, CJS-bundleable, no dynamic require): the shipped manifest is fine as a compiled import; the ~/.vole/scanners.json state read is a second runtime read that must be declared. Inherits #2's inverted admin precedence. C8 (third-party stores read-only) is what the manifest documents, so they reinforce each other.

name: People view
description: A sidebar section beside Overview and Incidents with one row per principal: tokens, cost, sessions, incident count, per-tool account_class badges, a binding_evidence badge and the bound/ambient/unbound triple. It requires getByPrincipal(range, includeSeed) in queries.ts and a hand-written DB.swift port, since the app opens SQLite through the C API and mirrors only summary, timeseries, anomalies, breakdown and collectorLastSeen today. Row order is fixed by token volume with no ranking language, no percentiles and no per-person deltas over time; clicking a row filters the existing Overview, Incidents and Breakdown panels rather than opening a separate profile screen.
desktop_surface: 'People' item in the Monitor sidebar group; a table of principal rows with badges; selection applies a principal filter to the other sections and shows as a removable chip in the filter bar.
data_source: v_events_principal (a view over usage_events.user/machine, unread by any query today) joined to session_identity and anomalies; queries.ts plus DB.swift port.
honest_limit: On a single-employee laptop this is exactly one row and adds nothing — it is meaningful only once fleet sync exists, and until then it is a self-view that must be labelled as one. Rows collected before identity stamping carry NULL user/machine and appear in a separate 'origin unknown' bucket, never merged into a named principal; and it inherits DB.swift's existing gaps (no zero-fill, limit 100 vs 500) unless the read-model contract lands first.
competitive_note: Cursor's and Copilot's per-user views are cloud consoles gated behind Enterprise; no local-first tool renders per-person attribution at all. market.md §2 warns that a leaderboard is exactly what fails a works council, which is why the ordering carries no rank and the screen ships no deltas.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: Half right, and the honest_limit is wrong on this machine. `v_events_principal` and `session_identity` do not exist. But the underlying columns are not merely present — they are fully populated: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM usage_events WHERE user IS NULL` returns **0**, and `SELECT user, machine, COUNT(*) GROUP BY 1,2` returns a single row `shiva|Marys-MacBook-Pro.local|29551`, because db.ts:129 spreads `...ORIGIN` over every insert. Confirmed unread: grep for `machine` across queries.ts and DB.swift returns zero hits. So a GROUP BY over user/machine works today and returns exactly one honest row.
constraint: No constraint break. market.md line 56 is the governing pressure — 'no performance scoring (GDPR 88, BetrVG, CNIL, Annex III 4(b))' — and the feature's no-rank, no-percentile, no-delta rule is the correct reconciliation, stated explicitly. Minor: neither `user` nor `machine` is indexed (live index list: idx_ue_ts, idx_ue_tool_ts, idx_ue_session, idx_ue_source_ts), fine at 29.6K rows, not at fleet scale. Text filtering on a selected principal needs feature 1's Bind enum.

name: PPPC payload generated from Vole's own signature, and the ad-hoc cdhash trap
description: `codesign -d -r- apps/mac/build/Vole.app` on this repo prints `designated => cdhash H"89b9c3c12129e12d83d9478271c004ebcbe1addc"` with `TeamIdentifier=not set`, because bundle.sh's non-`--release` path ad-hoc signs. A TCC grant is keyed on the bundle identifier **plus** the designated requirement, so under a cdhash DR every rebuild is a different application to TCC: every grant evaporates with no error, no prompt and no log line, and the whole fleet renders zeros. Add `vole pppc` and a Settings button that read the running app's own requirement via `SecCodeCopySelf` → `SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement` → `SecRequirementCopyString` (Security.framework, no dependency; the CLI falls back to spawning `codesign -d -r-` when headless), emit a `.mobileconfig` carrying a `com.apple.TCC.configuration-profile-policy` payload that grants `SystemPolicyAllFiles` to `com.launchsafe.vole` with that exact requirement string, and **refuse to emit** when the DR is cdhash-shaped, printing the reason. Persist `build_identity(cdhash, team_id, dr_string, first_seen, last_seen)` so a later coverage loss has something to point at.
desktop_surface: Settings > Deployment: the generated requirement string in a selectable copy field, a "Save .mobileconfig…" button, and a red inline note on ad-hoc builds — "this build's permission grants die on the next rebuild; ship a Developer ID build before enrolling any device". The docs MDM-kit page links the same generated payload rather than a hand-written example.
data_source: The running bundle's own code signature (SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement); apps/mac/Info.plist CFBundleIdentifier com.launchsafe.vole.
honest_limit: Vole can print the requirement its own binary satisfies; it cannot verify that an MDM delivered the profile, cannot read back which TCC services a profile granted, and cannot detect a profile that was pushed then removed. The payload is correct only for the exact signing identity that generated it — a re-signed, re-notarised or differently-versioned build needs a regenerated profile, which is the point.
competitive_note: market.md §7 cites the CrowdStrike/SimpleMDM recipe — PPPC profile before pkg — as the deployment order every Mac security agent follows; vendors ship a hand-written profile in a docs page. Generating it from the binary's actual designated requirement removes the single most common Jamf failure (a profile whose requirement string no longer matches the shipped build), and it is something a closed-source agent cannot let the admin verify locally.
v1_ref: MDM / Jamf deployment: signed .pkg and managed preferences
gap_area: macOS permission and endpoint reality: TCC/Full Disk Access preflight, PPPC payload, launchd resilience, measured footprint

name: Scoped, logged local MCP server
description: cli/mcp.ts exposes seven unscoped tools with no caller identity, so any agent that can spawn the binary enumerates every session of every tool on the machine — absolute project paths, branch names, session ids, and via vole_session any session id it can guess. For a product whose pitch is that it never stores prompts, that is the exact leak it detects, and on this machine an agent reading that inventory would carry it to whichever model the claude-code-router route points at. Add ~/.vole/mcp-scope.json: project paths default to repo-slug form, vole_session and vole_live_sessions default to the caller's own cwd subtree, and in managed mode results return pseudonyms only, cap row counts and carry a machine-readable privacy_notice field. Every call appends an access_log row (ts, tool, args hash, parent pid, cwd, row_count), and every call that returned subject-level rows also appends an mcp_subject_data_egress info incident with tool, purpose, range and count — because an analyst asking their Claude Code session 'who leaked a secret last week' ships employee monitoring data into a model provider's context: a second processing operation with its own basis, its own retention and, for an EU controller, an international transfer that no DPIA covering Vole would mention. Also fix getSessionDetail (queries.ts:399), which returns seed rows today because it omits the AND source='live' clause every sibling query passes.
desktop_surface: Settings → 'Local MCP access': recent queries by tool, caller cwd and row count, a master off switch and an 'MCP: restricted (managed)' status line beside the existing DB path row, linked from the About footer; Privacy Center → 'Analyst access' lists the calls that returned subject-level rows with tool, time and row count.
data_source: packages/core/src/cli/mcp.ts:19-94 TOOLS array (vole_summary, vole_live_sessions, vole_session, vole_incidents, vole_breakdown, vole_whatif, vole_digest), serverInfo.version hard-coded '0.1.0' at mcp.ts:94; queries.ts:396-400 getSessionDetail.
honest_limit: stdio MCP carries no authenticated caller identity — parent pid and cwd are the strongest evidence available and both are trivially spoofable by the same agent, so the log is a record, not a control. It covers Vole's own MCP server only: an analyst pointing a model at ~/.vole/vole.db directly, or reading the screen and pasting it into a chat, is invisible, and the guard cannot see what the model does with what it received.
