competitive_note: v1's MCP self-hygiene item only lints tool descriptions and reads serverInfo.version from package.json, leaving the query surface unscoped and unlogged. market-extracts calls a read-only local MCP server over Vole's SQLite a differentiator; shipping it unscoped hands that same surface to every agent on the laptop, which is what Agentjacking (CSA, 2026-06-12) abuses, and several vendors are adding MCP query interfaces to their consoles with no equivalent guard.
v1_ref: Self-protecting store and MCP self-hygiene
field_verified: Every claim confirmed. cli/mcp.ts:20-83 is the seven-tool TOOLS array (vole_summary, vole_live_sessions, vole_session, vole_incidents, vole_breakdown, vole_whatif, vole_digest), no auth, no caller identity, no row caps beyond vole_incidents' default 50. Line :94 hard-codes `serverInfo: { name: 'vole', version: '0.1.0' }` while package.json says version 0.1.4 -- a live drift. The bug is exactly as stated: queries.ts:396-400 `getSessionDetail` runs `SELECT * FROM usage_events WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY ts, id` with NO source clause and no tool clause, while every sibling query appends `AND source = 'live'`. And the leak is live on this machine: vole_breakdown by=project returns absolute cwds, 27,661 of 29,632 rows begin <redacted-local-path>, and ~/.claude-code-router exists here so those paths could be routed to a third-party model.
constraint: C6 (seed and live never mix) is currently VIOLATED by getSessionDetail, so fixing it inside this feature is a root-cause fix in the single place all callers route through -- correct. C1: capped row counts must report that they were capped rather than silently truncating.

name: execution_context_id on every row, and the origin quarantine for rows this machine did not produce
description: Today `db.ts:19-35` stamps `os.userInfo().username` and `os.hostname()` on every row at insert, which silently asserts that whoever runs the collector is whoever ran the agent. For a bind-mounted or synced agent home that assertion is false, and the People view presents another machine's work as this employee's. Add a nullable `execution_context_id` column to `usage_events`, `anomalies`, the tool-call ledger and the secret ledger via the existing add-nullable-column migrate() probe, plus a `PRAGMA user_version` stamp so DB.swift and queries.ts agree on the shape. Rows whose evidence resolves to a local root get `local`; rows whose cwd is a foreign root, or whose evidence arrived through the context import path, get that context's id and have `user` and `machine` written as NULL rather than as this machine's values — an explicit quarantine, not a guess. The ORIGIN spread at db.ts:129/154 takes an origin override instead of a constant, and the widening upsert's SET list is extended to allow NULL→value on `execution_context_id` only (never value→different value), so a later, better-evidenced pass can fill it without ever rewriting a bound context. `v_people` and every per-person aggregate group by (principal, execution_context_id) and render an explicit `unknown origin` band.
desktop_surface: People view rows split into 'this machine' and 'other contexts' bands, with the unknown-origin band shown even when empty so its absence is a measurement. Your-own-rows inspector gains an origin column so a subject can see exactly which of their rows Vole claims were produced here. Privacy Center's field dictionary gains execution_context_id with its three states and the rule that user/machine are NULL, never inferred, outside the local context.
data_source: packages/core/src/db.ts origin()/ORIGIN and the insert spreads; schema.ts add-column migration; the foreign-root classifier's verdict and the import path's declared context as the two non-local sources of a context id
honest_limit: A context id is only as good as the evidence that produced it, and there are exactly two kinds of evidence — a foreign root and a declared import — so everything else is `local` by default and that default is itself an assumption stated on the card. Rows collected before the column existed cannot be retro-assigned by upsert (the current SET list never rewrites user/machine, and widening it that far would break the monotone contract), so backfill happens only by re-scanning source files that still exist; rows whose transcript has been deleted stay NULL forever and are counted in the unknown band. This corrects attribution; it does not recover the runs Vole never saw.
competitive_note: Market white-space finding #2 — vendor consoles are identity-fragmented across email, user_login, IAM and credits — understates the problem: every one of them, and Vole's own ORIGIN stamp today, additionally assumes one host per identity. Cursor and Copilot server-side telemetry get this right for free because the vendor observes the request; a local-first collector has to earn it, and this is the column that earns it.
v1_ref: Principal resolution chain and the v_events_principal read-time join
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: session_identity ledger with a binding_evidence rank
description: Adds one append-only table `session_identity(tool, session_id, principal_id, account_id, org_id, account_class, class_evidence, plan, seat_role, surface, binding_evidence, first_seen, last_seen, source)` UNIQUE on (tool, session_id), written by the same collector pass that writes usage_events but through its own insert seam beside db.ts:insertEvents. Identity deliberately does not become columns on usage_events: db.ts:87-101 rewrites a stored row only when excluded.total_tokens is STRICTLY greater and its SET list excludes user/machine/model/session_id, so an identity value set wrong on the first insert could never be corrected. The ON CONFLICT clause is a monotone widening on an explicit evidence rank — session_proved > ambient_snapshot > os_assertion > none — mirroring the token upsert's shape but ordered on evidence, never on time, so an ambient guess is replaced by a later proof and never the reverse. binding_evidence is a second axis and must never be smuggled into `confidence`, which is exactly two values by policy (types.ts:22, enforced at verify.ts:473 and depended on by queries.ts TOKEN_FILTER). The table carries a `source` column and joins the seed/live partition and purgeSeed like every other table.
desktop_surface: Not a screen of its own: it is the join every People row, account chip and identity incident drills into. Wherever a person or account appears, a second visually distinct badge sits beside the existing exact/activity-only confidence badge — session-proved / ambient / origin-only / unbound — never merged into one indicator, with the artifact that decided it on hover. Session rows in the Dashboard incident feed gain the same account badge.
data_source: Fields already in hand inside each collector loop: claude-code.ts line stream (type:'bridge-session' ownerAccountUuid/ownerOrganizationUuid), codex.ts rollout payloads (token_count.rate_limits), grok.ts ctx objects, opencode.ts session rows; table lives in ~/.vole/vole.db beside usage_events.
honest_limit: A session with no identity-bearing line gets account_class NULL and binding_evidence='none' — never a guess — and on this machine that is the majority: 18 Claude transcript files carry a bridge-session line, 12 of 66 Codex rollouts carry plan_type, and OpenCode's account, account_state and control_account tables are all empty (0 rows), so every one of the 10,885 OpenCode rows is unbindable. The four-value scale is ordinal, not probabilistic: 'session_proved' means a field in the vendor's own file said so, which is only as trustworthy as the vendor's writer.
competitive_note: market.md white-space #2: vendor consoles are 'single-tool and identity-fragmented' (email vs user_login vs IAM vs credits) and none joins across tools; no competitor exposes how sure it is that a row belongs to a named employee — Cyberhaven and Harmonic present per-employee attribution as fact because their sensor sits in the user's own process.
field_verified: Confirmed. db.ts:87-101 upsert is exactly as described: `WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens`, SET list omits user/machine/model/session_id/project/git_branch/agent_id/confidence/source. types.ts:22 `export type Confidence = 'exact' | 'activity_only'`. Bridge lines: 575 across 18 files, sample keys `type=bridge-session, sessionId, bridgeSessionId=cse_01DWaemhfjew5NScmZWafmZd, lastSequenceNum, ownerAccountUuid, ownerOrganizationUuid` — exactly 18 distinct sessionId, 1 ownerAccountUuid, 1 org. THREE ARMS FAIL: (a) opencode.db `account_state` = 0 rows (also account 0, control_account 0) so the OpenCode arm writes nothing; (b) Grok's only account-bearing line, `paywall_check_result` {user_id, subscription_tier:'GrokPro'}, occurs 5 times and 0 of 5 carry `sid` — it cannot bind to a session; (c) claude-code.ts:93 is `if (!entry || entry.type !== 'assistant') continue;` so bridge-session is discarded, and it is the only incremental collector — all 632 collector_state rows already hold offsets past every existing byte, so the 575 historical lines will NEVER be re-read by the normal pass.

name: First-run scope gate: real consent in personal mode, declared lawful basis in managed mode
description: A four-step first-launch sheet — (1) every path Vole will read, listed from the paths.ts accessors with a live found/not-found probe beside each; (2) every column it stores, generated from the redaction manifest, beside the never-stored list (prompts, tool arguments, tool output, file contents, credentials); (3) where data goes — local only, sync off, update check off; (4) an explicit agreement — plus a gate in cli/collect.ts before collectAll (collect.ts:29-75) that refuses to run without it. The artifact splits by mode, because consent is not a valid basis for employee monitoring under GDPR Art. 88 and the EDPB employment opinion, so a consent.json signed by the employee becomes evidence against the employer and is unenforceable in a fleet: personal mode writes a real, revocable ~/.vole/basis.json carrying the manifest hash and timestamp; managed mode reads a lawfulBasis dictionary from the configuration profile — {basis, controller, dpia_ref, works_agreement_id, works_agreement_date, jurisdiction, notice_url} — and collection does not start until every key is present, showing 'Collection paused: no lawful basis recorded' rather than collecting silently. If the manifest hash changes in an update the app shows 'scope v2 pending' and re-asks instead of silently widening scope.
desktop_surface: A modal first-run sheet over the dashboard window, replacing today's straight-to-dashboard behaviour in VoleApp.swift:19-26; afterwards the same content is permanently browsable in the Privacy Center as a 'Why this is running' card quoting the controller, the declared basis, the works-agreement id and date with a link to the notice URL; a full-width amber banner across Dashboard and Incidents when the basis is incomplete and collection is paused, or when a scope change is pending acknowledgement.
data_source: paths.ts accessors probed with FileManager; the redaction manifest column list; ~/.vole/basis.json; /Library/Managed Preferences/com.launchsafe.vole.plist key lawfulBasis; the gate in cli/collect.ts before collectAll.
honest_limit: Vole cannot verify that a works agreement or a DPIA exists — it renders strings the profile declares and must label them 'declared by <org>, not verified'. A local consent record is documentation, not a lawful basis: a German works council still needs a §87(1) Nr. 6 agreement and a Dutch WOR Art. 27 decision. A paused collector means no evidence for the paused period, which the coverage report must state as 'not monitored', never as zero usage; and an MDM that pre-seeds the file must be rendered as 'pre-configured by your administrator on <date>' or the wizard is theatre.
competitive_note: v1 names the file consent.json and makes the employee the signer, which is the wrong instrument in an employment context and unenforceable across a fleet. No endpoint AI-security vendor ships a consent wizard, and none exposes the employer's declared legal basis to the monitored employee; ArbG Hamburg 24 BVGa 1/24 found no co-determination only because the employer had no per-employee usage data, so this is the feature that keeps a People screen deployable in the EU.
v1_ref: vole init and first-run wizard with ~/.vole/consent.json
field_verified: The insertion points are real. VoleApp.swift:17-22 holds the first-launch branch (`let key = "vole.hasLaunchedBefore"; let firstLaunch = !UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: key)`) so 'replacing today's straight-to-dashboard behaviour' lands exactly there. cli/collect.ts has `const db = openDb()` at :18 and `runOnce()` opening with `const results = collectAll(db);` -- a gate before collectAll is a three-line insert. `/Library/Managed Preferences/` exists on this machine with a per-user subdirectory, so the MDM plist path is a real structure (com.launchsafe.vole.plist is of course not deployed). ~/.vole/basis.json does not exist. sync/manifest.ts does not exist, so 'every column it stores, generated from the redaction manifest' has no generator.
constraint: C1 (never invent a number) bites hard and the feature only half-sees it: a paused collector writes no rows, and usage_events has no way to distinguish 'paused' from 'no usage'. That makes #13 a hard dependency on #3's coverage screen -- without it, a paused period renders as a true zero, which is inventing a number by omission. C17 reinforced.

name: Account-class classifier from the auth path
description: A pure function mapping observed fields to exactly one of org_oauth | personal_oauth | api_key | cloud_provider | team_seat | unknown, writing account_class plus the literal deciding field and value into session_identity.class_evidence so an incident can quote it. Rules verified here: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{organizationType:'claude_max', billingType:'stripe_subscription', seatTier:null, organizationRole:'admin', organizationRateLimitTier:'default_claude_max_20x'} → personal_oauth (a personal Max subscription, not a company seat); ~/.codex/auth.json auth_mode ('chatgpt', 7 chars) with OPENAI_API_KEY===null → OAuth not raw key; Codex rollout token_count.rate_limits.plan_type 'team' → team_seat and 'free' → personal_oauth; ~/.grok/auth.json's object key `https://auth.x.ai::<client uuid>` with auth_mode 'oidc', principal_type 'User' and a team_id present → org-bound OIDC; OpenCode account_state.active_org_id → org_oauth. Only opaque ids and enum-shaped strings are read: never emailAddress, fullName, displayName, and never organizationName, which is literally 'Shiva' here — a person's first name is what a personal plan puts in the org field, so the org name must never be stored or rendered; store organizationType plus an HMAC of organizationUuid instead.
desktop_surface: New Dashboard section 'Accounts': per tool a stacked bar of calls by account_class over the range with an explicit 'unproven (current-account snapshot)' band; account_class becomes a group-by in Breakdown beside model and project; each People row carries a class chip whose hover shows the literal field, e.g. "oauthAccount.organizationType = claude_max".
data_source: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{organizationType, organizationRole, workspaceRole, billingType, seatTier, organizationRateLimitTier, profileFetchedAt} and machineID/userID (64-hex, opaque); ~/.codex/auth.json {auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY presence, tokens.account_id presence}; ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl token_count.rate_limits.plan_type; ~/.grok/auth.json object key + {auth_mode, principal_type, team_id presence} and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl ctx.auth_mode ('Oidc' on 1019 lines); ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db account_state.active_org_id.
honest_limit: oauthAccount is a snapshot of the account signed in when Vole last collected — dated by profileFetchedAt (1788735002155 here), not by the session — so for Claude Code a class binds per session only where a bridge-session line recorded ownerAccountUuid/ownerOrganizationUuid (18 files here); everything else is stamped 'current account, not proven' and must never count as proof inside an incident. A re-auth under a different account reclassifies nothing retroactively, and a raw API key exported into one shell and used once leaves no on-disk trace at all. The OpenCode arm is declared but unverifiable on this machine: account_state has 0 rows.
competitive_note: Turns 'and 58.2% of Claude usage runs on personal accounts' (Cyberhaven 2026) into per-session evidence. Anthropic's Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry and personal accounts by construction (Speakeasy, 2026-05-15); OpenAI's Codex governance covers ChatGPT-workspace accounts only; Cursor can only block personal login via MDM Allowed Team IDs and cannot report it after the fact; every gateway vendor is blind to a subscription-auth CLI by definition.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: Every named field confirmed verbatim in ~/.claude.json: `oauthAccount.organizationType = claude_max`, `billingType = stripe_subscription`, `seatTier = None`, `organizationRole = admin`, `organizationRateLimitTier = default_claude_max_20x`, `workspaceRole = None`, `profileFetchedAt = 1788735002155`, `hasAvailableSubscription = False`; userID and machineID both 64-char and all-hex. ~/.codex/auth.json: `auth_mode = 'chatgpt' (len 7)`, `OPENAI_API_KEY = None`, `tokens{id_token:len1820, access_token:len1765, refresh_token:len196, account_id:len36}`. ~/.grok/auth.json object key is literally `https://auth.x.ai::b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828` with `auth_mode: oidc`, `principal_type: User`, `team_id` present. Codex plan_type: 43 'team' + 4 'free'. The organizationName warning is REAL — that field is 5 characters long here, i.e. the owner's first name, exactly as the proposal says. OpenCode arm dead: account_state 0 rows (columns are id, active_account_id, active_org_id — the column exists, the data does not).
constraint: C7 (DB holds no content) — satisfied: enums and an HMAC of organizationUuid are ids, not content, and the explicit ban on emailAddress/fullName/displayName/organizationName is the correct reading of C7. C5 (never invent a number) — 'unknown' must be a stored class, never a default that reads as a finding. Partial overlap with roadmap-v1 line 109, which already proposes comparing bridge-session owner uuids to the local oauthAccount; the new part is the enum plus class_evidence, so keep it but do not re-do the comparison twice.

name: Per-person view governance: default gate, access log, subject notices, no productivity axis
description: Three switches over one view, so a works council has a single named artifact instead of scattered defaults. The People view ships collapsed to a 'This is you' card whenever the store holds one principal and refuses to render a multi-person table unless a people_view: {enabled, granted_to, reason} block exists in the policy file — its absence is a hard off, not a warning. productivity_views defaults on in personal mode and off in managed mode; when off, every Tier-4 outcome read model (acceptance rate, cost per commit, session outcome labels, session report card) is unavailable in the app, the CLIs and MCP, BreakdownBy offers no subject axis, no sort control offers 'most tokens' as a ranking of people, and every export header carries productivity_views=off. Every read of subject-level rows appends access_log(ts, actor, role, purpose, reason, subject_id, range, row_count, policy_hash), the subject's own panel lists those accesses, and with sync on the relay pushes back notices so an entry reads 'Security team queried your incidents on 2026-09-10, reason INC-441'. A conformance test fails the build if any shipped query joins an outcome measure to subject_id while the flag is off.
desktop_surface: People view renders as one card by default; with the policy block present it shows a 'per-person view enabled by policy <hash>' strip and a mandatory reason field. Privacy Center gains 'Who looked at your data' (reverse-chronological actor / role / stated reason / range, empty state reading 'no access recorded' rather than 'none') and a 'Performance evaluation: disabled' card naming the policy key and the queries it removes; the Breakdown screen simply omits the per-person axis with a one-line explanation instead of a greyed-out control.
data_source: ~/.vole/policy/identity.json people_view and productivity_views blocks; new access_log table in ~/.vole/vole.db written by the purpose-bound query builder and cli/mcp.ts; queries.ts getBreakdown BreakdownBy union; the Tier-4 outcome queries; the export header in sync/manifest.ts.
honest_limit: A local admin holding the SQLite file bypasses every gate — this is the product's default behaviour plus an audit trail, not a security boundary against the machine's owner, and FileVault is the only real control there. Per-person token and cost totals remain performance-adjacent and an analyst can infer a ranking from cost alone: the switch bounds Vole's outputs, not what a reader concludes. Without sync the access panel shows local reads only and must say so rather than implying no remote access occurred.
competitive_note: v1 places the leaderboard rule and the access notices at the sync/relay layer, where the monitored person never sees them and where nothing applies until a relay exists; GDPR Art. 88, BetrVG §87(1) Nr. 6 and CNIL proportionality bite at the point the view exists on the endpoint. Copilot's usage metrics and Cursor's admin analytics are per-user cohort products with no off switch, which is exactly why they meet European works-council resistance.
v1_ref: No per-person leaderboards by default; per-person views need role, reason and notify the subject
field_verified: The axis genuinely does not exist yet: queries.ts:165 `export type BreakdownBy = 'model' | 'project' | 'branch'` and :166 BREAKDOWN_COL maps only those three -- there is no subject axis to remove, so the conformance test is a tripwire for a future axis, not a removal. usage_events.user IS populated (`select distinct user, machine` -> single row `shiva|Marys-MacBook-Pro.local`) and is read by no query, so the raw material for a leaderboard is already sitting there. access_log does not exist. The Tier-4 outcome models the productivity switch disables -- acceptance rate, cost per commit, session outcome labels, report card -- do not exist anywhere in queries.ts.
constraint: C12 (read-model parity) is the cost centre: the People card, its policy gate and the access panel must each be written twice, and DB.swift must stay a read-only consumer -- so access_log rows generated by an app-side read cannot be written by DB.swift. Reconcile: log reads at the TS query-builder boundary only, and have the app's reads route through it, or accept that app-side reads are unlogged and say so on the panel. C6: access_log is about reads not events, so it needs an explicit exemption from the source-column rule rather than silence.

name: Codex per-session plan from the rollout, not from auth.json
description: roadmap-v1 proposes reading a Codex account_id from ~/.codex/auth.json, while its own warning says never to open that file for identity — and rightly: it holds tokens.id_token (1820 chars), access_token (1765) and refresh_token (196). The rollout already answers the question in the session's own file with its own timestamp: token_count.payload.rate_limits carries plan_type, limit_id, individual_limit and spend_control_reached, and codex.ts:126-134 already parses that exact object for rate_limit_pressure and throws plan_type away. Store plan_type, limit_id and individual_limit on session_identity with binding_evidence='session_proved'; no credential file is opened.
desktop_surface: Codex rows in the People view show the plan (team / free / plus) with a 'from this session' evidence dot; Breakdown gains a per-plan split under the Codex tool section.
data_source: ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl, line type token_count, payload.rate_limits.{plan_type, limit_id, individual_limit, spend_control_reached} — the object codex.ts:56-58 already types.
honest_limit: 62 of 66 rollouts here carry a rate_limits object but only 12 carry plan_type (47 lines in total: 'team' 43, 'free' 4), so most Codex sessions have plan NULL and must render as '—', not as a default. plan_type is what the server told the client at that moment, not a billing record, and a short session that never hit a meter has no such line at all.
competitive_note: OpenAI's Codex governance covers only ChatGPT-workspace accounts (developers.openai.com/codex/enterprise/governance), so a 'free' plan_type on a corporate laptop is invisible to it by definition.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: Confirmed to the digit. 66 rollouts; 62 carry a rate_limits object; 12 carry plan_type; 47 plan_type lines = 43 'team' + 4 'free' — exactly the proposal's figures. Full key census of the 68 rate_limits objects: limit_id 68, limit_name 68, primary 68, secondary 68, credits 68, plan_type 68, rate_limit_reached_type 68, individual_limit 64, spend_control_reached 43 — every field the feature names exists. The object sits on `line.type='event_msg'` with `payload.type='token_count'`, which is precisely what codex.ts:124 already matches (`if (entry.payload?.type !== 'token_count') return;`) and then reads only `entry.payload.rate_limits?.primary` — plan_type is genuinely in hand and thrown away. The credential-avoidance argument also verifies: ~/.codex/auth.json really does hold id_token len 1820, access_token len 1765, refresh_token len 196.
constraint: C7 (never read credentials) — this feature is the reconciliation, not the violation: it reaches the same answer without opening auth.json. C11 (node:sqlite strict named binding) — three new columns need matching INSERT list, @params, type and schema changes. UNNAMED and serious: codex.ts:197 keys events `codex:<sessionId ?? filePath>:<line index>` and sub-agent rollouts replay the parent session_meta (ranked bug #2), so a session_identity row UNIQUE on (tool, session_id) inherits that collision — a child rollout can overwrite the parent's plan under one session_id, and at equal evidence rank the widening upsert makes it silent last-writer. Reconciliation: key on (tool, session_id, rollout file) or fix the collector key first.

name: Privacy Center: path receipts, field dictionary, egress and self-DSAR
description: One permanent screen answering 'what does this thing know about me', built from live rows rather than from documentation: per-path read receipts from sources/collector_runs (path, last read, bytes scanned, rows produced); a column data dictionary generated from the redaction manifest (column, type, example shape, why); the resolved principal with which source won, the machine-id and hostname history, per-tool account_class with the literal deciding field, and the identity fields read but discarded (emailAddress, fullName, displayName, key prefixes, tokens); the egress panel rendered from the generated network inventory; and any access_log rows naming who looked at this person's data and why. A 'vole transparency --identity' CLI prints the same content so it survives outside the app, and 'Export everything about me' produces the DSAR bundle scoped to the current principal.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center in the sidebar with sections Paths read (table with Reveal in Finder), Fields stored, Identity, Network and Who looked at your data — reachable in one click from the People card, every row citing its source path — plus Export my data and Delete my data buttons at the foot.
data_source: paths.ts accessors; sources/collector_runs rows; principals, machines, session_identity, access_log; packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts column list; the generated egress inventory.
honest_limit: It describes what this build stores and cannot prove that a modified or future build behaves the same, which is why the manifest, verify --content and verify --identity must ship with it. It reports Vole's own reads and egress and says nothing about what Claude Code, Codex or Grok CLI themselves upload — Grok's repo_state.upload lines sending repositories to xAI GCS belong on the Posture screen, not here.
competitive_note: v1's panel covers sync payloads and is only meaningful once sync exists; this one is useful on day one with sync off, and adds the identity and path-receipt halves it lacks entirely. Kolide's Privacy Center is the only endpoint precedent and no AI-monitoring vendor in the 62-row matrix ships an employee-facing manifest; against Cyberhaven and Harmonic, whose sensors inspect content and publish no retention statement, enumerating every path and field is what shortens the security questionnaire.
v1_ref: 'What leaves this machine' panel, vole transparency and the notice-acknowledgement gate
field_verified: paths.ts is exactly as described -- 11 source accessors plus db and pricingOverride, each with a VOLE_* env override, resolved at runtime via `const home = () => process.env.VOLE_HOME_OVERRIDE ?? homedir()`. But the per-path read receipt has no source for six of seven tools: `select tool,count(*) from collector_state group by 1` returns ONE row, `claude_code|634`. Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Devin, Cursor and Antigravity write nothing to collector_state (claude-code.ts is its only writer), so 'path, last read, bytes scanned, rows produced' is unavailable for them today. sources, collector_runs, principals, machines, session_identity and access_log do not exist; sync/manifest.ts does not exist.
constraint: C12 parity for every section of the screen. No principle is violated -- the feature is principle 7 and principle 2 rendered. The reconciliation for the receipt gap: either land collector_runs first (roadmap-v1 L16) or render 'not recorded' for six tools, which is honest but makes the screen's headline section mostly blank on day one.

name: Credential-shape probe that never reads a credential
description: For sessions the transcripts cannot classify, a shape-only reader records whether a credential file exists and what kind it is, under a hard rule that no retained string exceeds 16 characters. On ~/.codex/auth.json it records auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY===null (so: ChatGPT OAuth, not a raw key), presence of tokens.account_id and last_refresh — never the three token strings in the same object. On ~/.grok/auth.json it records the issuer host from the object key (https://auth.x.ai::<uuid>), auth_mode 'oidc' and the presence of team_id and principal_id — never .key (786 chars), .refresh_token, .email or .first_name, which sit in that same object. On ~/.claude.json it records customApiKeyResponses as counts plus a salted hash of each hint (approved 0, rejected 2 here: 'not-needed' and 'sk-litellm-local'), which is evidence a raw-key or local-gateway path was offered to Claude Code. Adds `auth_shape(tool, path, mode, has_api_key, has_oauth_tokens, has_team_binding, observed_at, source)` and a matching redaction-manifest entry so verify --content can assert no long string from these paths ever reached the DB.
desktop_surface: Settings → Identity lists each tool as 'signed in via OAuth' / 'raw API key configured' / 'org-bound OIDC' / 'not configured' with the path it was read from and the observation time; no value is ever displayed, and a 'what this reads' disclosure names each key by name.
data_source: ~/.codex/auth.json (auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY, tokens.account_id presence, last_refresh); ~/.grok/auth.json (object key, auth_mode, principal_type, team_id/principal_id presence); ~/.claude.json customApiKeyResponses.{approved, rejected}.
honest_limit: This is a snapshot of the credential configured now, not of any past session, and it is the one code path in the whole lens that opens a secrets file — it must be consent-gated, off by default, and it is the first thing a hostile security reviewer will read. It cannot see a key passed only through an environment variable or exported into one shell, and a rejected key hint proves a raw-key path was offered, never that it was used.
competitive_note: Claude Code's own OTel gives identity only on OAuth — API-key and Bedrock sessions get a bare user.id (code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage) — so the raw-key case is exactly the one every vendor console drops.
field_verified: Every field exists exactly as described. ~/.codex/auth.json: `auth_mode='chatgpt'` (7 chars), `OPENAI_API_KEY=None`, `tokens.account_id` len 36, `last_refresh` len 27 — alongside id_token 1820 / access_token 1765 / refresh_token 196 in the same object. ~/.grok/auth.json: key `https://auth.x.ai::b1a00492-...`, `auth_mode: oidc`, `principal_type: User`, `team_id` and `principal_id` present — alongside `key` len 786, refresh_token len 86, email len 22, first_name len 24 in that same object. ~/.claude.json: `customApiKeyResponses: {"approved": [], "rejected": ["not-needed", "sk-litellm-local"]}` — 0 approved, 2 rejected, exactly the quoted hints. HARD FINDING AGAINST THE DESIGN: the 16-character rule is not a safety property. ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl carries `"key_prefix":"PsQmpaqoOdtQ"` on 969 turn.terminal_failure lines — 12 characters, under the cap, and a live credential fragment. And 'sk-litellm-local' is itself exactly 16 characters, sitting on the boundary.
constraint: C7 head-on: 'credentials must never be SELECTed into memory beyond the collector loop'. JSON.parse on auth.json materialises id_token, access_token, refresh_token and grok's 786-char key in process memory whether or not they are retained. The honest statement is 'the values enter memory transiently and are never stored', not 'never reads a credential' — a hostile reviewer will make this exact point, so the entry should make it first. C17 (any new reach needs disclosure and an off switch) — the proposal's consent gate satisfies it. Also depends on a redaction manifest and `verify --content`, neither of which exists in cli/verify.ts today.

name: NON-GOALS charter with the canary proof behind it
description: Write down what Vole will never build and make each line executable rather than a memo: no proxy, MITM or base-URL rewrite; no browser extension; no prompt, tool-argument or tool-output storage; no per-person productivity, ranking or leaderboard view; no automatic agent kill without a human; no estimated numbers or third confidence tier; no kernel/ES sensor; no DNS interception. The load-bearing check is a canary test: plant a synthetic high-entropy string in a fixture transcript, run collect plus the DLP pass plus every export path, then grep the whole ~/.vole/vole.db including WAL and freelist pages — not just live rows — plus the NDJSON export, the webhook/OTLP payload and the digest markdown, failing if it appears anywhere; the test also asserts that its export list equals the export registry, so a new writer added without a canary assertion fails the build. The other lines bind to scripts/check-egress.mjs, a schema test that no column or view name matches /estimate|score|rank|productivity/, a grep that no query orders by user, and a test that the actions table has no code path that signals without a recorded confirmation. docs/NON-GOALS.md is generated from the check list so the doc cannot drift from the enforcement, and 'pnpm verify --content' is the runnable form a DPO or works council re-runs themselves.
desktop_surface: Settings → 'Scope and limits': the charter rendered as a list, each line green-checked with the name of its check and its last CI status, plus the last verify --content result and date replacing today's hard-coded 'Verification: Every stored row reconciled' string at DashboardView.swift:703; the page is the answer to the first three questions of every security questionnaire.
data_source: scripts/check-egress.mjs; packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts (top-level await today and not importable — this needs it refactored to a callable); a fixture transcript under packages/core/src/collectors/__fixtures__; schema.ts column names; queries.ts; the redaction manifest.
honest_limit: A CI check proves a property of the shipped source, not of a modified build — anyone can fork Vole and delete the test, so the charter is evidence about the release the user installed and says so. The canary proves only the paths the test enumerates and can say nothing about the freed pages of a database VACUUMed by an external tool. A promise not to store content is only as good as the scanner behind verify --content, which is a rule list with the same false-negative profile as any other, and the charter cannot constrain a third-party plugin or a future relay.
competitive_note: v1 declares verify --content but scopes it to running a secret rule table over vole.db, which cannot prove the absence of content the scanner has no rule for; a planted canary can, and the charter turns three README claims (README:22, SECURITY:13, DashboardView.swift:703, all already contradicted by UpdateChecker.swift:27) into named build checks. Of 27 security vendors covering coding agents none states its prompt-retention policy (Nightfall's own comparison, 2026-08); Gemini CLI logs prompts by default, Cowork's OTel includes full prompts, Cloudflare's AI Gateway stores them.
v1_ref: Redaction manifest and verify --content (prove the DB and exports hold no content)
field_verified: scripts/check-egress.mjs DOES NOT EXIST -- scripts/ contains only build-docs-pdf.mjs; it is proposed at roadmap-v1 L3 and the feature cites it as a data source as if shipped. verify.ts is confirmed not importable: `const db = openDb()` at :146, `await sleep(7_000)` at :315 (top-level await), `process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1)` at the end. DashboardView.swift carries the hard-coded `LabeledContent("Verification", value: "Every stored row reconciled")` around :696 (the file is 709 lines; the cited :703 is off by ~7). No __fixtures__ directory exists under collectors. The WAL leak path is real: ~/.vole/vole.db-wal is 5,965,792 bytes right now. The schema test would pass today -- no column name matches /estimate|score|rank|productivity/.
constraint: C4 (confidence is exactly two values) versus the project's OWN docs: docs/ROADMAP.md L162 says 'Keep exact / estimated / activity_only visible' while types.ts:22 is `'exact' | 'activity_only'`. So the charter line 'no third confidence tier' is contradicted by the principles doc it would sit beside -- the charter must fix ROADMAP.md L162 or it ships self-contradicting on day one. C15: verify.ts must lose its top-level await to become callable, the same refactor #6 and #27 need.

name: Cloud-provider class from model-id shape and the settings env snapshot
description: The cloud_provider class is the one arm the classifier cannot demonstrate on this machine, so it is built as an explicit shape rule with a no-data state rather than a silent zero. A session is classified cloud_provider when usage_events.model matches a provider-routed id shape (us.anthropic.*, anthropic.claude-* for Bedrock; publishers/anthropic/models/* for Vertex; the Foundry deployment form) or when the collection-time settings snapshot shows CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL / CLOUD_ML_REGION among the env key names in ~/.claude/settings.json. The matched shape or key name is stored in class_evidence so the classification is auditable rather than asserted, and only key names are stored, never values.
desktop_surface: Account badge reads 'Bedrock' / 'Vertex' / 'Foundry' with the matched model-id shape on hover; Settings → Identity lists the env key names observed (names only) and, when none exist, the line 'no cloud-provider routing observed on this Mac' rather than a zero.
data_source: usage_events.model; ~/.claude/settings.json env block — which on this install is absent entirely (keys present: permissions, enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, effortLevel, remoteControlAtStartup, agentPushNotifEnabled, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt).
honest_limit: Zero rows on this machine demonstrate the class, and the settings file carries no env block at all, so the rule ships unverified against live data. A model-id shape is forgeable by any proxy, and the settings snapshot describes now and must never be stamped onto historical rows. The IAM principal or service account behind a Bedrock call never appears in the transcript, so Vole can say 'this ran through Bedrock' but never 'this ran as role X' — the human behind a shared role is unknowable locally.
competitive_note: Anthropic's Compliance API and the Claude Code Analytics API both exclude Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry entirely (Speakeasy 2026-05-15; platform.claude.com Analytics docs), and Claude Code's own OTel gives Bedrock and API-key sessions a bare user.id — the class exists precisely because the vendor console cannot see it.
field_verified: Both arms confirmed EMPTY, as the proposal admits. ~/.claude/settings.json keys are exactly `['agentPushNotifEnabled','effortLevel','enabledPlugins','extraKnownMarketplaces','permissions','remoteControlAtStartup','skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt']` — `env: ABSENT`; settings.local.json has only `['permissions']`, also no env. Zero provider-routed ids across 29,491 live rows: no us.anthropic.*, no publishers/anthropic/*. BUT the proposal under-claims its own source: usage_events.model ALREADY carries provider prefixes on thousands of rows via OpenCode's providerID — `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.6` 2275, `github-copilot/gpt-5.5` 613, `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8` 303, `github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5` 95, `github-copilot/claude-fable-5` 41, plus `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha` 725, `ollama/hf.co/DavidAU/...` 150, `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` 26, and `anthropic/claude-ccr-h7177...` 456 (a local router).
constraint: C19 (bucketing/keys stable; a snapshot describes now) — the proposal correctly forbids stamping the current env snapshot onto historical rows. C5 — 'no cloud-provider routing observed on this Mac' rather than a zero is the right rendering and matches principle 1.

name: Scope-change ledger with an employee-visible field-level diff
description: § 87(1) Nr. 6 BetrVG co-determination attaches to changes in a monitoring system, not only to its introduction, and Dutch WOR Art. 27 consent is scoped to what was agreed. Hash the effective monitoring scope at every collector start — the redaction manifest column list, ~/.vole/policy.json, the enabled entries of the collectors/index.ts:21-29 REGISTRY, the enabled content scanners and the retention table — and append scope_changes(ts, prev_hash, new_hash, added_fields, removed_fields, set_by, first_seen) when it moves. The diff is field-level, so the ledger reads '+permissionMode, +entrypoint, +bash_command_class' rather than 'policy updated', which is the granularity a works council actually negotiates over.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Scope history' timeline, newest first, each entry expandable to the added and removed field list; a one-time dismissible banner on the Dashboard when a change is first observed.
data_source: packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts column list, ~/.vole/policy.json, collectors/index.ts:21-29 REGISTRY, schema.ts column inventory, hashed with node:crypto at collector startup.
honest_limit: Changes are detected only while the collector runs, so a scope changed while the app was off surfaces with the date it was first observed and must be labelled 'first seen', never 'changed on'. The ledger records Vole's own configuration and cannot see an admin editing the managed profile and reverting it before the next start.
competitive_note: v1 gates only the sync notice on a policy hash, so with sync off no scope change is recorded at all. Absent from all 62 vendors; Kolide's Privacy Center shows current scope but no change history, and a versioned field-level diff is the specific artifact a Betriebsrat asks for when re-approving a tool.
v1_ref: 'What leaves this machine' panel, vole transparency and the notice-acknowledgement gate
field_verified: collectors/index.ts:21-29 is EXACTLY the REGISTRY as cited -- `const REGISTRY: { tool: Tool; run: (db: DB) => CollectorResult }[] = [` at :21 through `];` at :29, seven entries. But there is no enable/disable switch on it, so 'the enabled entries of the REGISTRY' is a constant today and contributes nothing to the hash until a switch exists. schema.ts SCHEMA is a shipped inlined DDL string, hashable right now. node:crypto is a node: builtin so it is SEA-safe. ~/.vole/policy.json does not exist, no retention table exists, no content scanners exist -- three of the five hashed inputs have no source.
constraint: C14 satisfied (node:crypto is a builtin, no new dependency). C11: scope_changes is a new table, which is fine since migrate() only probes usage_events and anomalies and new tables come from SCHEMA. C6: needs a source-column decision like every other new table.

name: ~/.vole/policy/identity.json — the corporate declaration with a propose step
description: The one policy input every identity rule needs: {corporate_org_uuids[], corporate_email_domains[], corporate_repo_owners[], sanctioned_account_classes[]}, hash-stamped so every incident can name the policy version that judged it. Vole never guesses the contents: 'vole identity propose' reads ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths and the org UUIDs it has actually observed in session_identity rows and prints a candidate file to stdout for a human to edit and commit, writing nothing. Absent the file, every identity rule (shadow_account included) is inert and the People view shows account classes with no verdict.
desktop_surface: Settings → Identity shows the policy file path, its sha256, and 'no policy loaded — identity incidents are disabled' when absent, with copy-to-clipboard of the proposed file.
data_source: New file under ~/.vole/policy/; the propose step reads ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths and observed session_identity.org_id values.
honest_limit: A declaration is only as good as whoever wrote it — a contractor on a corporate-looking domain, or a personal repo under a company org, is classified wrong and Vole has no way to know. The propose step can only suggest what it has already seen, so a repo no agent ever touched never appears.
competitive_note: v1's shadow_account rule states that it 'needs a policy definition of corporate' and never defines one; this is that file. SASE and DLP vendors ship opinionated sanctioned-app catalogues, but market.md §2 buyers ask for their own inventory and Gartner's guidance is 'conduct regular audits for shadow AI', not adopt a vendor list.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: Both propose-step inputs verified on this machine. `~/.claude.json` githubRepoPaths is a dict whose keys are owner/repo: first three are 'launchsafe/docs', 'launchsafe/landing', 'launchsafe/engine' -- exactly the corporate_repo_owners candidates. oauthAccount carries organizationUuid ('4d93cf...'), organizationName, organizationRole ('admin'), accountUuid ('909a11...'), so an org UUID is readable TODAY without any identity collector. session_identity does not exist as a table; ~/.vole/policy/ does not exist.
constraint: None material. It writes nothing (propose prints to stdout), which keeps C8 clean, and hash-stamping the policy into incident keys is C3-compatible (deterministic, no now()). Worth noting ~/.vole is mode 0755 and vole.db 0644 today, so any 0600 policy file sits in a world-readable directory until the store-hardening item lands.

name: Inalienable exclusion floor for personal work on a corporate device
description: v1's monitoring-scope feature lets the org set exclusions.never_excludable with no floor, so an employer can forbid all exclusions and the personal-project carve-out that almost every works agreement contains becomes unenforceable in the tool. Add a floor the org cannot override: any path outside the profile's declared workRoots is always excludable by the employee, and for an excluded session the org receives a count only — never the project path, branch, model or token totals. The employee sets it in ~/.vole/exclude.json, and the resolution order is checked at insert from the transcript's first-line cwd, so an excluded project never produces a row rather than producing one that is filtered later.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Excluded paths': the employee's list with an add/remove control, the declared work roots shown read-only above it, and a count of sessions excluded this month — the same count the org can see.
data_source: usage_events.project (absolute cwd; 26,977 of 28,948 rows under <redacted-local-path>, 1,962 empty), the transcript first-line cwd, workRoots from the managed profile, ~/.vole/exclude.json.
honest_limit: Excluding by cwd cannot catch personal work done inside a work repository, and the 1,962 rows here with no project at all cannot be classified either way — those stay unknown and are released only as aggregates. The floor is enforced by Vole's code; an org that builds from source can remove it, which the docs should state plainly.
competitive_note: v1 makes every exclusion overridable by the org via exclusions.never_excludable, which is the one thing that makes the clause worthless in a Betriebsvereinbarung. Endpoint DLP vendors monitor the device wholesale with no employee-controlled carve-out; shipping the carve-out as an override-proof floor is what makes a German or Dutch pilot approvable.
v1_ref: Monitoring scope policy and personal-project exclusion
field_verified: The numbers are right: 27,661 of 29,632 rows have project beginning <redacted-local-path> and 1,962 rows have NULL or empty project -- the feature's 1,962 is EXACT. The cwd source is real for the two biggest tools: claude-code.ts reads cwd per line, and a Codex session_meta payload on this machine reads `"cwd": "<redacted-local-path>"`. But Grok's cwd comes from ~/.grok/sessions/<enc>/<sid>/summary.json and that directory is ABSENT on this machine (paths.grokSessionsDir), so grok's 1,758 rows can never be path-excluded; Cursor, Antigravity and Devin carry no usable cwd either. workRoots from a managed profile does not exist; ~/.vole/exclude.json does not exist.
constraint: C2 (upsert semantics) is the conflict the feature misses. Excluding at insert works for NEW rows, but the ON CONFLICT SET list never rewrites `project` and only fires when excluded.total_tokens is strictly greater -- so a row already stored under a path the employee excludes LATER cannot be re-scoped by re-collection. It must be deleted, which lands straight in #17's problem (six collectors re-read everything every five seconds and would resurrect it). Reconcile: the floor needs #17's ingest pre-filter to hold retroactively, and that coupling must be stated.

name: Identity in the detection partition and the anomaly key
description: detectBySource (detect/index.ts:45-57) partitions on source only and prefixes keys with the source, and no rule's anomaly_key contains user or machine — burn-rate.ts:52 is burn_rate_spike:<tool>:<model>:<bucket>. The moment a second identity's rows share one store — a shared Mac, a VOLE_DB on a network volume, or v1's Tier 7 relay running the same schema and rules — two employees' windows merge into one baseline and collapse into a single UNIQUE anomaly row, so per-employee incident counts are wrong in a way no reader can detect. Widen the partition to (source, user, machine), prefix keys the same way, and add nullable user, machine and project columns to anomalies so a per-repo policy rule can key on scope. This must land before any multi-identity row exists: anomaly_key is UNIQUE and INSERT OR IGNORE (db.ts:137), so it cannot be rewritten later without deleting incident history.
desktop_surface: Dashboard → Incidents gains a per-person filter once a second identity exists; today the pane is identical, which is the point — it is a zero-diff migration now and a data-loss migration later.
data_source: packages/core/src/detect/index.ts:45-57; the anomaly_key construction in detect/*.ts; db.ts:19-35 ORIGIN; the live DB has exactly one (user, machine) pair today across all 29,293 live rows.
honest_limit: os.hostname() is an mDNS/DHCP name that changes on network moves, so until the IOPlatformUUID-based id exists the widened partition can split one laptop's history in two — which understates baselines rather than merging people, the safer of the two failure modes but still wrong.
competitive_note: Per-employee attribution is buyer need 1 and 2 in market-extracts (47% lack an agent inventory; 67% of AI access on corporate devices uses non-corporate accounts), and vendor consoles are already identity-fragmented across email, user_login, IAM and credits — Vole must not ship a fourth broken identity.
v1_ref: Opt-in fleet sync of normalised rows (org relay / Vole Fleet)
field_verified: Confirmed line by line. detect/index.ts:42-58 partitions solely on `e.source` (`const arr = bySource.get(e.source)`) and prefixes keys `${source}:${a.anomaly_key}`; burn-rate.ts:53 is `anomaly_key: \`burn_rate_spike:${tool}:${model}:${bucket}\`` with no user or machine; db.ts:137 is INSERT OR IGNORE on a UNIQUE anomaly_key. The live store has exactly one (user, machine) pair across 29,491 rows, so this is a genuine zero-diff migration today. CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED CHANGE: anomalies ALREADY HAS user and machine — schema.ts:62-63 declare them, db.ts:46-47 backfill them via migrate(), and PRAGMA table_info on the live table returns them populated by the ORIGIN spread at db.ts:154. Only `project` is missing. The change is one nullable column, not three.
constraint: C3 head-on: anomaly_key is UNIQUE under INSERT OR IGNORE, so a key format cannot be revised after multi-identity rows exist without deleting incident history — which is precisely the feature's argument for landing it first. Reconciliation: the widened key stays deterministic and bucket-anchored, so C3's substance is preserved. UNOWNED COST: changing the format orphans the 249 live anomalies already stored, which keep their old keys and will re-fire once under the new format — a one-time duplicate of historical incidents that the entry should declare rather than let a user discover.

name: AI-dictionary-gated shell-history scanner with its own consent tier and a byte receipt
description: Shell history is the most privacy-charged read in the product, so it gets a mechanism rather than a checkbox. One named scanner, shell_history, appears in the shipped read manifest, defaults to OFF in both personal and managed mode, and is enabled only by an explicit toggle that writes who enabled it and when into the scope-change ledger. Its reader is two-pass: a byte-window prefilter tests each window against the shipped AI dictionary (provider hostnames, *_API_KEY name shapes, known CLI names) and non-matching windows are discarded without ever being decoded to a string; a matching window is reduced through the existing command-shape skeleton to (pattern_id, pack_version) plus the variable name and host, and only history_sightings(file, pattern_id, var_name, host, count, first_seen, last_seen, source) is written. Every pass writes a receipt - bytes read, windows tested, windows matched, rows stored - so the Privacy Center states a measured fact rather than a promise; on this machine that reads '1,162 lines read, 21 matched, 0 lines stored'. The scanner gets its own line in the Privacy Center, the DSAR export, the works-council pack and the erasure path.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center gains a dedicated 'Shell history' card: the toggle, the last receipt (bytes read / windows matched / rows stored), a worked example of what a stored row looks like, and a one-click erase that also drops every derived row. On the Shadow AI screen these rows appear only as evidence chips on an existing surface, never as a surface of their own.
data_source: ~/.zsh_history, ~/.bash_history, ~/.local/share/fish/fish_history - read through the prefilter, and only when the scanner is explicitly enabled
honest_limit: History is a lossy, editable record of one shell, not of the machine: HISTCONTROL and hist_ignore_space hide commands, a line proves a command was typed rather than that it ran or succeeded, and timestamps exist only where extended history is enabled. Nothing here is attributable beyond the account that owns the file. Because the default install produces no rows at all, an empty result means 'not read', and the coverage denominator must say so instead of implying zero findings.
competitive_note: Endpoint DLP suites (Cyberhaven, Nightfall, Forcepoint) reach this class of data through an ES-level sensor and store prompt content by default; the differentiating claim here is a scanner that is off by default and whose receipt proves, in bytes, how little it kept.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: Principal and account-class dimensions in every read model
description: Extend the read surfaces that exist rather than inventing a second one: getBreakdown gains by='principal' and by='account_class' beside the existing model/project/branch groupings, getSummary returns principal_id, machine_uuid and the bound/ambient/unbound triple, and the same three appear in vole_summary/vole_breakdown and as named NDJSON export columns. Values come from the principals and session_identity rows, so this is a read-model widening — one new GROUP BY branch in queries.ts, the matching hand-port in DB.swift, two extra TOOLS entries in cli/mcp.ts — and adds no collection. Every grouped row carries the confidence badge and the binding_evidence string beside it, so 'by person' can never render a total whose attribution was only ambient.
desktop_surface: Breakdown panel gains 'By person' and 'By account type' groupings beside the existing per-tool and per-model rows, each row showing both the confidence badge and the binding evidence; the unbound bucket renders as its own visible row rather than being dropped or folded into a named person.
data_source: packages/core/src/queries.ts getSummary/getBreakdown; apps/mac/Sources/Vole/DB.swift ports; packages/core/src/cli/mcp.ts TOOLS array; values from the principals and session_identity tables populated by identity binding.
honest_limit: The dimension is only as good as the binding: a principal resolved from a current-account snapshot (oauthAccount) rather than a per-session stamp is ambient and must stay in its own bucket, never merged into a named person's total. It exists only where identity binding has run — Cursor, Devin and Antigravity rows carry NULL — and a blank cell must render 'not recorded', never zero. Grouping by person on one device says nothing about the same human on a second laptop; that needs the device-scoped sync key, not this dimension.
competitive_note: OTel gen_ai.* has no per-employee identity attribute at all, so the export must carry principal as a resource attribute pinned to a semconv snapshot. Cursor's and Copilot's admin analytics are per-user by construction but single-vendor, and Anthropic's Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex and personal accounts — a cross-tool per-person breakdown on the endpoint is exactly what none of them can produce.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: HALF FALSE. The read surfaces exist: queries.ts:166 `const BREAKDOWN_COL: Record<BreakdownBy,string> = { model:'model', project:'project', branch:'git_branch' }` and getSummary at queries.ts:49 — so one GROUP BY branch is genuinely the shape. But the VALUES do not exist. `sqlite_master` on ~/.vole/vole.db returns exactly three tables — usage_events, anomalies, collector_state — no `principals`, no `session_identity`, and schema.ts has no `account_class` column. What does exist is the origin stamp: `select distinct user,machine from usage_events` → [('shiva','Marys-MacBook-Pro.local')], one pair over 29,511 live rows, written by db.ts:35 `const ORIGIN = origin()` from os.userInfo()/os.hostname(). So by='principal' over `user` is exact today for a single-seat box; the bound/ambient/unbound triple and account_class are gated on the identity shard.
constraint: Two. (a) Constraint 13 read-model parity: every grouping is written twice, and DB.swift:250 breakdown() is hard-coded `GROUP BY tool, model, confidence` with no `by` parameter at all, so 'by person' is a new Swift function, not a port of an existing one. (b) Constraint 2: the upsert SET list (db.ts:87-101) never refreshes `user`/`machine`, and ORIGIN is spread at insert — a row first seen under one account and upgraded under another keeps the first, permanently. Also inherited: queries.ts:80 `MIN(confidence)` would label a whole person 'activity_only' the moment one Cursor row lands in their bucket. Reconciliation: the per-person row must carry per-confidence subtotals, not MIN(), and the honest_limit must add 'origin is the account that ran the collector, frozen at first insert'.

name: Design-partner pilot mode with a hard expiry
description: Make the design-partner motion a product state rather than an email thread: 'vole pilot start --until=<date> --partner=<name>' writes an append-only record into ~/.vole/basis.json (start, end, the exact feature set enabled for the pilot, the policy hash, who set it) and the app renders a persistent pilot banner naming the end date. On expiry every pilot-only path — content-reading scanners, any sync, any webhook — reverts to off automatically and the banner switches to 'pilot ended, local-only'. 'vole pilot bundle' produces the aggregate-only artefact for the partner conversation: per month x tool x model x repo slug totals, incident counts with figures, posture booleans, coverage cells and a device hash, with no session ids, no cwd and no per-person rows.
desktop_surface: A per-session-dismissible banner across the top of the Dashboard for the pilot's duration showing days remaining and what is enabled; Settings → Pilot lists the record verbatim and the bundle history.
data_source: ~/.vole/basis.json; the assess aggregates; the policy hash from ~/.vole/policy.json.
honest_limit: An expiry enforced by the same binary a determined admin can replace is a control on the honest case, not a guarantee against the seat owner — the banner and the append-only record are the evidence and the docs say exactly that. The bundle's aggregates cannot answer per-person questions by design, so a partner needing those must run a per-user query under the role and reason gate instead. Consent is not the lawful basis for employee monitoring in the EU; this record is a transparency artefact, never a substitute for a works-council process.
competitive_note: v1's pilot report fills targets from consent.json's start date but has no expiry, no automatic revert to local-only and no state the app renders. The research prescribes 5-8 design partners with a written agreement and a hard convert-or-leave date (Bessemer); a pilot that quietly keeps collecting after it ends is the fastest way to lose the works-council acceptability that is Vole's structural advantage over Cyberhaven, Harmonic and Nightfall, all of whom collect content continuously.
v1_ref: Assessment merge (vole.assessment.v1) and pilot report (docs/PILOT.md)
field_verified: Nothing the expiry reverts exists. ~/.vole/basis.json does not exist (feature #13 creates it); ~/.vole/policy.json does not exist; there are no content-reading scanners, no sync, no webhook and no assess aggregates anywhere in packages/core/src (roadmap-v1 L172 proposes vole assess). The only real artifact is the append-only JSON record and the banner, both of which are ordinary local file writes -- no instrumentation is actually needed, which is why I corrected the self-assigned needs_new_instrumentation.
constraint: None technical. The governance conflict it names is correct and worth keeping: consent is not the lawful basis for employee monitoring in the EU, so the pilot record is a transparency artefact and never a substitute for a works-council process. That means it must not be positioned as the thing that makes a pilot lawful.

name: People view (v_people) with attribution coverage on every figure
description: db.ts:19-35 stamps user and machine on every row at insert and no query, view or CLI has ever read them. Add a `v_people` view grouping usage_events and anomalies by resolved principal (through v_events_principal, not the raw column) with agents used, sessions, tokens, cost, unpriced count, incidents by severity, first and last seen, and the account_class joined from session_identity. Principle 1 then applies to identity itself: every figure is returned beside a bound / ambient / unbound triple — the count and token sum of rows by binding_evidence — as fields of the read model rather than a footnote in the view, so the CLI, MCP, app and export all carry the denominator. It is written twice per the read-model parity rule (queries.ts plus a DB.swift port) and is the enterprise unlock over columns that already exist.
desktop_surface: New People section: one row per resolved principal with an agent-logo strip, tokens, cost, incident severity chips, account chip and last-seen; a coverage strip at the top states the overall bound share; each row shows the bound/ambient/unbound triple under its token figure; the drill-down is a per-person tab set (Agents, Sessions, Exposure, Incidents) reusing the section screens with the person filter pinned.
data_source: usage_events.user/machine and anomalies.user/machine stamped by db.ts ORIGIN; session_identity.binding_evidence and account_class; live counts here — claude_code 16,363, opencode 10,885, grok 1,758, devin 204, codex 83.
honest_limit: The honest row on this store reads session-proved for a handful of Claude and Codex sessions, ambient for the rest of those two tools, and unbound for all 10,885 OpenCode rows, because OpenCode's account, account_state and control_account tables are empty. The unbound bucket is a floor, not a total: rows whose session never appeared in any identity-bearing artifact are indistinguishable from rows whose artifact Vole does not yet parse. The OS username is not a corporate identity, a shared or service account collapses several humans into one row, and until fleet sync the screen shows this Mac only — one row on a personal laptop.
competitive_note: Anthropic's Claude Code Analytics API reports daily per-user figures with no coverage statement and excludes Bedrock/Vertex entirely; a per-employee number with no denominator is the specific thing market.md §2 says CISOs stop trusting. Vendor consoles are identity-fragmented across email, user_login, IAM and credits, and each is blind to personal accounts, API keys and other vendors' agents.
field_verified: Confirmed: user/machine are stamped by db.ts ORIGIN and read by no query (queries.ts and DB.swift both verified). Live tool counts today: claude_code 16,561, opencode 10,885, grok 1,758, devin 204, codex 83, total 29,491 (the proposal's 16,363/29,293 are a few hundred stale — the store is live and growing, not wrong). I MEASURED THE COVERAGE THE FEATURE ONLY ESTIMATES: the 575 bridge-session lines resolve to 18 distinct sessionIds, and joining them to the store binds exactly 18 of 100 distinct claude_code sessions — 18.0% — covering 1,852 of 16,561 Claude rows (11.2%), under a single ownerAccountUuid and a single org. Add Codex's 12-of-66 plan-bearing rollouts and session-proved binding lands near 6% of all 29,491 live rows. OpenCode's 10,885 rows are unbindable (account/account_state/control_account all 0 rows).
constraint: C4 — the bound/ambient/unbound triple must stay a separate axis and must never be folded into `confidence`, which queries.ts TOKEN_FILTER and verify.ts:473 both depend on being exactly two values; the proposal is explicit about this and is right. C13 — written twice (queries.ts + DB.swift) or the app cannot show it. C6 — every new query needs the `AND source='live'` clause; note getSessionDetail (queries.ts:399) already omits it, so do not copy that pattern.

name: Device tenancy band and the pre-tenancy quarantine
description: Corrects a real mis-attribution: db.ts:19-35 stamps os.userInfo().username on every row at insert, six of seven collectors re-read their entire source every poll (codex.ts:72, opencode.ts:53, grok.ts:75, devin.ts:30, cursor.ts:32, antigravity.ts:21), and the upsert SET list (db.ts:87-101) never rewrites user — so on a reassigned laptop the new holder's first pass ingests the predecessor's rollouts (this store holds Codex rows dated 2026-05-24) and brands them permanently. Adds device_tenancy(principal_id, device_id, from_ts, to_ts, basis, evidence) anchored on ~/.claude.json firstStartTime (2026-07-02 here) and claudeCodeFirstTokenDate, the ctime of $HOME and /var/db/.AppleSetupDone (both 2026-04-28 here), and `dscl . -list /Users UniqueID` filtered >=500 for the shared-device case; a read-time band on v_events_principal resolves any event with ts < from_ts to 'pre_tenancy' instead of to the current principal. Every per-person aggregate carries a pre_tenancy_rows count beside it, exactly the way unpriced rows sit beside a cost total.
desktop_surface: People view and every departure pack print 'N rows predate this principal's tenancy — excluded, holder unknown'; the coverage strip on the timeline gains a tenancy band with the anchor that set it.
data_source: ~/.claude.json firstStartTime/claudeCodeFirstTokenDate/machineID; stat ctime of $HOME and /var/db/.AppleSetupDone; dscl . -list /Users UniqueID; principal_lifecycle.effective_from
honest_limit: macOS keeps no record of who held the device before, so pre-tenancy rows stay unattributed unless an admin declares a predecessor. Home-dir ctime is reset by Migration Assistant and a restore, so it is labelled basis='home_ctime' and treated as evidence, never proof.
competitive_note: Consoles that key on the IdP identity of the current session inherit the same error silently; none of the 62 vendors prints a tenancy band or an excluded-rows denominator.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: shadow_account_on_corporate_repo, with 'corporate' defined in policy
description: roadmap-v1 proposes a shadow_account rule and then concedes it 'needs a policy definition of corporate', which leaves it unshippable; this defines it. policy.json `identity.corporate = {org_uuids[], git_remote_hosts[], repo_globs[]}` (user ~/.vole/policy.json, or /Library/Application Support/Vole/policy.json when managed), and the rule fires when a session whose cwd resolves through <cwd>/.git/config remote origin (a file read, no git spawn) or ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths to a listed remote ran under an account_class other than org_oauth, or under an org id not in org_uuids. anomaly_key = `identity:shadow_account:<tool>:<principal>:<org_id_hmac|none>:<utc_day>` with no now() anywhere, and the incident stores observed = the class and HMAC'd org ref, baseline = the policy clause id, threshold = the matched remote — three columns schema.ts:42-64 already has that queries.ts:230 and DB.swift:227 never select, so both read models must be widened for the incident to explain itself.
desktop_surface: Incident feed row naming the repo slug, the account class and the policy clause quoted verbatim, with a 'Show the account evidence' drill-down; the Accounts section shows an unresolved line 'N sessions could not be bound to an account (see why)'; contributes to the menu-bar severity tint like any live incident.
data_source: session_identity.account_class and class_evidence; <cwd>/.git/config remote origin; ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths (launchsafe/docs, launchsafe/landing, launchsafe/engine, launchsafe/backend here); ~/.vole/policy.json identity.corporate.
honest_limit: The rule is inert without a populated policy block and says so in the rule list rather than inferring 'corporate' from a path name. It must render NULL, not a pass, in three common cases: the repo has no remote, the cwd no longer exists, or the class came only from the current-account snapshot. A local-only repo containing company code is undetectable by definition, and rows with an empty project (1,962 here) can never be tested. It is a policy statement, not a security truth — it fires on a mismatch with a list an admin typed, and the incident says exactly that.
competitive_note: 67% of AI access on corporate devices uses non-corporate accounts (DBIR 2026 via Kiteworks) and 58.2% of Claude usage runs on personal accounts (Cyberhaven 2026) — the fact Netskope, Forcepoint and Harmonic sell on, each detecting it from network identity or a browser session, neither of which exists for a CLI agent authenticated by a subscription token in a config file.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: ~/.claude.json `githubRepoPaths` keys are exactly `['launchsafe/docs','launchsafe/landing','launchsafe/engine','launchsafe/backend']` — confirmed. 1,962 live rows have NULL/empty project — confirmed exactly. The widening claim is real: anomalies has observed/baseline/threshold (schema.ts:47-49) and neither queries.ts:229 nor DB.swift:224 selects them. BLOCKING SCHEMA ERROR: schema.ts declares `observed REAL NOT NULL`, `baseline REAL`, `threshold REAL`. The feature stores `observed = the class and HMAC'd org ref`, `baseline = the policy clause id`, `threshold = the matched remote` — three strings into three REAL columns. That is not a widening, it is a type violation that will fail on the first insert. Also: ~/.vole/ contains only vole.db, -wal and -shm — no policy.json and no identity.json exist, so the rule is inert until a file that has never existed is authored.
constraint: C3 (deterministic keys, never now()) — satisfied by the utc_day bucket. C8 (third-party stores read-only) — reading <cwd>/.git/config as a file rather than spawning git is the right call, but paths.ts gives every other source a VOLE_* env override and this new read has none, breaking source-path parity. Reconciliation for the type violation: put the class and clause text in `detail` (TEXT NOT NULL, already selected by both readers) or add a new TEXT evidence column, and keep observed/baseline/threshold numeric.

name: account_switched incident
description: Fires when the account_id, org_id or plan observed for one tool on one machine changes between sessions — the same Codex binary here produced rollouts under plan_type 'team' (43 lines) and 'free' (4). The rule groups session_identity by (tool, machine_uuid) ordered by first_seen and emits on each transition, with anomaly_key = `identity:account_switch:<tool>:<machine_uuid>:<from>:<to>:<first_seen_bucket>` anchored on the observed session's UTC bucket and never on detection time, so re-running collect cannot produce a second incident; the detail quotes both literal values.
desktop_surface: Incident feed entry 'Codex switched from team to free on this Mac'; the People row for that principal shows both classes with their dates.
data_source: session_identity rows built from rollout rate_limits.plan_type, Claude bridge-session ownerAccountUuid/ownerOrganizationUuid, ~/.grok/auth.json principal_id and team_id.
honest_limit: For any tool classified from an ambient config snapshot rather than a session line, the switch can only be dated to 'between two collection passes', and a switch that happened and reverted between passes is invisible. It cannot distinguish a deliberate account change from a token refresh that returned different plan metadata.
competitive_note: Vendor consoles see only their own tenant, so an employee moving from the corporate workspace to a personal plan simply stops appearing — an absence no console reports as an event.
field_verified: The Codex motivation is real: plan_type across this machine's rollouts is 43 'team' and 4 'free' lines in 12 of 66 files — a genuine within-machine divergence. TWO ARMS DO NOT SUPPORT A TRANSITION: (a) Grok — `~/.grok/auth.json` principal_id/team_id is a single ambient snapshot, and in unified.jsonl the only account-bearing line is `paywall_check_result` {user_id, subscription_tier:'GrokPro'}, which occurs 5 times and carries NO `sid` (0 of 5; by contrast 969 turn.terminal_failure and 1,759 shell.turn.inference_start lines do carry sid). Grok therefore cannot produce a session-anchored switch at all. (b) Claude — all 575 bridge-session lines resolve to exactly 1 ownerAccountUuid and 1 ownerOrganizationUuid, so the rule fires on nothing locally. Realistically this is a Codex-only rule on day one.
constraint: C3 satisfied — the key is anchored on the observed session's UTC bucket, not detection time, so re-collection cannot double-fire. UNNAMED INTERACTION: anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE (db.ts:137), so a switch emitted from an ambient guess is frozen forever; when feature 1's rank-widening later replaces that guess with a session proof, the already-stored incident becomes provably wrong and cannot be corrected without deleting history. Reconciliation: emit account_switched only from binding_evidence='session_proved' rows, never from ambient ones.

name: principal_conflict guard (shared laptops, CI runners, sudo)
description: An info-severity rule over the principals map: one machine_uuid observed under more than one OS username, or one OS username observed under more than one machine_uuid, within the same range. Both shapes break per-employee reporting silently today — a shared laptop attributes a second person's spend to the first, and a CI runner or an sudo invocation creates a phantom principal. anomaly_key = `identity:principal_conflict:<machine_uuid|user>:<sorted peers>:<utc_day>`; the incident emits the literal usernames and machine ids observed with counts, and the People view suppresses its per-person breakdown for that machine until a human resolves it in identity.json.
desktop_surface: A banner at the top of the People view — 'two OS accounts seen on this Mac; per-person figures are held back' — listing the conflicting values, plus an info entry in the incident feed.
data_source: usage_events.user and .machine (a single pair here: shiva / Marys-MacBook-Pro.local across all 29,293 live rows) joined to the machines and principals tables.
honest_limit: It cannot tell a genuinely shared laptop from one whose OS account was renamed, nor a CI runner from a human, without the principal being declared. It sees only usernames Vole itself ran under — an agent run by another OS user writes to a home directory Vole never reads, so that person is absent rather than conflicting.
competitive_note: EDR and MDM vendors solve this with an enrolled device record; open-source local-first tooling (ccusage, agent-audit) has no concept of a second principal at all.
field_verified: Confirmed inert here, exactly as claimed: `SELECT user, machine, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY 1,2` on live rows returns a single row — ('shiva','Marys-MacBook-Pro.local', 29491). anomalies already carries user and machine columns (schema.ts:62-63, populated by the ORIGIN spread at db.ts:154), so the join target exists.
