A SHARPER SIGNAL THE FEATURE MISSES: all 632 collector_state primary keys are paths under <redacted-local-path>, and raw_ref values embed <redacted-local-path> — so a sudo-launched collector writing user='root' while reading <redacted-local-path> is detectable from the mismatch between `user` and the home prefix in the paths it read, without waiting for a second username to appear in a second pass.
constraint: C3 satisfied (utc_day bucket, no now()). No conflict with C4 — info severity is an existing level. The suppression behaviour interacts with C13: if v_people withholds its per-person breakdown, the DB.swift port must implement the same suppression or the app will show a per-person split the CLI refuses to show, which is worse than either behaviour alone.

name: Account class on shadow surfaces that have no collector
description: Applies the same classifier to the surfaces in the discovery registry that Vole has no collector for — the agents a company never provided — by adding account_class and class_evidence columns to the ai_surfaces row, resolved from opaque identifiers only and defaulting to unknown rather than a guess. ~/.copilot/config.json (present here) dates the surface via firstLaunchAt but carries no plan; ~/.claude.json oauthAccount answers org-vs-personal for Claude-family surfaces without touching emailAddress, fullName, displayName or organizationName. The point is that org-vs-personal matters most exactly where there is no usage collector to attribute spend, so the column is the only identity signal such a surface will ever have.
desktop_surface: An 'Account' column in the AI Surfaces grid showing the class chip (Org / Personal / API key / Unknown); hovering names the file and field that decided it, never the organisation name.
data_source: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{organizationUuid, organizationType, seatTier, billingType, organizationRole}; ~/.copilot/config.json firstLaunchAt; presence-only checks on each surface's credential path.
honest_limit: Personal-vs-org for Copilot, Antigravity/Gemini and Kiro is not determinable from local files at all and stays unknown rather than being guessed — ~/.copilot here holds only config.json, ide/ and logs/, with no session-state directory, so the CLI has never run. Because Vole deliberately never reads the email or name that would distinguish them, it cannot tell two people apart on a shared machine.
competitive_note: v1's identity binding scopes to the seven supported collectors; this applies the classification where the answer actually matters. 67% of AI access on corporate devices uses non-corporate accounts (DBIR 2026 via Kiteworks, 2026-05-20), and Anthropic's Compliance API cannot see personal or API-key sessions by design.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: ~/.copilot/config.json confirmed present and contains exactly `{"firstLaunchAt": "2026-07-25T16:00:13.753Z"}` under a `// This file is managed automatically.` header — no plan field, as claimed. ~/.copilot/ holds only config.json, ide/ (three .lock files) and logs/; there is no session-state/. oauthAccount fields confirmed (see feature 2). CRITICAL SOURCING GAP: the table this feature adds columns to does not exist. schema.ts declares exactly three tables (`usage_events`, `anomalies`, `collector_state`) and I grepped roadmap-v1.md for `ai_surfaces` — zero hits. There is no discovery registry to hang a column on, under that name or any other.
constraint: C12 (add-nullable-column-only migration via PRAGMA probing) is fine IF the host table exists; it does not, so this silently depends on an unnamed prerequisite. C7 — presence-only credential-path checks are compliant. Reconciliation: restate as 'adds account_class/class_evidence to the shadow-AI surface inventory, which must land first' and name that dependency in the entry, or give it its own two-column table so it can ship alone.

name: surface_principal: attributing a surface that has no session, and saying how weakly
description: Every artifact behind a homegrown surface has a filesystem owner and an mtime, and a repo has a git identity - that is the only attribution available when there is no session to bind to. Each inventory row records the owning uid, the file mtime as evidence_ts, and, for repo-scoped rows, the repo .git/config user.email domain plus the HMAC of the address under the existing identity rules, with the address itself never stored. This introduces one new binding_evidence rank, 'file_owner', placed deliberately below every session-derived rank in the existing session_identity ladder, so a homegrown surface can never outrank a real session in the principal resolution chain. Where the machine resolves to a single uid the rows are stamped principal_scope='endpoint' and the People view files them under the endpoint rather than under a person.
desktop_surface: People view gains a 'surfaces with no session' count per principal, greyed and footnoted with its binding rank. Each Shadow AI card shows an 'attributed by file owner' badge whose tooltip spells out exactly what file ownership does and does not establish, matching the wording in the 'what per-employee attribution cannot establish' page.
data_source: stat(2) uid and mtime on every cited manifest, plist, config and env file; repo .git/config user.email (domain + HMAC only)
honest_limit: File ownership is not authorship: a cloned repo carries a teammate's committer identity, CI and sudo write files as other uids, a shared laptop collapses everyone into one account, and on a single-user Mac every row resolves to the same uid, which makes the signal endpoint-level and nothing more. It is the weakest rank in the ladder by construction and must never be the basis of a per-person view or a per-person figure.
competitive_note: Buyer need #1 asks for per-employee inventory including raw API keys, and every console-side vendor attributes by account - precisely the identity a shadow surface does not have. No endpoint vendor publishes what its attribution cannot establish, which is the only defensible way to ship a weak rank at all.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: browser_identity: the account the browser is signed into, and whether AI threads sync out of it
description: The account-class classifier resolves an agent's auth path, but a browser has no auth path, so every non-engineer seat currently resolves to nothing. Read Local State -> profile.info_cache.<dir>.{hosted_domain, user_name, gaia_id, is_ephemeral} (verified hosted_domain = "NO_HOSTED_DOMAIN", i.e. a consumer Google account, on a machine that also runs corporate repos), signin.active_accounts_managed (false here) and management.platform.enterprise_mdm_mac (0 — the browser is not MDM-enrolled); then Default/Preferences -> enterprise_profile_guid, sync.selected_types_per_account (verified sync.typed_urls true) and sync.data_type_status_for_sync_to_signin.{ai_thread, gemini_thread} — the two datatypes that carry AI conversations off the device, both false here but present in the schema. Adds browser_identity rows feeding the existing session_identity model with account_class in {corporate_managed, consumer, unknown} derived from hosted_domain plus active_accounts_managed plus enterprise_mdm_mac. The address itself is never stored: domain plus the existing HMAC, exactly as verify --identity already enforces. Rules: browser_ai_thread_sync_off_device (ai_thread or gemini_thread selected while account_class is consumer) and browser_personal_account_on_managed_device (consumer hosted_domain on a device in managed deployment mode).
desktop_surface: People view gains a browser row per seat showing account class, sync datatypes selected and a coverage denominator; Privacy Center's path receipts list the three pref keys read and show that only the domain and an HMAC were kept, with the raw address never entering the store.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/<Chromium root>/Local State -> profile.info_cache.<dir>.{hosted_domain,user_name,gaia_id,is_ephemeral}, signin.active_accounts_managed, management.platform.enterprise_mdm_mac; <Profile>/Preferences -> enterprise_profile_guid, sync.selected_types_per_account, sync.data_type_status_for_sync_to_signin.{ai_thread,gemini_thread}
honest_limit: Chrome's account state is per-profile and stale between flushes. A signed-out profile yields account_class 'unknown', never 'consumer'. The AI-thread sync flags say a datatype is SELECTED, not that a thread was uploaded — Vole sees the switch, never the traffic. Distinguishing a personal Workspace domain from a corporate one requires the ~/.vole/policy/identity.json declaration Vole already ships; without it the domain is recorded and the class stays unknown.
competitive_note: Nudge, Obsidian and Reco discover SaaS identity through API connectors and see nothing on the endpoint; this row is exactly the market's 67%-of-AI-access-on-corporate-devices-uses-non-corporate-accounts figure, measured on the device rather than inferred from an IdP.
v1_ref: Account-class classifier from the auth path
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: What per-employee attribution cannot establish, regenerated from the store
description: A shipped, enumerated and falsifiable statement of the limits of local attribution, generated from this machine's own counts rather than written as a disclaimer: there is no proof the OS user is the human at the keyboard; no SSO principal exists anywhere on disk; a Bedrock/Vertex session's IAM identity never appears in a transcript; OpenCode's account, account_state and control_account tables are empty here so 10,885 rows have no account of any kind; Grok yields a user_id on 38 log lines against 1,758 usage rows; Cursor's ai-tracking directory is empty so no team id exists; Devin's ACP stores carry no account; Antigravity offers only an installation_id; only 18 of 591 Claude transcripts and 12 of 66 Codex rollouts carry a per-session identity line; browser and web-chat AI use is out of scope entirely. A script regenerates the numbers in CI so the document cannot drift the way the eighteen doc-versus-code mismatches in the code map already have, and it renders as a panel as well as docs/IDENTITY-LIMITS.md so the claim travels with the product.
desktop_surface: Settings → Privacy → 'What Vole cannot know', linked from the People view's coverage strip and from every account-class badge tooltip.
data_source: Counts computed from ~/.vole/vole.db (session_identity, usage_events) and the artifact trees named; regenerated by a script wired into CI.
honest_limit: Correct only for the tools and versions Vole parses today — agent log formats are explicitly internal and version-unstable, so without the regeneration step this becomes the nineteenth stale claim. It is a statement about attribution, not about coverage; the Coverage screen carries the surfaces half and the two must be read together.
competitive_note: market.md §8 recommends an explicit scope statement as GTM material, and no vendor in the 62-row matrix publishes what its per-employee attribution cannot see. v1 has no equivalent artifact, and this is the fastest way through a security questionnaire and a works-council review.
field_verified: I re-measured all eight facts. CORRECT: OpenCode account / account_state / control_account = 0, 0, 0 rows against 10,885 opencode rows in Vole (both exact). Grok `grep -c user_id ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl` -> 38, against 1,758 grok rows (789 exact + 969 activity_only) -- exact. Antigravity ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/installation_id exists. WRONG: 'Cursor's ai-tracking directory is empty' -- ~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db is 73,728 bytes with six tables; it is ai_code_hashes that has 0 rows. WRONG: '12 of 66 Codex rollouts carry a per-session identity line' -- `grep -rlE '"(chatgpt_account_id|account_id)":'` over ~/.codex/sessions returns 0 files; all 66 carry only `"originator": "Codex Desktop"`, a client name. Codex identity lives outside transcripts in ~/.codex/auth.json (keys: auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY, tokens, last_refresh). STALE 4x: '18 of 591 Claude transcripts' -- today 72 of 634 files contain ownerAccountUuid.
constraint: None. Read-only script plus a doc plus a panel. It does interact with C12 for the panel.

name: vole whoami and the vole_identity MCP tool
description: The smallest surface that makes the whole lens testable: `vole whoami` prints the resolved principal and its source, machine_uuid plus current hostname, and one line per tool giving account_class, plan, truncated org id, binding_evidence and the artifact path that decided it. The same read model is exposed as an eighth MCP tool `vole_identity` beside the existing seven in cli/mcp.ts, so an analyst's own agent session can ask 'which account is this machine using for Codex' without a console. Both honour the policy gate: on a multi-principal store they return only the caller's own principal unless people_view is granted.
desktop_surface: Not an app screen: it is the CLI and MCP mirror of Settings → Identity, and the support path when the app shows an unexpected account badge.
data_source: principals, machines and session_identity, served through queries.ts like every other read model.
honest_limit: MCP exposure means an agent can read the identity table, so the tool must return truncated ids and must never expose auth_shape rows; and like every MCP tool here it runs with includeSeed=false and with no authentication beyond the stdio transport, so it inherits whatever trust the client has.
competitive_note: market.md's feature list calls for a 'read-only local MCP server over Vole's SQLite so analysts' sessions can query incidents and cost without any cloud'; identity is the first question such a session asks and no vendor answers it locally.
field_verified: Confirmed: cli/mcp.ts registers exactly seven tools — vole_summary (L21), vole_live_sessions (L27), vole_session (L43), vole_incidents (L54), vole_breakdown (L60), vole_whatif (L66), vole_digest (L72) — so 'an eighth MCP tool beside the existing seven' is accurate. serverInfo is hard-coded `{ name: 'vole', version: '0.1.0' }` at mcp.ts:94. IOPlatformUUID and hostname sources verified under feature 7; there is no existing whoami-shaped CLI to duplicate.
constraint: C17 (keep it local) — stdio MCP adds no egress, no conflict. C6 — note that getSessionDetail (queries.ts:399) already omits the source clause, so seed rows can already reach an MCP caller; the identity tool must not copy that pattern. The honest_limit's rule that vole_identity must never expose auth_shape rows is the right boundary and should be enforced by the read model, not by the tool's prompt text.

name: dlp_detectors: versioned detector pack with offline checksum validators
description: Detectors are rows, not code: dlp_detectors(id, pack_version, class, provider, keyword, regex, entropy_floor, validator, severity) compiled into the SEA from a Gitleaks/Betterleaks-shaped TOML, the way data/pricing.json is already frozen in at pricing.ts:55, so the rule set is inspectable and diffable rather than buried in a parse loop. Validators run entirely offline -- CRC32 tail check on GitHub gh[pousr]_ tokens, Luhn for PAN, mod-97 for IBAN, structural base64url decode for JWT keeping only whether alg/iss/exp parse, PEM header plus DER length sanity -- because entropy alone is a known false-positive engine (gitleaks#1830). Every sighting stores detector_id and pack_version, and bumping the pack sets dlp_scan_state.backfill_done = 0 for the affected sinks so history is re-scanned rather than history silently meaning something different. GitHub's published detector taxonomy supplies the class names so findings land in the vocabulary a security team already triages.
desktop_surface: Settings -> Detection: pack version, rule count by class, last pack change date and a 'rescan queued' badge with the bytes it will replay; every Data Exposure row shows the detector id and the pack version that produced it.
data_source: packages/core/data/dlp-detectors.toml (new, bundled into the SEA at build time like data/pricing.json); dlp_detectors table read once at collector start
honest_limit: No network verification, so a shape that passes a checksum is never claimed to be a live credential -- the UI says 'matched <detector>, checksum valid', never 'active key'. A rotated key and a working key are indistinguishable locally. A pack bump replays history through the byte budget, so a large rescan is visible as scan debt for hours, not instant.
competitive_note: TruffleHog, Gitleaks, detect-secrets and Kingfisher are all repo-oriented and none is agent-aware; their findings carry the secret value unless separately redacted. Shipping the rule table as data rather than code is what lets a customer diff what changed between two versions of Vole's verdicts, which no agent-security vendor offers.
v1_ref: Secret pattern scanner with entropy gate (secret_findings)
field_verified: Precedent CONFIRMED: pricing.ts:15 `import builtin from './data/pricing.json'`, with the header comment 'The rates live in a data file (./data/pricing.json), not in code, so new models can be added without a release' and a per-installation override at ~/.vole/pricing.json. So a data-not-code rule table is an established pattern here.
constraint: Constraint 14 (SEA: zero runtime dependency, node: builtins only, no dynamic require, no runtime file reads except the pricing override) — TOML CANNOT SHIP. Node has no TOML parser and esbuild has no TOML loader; pricing.json works only because esbuild inlines JSON natively. Reconciliation: author in Gitleaks-shaped TOML if you like, but convert to `data/dlp-detectors.json` at build time and `import` it, exactly as pricing.json does; a user override file needs the same explicit allowance pricing.ts already carved out. Constraint 3 (deterministic keys) — a pack bump resetting backfill_done must not silently rewrite prior verdicts; the widening upsert in the sightings feature is what makes a replay idempotent.

name: Leak Ledger screen
description: A Risk-group sidebar section listing secret sightings grouped by fingerprint, with columns class / detector / direction / provider / tool / first-seen / occurrences / status, filter chips for class, direction and status, and tabs splitting 'Sent to a model' from 'At rest'. The coverage strip is pinned above the list so an empty result can never be read as 'clean'. Per the read-model parity constraint the query is written twice — queries.ts and the DB.swift C-API port — and the app remains a read-only consumer of ~/.vole/vole.db.
desktop_surface: The screen itself, plus a critical-sighting count contributed to the menu panel's security strip so a leak is visible without opening the dashboard.
data_source: secret_sightings, dlp_coverage and dlp_egress tables via new queries.ts read models and their DB.swift ports.
honest_limit: The app cannot write to the store (DB.swift opens READONLY with a read-write fallback but performs no writes), so triage actions — mark fixture, mark rotated — go through the CLI until a write path exists: the screen shows status but does not set it. Grouping by fingerprint means a value seen under two HMAC key epochs appears as two unrelated rows, and every count is bounded by which content fields the scanner was consented to read.
competitive_note: The comparable screens all live in a vendor cloud console; the buyer objection Vole answers is 'not another console' — this one runs on the endpoint over a local SQLite file with no account and no tenant.
v1_ref: Secrets surfaced in MCP, CLIs, digest and the incident-response evidence bundle
field_verified: `secret_sightings`, `dlp_coverage` and `dlp_egress` do not exist — `.tables` returns only `anomalies collector_state usage_events`. The read-only claim is verified and correct: DB.swift:129-135 opens SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY and falls back to SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE, and no method in the file executes a write — every one of summary/timeseries/anomalies/breakdown/collectorLastSeen goes through `run()` which only prepares, binds and steps. So the honest_limit ('the screen shows status but does not set it, triage goes through the CLI') is not a workaround, it is the constraint correctly obeyed.
constraint: None broken, and the design respects the three that matter. Constraint 7: a ledger of fingerprints, classes, detectors and paths stores no content, which is the only shape a leak ledger can legally take in this product. Constraint 13: the app stays a read-only consumer, which is why triage is a CLI action. Constraint 6: the new tables need a source column and purge coverage — say so in the table spec. The fingerprint-across-HMAC-epochs caveat is a genuine limit and correctly stated.

name: key_residency: naming where else this key lives, so a spend gap stops being a mystery
description: Under consented repo roots, read deploy and CI manifests for references to provider key NAMES - .github/workflows/*.yml (secrets.X and env:), .gitlab-ci.yml, vercel.json, fly.toml, app.yaml, serverless.yml, docker-compose*.yml environment:, Dockerfile ENV/ARG, Terraform variable blocks and *.tfvars, and .env.production. Adds key_residency(repo, manifest_path, var_name, target_class IN ('ci','container','paas','iac'), first_seen, last_seen, source), joined to provider_keys on the variable name. Its whole purpose is one column on the reconciliation screen: where vendor spend exists that no local session explains, reconcile_gap and shadow_account_spend render 'this provider's key name is referenced by N off-endpoint targets, listed' instead of an unexplained delta - the METR shape stated as a fact rather than an alarm. On this machine .github/workflows reference secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, so any unattributed Anthropic spend already has a named, non-speculative candidate origin.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen: a 'possible off-endpoint origins' expander under any gap or not_comparable cell, listing repo, manifest path and target class. The same list appears as an 'Off this machine' block inside that key's row on the Shadow AI screen.
data_source: .github/workflows/*.yml, .gitlab-ci.yml, vercel.json, fly.toml, app.yaml, serverless.yml, docker-compose*.yml, Dockerfile, *.tf / *.tfvars, .env.production
honest_limit: A manifest reference is a reference, not a deployment: it cannot confirm the target ever received the key, cannot see the value, cannot distinguish a live workflow from one dead for a year, and cannot enumerate residencies that never touch this disk. It narrows a gap and never closes one - the cell stays not_comparable unless a reconciliation adapter says otherwise, and the count of candidates is never subtracted from the delta.
competitive_note: Console-side vendors (Anthropic Admin API, Cursor, Copilot) can show the spend and none can name where the key ran; gateway vendors see only routed traffic. No competitor produces the local artifact that names the off-endpoint candidates, which is the only honest half of the METR case a local-first product can hold.
gap_area: The un-instrumented AI: provider keys, SDK dependencies and homegrown code that writes no agent log

name: Exclusion enforced at open(), with a counted skip receipt
description: The covered exclusion floor defines what is out of scope; this defines where the decision is taken — before the first open() on a root, so an excluded root is never read rather than read and then filtered. Every repo read routes through one openRootFile(root, relPath) chokepoint that refuses an excluded root and refuses any relPath the manifest does not declare, with a self-check asserting the sweep opened nothing outside the manifest and nothing under an excluded root. Classification comes from ~/.vole/policy/scope.json (admin, managed mode) and ~/.vole/exclude.json (user, bounded by the never-excludable list), keyed on the origin owner where one exists: here four origins are launchsafe/* and one is shivanagendrakore/trivital, so an owner allowlist separates corporate from personal exactly. Adds work_roots.classification ∈ {in_scope, excluded_personal, excluded_policy, unclassifiable} with excluded_by naming the clause, and writes a repo_scan_state row with files_opened=0, bytes_read=0 and reason='excluded:<clause>' so the skip is auditable and the denominator never silently shrinks.
desktop_surface: The Repos band splits roots into readable / skipped-by-policy / unreadable with counts on each, and every skipped row names the clause that excluded it; the Privacy Center's path-receipt list gains the same rows, so a developer can prove their personal repo was never opened.
data_source: ~/.vole/policy/scope.json, ~/.vole/exclude.json; work_roots.origin_slug derived from <root>/.git/config [remote "origin"] url and ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite threads.git_origin_url
honest_limit: Classification needs an origin. Here 34 of 58 roots no longer exist and 13 of the 24 survivors resolve to no git root, so 'unclassifiable' is the majority state; in managed mode that must fail closed to excluded, which shrinks coverage and has to be printed as a coverage loss rather than hidden. A personal repo cloned from a corporate org, or a corporate repo cloned from a personal fork, is classified by origin owner and will be wrong — the classification is the policy's reading, never a fact about ownership.
competitive_note: Every SaaS-console vendor in the matrix — Cyberhaven, Nightfall, Harmonic, CrowdStrike — filters after ingest and stores prompts by default, so 'excluded' there means 'collected then hidden'. Vole is the only one where excluded can mean the file descriptor was never opened, and where the skip itself is a countable row.
v1_ref: Inalienable exclusion floor for personal work on a corporate device
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: answerable_from: the horizon that makes "not seen" an answer instead of a shrug
description: Computes, per (source × indicator_kind), the earliest timestamp at which a hunt over that ledger can return a truthful negative, plus the basis that produced the bound. Bases are read, never assumed: Claude Code's `cleanupPeriodDays` from settings.json/managed-settings.json (default 30 — the vendor's own on-disk `~/.claude/cache/changelog.md` records the sweep covering `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.claude/tasks/`, `~/.claude/shell-snapshots/`, `~/.claude/backups/`) checked against the real mtime span of the retained transcripts (655 files spanning 23 days on this machine); `npm config get logs-max` (10 here) bounding `~/.npm/_logs`; `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl` (56 rows) against `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` (66 files), where an index row can name a thread whose rollout is already gone; plus store_epoch, evidence_gaps and collector_runs. Adds `answerable_from(source, indicator_kind, earliest_ts, basis, basis_ref, computed_at)`, and every hunt verdict, count and export row carries the covered-days denominator from it. This is the table that turns the third verdict from a caveat into a computed figure.
desktop_surface: A horizon bar pinned above every hunt result and mirrored as a band on the Coverage strip: "answerable back to 15 Aug (23 d) — Claude transcripts 655 files; npm logs 10; MCP config backups 3; Codex rollouts 66 of 56 indexed threads". Each segment drills into the artifact list and the knob that set the bound.
data_source: ~/.claude/settings.json + managed-settings.json cleanupPeriodDays; mtime span of ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl; ~/.claude/cache/changelog.md (retention-sweep scope, read offline); npm config logs-max and ~/.npm/_logs; ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl vs ~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl; existing evidence_gaps, store_epoch, collector_runs tables
honest_limit: A horizon is the earliest evidence that still exists, not proof the evidence was complete then — a collector that was down inside the window is a separate evidence_gaps fact and the two must be read together. It also cannot see evidence a user deleted by hand, so the floor is a floor on answerability, never a guarantee of coverage above it.
competitive_note: market.md L133 names it as Vole's own handicap ("local evidence is deleted after 30 days by default", anthropics/claude-code#23710) — this converts the handicap into the product's differentiating figure. No competitor states its own retention: CrowdStrike Falcon AIDR's retention is "not stated", MintMCP quotes 90d-7y but only for gateway-routed agents, and Fleet/osquery answers "now" with no history at all (market-extracts competitor_matrix).
gap_area: Indicator retro-hunt: 'an advisory just named X — were we exposed, when, and what happened next'

name: Out-of-path scan engine: dlp_scan_state cursors, keyword prefilter and byte budget
description: A DLP scanner cannot reuse collector_state.last_offset: claude-code.ts:85 reads from that offset and commit() advances it after insert, so the day DLP ships the offset is already at EOF and zero history is ever scanned. New table dlp_scan_state(sink_id PK, kind, cursor_kind, cursor_text, cursor_int, inode, size_bytes, bytes_scanned, scan_debt_bytes, backfill_done, pack_version, last_run_at) with a cursor shape per sink: byte-offset+inode for JSONL, `id < :cursor` for OpenCode `part` (its ids are DESCENDING ULIDs, so an id cursor is a time cursor), (thread_id, updated_at_ordinal) for ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite, (mtime,size) for config sinks; a separate backfill_done flag lets the first run walk history from offset 0 without disturbing the usage collector's offsets or its commit-after-insert contract. Cost is bounded in the same pass: one combined RegExp of every detector keyword (sk-, ghp_, AKIA, xox, eyJ, -----BEGIN, password=) prefilters each raw line, only +/-256 bytes around a hit reaches the full rule set, and a per-pass byte budget (default 32 MB) caps the work with the remainder written to scan_debt_bytes so falling behind is a visible number rather than a silent gap. This corrects v1's instruction to watermark OpenCode on part.time_updated: verified today, that table has 46,584 rows in a 507 MB file with only part_session_idx and part_message_id_id_idx, so a time cursor full-scans the DB every poll and the id cursor is the only cheap one.
desktop_surface: Settings -> Data sources gains one row per sink: cursor position, bytes scanned, backfill progress bar, scan debt with estimated catch-up time, and an explicit 'never scanned' state; a persistent banner appears when debt grows for three consecutive passes. The same rows feed the coverage strip along the top of the Data Exposure screen.
data_source: ~/.vole/vole.db collector_state (existing, left untouched); ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl byte offsets plus inode; ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db part.id (verified 46,584 rows, 506,990,592 bytes, indexes part_session_idx and part_message_id_id_idx only); ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite thread_items.updated_at_ordinal (idx_thread_items_updated_page exists); new packages/core/src/dlp/scan.ts invoked from the cli/collect.ts:36-60 results loop
honest_limit: An in-place rewrite that preserves both size and inode is missed until the file grows. The OpenCode id cursor breaks if OpenCode ever changes its id scheme, so the scanner must compare id order against time_created each pass and fall back to a full scan flagged in coverage. A secret with no keyword and below the entropy floor (a short database password, an internal hostname, a customer name) is never reached, so the ledger prints findings beside a coverage figure and never prints 'clean'.
competitive_note: No competitor has this problem: everyone scanning coding agents (Cyberhaven, Nightfall, Harmonic, CrowdStrike) is in-path via a hook or endpoint sensor and sees data as it flows. Out-of-path is Vole's differentiator and a watermark table plus a byte budget is its price -- Nightfall's published ~50 MB / 1% CPU endpoint bar is exactly what a scanner blocking the 5 s poll loop would blow past, the failure mode the OSS claude-code-redaction-hooks author warns about.
v1_ref: Secret pattern scanner with entropy gate (secret_findings)
field_verified: Premise CONFIRMED in code: claude-code.ts reads `readNewLines(filePath, state?.last_offset ?? 0)` and `commit: () => { for (const [p, off, mtime] of pending) setState(db, p, 'claude_code', off, mtime); }` — a DLP scanner reusing that offset starts at EOF. OpenCode part table CONFIRMED: 46,584 rows, file 506,990,592 bytes, indexes exactly ['sqlite_autoindex_part_1','part_session_idx','part_message_id_id_idx'] — no index on time_created/time_updated, so v1's time watermark does full-scan. Codex `idx_thread_items_updated_page` CONFIRMED present. THE ID-CURSOR CLAIM IS FALSE: sorting part by id ASC gives time ASCENDING with exactly one backward jump — at `prt_073389eff001OAyEo8xcnRMu5P` (2026-09-05 20:18:05) -> `prt_e9d6cd504002YGNXXSNRC7gWRD` (2026-06-06 14:53:43). Ids ascend with time and the space has wrapped once, so `id < :cursor` walks backwards and stalls forever at the wrap. Measured `rowid` order: 0 time-inversions in 46,583 pairs. Also `select sum(length(data)) from part` = 136,777,096 — scannable content is ~137 MB, not 507 MB.
constraint: Constraint 6 (new tables must carry `source` and the seed/live partition) — dlp_scan_state is collector state, not observation; reconcile by mirroring collector_state, which carries no source column, and documenting state tables as exempt. Constraint 9 (commit only after insert) — the DLP cursor needs its OWN commit-after-write; it must not ride the usage collector's commit or a failed sighting insert silently advances the scan. Constraint 12 (add-nullable-column-only) — a brand-new CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in SCHEMA is how all three current tables ship, so no conflict.

name: Coverage and denominators: what Vole did not read
description: One shipped screen that refuses to let a partial number read as a complete one, on two axes. Structural blind spots become a versioned table with a live status probed cheaply at scan time: no Endpoint Security entitlement means no process-exec, per-process network flow or file-open events; no Full Disk Access means ~/Library/Safari/History.db, other users' homes and TCC-protected folders read as 'not granted' (one attempted read records which); encrypted stores (ChatGPT conversations-v2-* under a Keychain key, Antigravity .pb) yield mtime only; browser extensions, web chat and hosted agents (Copilot cloud, Codex cloud, Claude Managed Agents) leave nothing on the endpoint. Scan coverage becomes the view dlp_coverage(sink_id, day, bytes_available, bytes_scanned, files_missed, scan_debt_bytes, deleted_before_scan, oldest_unscanned_ts, pack_version) computed from dlp_scan_state against statSync sizes, so every DLP claim carries its denominator: 'zero findings across 94% of 1.24 GB; 71 MB unscanned; 3 files deleted before scan'. Sinks with no incremental cursor report bytes_available NULL rather than 0, and the app is forbidden from rendering an empty finding list without the strip.
desktop_surface: A 'Coverage' sidebar screen with two sections — blind spots (granted / not granted / n-a, expandable to the reason and the remediation such as grant FDA or deploy the PPPC profile) and per-sink scanned-versus-available bars; a coverage strip pinned above the Leak Ledger; a 'Coverage' block in vole digest; and a one-line footer on every summary and breakdown panel: 'Covers 9 of 22 known AI surfaces on this Mac — see Coverage'.
data_source: Probe results (attempted reads of ~/Library/Safari/History.db, /Users/*, ~/Library/Application Support/com.openai.chat); the shipped catalog of 22 tool profiles from market-extracts local_artifacts_by_tool as the surface denominator; dlp_scan_state joined to statSync sizes of ~/.claude/projects (627 MB here), ~/.codex/sessions (100 MB, 66 rollouts), ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (507 MB), ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl (5 MB).
honest_limit: The surface denominator is 'surfaces in Vole's catalog', not 'AI tools that exist', and the screen must say so or it becomes the overclaim it exists to prevent. 'granted' means one read succeeded at scan time, not that it will succeed later. bytes_available for a transcript already deleted by cleanupPeriodDays is unknowable — those rows carry only a deleted_before_scan count, so the percentage is explicitly of what still exists, never of what was ever written. The feature adds no detection of its own.
competitive_note: v1's coverage matrix reports per-tool freshness and backlog; neither the structural blind-spot list nor the DLP byte denominator appears in it, and no competitor publishes a coverage denominator at all. Every vendor in the 62-row matrix that claims coding-agent coverage states it as a checkmark; only Bifrost and Anthropic's own Compliance API docs admit their gaps in writing, and SASE and browser vendors quietly miss subscription-auth CLI traffic.
v1_ref: Collector self-health: collector_runs, vole doctor, coverage matrix, freshness attestation
field_verified: The blind-spot probe is REAL and I reproduced it: `ls -la ~/Library/Safari/History.db` shows 376,832 bytes, but `head -c 16 ~/Library/Safari/History.db` returns 'Operation not permitted' -- one attempted read distinguishes granted from not-granted, exactly as designed. Sizes today: ~/.claude/projects 647M, ~/.codex/sessions 100M (66 rollout files), ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db 496M, ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl 5.0M (the feature's 627M/507M are 3 days stale, shape correct). The 22-surface denominator is real: market-extracts local_artifacts_by_tool has exactly 22 entries. ChatGPT profile confirms 'conversations-v2-<uuid>/ encrypted with Keychain key ... Presence/activity (mtimes) only'. BUT dlp_scan_state does not exist, no DLP scanner exists, and collector_runs does not exist (roadmap-v1 L16 proposes it).
constraint: C1 (never invent a number) -- this feature IS the constraint made visible, and 'bytes_available NULL rather than 0' respects it correctly. C12 (read-model parity): a Coverage screen plus a strip above the Leak Ledger plus a footer on every summary panel means every query written twice, queries.ts and DB.swift. That is where the effort actually goes.

name: 'Where it landed' chain panel: six hops, each badged with its evidence rank
description: The brief asks for a jurisdiction column; a column cannot show that the answer was inferred four hops away. This draws one horizontal chain per selected leak or surface — session → principal → account/plan → endpoint/recipient → region → terms — with each hop carrying the badge of the evidence that produced it (measured / route-declared / pack-asserted / admin-authored / unknown), and drawing an explicit visual break where a hop is NULL rather than closing the line. The CCR case renders as session → shiva → api-key → raw IP 195.242.30.141 (unattributable) → region unknown → no terms entry, with the model label 'anthropic/claude-ccr-…' shown struck through beside a note that the label was not used. Read-only; every hop links to the file and byte offset that evidenced it.
desktop_surface: A panel on the Leak Ledger detail and on each Shadow AI surface card, plus the same chain rendered inline in an incident evidence bundle; hovering a hop shows the exact field name and file path, and a global 'show only chains with a break' filter on the Processing Register.
data_source: joins terms_basis, recipient_state, residency_rank, processing_terms and terms_overrides; every hop's evidence_ref points at an existing raw_ref path plus byte offset
honest_limit: The chain is only as honest as its weakest badge, and a chain rendered entirely in pack-asserted badges tells the reader nothing was measured — the UI must make that visually obvious rather than uniform. Requires the read-model to be written twice (queries.ts and DB.swift) or the app cannot draw it, and DB.swift must stay a read-only consumer. Nothing here can be clicked to act; it is an explanation surface.
competitive_note: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian ships a causal chain for agent actions but stops at the endpoint boundary; nothing in the matrix draws the chain outward to the receiving legal entity, because no competitor holds an entity table.
gap_area: AI-vendor processing register: where the data landed, under whose law, and on what default terms

name: secret_sightings ledger with a widening upsert, and the Data Exposure screen
description: v1's secret_findings would inherit Vole's INSERT OR IGNORE habit and freeze last_seen, occurrences and status at first sight exactly as db.ts:137 freezes anomaly severity today. Schema: secret_sightings(sighting_key UNIQUE, fingerprint, key_epoch, detector_id, pack_version, class, provider, tool, session_id, agent_id, direction, normalisation, sink_id, raw_ref, byte_offset, reached_model, first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts, occurrences, status, fixture_reason, source, user, machine) with an explicit ON CONFLICT(sighting_key) DO UPDATE SET last_seen_ts = max(excluded.last_seen_ts, last_seen_ts), occurrences = occurrences + 1 -- the widening the constraint list demands, since the tokens-only-grow upsert cannot express it. sighting_key = fingerprint + entry id + detector id and never contains now(), so re-scans are idempotent; source carries 'live'/'seed' and purge follows the usage_events partition. The screen renders one card per distinct fingerprint with class, direction, occurrences, sessions, agents, first and last sighting and a status chip, and its evidence link is the raw_ref pointer (file path plus byte offset) with Reveal in Finder, so the operator reads the value in the vendor's own log and vole.db never holds it.
desktop_surface: A new Data Exposure screen in the sidebar: coverage strip along the top, 'Sent to a model' and 'At rest' tabs, findings grouped by detector class with a severity rail, filter chips per direction. Drill-down shows the sighting timeline with the destination per sighting and Reveal in Finder / Mark rotated / Mark fixture with a required reason; a standing footer states that no prompt, tool argument or file content is stored in vole.db. Needs the DB.swift read-model port per the read-model-parity constraint.
data_source: packages/core/src/schema.ts (new table via the add-nullable-column migration path at db.ts:41-53); usage_events.raw_ref for the evidence pointer; sightings produced in the collector parse loops (claude-code.ts:91-99, codex.ts:118, opencode.ts:104, devin.ts:71, grok.ts:102)
honest_limit: occurrences counts appearances in transcripts, not API requests: Claude Code writes each assistant message 2-3 times as it streams, so the figure is an upper bound on transcript copies and says nothing about how many requests carried the value. No key is verified against its provider, so a card reads 'a string matching <detector>, checksum valid, at this offset', never 'a live credential leaked'. PII beyond checksum-gated patterns is reported as not detected, never as absent.
competitive_note: Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic all inspect and retain content, and none of the 27 coverage vendors states its prompt-retention posture. detect-secrets' hashed baseline is the nearest prior art and it is a flat file with no lifecycle. A published findings schema plus a pointer into the vendor's own log answers the security questionnaire's hardest question by construction.
v1_ref: Secret pattern scanner with entropy gate (secret_findings); also the surface half of 'Secrets surfaced in MCP, CLIs, digest and the incident-response evidence bundle'
field_verified: Both freeze bugs CONFIRMED verbatim. db.ts: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO anomalies (...)` — anomaly rows never update. db.ts usage_events upsert ends `WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens`, with the comment 'upgrades a stored row only when a later copy carries strictly more tokens' — that clause cannot express `occurrences = occurrences + 1`, so the explicit widening is genuinely required. migrate() CONFIRMED add-nullable-column only via `PRAGMA table_info` probing. usage_events.raw_ref CONFIRMED present in SCHEMA. The occurrences honest_limit is corroborated by the collector's own coalescing comment: 'Claude Code writes each message to the transcript several times while streaming; the first copy is a placeholder with output_tokens: 0.'
constraint: Constraint 7 (DB holds no content) — fingerprint + raw_ref + byte_offset is a pointer, compliant. BUT roadmap v1 #86 already flags '⚠ P5: do not expose raw_ref+offset to arbitrary agents by default'; reconcile by keeping the pointer in the desktop app and Reveal in Finder only, and never returning it from the MCP server. Constraint 13 (read-model parity: every query written twice, queries.ts + DB.swift) — DB.swift is 274 lines today and DashboardView.swift 709; a whole Data Exposure screen with a coverage strip, two tabs and a drill-down timeline is the single largest Swift addition in the shard.

name: Keychain-held fingerprint key with epoch rotation
description: v1 puts the HMAC key in ~/.vole/hmac.key, inside the home directory of the very agents Vole watches -- Claude Code Bash and Codex custom_tool_call demonstrably read dotfiles, and a stolen key turns fingerprints of low-entropy secrets into a brute-forceable rainbow set. Store 32 random bytes as a generic password item (security add-generic-password -a vole -s computer.vole.dlp -w) and read it once per collector start by spawning /usr/bin/security through node:child_process, which keeps the SEA zero-dependency and native-module-free as the bundling constraint requires. A key_epoch integer is stored alongside every fingerprint; rotating the key writes a new epoch and marks prior rows stale_fingerprint rather than pretending they still correlate.
desktop_surface: Settings -> Privacy: 'Fingerprint key: login keychain (epoch 1)', a Rotate button, and the count of sighting rows that would become uncorrelatable if rotated; the badge reads 'file (0600)' in red on any host where the keychain path was unavailable.
data_source: macOS login keychain via /usr/bin/security (spawn, no native module); ~/.vole/ holds the epoch integer only, never the key
honest_limit: Any process running as the same user can read the item once the ACL is granted, so this defends against file-scraping agents and repo scanners, not against malware already running as the user. On a non-macOS host the collector falls back to a 0600 file and records key_store='file' on every sighting so the weaker guarantee is visible rather than silent. Fingerprints from a previous epoch cannot be compared with current ones at all.
competitive_note: Every vendor that stores content off-device (Cyberhaven, Harmonic, Nightfall, CrowdStrike inline redaction) sidesteps this question by holding the value. Vole's entire answer to 'do you store prompts' is the fingerprint, so where its key lives is the load-bearing detail of the claim.
v1_ref: Secret pattern scanner with entropy gate (secret_findings)
field_verified: Mechanism precedents CONFIRMED: collect.ts:1 `import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'` and pr.ts:22 `execFileSync('git', a, {...})`, so spawning a system binary is established and needs no native module. Collector.swift CONFIRMED: the app spawns the collector itself — `let p = Process(); p.executableURL = exe; try p.run()` on Contents/MacOS/vole-collector — and `static let isEmbedded` distinguishes the bundled app from an unbundled `swift run` where start() is a no-op.
constraint: Constraint 14 (no native modules) is what forces the /usr/bin/security spawn, and that is the flaw: to let the collector read the item by spawning /usr/bin/security, the item's ACL must trust /usr/bin/security — a system binary ANY process can invoke — so every process running as the user reads the key silently. `Bash(security find-generic-password -s computer.vole.dlp -w)` is one line for Claude Code and strictly easier than reading ~/.vole/hmac.key. The stated threat model collapses. Reconciliation available today with no new dependency: the SIGNED, hardened-runtime Swift app holds the keychain item under its own code-signing identity (ACL trusts the app, not /usr/bin/security) and passes the key to the child through Process()'s environment or stdin — Collector.swift already owns that spawn. The unbundled dev path has no app to ask, so it falls back to the 0600 file and stamps key_store='file', which the feature already provides.

name: Pre-match normalisation layer with a provenance badge
description: Everything Vole scans is JSON, so a value arrives as \"sk-...\" with escaped quotes and newlines, and agents routinely percent-encode a token into a URL or base64 a file to move it -- naive regexes miss all three. Before matching, each candidate string passes through JSON unescape (free via JSON.parse), percent-decode, one level of base64 decode when a run of >=40 base64 characters decodes to printable ASCII, a zero-width and bidi character strip, and a homoglyph fold (the Rules File Backdoor class of hiding). The sighting's normalisation column records which transform exposed it (raw|url|b64|unicode), so a triager immediately knows whether the value was literally on the wire or was being smuggled.
desktop_surface: Data Exposure row badge: 'found after base64 decode' / 'found after URL decode' / 'found after zero-width strip' -- a strong signal on its own, and a filter chip so a CISO can list only encoded sightings.
data_source: claude-code.ts user-line content and content[].tool_use.input, codex custom_tool_call.input and function_call.arguments, opencode part.data.state.input -- all currently read into memory and discarded
honest_limit: One decode level only. A double-encoded, gzipped, encrypted, or split-across-two-messages value is not found; those bytes count toward scanned but the span is recorded as unscannable-shape rather than clean, so the coverage figure never overstates what was actually checked.
competitive_note: In-path scanners see the pre-serialisation value and never need this; a log-derived scanner does, and it is the difference between catching the 2025-07-28 Gemini CLI env-var exfiltration shape and missing it entirely.
field_verified: Every named input CONFIRMED with counts. Claude transcripts: `"type":"tool_use"` 23,147 and `"type":"tool_result"` 23,143 occurrences across ~/.claude/projects. OpenCode: `count(*) where json_extract(data,'$.state.input') is not null` = 12,292 and state.output = 12,201. The escaped-JSON premise holds structurally — every sink here is JSONL or a JSON `data` column. Encoded-credential shape CONFIRMED live: ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl carries `"key_prefix":"eyJ0eXAi"` — a base64url JWT head sitting in a log.
constraint: Constraint 7 explicitly permits this — 'DLP scanning happens on the raw line in the collector' — so normalising in-loop and discarding is compliant. The real conflict is INTERNAL, with feature 1: that feature's keyword prefilter runs on the RAW line, but a base64'd secret has no raw keyword, so the prefilter drops it before this layer ever runs and the encoded-exfiltration case — the entire point of this feature — becomes unreachable. Reconcile explicitly: the combined prefilter RegExp must also carry the encoded forms of its keywords (percent-encoded and the base64 encodings of 'sk-', 'AKIA', 'ghp_' at all three phase offsets), or the base64-candidate scan runs as a separate cheap pass with its own share of the byte budget.

name: Direction tagging normalised across all six content-bearing collectors
description: v1 tags direction from Claude entry shapes only, so every non-Claude sighting would be direction-NULL. The mapping table: Claude last-prompt.lastPrompt, user.message.content[].text and history.jsonl pastedContents -> human_pasted; assistant.message.content[].tool_use.input -> agent_typed; user.message.content[].tool_result.content plus toolUseResult.{stdout,stderr} -> tool_returned; assistant text blocks -> model_echoed. Codex: message.content -> human_pasted, function_call.arguments / custom_tool_call.input -> agent_typed, *_call_output.output -> tool_returned. OpenCode: part.data.state.input -> agent_typed, .state.output -> tool_returned; Devin content.rawInput vs user_message; Grok exec_done args. Direction is the whole difference between 'the developer pasted a customer key' (a training problem) and 'the agent read it out of a file' (a policy problem), and it is what makes the monthly count comparable to Netskope's benchmark.
desktop_surface: Filter chips per direction on Data Exposure, and a direction breakdown in the digest so the monthly figure a CISO benchmarks is split by who did it rather than being one aggregate number.
data_source: claude-code.ts:93 skipped user/last-prompt lines (56% of transcript bytes here); ~/.claude/history.jsonl (18 pastedContents entries verified); codex rollout function_call.arguments / custom_tool_call.input / *_call_output.output; opencode part.data.state.{input,output} (12,292 tool parts); devin messages.payload content.rawInput; grok exec_done ctx
honest_limit: Cursor and Antigravity expose no per-message direction at all, so their sightings carry direction = NULL rather than a guess. Claude's model_echoed is indistinguishable from a mirror-write of the same message, so echoes are deduped by message id and counted once. A value that arrives inside a tool_result the agent then retypes appears under two directions and is deliberately not collapsed.
