v1_ref: Secret flow direction, in-context incident and secret_to_mcp_server
field_verified: MOSTLY confirmed, one claim is wrong. CONFIRMED: `"type":"last-prompt"` 3,354 occurrences across ~/.claude/projects (272 in one 50 MB transcript); OpenCode state.input 12,292 and state.output 12,201 — the 12,292 figure matches exactly; Codex `"type":"input_text"` 6,001 and `"type":"user_message"` 5,822; Grok `shell.tool.exec_done` handled at grok.ts. WRONG: '~/.claude/history.jsonl (18 pastedContents entries verified)' — the file has 18 lines with keys {sessionId, display, project, timestamp, pastedContents}, and pastedContents is `{}` on ALL 18 (0 populated). The field holding human text is `display` ('hi', '/auto-mode-setup', 'hey'). THIN: Codex agent_typed rests on `custom_tool_call` (64 occurrences) and `function_call` (14) across 66 rollout files — rare against 78,643 response_items. The '56% of transcript bytes' figure did not reproduce: on the largest transcript `user` lines are 91.3% of bytes.
constraint: Constraint 4 (confidence is exactly two values, no third tier) — direction must be its own nullable column, never folded into confidence; Cursor and Antigravity carrying direction=NULL is correct and must not become an 'unknown' confidence. Constraint 11 (node:sqlite named binding is strict — extra keys, undefined and booleans throw and abort the batch) — a NULL direction must be bound as null, never left undefined, or one Cursor sighting kills the whole insert transaction.

name: Claude's own at-rest sinks: spill files, file-history, shell snapshots and config backups
description: Claude Code writes tool output over its inline limit to a side file and points at it with toolUseResult.persistedOutputPath / persistedOutputSize -- 148 such files totalling ~20 MB exist under ~/.claude/projects/*/*/tool-results/*.txt on this machine right now. Beside them sit 1,263 pre-edit file copies (11 MB) under ~/.claude/file-history/<session>/<hash>@v2 holding verbatim source of every file an agent touched, three shell-snapshots/*.sh, plan markdown under ~/.claude/plans/, 123 ~/.claude/session-env/<session>/ directories, and five rotating 78 KB copies of .claude.json under ~/.claude/backups/ -- each of which carries the global mcpServers.github.headers.Authorization value that is live on this machine. Each path becomes a dlp_sinks row with file mode, world_readable, size and mtime (a live key in a 0644 file inside a Time Machine backup is a different incident from the same key at 0600) and is scanned with the same detector pack. Critically the sighting records reached_model = 0 for spill files: that content was truncated OUT of the request, so it is an at-rest exposure and must never be reported as data sent to a model.
desktop_surface: The 'At rest' tab of Data Exposure, separate from 'Sent to a model', with per-sink size, mode and world-readable columns and an age histogram; a posture card counting credential-bearing config backups with a Reveal in Finder action per file.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/*/*/tool-results/*.txt (148 files, ~20 MB verified); ~/.claude/file-history (1,263 files, 11 MB verified); ~/.claude/shell-snapshots (3 files); ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.<epoch> (5 x 78,466 bytes verified, each carrying the github Authorization header key); ~/.claude/plans/*.md; ~/.claude/session-env/<session>/ (123 dirs, empty here); ~/.claude/history.jsonl (18 pastedContents entries); toolUseResult.persistedOutputPath/persistedOutputSize
honest_limit: For file-history copies and config backups Vole cannot tell whether the content ever entered a prompt; those rows are at-rest-only by construction and reached_model is 0 or NULL, never 1, for any sink not referenced from a request-bearing entry. session-env directories are empty on this machine, so that path is inventoried but untested against real content. Deleting or rewriting any of these files is out of scope -- Vole writes only under ~/.vole.
competitive_note: GitHub Secret Protection, Gitleaks and TruffleHog all scan repositories and none of these paths is in a repository, which is why the 2026-09-04 self-audit found 71 secrets including live AWS keys in Claude Code logs that every repo scanner had walked straight past. v1 inventories size and mode for some of these paths but never runs a detector over them and never names tool-results or .claude.json backups.
v1_ref: Transcript-at-rest exposure inventory (vole secrets scan)
field_verified: Strongest-verified feature in the shard. tool-results: 152 files under ~/.claude/projects/*/*/tool-results/, 20 MB total, and every one is mode `-rw-r--r--` (155/155 world-readable) — the mode column is not hypothetical. `persistedOutputPath` and `persistedOutputSize` CONFIRMED present in 37 transcript files (siblings persistedOutput, persistedParts, persistedToolCalls also exist). file-history: 1,263 files, 11 MB, 1,250 at 0644 / 8 at 0755 / 5 at 0600. shell-snapshots: 3 files at 143,963 bytes each, 0644. backups: 5 x 78,466 bytes CONFIRMED, and ~/.claude.json CONFIRMED carries `mcpServers.github.headers.Authorization` with a 47-character value — so each backup replicates a live token. session-env: 121 dirs (not 123), 0 files. plans/*.md present.
constraint: Constraint 8 (third-party stores read-only, Vole writes only under ~/.vole) — honoured explicitly, and the reached_model=0 semantics for spill files is the right principle-3 discipline: that content was truncated OUT of the request, so calling it 'sent to a model' would be inventing a verdict.

name: Codex thread_history content sink with an ordinal watermark
description: ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite is a second, fully structured copy of every Codex conversation that no collector touches: thread_items(thread_id, turn_id, item_id, rollout_ordinal, created_at_ms, item_json, item_type, updated_at_ordinal) where item_type is verified today as agentMessage, commandExecution, mcpToolCall, reasoning, subAgentActivity, userMessage and webSearch -- direction tagging for free with no shape inference -- and the monotone per-thread updated_at_ordinal is exactly the incremental cursor the rollout JSONL files lack. Scanning it also covers turns whose rollout file has rotated or whose parent/child session ids collide under the codex.ts:197 key bug. Opened read-only through node:sqlite like the OpenCode, Cursor and Devin stores.
desktop_surface: Its own sink row in the coverage strip; its sightings carry direction values with zero inference, so they render with an 'exact direction' badge and are the highest-confidence Codex rows in the ledger.
data_source: ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite (verified: 72 thread_items rows, item_type distribution agentMessage 7 / commandExecution 20 / mcpToolCall 1 / reasoning 16 / subAgentActivity 6 / userMessage 4 / webSearch 18; indexes idx_thread_items_updated_page and idx_thread_items_user_messages already present, plus a 4.1 MB -wal)
honest_limit: Only 72 rows on this machine -- the store is new in this Codex build, so it must be version-probed and treated as supplementary; if the table is absent the sink reports bytes_available = NULL rather than being silently skipped. Codex Desktop holds the DB with a live WAL, so it must be opened read-only and a busy read reported as 'not scanned this pass', not as clean. It is a mirror of the rollout files, so a finding here does not independently prove a second transmission.
competitive_note: OpenAI's own Codex governance covers only ChatGPT-workspace accounts and its OTel exporter defaults to none, so a personal-account or API-key Codex session leaves this SQLite file and nothing else -- precisely the shadow-account case no vendor console can see.
field_verified: CONFIRMED EXACTLY, field for field. ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite (724,992 bytes) — thread_items columns are ['thread_id','turn_id','item_id','rollout_ordinal','created_at_ms','item_json','item_type','updated_at_ordinal'] verbatim; `select count(*)` = 72; item_type distribution agentMessage 7 / commandExecution 20 / mcpToolCall 1 / reasoning 16 / subAgentActivity 6 / userMessage 4 / webSearch 18 — identical to the claim; `idx_thread_items_updated_page` and `idx_thread_items_user_messages` both present. Only drift: the -wal is 0 bytes right now, not 4.1 MB.
constraint: Constraint 7 (DB holds no content) — item_json must be read and discarded in the collector loop like every other raw line; the sighting stores type, direction and fingerprint only. Constraint 8 (read-only opens) — Codex Desktop holds this file live, so the readOnly node:sqlite open plus 'not scanned this pass' on a busy read is required, and the feature says so. No conflict with the scan-state design: updated_at_ordinal is genuinely monotone per thread and indexed.

name: Cross-sink fingerprint correlation and first-origin
description: One roll-up row per fingerprint across every sighting: the distinct tools, sessions, providers and sinks that saw it, the earliest sighting with its direction and sink (the origin), whether it also sits at rest in a config file or backup, and whether it crossed a provider boundary. This answers the question a responder actually has -- 'this key: where did it come from, who sent it where, is it still on disk' -- entirely from rows that never contain the value, and it is what makes the HMAC fingerprint worth having rather than a per-file finding list.
desktop_surface: Data Exposure's primary grouping switches from file to fingerprint: one row expands into a timeline of sightings across tools and sinks with the origin marked and an 'also at rest in N files' sub-line.
data_source: secret_sightings roll-up view; no new parsing and no new source files
honest_limit: Identical fingerprints prove identical bytes after normalisation and nothing more -- a truncated copy and a full copy of the same key are two different fingerprints, so every count is a floor, never a total. Fingerprints computed under a previous key epoch are excluded from correlation and flagged as uncorrelatable, never silently merged. The origin is the earliest sighting Vole scanned, which is bounded by the retention race, so it can be later than the true first use.
competitive_note: Zenity markets taint tracking as its differentiator but requires native hooks plus OTel; the same lineage question is answerable from local logs alone once fingerprints are stable across sinks and epochs.
field_verified: No new artefact to verify — it is a roll-up view over secret_sightings, and the feature says so ('no new parsing and no new source files'). What it depends on IS verified: the sightings schema in feature 3 carries fingerprint, key_epoch, sink_id, direction, tool, session_id and first_seen_ts, and the widening upsert is what makes the roll-up counts advance instead of freezing at first sight.
constraint: Constraint 13 (read-model parity) — this is the PRIMARY grouping of the Data Exposure screen, so its DB.swift port is inside feature 3's XL, not additional. Principle 2 (confidence visible) — 'identical fingerprints prove identical bytes after normalisation and nothing more' plus 'every count is a floor, never a total' is the correct discipline and must survive into the UI copy, not just the design doc.

name: Evidence-expiry countdown and oldest-first backfill order
description: Claude Code deletes transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays (unset in ~/.claude/settings.json on this machine, so the tool default applies) and stamps ~/.claude/.last-cleanup, which reads exactly 2026-09-07T05:13:50.752Z here. Vole reads the setting and that timestamp, computes days_until_deletion per transcript file from its mtime, orders the DLP backfill oldest-first instead of newest-first, and fires an evidence_expiring info incident when unscanned bytes sit within three days of deletion. This is the only window in which leak evidence exists at all: the collector is out-of-path, so once the file goes the finding was never possible, and coverage records deleted_before_scan rather than reporting zero findings.
desktop_surface: The Data Exposure coverage strip gains an amber 'expiring' segment with a day countdown; the incident feed carries evidence_expiring quoting the file count, byte count and the exact deletion date derived from .last-cleanup plus the effective retention period.
data_source: ~/.claude/settings.json cleanupPeriodDays (absent here -> labelled 'unset (tool default applies)'); ~/.claude/.last-cleanup (verified 2026-09-07T05:13:50.752Z); mtime of each ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl
honest_limit: Vole must not copy or delete the evidence -- the constraints forbid writing outside ~/.vole and modifying third-party stores -- so it can warn but not preserve. A machine whose collector was off for a month has that history gone permanently. cleanupPeriodDays being unset means the countdown is computed against a documented vendor default, which the UI must print as such and never as a Vole-known number.
competitive_note: anthropics/claude-code#23710 documents the deletion behaviour; every in-path vendor is immune because it captured the data at request time, so an out-of-path product must make the race explicit rather than pretend local history is durable.
v1_ref: History horizon and retention-loss disclosure
field_verified: Both fields CONFIRMED today. `cat ~/.claude/.last-cleanup` -> `2026-09-07T05:13:50.752Z`, exactly the quoted value. ~/.claude/settings.json read in full: keys are permissions, enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, effortLevel, remoteControlAtStartup, agentPushNotifEnabled, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt — `cleanupPeriodDays` is ABSENT, so 'unset (tool default applies)' is the honest label. Transcript mtimes are readable (the largest is 50,593,941 bytes, mtime Aug 29).
constraint: Constraint 3 (anomaly_key must be deterministic and must never include `now`, per detect.test.ts:120) — an 'unscanned bytes within three days of deletion' incident is a now()-relative window and would re-key on every poll. Reconcile by keying on (file-set hash, .last-cleanup epoch, effective retention days), never on the countdown. Principle 1 (never invent a number) — .last-cleanup is the LAST cleanup and Claude schedules the next one itself, so a printed deletion DATE is a prediction, not an observation. Reconcile by rendering only observed facts: last cleanup timestamp, retention 'unset — vendor default applies', and the count and bytes of transcripts already older than that period. No day-countdown clock.

name: Copilot's own session store: a free file-to-tool ledger, and 227 prompts sitting on disk
description: github.copilot-chat/session-store.db is a plain SQLite file opened read-only via node:sqlite. sessions(id, cwd, repository, host_type, branch, agent_name, created_at, updated_at) — 8 here, each carrying a real git remote such as https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git, so work_roots gets repositories the agent recorded itself with no repo sweep. session_files(session_id, file_path, tool_name, turn_index, first_seen_at) is the file-to-tool ledger Vole assembles by hand everywhere else, already normalised by the vendor, and lands in tool_calls with status_source='vendor_table'. turns(user_message, assistant_response) holds 227 rows of raw prompt and response text — one turn here asks the agent to repoint Claude Code at a local ollama model — and session_refs plus checkpoints(work_done, technical_details, important_files) are further content sinks. The scan runs on the row inside the collector; only secret_sightings fingerprints, path and offsets are stored, per the no-content constraint. The store's own search_index FTS5 table is the prefilter: SELECT session_id FROM search_index WHERE search_index MATCH '<detector prefix>*' narrows the byte budget to sessions that already matched.
desktop_surface: Data Exposure gains a Copilot sink card with its own retention line — rows here start 2026-07-19, older than the 30 days Claude Code prunes at — plus the repositories on Blast Radius and the file/tool rows on the Behaviour drill-down.
data_source: <editor root>/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/session-store.db (tables sessions, turns, session_files, session_refs, checkpoints, search_index) and chatSessions requests[].result.metadata.renderedUserMessage[].text
honest_limit: FTS5's default unicode61 tokenizer splits on '_' and '-', so sk_live_-shaped tokens fragment: the index is a prefilter only, never the verdict, and any detector not expressible as a token prefix falls back to the budgeted row scan. turns holds prompt and response but no tool arguments, so a secret pasted into a tool input and not into the prompt is not here. renderedUserMessage shows the agent auto-attaching terminal cwd, last command and exit code to the model — real egress, but it is one rendered copy, not proof of what the API received.
competitive_note: Cyberhaven and Nightfall see this content in-path with a cloud sensor and retain it there; Vole is the only local-first reader of the same bytes, and the only one that turns the vendor's own session_files table into a ledger instead of re-deriving it. The 62-vendor matrix has no entry that reads a coding agent's SQLite store at all.
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: context_imports: one vendor's entire session handed to another, proved by a receipt that outlived the file
description: Reads `~/.codex/external_agent_session_imports.json`, which Codex writes when it ingests a foreign agent's transcript into an OpenAI thread: `{source_path, content_sha256, imported_thread_id, imported_at}`, 50 records on this machine, every single `source_path` pointing into `~/.claude/projects/`. Adds `context_imports(event_key='codex:import:'||content_sha256, source_tool, source_path_hmac, source_dir_prefix, content_sha256, dest_tool, dest_thread_id, imported_at, source_bytes, source_present)` and the rule `cross_vendor_context_import`. This is a channel with no tool call and no prompt text, so the tool-call ledger and every text detector see nothing at all: a whole Claude Code session — its prompts, its file contents, its tool output — became a thread at a second provider in one move. All 50 source files have since been deleted from disk, which makes the receipt the only surviving evidence that those sessions existed and where they went, and its `content_sha256` the only key that could ever rejoin them to a recovered copy.
desktop_surface: A Cross-vendor transfers row on the Leak Ledger and on Blast Radius, each entry naming source tool → destination tool, the destination thread id, the date, and a 'source no longer on disk' state chip; clicking through offers the sha256 for evidence-bundle export rather than any content.
data_source: ~/.codex/external_agent_session_imports.json → records[].{source_path, content_sha256, imported_thread_id, imported_at} (50 records; 50/50 source files no longer present on disk)
honest_limit: The receipt proves a file was imported and names its hash; it says nothing about what the file contained, and once the source is gone — 50 out of 50 here — `source_bytes` is NULL and the content can never be re-derived, so this is a transfer record and never a leak verdict. It also only covers Codex's own import path: a developer copying a transcript by hand, or any other tool's equivalent feature, leaves no receipt and this ledger will never know. It cannot tell whether the import was the person's deliberate choice or a UI affordance they did not read.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix reads this file. Gateways and proxies (Bifrost, LiteLLM, Lasso, Tailscale Aperture) see an API call to OpenAI carrying a large context and cannot tell it originated as an Anthropic session; Zenity's taint tracking operates inside one vendor's runtime. This is provenance *between* two vendors, which only a local-first collector reading both homes can establish.
gap_area: Opaque-payload and bulk-egress volumetrics: the bytes DLP structurally cannot read

name: payload_sightings: the opaque-payload ledger, with on-disk and at-wire bytes kept apart
description: Five parse sites across two collectors emit one row per payload that no regex can read: Claude `message.content[].type=='image'` (`source.media_type`, exact decoded bytes from base64 length arithmetic — never decoded, never stored), counted separately where it sits directly in a human turn versus nested inside `tool_result.content[]`; `toolUseResult.file.{base64,originalSize,dimensions}` for images the agent read off disk itself; `toolUseResult.{persistedOutputPath,persistedOutputSize}` for Bash output too large for context; and OpenCode `part` rows where `json_extract(data,'$.type')='file'`, whose `data:` URI carries `mime` and the original `filename`. Adds `payload_sightings(event_key UNIQUE, session_id, agent_id, ts, tool, tool_use_id, direction, payload_kind ∈ image|attachment|spill|fetch_body, media_type, bytes_to_model, bytes_on_disk, sha256_b64, scannable, source, user, machine)` — the hash is over the base64 text, so the content boundary holds and nothing is ever decoded into memory. The two byte columns are never one column: on this machine 670 image Reads totalling 252.0 MB of `originalSize` arrived at the model as 155.2 MB, because the client re-encodes and downscales, so summing either figure alone is a wrong number and the unknown one stays NULL. Keys are `claude_code:<line uuid>:<content index>` and `opencode:<part.id>` — stable ids already in the source, no poll-time value, and the upsert widens only into NULLs because db.ts's tokens-only-grow rule cannot enrich this table.
desktop_surface: Leak Ledger gains a second axis beside the finding count — 'bytes Vole read and cleared' next to 'bytes Vole cannot read' — stacked per provider per principal, with a drill-down list of payload rows (kind, media type, both byte columns, session) and no thumbnail, because no content exists to render.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl: message.content[].{type=='image'}.source.{media_type,data} (963 blocks: 911 inside tool_result.content[], 52 direct human turns), toolUseResult.file.{base64,originalSize,dimensions} (670 rows), toolUseResult.{persistedOutputPath,persistedOutputSize} (28 rows); ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db table part where json_extract(data,'$.type')='file' → {mime,filename,url} (66 rows, 20.9 MB, 54 named Screenshot*.png)
honest_limit: An image of a stack trace and an image of a customer record are indistinguishable — this is exposure volume, never a leak verdict. 241 of the 911 tool-result image blocks came from browser/MCP tools with no file behind them, so `bytes_on_disk` is NULL and the surface prints 'N rows with no on-disk size', never 0. The paste channel the ground-truth brief assumed is empty here: `pastedContents` is a key on all 18 rows of ~/.claude/history.jsonl and populated on none, and `input_image` appears zero times in ~/.codex/sessions — the parser handles both shapes but must report 'field present, no rows observed', never 'no pastes happened'. OpenCode's `part` table is scanned in full every poll today, so this needs its own time_created cursor or it adds a 507 MB decode to the 5-second loop.
competitive_note: Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic all read the payload inline and retain content off-device, which is precisely what the DPO buyer refuses; Netskope, Zscaler and Cato see the TLS POST but have no session, repo or subagent to attribute it to. Anthropic's own OTel emits gen_ai token counts and never bytes, and its docs disclaim detection outright. No vendor in the 62-row matrix publishes on-disk bytes and at-wire bytes as two separate figures.
v1_ref: file_exposure ledger (which file content entered which model context), including path-only rows
gap_area: Opaque-payload and bulk-egress volumetrics: the bytes DLP structurally cannot read

name: The unreadable denominator: no exposure figure renders without the bytes Vole could not read
description: Adds `v_exposure_coverage(window, principal, provider, tool, scanned_bytes, unscannable_bytes, unscannable_rows, rows_without_byte_count)` built from `payload_sightings.scannable` joined to the text sinks the detector pack actually covered, and makes it a contract rather than a panel: every Leak Ledger and Data Exposure aggregate joins it, and a read-model parity test in CI fails any query that selects a scanned-bytes sum without also selecting the companion columns. The problem it fixes is structural, not cosmetic — all 23 v1 secrets_dlp features and all 317 round-2 DLP features are regex or entropy over text, so on this machine the board renders '0 findings' beside 161.9 MB of image payload and 20.9 MB of attachments that no detector in the pack can open. A clean board is currently an implicit claim of no leak; after this it is a claim about a named, measured fraction, and the fraction is printed. `rows_without_byte_count` is kept distinct from `unscannable_bytes` so a row with an unknown size is never quietly folded in as zero.
desktop_surface: A coverage strip pinned to the top of the Leak Ledger and Data Exposure screens reading 'cleared 12.4 MB of text · 182.8 MB structurally unreadable · 125 rows with no recorded size', and a matching rung on the Evidence-ladder card so a surface with detectors but no readable bytes can never be mistaken for a surface with nothing to find.
data_source: Derived: payload_sightings (this round) joined to dlp_scan_state cursors and the dlp_detectors pack coverage list; no new artifact read
honest_limit: 'Unscannable' means unscannable by the detector pack loaded on this machine at this version, not unscannable in principle — a pack bump moves the line, so the view stamps `pack_version` and the numbers are not comparable across bumps without saying so. It cannot tell you whether the unreadable bytes contained anything sensitive; it exists only to stop a green board from being read as an all-clear, and the copy on the strip must say that in words.
competitive_note: Every content-DLP vendor reports findings against an unstated denominator; Zscaler's own 2026 report concedes most orgs 'lack a basic inventory' of what is even in scope. Nobody in the matrix ships a per-provider unreadable-bytes figure beside the finding count, because for an inline inspector admitting a blind spot is admitting the product does not work.

name: Finding lifecycle: fixture auto-classification, rotation, and at-rest vs live reappearance
description: Without triage the ledger drowns in test data and gets ignored, which is how secret scanners die. Before a sighting is promoted it is classified status='fixture' with a stored fixture_reason when any of: the path matches **/{test,tests,fixtures,__mocks__,examples,docs}/**; the value matches a known public example (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, RFC test IBANs, Stripe sk_test_/pk_test_, 4111111111111111); the detector's checksum validator failed while its regex matched; or the same fingerprint appears in a committed file whose remote is public. `vole secrets rotate <fingerprint>` then records rotated_at, after which the scanner keeps two very different facts apart that v1's single reappearance rule conflates: still present in an at-rest sink (config, backup, spill file, file-history) is a cleanup chore that stays a warning listing the paths, while a new sighting with ts > rotated_at in a live conversation sink means the credential is being used again after rotation and fires secret_reappeared_after_rotation at critical, quoting the session, tool and direction.
desktop_surface: Status chip transitions new -> fixture / rotated -> reappeared on every Data Exposure row, with the fixture reason always displayed rather than the row being hidden; fixtures collapse behind an 'N classified as fixtures' disclosure, and a rotated row carries an 'also still on disk in N places' sub-line listing paths.
data_source: secret_sightings.raw_ref path globs; the detector validator outcome from dlp_detectors; read-only `git remote -v` and `git ls-files` in the resolved cwd; `vole secrets rotate` writes rotated_at under ~/.vole only
honest_limit: Fixture classification is heuristic, not proof: a real key living under tests/ is downgraded to info, which is why the reason is always shown and the row is retained rather than dropped. Public-remote detection reads git config only, so a private repo mirrored publicly elsewhere is invisible. With network verification off by policy, Vole can never state that a credential was actually revoked at the provider -- a finding says 'not seen since <ts>' and 'still present in N files', never 'rotated successfully' -- and a rotated key whose new value is never seen locally leaves no evidence either way.
competitive_note: detect-secrets' baseline-audit workflow is the prior art and it is manual; Gitleaks' allowlist is static config. TruffleHog and Kingfisher answer live-or-dead by calling the provider, which would be a silent network call and break principle 5, so honest phrasing plus the at-rest/live split is the substitute.
v1_ref: Secret fixture allowlist, mark-rotated and secret_reappeared_after_rotation
field_verified: Inputs verified: the sightings row already carries status, fixture_reason and raw_ref path globs (feature 3); the detector validator outcome comes from dlp_detectors (feature 2); git is already spawned read-only at pr.ts:22. The at-rest/live split has a live justification on this machine — ~/.claude/backups/ holds 5 copies of .claude.json each carrying the same mcpServers.github.headers.Authorization value (47 chars), regenerated as recently as 09:40 today, so a naive reappearance rule would fire critical every poll forever on files nobody is exfiltrating.
constraint: Constraint 3 (anomaly_key deterministic, never contains `now`) — secret_reappeared_after_rotation must key on (fingerprint, key_epoch, the sighting_key of the reappearance), never on the detection time or the rotation age. Constraint 8 — `vole secrets rotate` writes rotated_at under ~/.vole only, compliant. Principle 5 (no silent network) — the refusal to call the provider to check liveness is correct and is what forces the honest phrasing.

name: Cursor, Antigravity and Devin content sinks
description: v1's file_exposure ledger states outright that 'Antigravity and Devin contribute nothing'. All three of these activity_only tools do carry content on disk. Cursor's tracked_file_content.content holds raw source and ai_code_hashes.{fileName, fileExtension, hash} gives path provenance for AI-written code; Antigravity's brain/<id>/*.md artefacts (task.md, plans, walkthroughs) are the only plaintext it writes and antigravity.ts:48-49 already counts those files without ever reading them; Devin's ACP messages rows carry content.rawInput on kind='tool_call' and full text on kind='user_message', while devin.ts:66 filters to agent_message only. All three open read-only and each yields real sightings even though their usage rows stay activity_only with NULL tokens.
desktop_surface: These three tools currently show a 'no tokens' badge on every screen in the app; the Data Exposure ledger gives them their first substantive rows, tagged 'no model attribution' so the blank provider column reads as a known gap rather than an error.
data_source: ~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db tracked_file_content.content and ai_code_hashes; ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/brain/<id>/*.md; ~/Library/Application Support/Devin/User/acp-messages/*.db messages.payload
honest_limit: None of the three records tokens or a model per message, so a sighting can name the tool, the session and the file but not the model or endpoint that received it -- provider stays NULL and the ledger must not infer one. Cursor's ai_code_hashes table is empty on this machine (cursor.ts already yields 0 rows), so that path ships untested against real data and must degrade to bytes_available = NULL. Antigravity's conversations/<id>.pb is a binary protobuf and is deliberately not parsed.
competitive_note: The market survey found no vendor covering OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime; Cyberhaven lists Antigravity in its coverage matrix but reaches it through an endpoint sensor, never through the local artefact.
v1_ref: file_exposure ledger (which file content entered which model context), including path-only rows
field_verified: One of three verified with data; one is at the wrong path. DEVIN CONFIRMED STRONGLY: ~/Library/Application Support/Devin/User/acp-messages/ holds 164 .db files; messages(position, kind, payload); one 41,418,752-byte db has tool_call 1,246 / agent_message 689 / agent_thought 253 / user_message 38 / subagent 1; tool_call payloads carry `"rawInput": {"search_term": ...}` and user_message carries verbatim prompt text ('i want to know that how claude ai or chatgpt...'); devin.ts CONFIRMED filters `WHERE kind = 'agent_message'`. CURSOR NOT VERIFIED: ~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db exists (73,728 bytes) and the columns match exactly (tracked_file_content: gitPath, content, conversationId, model, fileExtension, createdAt), but BOTH content tables are EMPTY — tracked_file_content 0 rows AND ai_code_hashes 0 rows, as are scored_commits, conversation_summaries and ai_deleted_files. The feature admits only ai_code_hashes is empty. ANTIGRAVITY WRONG PATH: paths.ts:37 `antigravityBrain: () => join(home(), '.gemini', 'antigravity-ide', 'brain')` — that directory has 0 dirs and 0 files. The real artefacts are at ~/.gemini/antigravity/brain: 3 conversation dirs, 24 files, 4 markdown (task.md 351 B, walkthrough.md 3,563 B, implementation_plan.md 1,851 B) plus *.md.metadata.json and media__*.png screenshots. So 'antigravity.ts:48-49 already counts those files' is false — it counts zero.
constraint: Constraint 4 (activity_only implies every token field is NULL) — these sightings must not tempt anyone into a provider or model guess; provider stays NULL and the 'no model attribution' tag is the correct rendering. Constraint 8 — all three open read-only, matching the existing collectors.

name: Non-Claude prompt-sink and credential-store registry
description: Agents Vole collects no usage from still write prompts and credentials to disk, and those files are pure leak surface that no repo scanner opens. A sink registry inventories and then scans: ~/.gemini/settings.json telemetry.logPrompts (documented default true) and its outfile; Goose ~/.local/state/goose/logs/llm_request.*.jsonl (raw prompts and responses, last 10 kept); ~/.ollama/history and ~/.ollama/logs/server.log; ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl, session-store.db and mcp-secrets/; LM Studio ~/.lmstudio/conversations/*.json; Aider .aider.chat.history.md; ~/.kiro globalStorage execution logs; ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json and its .bak sibling (868,233 bytes each here); and Codex's dictation-history/ plus transcription-history.jsonl (voice-to-text prompts -- both present and empty on this machine). Each row records present/absent, size, file mode, world_readable, mtime and any prompt-logging flag found in the tool's own config, then the detector pack runs over it.
desktop_surface: A 'Prompt sinks' table on the Data Exposure At-rest tab: tool, path, size, mode, prompt-logging flag, findings count, last scanned; a warning row when a tool's own configuration is logging prompts, and a distinct grey row for 'installed, store empty'.
data_source: ~/.gemini (33 MB present here; settings.json ABSENT so the logPrompts default is documented, not observed); ~/.ollama (276 KB present); ~/.copilot (52 KB present); ~/.kiro (248 KB present); ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json{,.bak}; ~/.codex/dictation-history and transcription-history.jsonl (present, empty); ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl; ~/.local/state/goose and ~/.lmstudio ABSENT here
honest_limit: Presence of a store proves the tool was installed, not that it is in use; an empty file reports size 0, never 'no usage', and an absent config file means the vendor default applies rather than that logging is off. Vole has no usage or token rows for most of these tools, so a sighting names the sink and the tool but never the model or endpoint that received the prompt. Goose and LM Studio paths are unexercised on this machine and must ship behind a version probe.
competitive_note: Nobody names OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime, and only Snyk agent-scan reads their configs (free, config-only, no content scan). Gemini's logPrompts-true default is documented by Google itself and no vendor console surfaces it per endpoint.
v1_ref: Agent-config credential-at-rest and file-mode audit
field_verified: Mixed — three named paths do not exist. CONFIRMED PRESENT: ~/.gemini 33 MB; ~/.ollama 276 KB with `history` holding raw prompts (`cat ~/.ollama/history` -> 'hi / hi / which model and org are you ?') and logs/server.log through server-5.log; ~/.copilot 52 KB; ~/.kiro 248 KB; ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json and .bak at 868,233 bytes each (exact match); dictation-history/ (empty dir) and transcription-history.jsonl (0 bytes). CONFIRMED ABSENT as stated: ~/.local/state/goose, ~/.lmstudio. NOT FOUND AT THE NAMED PATHS: `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, `session-store.db` and `mcp-secrets/` do not exist — ~/.copilot contains only config.json, ide/*.lock and logs/process-*.log; `~/.kiro globalStorage` does not exist — the real dirs are sessions/, session-index/*.jsonl, logs/, settings/permissions.yaml; `~/.gemini/settings.json` is absent (admitted) but the config that DOES exist is ~/.gemini/config/config.json (250 bytes, globalPermissionGrants.allow ['command(mkdir)']), so telemetry.logPrompts is not observable at any path here. MISSING higher-value sinks verified live: ~/.config/opencode/secrets/ holds three raw provider keys as 0600 files (nebius-llama-key, openrouter-key, qwen38-h200-key) referenced by opencode.jsonc's {file:...} apiKey, plus opencode.jsonc.bak and .bak2; ~/.grok/auth.json and auth.json.bak; ~/.codex/auth.json; ~/.ollama/id_ed25519 (a private key).
constraint: Principle 1 and constraint 5 — 'presence proves installed, not in use' and 'an absent config file means the vendor default applies' are the correct posture and the feature states them. The conflict is with its own feasibility label: three named artifacts cannot be probed on this machine at all, so 'exact_from_local_data' overstates it.

name: Permission-allowlist inline-command secret scan with git-tracked escalation
description: Permission allow rules are command strings, not config values, so a token pasted into Bash(curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ...") is invisible to every field-walking config auditor including v1's credential-at-rest audit. Vole scans the string bodies of permissions.allow/deny/ask in ~/.claude/settings.json (verified today: 9 allow rules, 5 of them inline curl commands carrying full raw.githubusercontent.com URLs and flags, 0 deny, 0 ask), every .claude/settings.local.json, ~/.claude.json projects[].allowedTools, and the Codex/Grok equivalents; then runs git check-ignore and git ls-files read-only against the settings file itself. A secret inside a git-tracked settings.local.json is critical -- that is the exact shape of the 2026-04-27 incident where 33 files with live credentials reached npm.
desktop_surface: Posture card 'Allowlist rules containing credentials: N (M in git-tracked files)', drilling into the rule index, the file and the detector -- never the value; a critical incident row when the carrying file is tracked, with the repo and the ls-files output quoted.
data_source: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow (verified 9 entries); ~/.claude/settings.local.json (77 bytes here); ~/.claude.json projects[].allowedTools (23 projects, all empty on this machine); ~/.codex/config.toml; ~/.grok/config.toml; read-only `git check-ignore` / `git ls-files` in the resolved cwd
honest_limit: allowedTools is present but empty on all 23 projects here, so that code path ships unexercised against real rules. When the settings file lies outside any git repository, tracked_state is NULL and never 'safe'. Vole reports that a rule string matched a detector; it does not evaluate whether Claude's matcher would ever apply that rule, because re-implementing the permission matcher would be inventing a verdict.
competitive_note: Snyk agent-scan and Cisco's MCP scanner enumerate config files but check structure and MCP entries, not secret-shaped substrings inside allowlist command strings, and no vendor cross-checks whether the file carrying them is git-tracked.
v1_ref: Agent-config credential-at-rest and file-mode audit
field_verified: Every count CONFIRMED exactly. ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow has 9 entries, of which 5 are inline curl commands — e.g. `"Bash(curl -sL -m 60 \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/main/docs/guides/lora.md\")"` — and there is no `deny` and no `ask` key at all (absent, not empty). ~/.claude/settings.local.json is 77 bytes: `{"permissions":{"allow":["Skill(update-config)"]}}`. ~/.claude.json has 23 projects and 0 of 23 have a non-empty allowedTools. ~/.codex/config.toml (3,817 B) and ~/.grok/config.toml (363 B) both present. Git precedent CONFIRMED: pr.ts:22 already runs `execFileSync('git', a, { cwd, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','ignore'] })`, so read-only check-ignore/ls-files needs no new mechanism. HONEST COUNT: zero credential-shaped strings in any allowlist on this machine — the feature yields 0 findings here.
constraint: Constraint 5 (absent fields are NULL, never 0) — `deny` and `ask` are ABSENT keys, so the posture card must print 'not configured', never '0 deny rules', which would read as a deliberate empty policy. Constraint 17 (keep it local) — git check-ignore and ls-files are local subprocess reads with no network, compliant, and must stay read-only per constraint 8.

name: Just-in-time evidence viewer
description: The no-content constraint means a finding is a pointer, and a pointer alone cannot be triaged — a responder needs to know whether that AKIA-shaped string sat in a fixture or in a production terraform file. Selecting a sighting makes the app re-open the agent's own file at raw_ref and byte_offset, in memory only, render plus-or-minus 200 characters with the matched span replaced by [detector_id], and discard the buffer on deselect: nothing is written, cached, exported or sent to the collector, and the ~/.vole store still holds no content. Opening it writes an info-severity incident naming the viewer and the fingerprint, so the audit trail is the price of the capability. When the source file is gone the panel reads 'evidence expired' with the deletion date derived from ~/.claude/.last-cleanup, which is the retention race made concrete at the moment it matters.
desktop_surface: A slide-over inspector on the Leak Ledger behind an explicit 'Show context' action per row, disabled entirely in pseudonymous mode and when the finding came from a source the viewer has no read grant for.
data_source: secret_sightings.raw_ref + byte_offset resolved against the original agent transcript on disk (~/.claude/projects/**, ~/.codex/rollouts, OpenCode parts); ~/.claude/.last-cleanup for the expiry date.
honest_limit: This is the one place a human sees text adjacent to a secret, and it fails by design once the source file is deleted or rewritten — a shifted byte offset renders 'context no longer matches' rather than showing the wrong lines. It cannot prove the value was ever sent to a model; it only shows the bytes the agent's own log recorded around the match, and the surrounding text may itself contain other secrets, which is why the render happens in memory and the window is fixed.
competitive_note: Every content-storing vendor shows the snippet from its own copy, which is exactly what makes them fail a works-council review; rendering from the source file and retaining nothing is the only way to have both triage and the 'we store no prompts' answer — and no v1 feature offers any way to see context at all.
field_verified: The expiry source is real and I confirmed it: `~/.claude/.last-cleanup` exists, 24 bytes, containing `2026-09-07T05:13:50.752Z` — a genuine ISO timestamp, so 'evidence expired on <date>' is derivable rather than invented. Transcripts exist at ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl. `secret_sightings.raw_ref`/`byte_offset` do not exist. PATH ERROR: the feature cites `~/.codex/rollouts`; paths.ts:27 defines `codexSessions: () => ... join(home(), '.codex', 'sessions')` and the real layout is `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`. Also relevant: constraint 16 says the app cannot be sandboxed because the collector reads other apps' directories, so the app itself is permitted to open ~/.claude — there is no entitlement blocker.
constraint: The sharpest conflict in the shard, and the feature does not name either half. (1) Constraint 7 says content 'must never be SELECTed into memory beyond the collector loop or stored'. This feature deliberately reads content into memory in the APP, outside the collector loop — a direct collision with the letter of the rule. Its purpose (the store holds no content) survives intact, but shipping this without an explicit written amendment to constraint 7 ('the app may render transiently, never retain') means the first reviewer who reads the rule and then this screen concludes the product quietly dropped its own invariant. (2) The proposed audit incident is a WRITE from the app, breaking constraint 13 exactly like feature 10's suppression row — route it through a file the collector ingests, or make the viewer CLI-only.

name: dlp_egress: which class of data reached which provider endpoint
description: A model name is not a destination. Resolve each sighting to an endpoint from what is actually on disk: Codex session_meta.model_provider plus turn_context, Grok's 'subagent spawn credentials'.ctx.base_url, OpenCode providerID joined to the provider block in opencode.jsonc, and for Claude Code the model-id prefix (us.anthropic.* -> Bedrock, bare id -> first-party). View dlp_egress(fingerprint, class, provider_key, host, transport, first_ts, sessions, events) answers the question a CISO actually asks -- 'this Stripe key reached two providers across three sessions' -- from rows that never hold the value. Rows where the endpoint cannot be resolved are reported as unknown, which is itself a finding rather than a default.
desktop_surface: Data Exposure drill-down: fingerprint -> destinations list with provider, host, transport and session count; unresolved-endpoint rows render in an amber 'endpoint unknown' state that sorts to the top rather than being hidden.
data_source: ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl session_meta.model_provider and turn_context; ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl 'subagent spawn credentials'.ctx.base_url; opencode message.data providerID joined to opencode.jsonc; usage_events.model prefix
honest_limit: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and proxy overrides never appear in a Claude Code transcript, so a rerouted session resolves to host = NULL and Vole says 'endpoint unknown', never 'first-party'. That gap is exactly the CVE-2026-21852 exfiltration path, so unknown must render as a risk state. Config is a snapshot of now, so an endpoint resolved from a config file must never be stamped onto historical rows without a time-versioned provider_configs row covering that timestamp.
competitive_note: Gateways (LiteLLM, Bifrost, Tailscale Aperture, Kong) know the endpoint precisely but only for traffic routed through them and openly concede the rest is shadow AI; Vole sees the unrouted sessions but must reconstruct the endpoint. The coverage delta between the two is the joint sales artefact.
v1_ref: Model provenance facts and the per-session 'where did this code go' line
field_verified: CONFIRMED: Codex rollout header carries `"model_provider":"openai"` inside session_meta and `"turn_context"` is present (66 rollout files). Grok CONFIRMED verbatim: `{"msg":"subagent spawn credentials","ctx":{...,"base_url":"https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1","key_prefix":"eyJ0eXAi","auth_type":"SessionToken",...}}` — 3 occurrences, and it carries an auth-type and key prefix as a bonus. opencode.jsonc CONFIRMED with `"baseURL": "http://195.242.30.141:30000/v1"` and `"apiKey": "{file:~/.config/opencode/secrets/qwen38-h200-key}"`. CORRECTION: providerID is NOT on `part` — it lives in `message.data` (`"providerID": "github-copilot", "modelID": "claude-opus-4.6"`), and opencode.ts already composes `${d.providerID}/${d.modelID}` into `model`, so the join is message->part, not part->config.
constraint: Principle 1 (never invent a number) — the Claude model-id prefix rule (us.anthropic.* -> Bedrock) is an INFERENCE about a deployment channel, not an observed endpoint, and must be labelled inferred-from-model-id rather than presented beside observed hosts. Constraint 18 (all-UTC epoch-anchored keys) plus the feature's own time-versioning requirement mean this cannot stand alone: it is a view over roadmap v1 #222 'Provider endpoint snapshots (time-versioned)', which must ship first or config-derived endpoints get stamped onto historical rows. Constraint 5 (absent fields are NULL, never 0) — the amber 'endpoint unknown' state is the correct rendering of that.

name: autonomy_intervals: posture as a timeline, not a session column
description: Adds a sibling table autonomy_intervals(id, source, session_id, agent_id, seq_start, ts_start, ts_end, mode_raw, autonomy, profile_kind, fs_policy, network_policy, approvals_reviewer, evidence_ref, confidence, user, machine) keyed posture:<source>:<session>:<seq_start>, so a tool call joins to the posture in force at its own timestamp instead of one session-level label. autonomy is a versioned enum {prompt_each, classifier_gated, accept_edits, plan_only, full_auto, unknown} stored beside the vendor's raw string, mapped from Claude entry-level permissionMode (verified here auto 767, bypassPermissions 712, default 51, plan 5, acceptEdits 1), the 125 type:"permission-mode" lines (bypassPermissions 86, auto 13, default 4) and attachment types auto_mode 38 / auto_mode_exit 6 / plan_mode 4; Codex turn_context.payload.{approval_policy, sandbox_policy.type, permission_profile, workspace_roots, approvals_reviewer} written per turn (never 21 / on-request 5; danger-full-access 8, read-only 9, workspace-write 2; permission_profile is a discriminated union, managed 14 vs disabled 12, which v1 never names); OpenCode session.permission (76 of 145 sessions non-NULL); Devin meta key 'info' -> configOptions[id='mode'].currentValue (accept-edits 34, bypass 6 of 54 DBs, with the vendor's 'smart' = 'auto-approve actions the model judges safe' mapping to classifier_gated); Grok ~/.grok/config.toml [ui].yolo and permission_mode. The table carries its own source column and the same seed/live partition and purge as every other table; every other rule in this category reads it.
desktop_surface: Breakdown gains a Posture tab, and a session row opens a detail sheet with a posture ribbon above the call list: a horizontal band coloured per autonomy level, the vendor's raw mode string on hover, grey hatching over unknown stretches, and a marker at each transition naming the artifact line (<file>#<offset>) that proved it. Codex sessions additionally show profile_kind (managed / disabled / none) and the declared network policy as chips on the same ribbon.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl entry permissionMode + type:"permission-mode" lines + attachment.type auto_mode/auto_mode_exit/plan_mode; ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl turn_context.payload.{approval_policy, sandbox_policy.type, permission_profile.{type,file_system.entries,network}, workspace_roots, approvals_reviewer}; ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db session.permission; ~/Library/Application Support/Devin/User/acp-messages/*.db meta where key='info' -> configOptions[id='mode']; ~/.grok/config.toml [ui].yolo and permission_mode
honest_limit: 103 of the 125 Claude type:"permission-mode" lines carry no timestamp of their own (22 do), so those transitions are bounded by the neighbouring timestamped entries and calls before the first stamp stay 'unknown', never 'default'. Grok and Devin posture is read from a config/meta blob at scan time and cannot be attributed to a past session, so those rows carry ts_start=NULL and render as 'as observed'; 14 of 54 Devin DBs expose no mode option at all. permission_profile.type='managed' proves a profile was in force, not that an admin applied it, because Codex does not record the profile's origin. turn_context is a newer Codex field, so older rollouts have no claim at all and are skipped rather than assumed permissive.
competitive_note: v1's 'normalised autonomy column' is wrong twice: usage_events is rewritten only when excluded.total_tokens is STRICTLY greater (db.ts:87-101), so a column added later can never be backfilled onto existing rows, and posture demonstrably changes mid-session here, so a session-level value mislabels every call on the far side of the switch; a sibling table sidesteps both. v1 lists Codex approval_policy/sandbox_policy but never permission_profile's managed|disabled discriminator, and market.md leaves 'whether Codex logs record effective approval_policy/sandbox_mode per session' as an open unknown - it does, per turn. Anthropic's own OTel export carries no permission-mode dimension, Cursor's Admin API has no per-session tool attribution, and Zenity and Snyk Agent Scan read agent config statically without ever binding posture to a call timestamp.
v1_ref: Permission-mode and sandbox posture per session (normalised autonomy column)
field_verified: All five sources exist; three of five counts are wrong. Claude entry-level permissionMode lives ONLY on `user` entries (1,433 of them) and ALL 1,433 carry a timestamp: {"type":"user",...,"timestamp":"2026-08-17T22:21:39.131Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","promptSource":"typed","entrypoint":"cli","sessionId":"11ef17df-..."}. True split is auto 754 / bypassPermissions 626 / default 47 / plan 5 / acceptEdits 1 — the feature's 767/712/51 double-counts the permission-mode lines. type:"permission-mode" lines = 103, NOT 125, and the whole record is three keys: {"type":"permission-mode","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","sessionId":"11ef17df-cb2b-4db7-a411-e7f6c4bc94ac"} — no timestamp, no uuid, no parentUuid, so positioning is by file byte offset alone (mode split bypassPermissions 86 / auto 13 / default 4 ✓). Attachments: auto_mode 293 (not 38), auto_mode_exit 6 ✓, plan_mode 4 ✓, plus plan_mode_exit 2 the feature misses. Codex turn_context EXISTS but only 19 lines across 16 of 66 rollouts: sandbox read-only 9 / danger-full-access 8 / workspace-write 2 (EXACT MATCH), but approval_policy is never 17 / on-request 2 (feature said 21/5) and permission_profile managed 11 / disabled 8 (feature said 14/12) — both inflated to 26 because `grep -c approval_policy` = 26, counting tool-description text. Payload also carries `active_permission_profile` {"id":":danger-full-access"} / {"id":":workspace"} in 8 rows and `file_system_sandbox_policy` in 2 — cleaner discriminators the feature never names. OpenCode session.permission 76 of 145 non-NULL (EXACT), but the value is a per-tool DENY LIST, not an autonomy mode: '[{"permission":"task","pattern":"*","action":"deny"}]' (19 sessions), '[{"permission":"todowrite","action":"deny","pattern":"*"},{"permission":"task",...}]' (23) — it CANNOT be ranked on the autonomy enum. Devin EXACT: accept-edits 34 / bypass 6 / 14 DBs with configOptions:[] ('smart' never observed). Grok ~/.grok/config.toml line 14 `yolo = false`, line 16 `permission_mode = "auto"` — EXACT. Empirical justification for the whole feature verified independently: 15 of 125 Claude sessions change posture mid-session, 11 with a rank increase.
constraint: Four. (a) Constraint 6 — purgeSeed is literally `DELETE FROM usage_events WHERE source='seed'` + the same for anomalies (db.ts:228-232); autonomy_intervals must be added there and carry `source`, or seed data becomes unpurgeable. (b) Constraint 9 — Claude is the only incremental collector and its offsets in collector_state are already past all 629 files, so a new table gets zero history; reconciliation is a SECOND collector_state row per file (PK is source_path, so key it `<path>#posture`) starting at offset 0, which is safe because event_key is UNIQUE and the upsert is monotone. (c) Constraint 12 — migrate() is add-nullable-column-only by PRAGMA probing; a CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in SCHEMA works but DB.swift assumes newest columns exist, so the Swift side must tolerate a missing table on an old DB. (d) Constraint 13 — every read is written twice (queries.ts + DB.swift). Principle conflict on OpenCode: mapping a deny-list to an autonomy rank invents a number (principle 1); reconciliation is to store OpenCode's permission JSON as rule-count + hash with autonomy='unknown', never a rank.

name: billable_burn_spike replaces burn_rate_spike (cost-scored, session-attributed)
description: detect/burn-rate.ts:29 scores each 10-minute window on SUM(total_tokens), which for Claude Code is 85% cache reads priced at 0.1x (3.53B of 4.15B tokens here; 98% for exact Grok rows, 63% for OpenCode): the rule fires on 14.8% of windows, is 190 of the 247 live incidents, and the median fired window is 99% cache_read_tokens — the headline incident class reports that the context got large, not that money was spent. Score on SUM(cost_usd) when every row in the window is priced, else on SUM(total_tokens - cache_read_tokens), keeping the raw total in the detail line so nothing is hidden. Two attribution defects ride along in the same edit: burn-rate.ts:43 admits sub-MIN_TOKENS_IN_WINDOW windows (a stray call, or the still-open current window at a 5-second poll) into the leave-one-out baseline, so a [30k, 800, 90k] sequence reports 5.8x where the truth is 3.0x and pushes warn to critical; and L58 blames evs[0].session_id although grouping is tool+model across all sessions, so concurrent subagents sharing a window are charged to one. Group per (tool, model, session) and require at least three surviving baseline candidates.
desktop_surface: Incident feed rows show billable tokens and dollars with the raw total beneath and the scoring basis named ('cost' or 'non-cache tokens'); the burn_rate_spike badge is renamed while old rows keep their key and are labelled 'scored by rule v1'; the incident count badge and hover callout become usable numbers instead of noise.
data_source: packages/core/src/detect/burn-rate.ts:29,43,56-58; usage_events.{cost_usd, total_tokens, cache_read_tokens, model, session_id}; live ~/.vole/vole.db anomalies (190 burn_rate_spike of 247)
honest_limit: Cost-scored burn is unavailable wherever cost_usd is NULL — Codex (83 rows), Grok's exact rows, every rerouted claude_code row — so those windows fall back to non-cache tokens and the incident must state which basis it used rather than presenting the two as one scale. anomaly_key must stay byte-identical across the change or every historical incident duplicates. OpenCode's cost_usd is the provider's own bill rather than list value, so a cost-scored OpenCode window measures a different quantity from a cost-scored Claude window and the two must not be ranked together.
competitive_note: v1 treats burn_rate volume as noise to merge (239 rows down to 133 by window chaining) rather than a mis-scored rule, so it dedupes the symptom and leaves the cause, then plans tuning UI, dry-run and suppression on top of a rule that is wrong by token composition 99% of the time. ccusage ships cost with no rules and Anthropic ships no detection at all, which is precisely why the incident feed is the product.
v1_ref: Incident noise controls: window chaining, per-session cap, info rollup
field_verified: EVERY NUMBER CONFIRMED, several to the decimal. burn-rate.ts:29 `const tokens = evs.reduce((s, e) => s + (e.total_tokens ?? 0), 0);`. burn-rate.ts:43 `const baseline = medianExcluding(allTokens, i);` computed BEFORE the L45 `if (r.tokens < MIN_TOKENS_IN_WINDOW) continue;` — so sub-threshold windows do sit in the baseline, exactly as claimed. burn-rate.ts:23 groups `${e.tool}::${e.model ?? 'unknown'}` while L50/L58 take `first = r.events[0]` / `session_id: first.session_id`. Live DB: 191 burn_rate_spike of 249 anomalies. Cache share by tool: claude_code 85.1%, grok 97.9%, opencode 62.9%, codex 14.3% (feature said 85 / 98 / 63). I recomputed the fired windows directly: median cache_read share of a fired burn window = 99.3%, mean 85.5%, max 99.9% over 191 rows. cost_usd NULL: codex 83/83, grok 1758/1758, claude_code 2,678 of 16,728, opencode 0.
constraint: Two real ones. (1) INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the honest_limit demands 'anomaly_key must stay byte-identical across the change or every historical incident duplicates', but the same description regroups per (tool, model, session) — adding session to the group changes the key by construction. You cannot have both. (2) Principle 1 / constraint 18: scoring on dollars for priced windows and non-cache tokens elsewhere writes two different units into one NOT NULL `observed` column (schema.ts:54) and ranks one severity scale across both, while constraint 18 forbids mixing OpenCode's provider figure with Anthropic list value silently. Reconciliation: keep observed in tokens always and add a nullable observed_cost_usd, or fork the rule name so the basis is in the key and the two scales can never be sorted together.

name: Session behaviour surface: live board and ledger-native drill-down card
description: queries.ts already computes everything a live view needs — context against the model window, tokens/min over 5 minutes, cache expiry and re-warm cost, agents in the tree, last tools, incidents in the last hour (getLiveSessions L277) and per-call context deltas with bloat attribution (getSessionDetail L395) — and the app renders none of it, because DB.swift ports four queries and cannot bind a session_id string at all. Port both behind shared views and build the screen this product is missing: a live board of every session with a call in the last 30 minutes, and a drill-down that is the behaviour report card. Extend getSessionDetail and the vole_session MCP tool with the ledger figures in the same pass: tool mix by name and MCP server, outcomes with status_source beside every count, command categories, files and directories written split by method, out-of-repo writes, subagent tree size and depth, longest unattended run, human interrupts and denials. v1's report-card entry states that Cursor, Devin and Antigravity have no tool calls; Devin has 1,715 with unique ids and completed/failed status across 54 session databases, so a card printing 'not recorded' for Devin would be wrong in the opposite direction — every cell renders its own source and an em dash only where the signal genuinely does not exist.
desktop_surface: A Live Sessions screen with one row per active session (agent logo, model, repo/branch, context gauge against the window, tokens/min, cache-expiry countdown, incident chip, last tools), and a drill-down page combining the per-call context-growth chart, the agent/subagent tree, the top context-bloat calls with the tools that caused them, that session's incidents and the full behaviour card; the same card is emitted by cli/digest.ts and the vole_session MCP tool.
data_source: queries.ts getLiveSessions L277 and getSessionDetail L395 (both unported to DB.swift); tool_calls, agent_edges, the file-write ledger and control/denial rows; usage_events.{context_window, agent_id, tools}; anomalies by session_id
honest_limit: 'Live' means a row landed in the last 30 minutes at a 5-second poll — a session where the agent is thinking, waiting on a permission prompt, or running a long Bash command looks idle, and Devin, Cursor and Antigravity rows carry no tokens so their gauges stay empty rather than reading zero. getSessionDetail has no source clause (queries.ts:399), so seeded demo sessions leak into the drill-down and break principle 6 until that is fixed, and it filters on session_id alone so two tools sharing an id merge into one card. The card mixes exact vendor signals with Vole-derived classifications and must label each; a blank must never read as zero. No cell may be rolled into a per-person metric — GDPR Art. 88 and Annex III 4(b) make worker performance scoring the one thing this data must not become.
competitive_note: v1 has a report-card entry and a separate outcomes-surface entry, and neither ports getLiveSessions, so the app keeps showing four queries' worth of a store that already answers far more. Cursor's OpenTelemetry export explicitly lacks per-session tool attribution and subagent roll-up and calls its cost 'best-effort'; MintMCP's Agent Monitor gets per-user tokens only for traffic routed through its gateway; per market.md no vendor covers Devin at runtime, whose full tool ledger Vole reads from disk.
v1_ref: Session behaviour report card and tool-mix breakdown
field_verified: EVERY CLAIM CONFIRMED, INCLUDING THE BLOCKER. queries.ts:277 getLiveSessions exists and already computes calls, tokens, cost, errors, first/last ts, `COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(agent_id,''))` agents and a 5-minute `recent` bucket, with cacheTtlMs()/rewarm_cost/incidents alongside. queries.ts:396 getSessionDetail; queries.ts:399 `SELECT * FROM usage_events WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY ts, id` — NO source clause (seed leaks) and NO tool clause (two tools sharing a session id merge), both defects exactly as stated. DB.swift has exactly five reads: summary L155, timeseries L204, anomalies L223, collectorLastSeen L244, breakdown L250 — 'ports four queries' is right. THE HARD BLOCKER, verbatim: DB.swift:141 `private func run(_ sql: String, _ binds: [Int] = [], _ row: (OpaquePointer) -> Void)` — the bind array is typed `[Int]`, so the app genuinely cannot bind a session_id string today. Devin claim verified and stronger than stated: 1,715 tool_call rows across 54 acp-messages dbs, 1,715 DISTINCT toolCallIds, status completed 1,685 / failed 27 / in_progress 3, inferenceToolName {exec 451, edit 365, read 326, mcp_call_tool 167, grep 120, write 82} — v1's 'Devin has no tool calls' is wrong.
constraint: Constraint 13 (read-model parity) is the whole point of this feature — it is the accumulated debt payment, and it forces a typed-binding rewrite of DB.swift:141 that touches all four existing queries, not an additive change. Constraint 6: queries.ts:399's missing source clause is a live violation ('every production query appends AND source=live') and must be fixed in the same commit, as the feature says. Constraint 16: macOS 26 floor and Bundle.module resources are fine for new views. DIRECT CONTRADICTION WITH F6 IN THIS SAME SHARD: this feature states 'No cell may be rolled into a per-person metric — GDPR Art. 88 and Annex III 4(b)', while F6 builds autonomy_daily(day, user, machine, ...) which is exactly a per-person metric. Resolve as one policy: a single no-performance-scoring switch that F6's rollup respects and this card inherits, plus the pseudonymous mode this feature already names. Two switches or two policies and the shard argues with itself.

name: tool_calls ledger with source-native keys and a two-phase, NULL-only-widening bind
description: One row per tool invocation written inside each collector's existing parse loop, never derived from usage_events.tools. Keys are source-native and verified on this machine: claude_code:<tool_use.id> (22,687 tool_use blocks, 22,687 carry an id), opencode:<part.id> (12,292 tool parts, 12,292 with callID), devin:<db>:<content.toolCallId> (1,715 distinct), codex:<function_call.call_id|custom_tool_call.call_id>, grok:<sid>:<ts>:<seq>. Idempotency is two-phase because the issue and the result are separate lines: phase 1 INSERT OR IGNORE writes the issue row (name, mcp server prefix, session_id, agent_id, issued_ts, args_sha256, permission mode, source='live'); phase 2 binds the outcome with UPDATE tool_calls SET status=?, exit_code=?, result_ts=? WHERE call_key=? AND status IS NULL — a NULL-only widening that makes re-reads no-ops and refuses to overwrite a bound outcome. It must not route through insertEvents, whose ON CONFLICT ... WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens (db.ts:101) can never widen a NULL and refreshes no identity columns; the table carries source ('live'|'seed') and its own purge/partition rule like usage_events.
desktop_surface: New 'Behaviour' section in DashboardView with a per-session tool-call table (time, tool, mcp server, outcome, duration); MenuPanel's top-5 tools reads this ledger instead of usage_events.tools; session drill-down gains a per-tool call count with 'not recorded' rows for tools that write no invocations.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl assistant content[].tool_use.{id,name} joined to user content[].tool_result.{tool_use_id,is_error}; ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db part.data $.callID/$.state (verified 12,292 rows where $.type='tool'); Devin acp-messages/*.db messages kind='tool_call' payload.content.toolCallId/status; ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl response_item function_call.call_id and *_call_output.call_id; ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl shell.tool.exec_done
honest_limit: Cursor (ai_code_hashes) and Antigravity (.pb blobs) record no tool invocations at all — those tools must render 'not recorded', never 0. Grok emits no call id, so its key is (sid, ts, seq) and two calls in the same millisecond collide. Codex writes 0 local_shell_call and only 6 function_call across 66 rollouts here, so its ledger is near-empty and the UI must say so rather than imply a quiet agent. The ledger holds names, ids, hashes and path classes only — never argument or output text, per the 'DB holds no content' constraint.
competitive_note: Cursor's enterprise OTel export states it has no per-session tool attribution and no subagent roll-up and calls its cost figure 'best-effort' (market.md §buyer needs, competitor row 109); Claude Code's OTel collapses MCP tool names to 'custom'/'mcp_tool' (§4); market.md white space 3: no vendor covers OpenCode, Grok CLI, Devin or Antigravity at runtime.
v1_ref: tool_calls ledger with tool_result error join (Tier 1)
field_verified: Yes, with two count corrections. Claude: 22,913 tool_use blocks today, 22,913 carry an id — but only 20,761 DISTINCT ids (blocks are re-written across streaming copies and forked session files), and 20,756 of those join to a tool_result.tool_use_id (99.98%); 22,909 tool_result blocks, 742 with is_error. OpenCode (sqlite3 -readonly): part total 46,584; tool parts 12,292; with $.callID 12,292; status completed 12,201 / error 89 / running 2 — every number in the feature matches exactly. Devin: 54 acp-messages DBs, kind='tool_call' 1,715 rows, 1,715 distinct (db,toolCallId) — exact. Codex: 66 rollouts, 104.7 MB, ri:function_call 6, ri:custom_tool_call 32, ri:local_shell_call 0; all 38 carry call_id and all 38 outputs carry call_id — so the Codex ledger is 38 rows, not the 6 the feature states. Grok: shell.tool.exec_done 1,402, every one with {tool_name, elapsed_ms, success} and NO call_id/id/tool_call_id of any kind. Cursor: ai-code-tracking.db holds only ai_code_hashes/scored_commits/conversation_summaries/tracked_file_content/ai_deleted_files/tracking_state, 0 rows — no tool table exists. ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/brain is empty. The upsert trap is real: db.ts:101 `WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens`, and its SET list omits every identity column — routing the ledger through insertEvents would indeed be unable to bind an outcome.
constraint: Four strains. (1) NEW BUG in the phase-2 design: `UPDATE ... WHERE call_key=? AND status IS NULL` cannot bind an OpenCode part first observed as state.status='running' (2 such rows today), because phase 1 would have written 'running' and the guard then refuses forever — the exact shape of constraint 2's 'a NULL stored total can never be upgraded', reproduced one level down. Fix: phase 1 writes status NULL and only terminal statuses bind, or the guard becomes `status IS NULL OR status='running'`. (2) Constraint 1 (keys never embed poll-time/positional values): the Grok key `grok:<sid>:<ts>:<seq>` must define seq as the ordinal among lines sharing an identical (sid,ts), never a file line index — a line index is precisely the codex.ts:197 principle-5 violation this shard elsewhere sets out to fix, and unified.jsonl can rotate. (3) Constraint 12 (schema evolution): a new table arrives free via SCHEMA's CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, but migrate() probes only usage_events and anomalies, so any later tool_calls column needs migrate() extended. (4) Constraint 13 (read-model parity): DB.swift contains zero references to tool data today; the Behaviour panel is an entirely new Swift read model, written twice. Reconciliations are all mechanical; constraint 6 (source column + purge) and constraint 8 (read-only third-party opens) are already honoured by the design.

name: Session-tree cost roll-up, and the two event_key bugs that make it wrong today
description: A vendor console bills per API request; a human bills per task. The subagent contract says child events carry the parent's session_id and their own agent_id, so Vole can produce cost-per-root-session including every descendant — a unit Cursor's OTel export explicitly lacks and that appears in no admin API. Add a `session_tree` read model returning, per root session: own cost and tokens, descendant cost and tokens, agent fan-out, max depth, and the unpriced and activity_only counts on each side. Two collector fixes are prerequisites rather than nice-to-haves: Codex's `event_key` of `codex:<session>:<line index>` collides across parent and sub-agent rollout files because the child replays the parent's session_meta and codex.ts:107 rebinds sessionId unconditionally, so subagent rows are silently lost today and the key must move to `token_usage_record.payload.response_id` or the file-scoped ordinal; and Grok's subagent-spawn ctx currently lands as an unrelated session and must fold into its parent.
desktop_surface: Session detail drill-down gains a tree with own-versus-descendant cost per node and a fan-out count; the Dashboard's biggest-session KPI switches to biggest root tree, with a per-tool 'folded / not folded' badge so an under-reported tree is visible rather than silent.
data_source: usage_events.{session_id, agent_id}; ~/.claude/projects/**/subagents/agent-*.meta.json {agentType, spawnDepth}; ~/.codex/sessions rollout session_meta.payload.source.thread_spawn.{parent_thread_id, depth, agent_nickname} and token_usage_record.payload.response_id; ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl subagent spawn lines; OpenCode session.parent_id.
honest_limit: Only Claude Code and OpenCode fold subagents correctly today, so the Codex and Grok trees are wrong until their keys are fixed and the view must show which tools are folded rather than silently under-reporting. A tree spanning a compaction boundary or a forked session file can attribute a shared message.id to whichever file was scanned first. Devin, Cursor and Antigravity are activity_only, so their trees have call counts but no tokens and no cost, and those cells stay em dashes.
competitive_note: v1 builds an agents registry and edge table but never makes the tree a billing unit, and it does not name the event_key collision that is dropping subagent rows right now. market.md records Cursor's OTel export as having no subagent roll-up — a field no console can ever ship, because the console never sees the tree.
v1_ref: Subagent and workflow fan-out monitor (fanout_burst)
field_verified: The collision is REAL and I reproduced the exact mechanism — but the proposed fix reads a field the collector never sees. Mechanism: a Codex subagent rollout contains TWO session_meta lines — first the child's own (`id: '01a07a53-d40e-…', session_id: '01a07a53-4b99-…', parent_thread_id: '01a07a53-4b99-…', source.subagent.thread_spawn: {parent_thread_id, depth: 1, agent_nickname: 'Goodall', agent_path: '/root/platform_evidence'}`), then a REPLAY of the parent's session_meta (`id: '01a07a53-4b99-…'`). codex.ts:104 does `sessionId = entry.payload?.id ?? null` on every session_meta unconditionally, so after the replay sessionId becomes the parent's, and event_key `codex:<parent-id>:<line index>` collides across files. Measured across all 66 rollouts: **session_meta.id '01a07a53-4b99-7b23-9a77-53be7efc41ff' appears in 3 separate files** ✓; the code map measured 41 token_count events → 28 rows stored. **The fix is wrong**: `token_usage_record.payload.response_id` exists (`resp_0d14883132f73de0016a9e4a9476bc87d082a78f0a40daf013`) but lives on a record type codex.ts never reads — codex.ts:122 returns early unless `entry.payload?.type === 'token_count'`, and token_usage_record has no payload.type at all. Counts differ too: **118 token_count events vs 39 token_usage_record lines**, so keying on response_id changes what is counted, not just how it is keyed. The verified correct fix is the **top-level `ordinal` field** (present on every rollout line: `"ordinal": 13`) plus the file path, or guarding the session_meta rebind to the first occurrence. Other sources verified: **492** `agent-*.meta.json` files, contents `{"agentType":"workflow-subagent","spawnDepth":1}` ✓; opencode `session.parent_id` is a real typed column ✓; ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl has 24 subagent/spawn lines.
constraint: Constraint 1 (event_key stable across re-reads) and constraint 10 (subagent contract), plus one the feature does not name and must: **changing codex's event_key orphans every existing row**. The 83 stored codex rows keep their old keys forever while the next pass re-inserts all 118 events under new ones — double-counting, not healing, because the upsert (constraint 2) matches on event_key. There is no delete-and-recollect path for a single tool anywhere in the codebase. Reconciliation: ship a one-shot `DELETE FROM usage_events WHERE tool='codex' AND source='live'` plus a collector_state reset, gated behind the user_version scheme constraint 12 says does not exist yet — that scheme is a prerequisite, not a detail.

name: repo_state_uploads: the whole-repo tarball, and the vendor server that decided to send it
description: Reads Grok's own `~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl`, which records the client tarring the working tree and shipping it to xAI's GCS: `repo_state.upload.start.ctx.{phase,turn_number,repo_path,max_file_bytes}` and `repo_state.upload.enqueued.ctx.{size_bytes,gcs_path,blobs}`, and — decisively — `trace.upload.decision.ctx.{uploads_enabled,upload_reason,trace_upload_source,telemetry_mode,data_collection_disabled,in_env_trace_upload,in_cfg_telemetry_trace_upload,in_remote_trace_upload_enabled,has_remote_settings}`, the client's full precedence chain for why it decided to upload. Adds `bulk_uploads` and `upload_decisions` (one column per input in the chain) and two rules. `repo_upload_decided_remotely` fires when `uploads_enabled=1 AND trace_upload_source='remote'`: 207 of 209 decisions on this machine, every one with `upload_reason='proxy'` and all four local `in_env_*`/`in_cfg_*` inputs NULL, while the only 2 sessions with uploads off were turned off by `zdr_team` — the customer's local config never decided this, so any posture report that reads only local config is asserting a control the customer does not hold. `upload_root_outside_work_roots` fires on the 2 starts whose `repo_path` was `<redacted-local-path>`, the entire home directory, against a declared `max_file_bytes` of 1,073,741,824.
