A user-writable local marketplace path is a fact about file location; whether it is acceptable is policy, and the finding quotes the path and the mode rather than a score. plugin.json here contains only {"name"}, so version and publisher come from installed_plugins.json and are NULL where no manifest exists; Codex records enabled/disabled per plugin (15 enabled here) but no version at all.
competitive_note: v1 enumerates the same registries and words verification as 'verify trees against source (plugin_tampered)' but never names the pinned-revision fields Codex and Claude already write, and never joins per-tool plugin lists into a cross-agent reach figure. Snyk agent-scan discovers configs per tool for free; nothing in the 62-vendor matrix reports that one approval installed hooks into four other agents, and the poisoned postmark-mcp package (ATLAS CS0053, 2025-09) is precisely a revision change between sessions.
v1_ref: Plugin, skill and marketplace supply-chain inventory
field_verified: Verified, and the reach figure is badly understated. `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` = `"ponytail@ponytail": [{"scope":"user","installPath":"<redacted-local-path>","version":"4.9.0","installedAt":"2026-08-29T07:18:06.167Z","gitCommitSha":"2ed6c52c9d7e5e56942508591085fd45dea277d3"}]`. `known_marketplaces.json` = ponytail -> `{"source":{"source":"git","url":"https://github.com/dietrichgebert/ponytail.git"},"installLocation":"<redacted-local-path>","lastUpdated":"2026-08-29T07:17:57.509Z"}`. Codex verified: three marketplaces, `[marketplaces.openai-bundled] source_type="local" source="<redacted-local-path>"`, `[marketplaces.openai-primary-runtime] source_type="local" source="<redacted-local-path>"`, `[marketplaces.claude-plugins-official] last_revision = "10dee3b37671692f9c2437988b68faa5e1256b38"`, plus 15 `[plugins."x@y"] enabled = true` blocks. Grok verified: `[[marketplace.sources]] git = "https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace.git"`. REACH IS ~13 AGENTS, NOT 5: the installed tree carries .cursor/rules, .windsurf/rules, .qoder/rules, .qoder-plugin/, .opencode/ + opencode.json, .agents/, .devin-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, .grok-plugin/, .clinerules, .kiro/, .openclaw/, gemini-extension.json, pi-extension/, alongside hooks/, skills/, commands/, scripts/ and its own ponytail-mcp/ server.
constraint: C8/C17 — `git rev-parse HEAD` inside the marketplace clone is a subprocess in a user directory, the same new capability class as codesign, and it must be read-only, never fetch, and share that consent entry; when the tree is absent, drift is 'not evaluable', never 'clean'. C5: Claude's known_marketplaces.json records only `lastUpdated` and NO pinned revision (verified above), so marketplace_revision_changed is Codex-only from config alone — for Claude the pin must come from installed_plugins.json's gitCommitSha compared against the cloned tree, or the column stays NULL. C6: posture_marketplaces and posture_plugin_targets both need the source column.

name: Vendor retention clock: is the vendor's copy still inside its own stated window
description: Once a leak row has a resolved recipient and a pack retention default, the actionable question is whether a deletion request is still worth sending. For each secret_sighting or dlp_egress row this computes `deletion_window_ends_at = evidence_ts + retention_days(recipient, contract_scope, in_force_at(evidence_ts))` and sorts an incident worklist into 'inside the vendor's published window — deletion request actionable until <date>' and 'window elapsed — deletion unverifiable'. Adds view `v_deletion_window` and rule `vendor_window_closing` whose anomaly_key steps by remaining-window bucket (14d / 7d / 48h) rather than by day, honouring the no-now()-in-the-key rule the way content_stale already does. Rows whose recipient is `unattributable` or `broker_truncated` land in a third bucket that is explicitly 'no window can be computed', never zero days.
desktop_surface: A 'Deletion window' column on the Leak Ledger with a stepped chip (14d/7d/48h/elapsed/uncomputable) and a sort control; the incident detail card prints the arithmetic — evidence date, retention days, in-force pack entry, resulting date — as the figures that fired.
data_source: secret_sightings.first_seen / dlp_egress.ts joined to processing_terms retention_default via the as-of resolver and terms_basis.contract_scope
honest_limit: Retention days are the vendor's published default, not a measurement, and a vendor legal hold, an abuse investigation or a training snapshot taken during the window all outlive it invisibly. Vole cannot confirm a deletion happened, only that a request falls inside a stated window. Enterprise/ZDR entries with retention 0 must render 'vendor states none retained', which is still an assertion and must not be shown as proof.
competitive_note: The DLP vendors stop at 'a secret was sent'; none of the 62 turns that into a per-row deletion deadline, because none of them holds a dated terms table beside the finding.
gap_area: AI-vendor processing register: where the data landed, under whose law, and on what default terms

name: Package execution ledger: installs, fetch-and-run, and registry provenance
description: The entry vector for Nx, the Keyv worm, postmark-mcp and Agentjacking is an agent running a package command, and `npx` matters more than `install`: it fetches and executes with no install record and no lockfile line. `package_execs(call_id, ecosystem, name, version_spec, pinned{yes|no}, mode{install|fetch_exec}, registry_host, first_seen_on_machine, posture)` is built from the agent's own npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/pip/uv/brew/cargo and npx/uvx/pipx-run commands (54 distinct package references here), then corroborated offline against three local artifacts nothing else reads: `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/package.json`, which names exactly what npx fetched (all three entries on this machine are MCP servers — @playwright/mcp ^0.0.80, mcp-searxng ^2.1.0, @upstash/context7-mcp ^4.0.5), the `~/.npm/_cacache/index-v5` entries, which carry the package name, the registry host that served it, the fetch date and the integrity hash (867 index files here), and lockfile mtime. Rules: `agent_ran_unpinned_package` (`@latest` or no version — `clerk@latest`, `create-payload-app@latest`, `wrangler@latest` here), `nondefault_registry_fetch` (a `--registry`/`--index-url` override or a cacache host that is not the configured default — 5 commands here), and `agent_fetch_executed_without_install`.
desktop_surface: A Supply Chain table on the Posture screen with one row per package: ecosystem, spec, pinned badge, registry host, mode, first seen, and the sessions that ran it; a cacache column shows the corroborating fetch date and integrity prefix or an em dash.
data_source: Bash/exec command strings; ~/.npm/_npx/*/package.json; ~/.npm/_cacache/index-v5 entries (key, time, integrity); ~/.npmrc registry keys (names only); lockfile mtimes at the recorded cwd.
honest_limit: cacache proves this machine fetched a version, never that this agent's command caused that fetch — the two are correlated by time and reported as corroboration, not as the same event. A package already in node_modules or in the pnpm store produces no fetch record at all, so absence is not evidence. `npx tsc` and `npx next` (369 and 316 calls here) resolve to a local binary and are not registry fetches; the ledger marks them `local_resolution` rather than counting them. Transitive dependencies are out of scope: only the name the agent typed is stored. A version-vs-CVE verdict belongs to the shipped offline advisory floor table, not here.
competitive_note: Snyk Agent Scan and mcp-scan read MCP config to find `npx -y` entries but never observe an agent running one mid-session, and no vendor in the matrix reads the npx cache or cacache index; Fleet/osquery can inventory installed packages but has no agent attribution.
v1_ref: MCP server inventory, trust posture, usage diff and pin/sign rules (mcp_unpinned_package)
gap_area: Blast radius beyond the filesystem: cloud/SaaS/DB/VCS action targets, and agent-initiated package installs

name: work_roots: the root registry, with git as an attribute and not the identity
description: Discovery-only registry built from evidence Vole already holds, never a filesystem crawl: distinct usage_events.project values, ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite project_roots.path and threads.{cwd,git_origin_url}, ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths and projects[] keys, and ~/.claude/projects/<slug> directory names used as an existence hint only. Each candidate cwd is resolved upward to the nearest ancestor holding a .git entry (dir or gitdir-pointer file) to give root_kind='git_repo'; when no ancestor has one the cwd itself is the root with root_kind='work_dir', and $HOME plus an enumerated system-path list are never roots by construction. Adds work_roots(id, root_path, root_kind, origin_slug, origin_source, first_seen, last_agent_activity, exists_now, disappeared_at, classification, excluded_by, source) and root_cwds(root_id, cwd, event_count) because a root has many cwds and 34 of 246 sessions here move between up to 5 of them. This corrects roadmap-v1's 'repos table keyed on normalised origin': on this machine only 11 of 58 cwds sit under any git root at all and only 6 distinct git roots exist, so an origin-keyed table would discard three quarters of the agent's actual working surface.
desktop_surface: Posture screen gains a Repos band listing every root with its kind chip (git repo / work dir / scratch / gone), origin slug or an em dash, last agent activity, and the cwd count folded under it; clicking a root opens the artifact ledger drill-down (F2).
data_source: usage_events.project (58 distinct live values); ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite tables project_roots.path (7 rows) and threads.{cwd, git_origin_url} (33 of 63 threads carry an origin); ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths (4 entries) and projects[] keys (23); <root>/.git/config [remote "origin"] url; ~/.claude/projects/<slug> names
honest_limit: A root Vole never observed an agent run in is invisible, so the registry is a lower bound and every figure must print its denominator. The Claude slug is not reversible — '-Users-shiva-Developer-landing-new' could be Developer/landing-new or Developer/landing/new — so slugs prove a root existed, never which path it was; the authoritative cwd comes from inside the transcript. A git root with no [remote] (apiup here) has origin_slug NULL, not 'unknown-org'.
competitive_note: Legit Security and Cycode are 'repo/CI signals only' — they know the repo from the SCM side and can never see a root that was never pushed or a work_dir with no git at all. The ES-sensor vendors (Cyberhaven, Nightfall, Harmonic, CrowdStrike Falcon AIDR) observe file opens without knowing which root the agent declared as its project. ccusage reads 18 agent sources and keeps no root registry.
v1_ref: Repo identity and attribution keys (repo slug, team, ticket)
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: Bounded repo sweep: a declared manifest, a per-pass byte budget, and a receipt
description: A scanner that may only open files named literally in a shipped repo_artifact_manifest (a content_packs kind, so it versions and validates offline like the detector pack): .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/hooks/*, .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, .mcp.json, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules/**, .cursor/mcp.json, .github/copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, .continue/config.yaml, .clinerules, .roomodes, .vscode/settings.json, .git/hooks/<name> excluding *.sample. readdir is permitted only on the manifest's declared directory prefixes at the manifest's declared depth; every other path is opened by exact name or not at all, so no glob and no walk of the repo tree can ever happen. Adds repo_artifacts(root_id, artifact_kind, rel_path, sha256, bytes, mtime, mode, tracked_state, first_seen, last_seen, source) and repo_scan_state(root_id, last_scan_at, bytes_read, files_opened, files_skipped_over_budget, dirs_denied, manifest_version) on the discovery cadence, never the 5-second loop; a per-root budget (2 MiB default) and per-file cap (512 KiB) leave over-cap files with bytes+mtime and sha256 NULL in state 'budget_skipped', counted rather than silently dropped. This sweep is the declared input the already-planned hidden-Unicode instruction scan and permission-allowlist scan currently assume without defining.
desktop_surface: Each Repos-band row expands to an artifact list — kind, relative path, bytes, mtime, first seen — with a footer receipt reading 'read 88 KB across 12 files in 3 roots, 0 skipped over budget, manifest v3'.
data_source: The declared relative paths above under each work_roots.root_path; measured here: .claude present at 3 roots, <redacted-local-path> = 88 KB / 12 files including skills/apple-hig/references/*.md; .git/hooks holds only *.sample on every root
honest_limit: A sha256 proves drift, never intent — an identical hash means unchanged bytes, not a benign file. A root that is unreadable (permissions, unmounted volume, a container-only path) records state 'unreadable', never 'clean'. Anything the manifest does not name is invisible by design, so a novel agent's config file is missed until the pack ships a new entry, and the manifest version is stamped on every row so a later reader knows what was and was not looked for.
competitive_note: Snyk Agent Scan and Invariant mcp-scan do local config discovery but as an unbounded one-shot CLI with no byte receipt and no cursor. Fleet/osquery can expose declared paths as an ATC table but has no way to discover which roots to point it at. No console vendor can state how many bytes it read from a developer's repos.
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: tracked_state from .git/index, not from git ls-files or .gitignore
description: Parse <root>/.git/index directly — the DIRC header, version, entry count, and entry path names only, never a blob — to answer whether each repo_artifacts row is in the staged tree, and cache the answer against the index's own mtime and size so an unchanged index is not re-parsed. No git subprocess is spawned, so the answer works with git absent from PATH, cannot mutate the repo, and needs no per-repo opt-in for a spawn. Adds tracked_state ∈ {tracked, untracked, unknown} on every repo_artifacts row plus index_mtime/index_size on repo_scan_state. This corrects two v1 features that planned to shell out: on this machine <redacted-local-path> line 65 is '.claude/' and yet .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json and two .claude/plans/*.md are all in the index, because a later ignore rule does not untrack — so a git check-ignore answer returns 'ignored' and is simply wrong; and Claude's own localSettingsSeenGitTracked is null for all 23 projects in ~/.claude.json, so the vendor flag cannot be used either.
desktop_surface: A tracked/untracked chip on every artifact row in the Repos-band drill-down, with 'unknown' rendered as an em dash and a tooltip naming the reason (no .git, index version unsupported, index unreadable).
data_source: <root>/.git/index (verified DIRC v2 here: 9,922 B in vole, 87,225 B in platform); <root>/.git/HEAD for the ref label; <root>/.git as a file for worktree and submodule gitdir pointers
honest_limit: The index is the staged tree on this laptop — not HEAD, not origin. A file tracked here may never have been committed or pushed, so tracked_state bounds blast radius upward and never proves distribution. Index v4 uses path-prefix compression; until the reader implements it those rows are 'unknown', never 'untracked'. A root with no .git is 'unknown', never 'untracked'.
competitive_note: Legit Security and Cycode answer tracked-state server-side against the pushed tree and therefore cannot see a staged-but-unpushed grant; no endpoint vendor answers it from the local index at all. TruffleHog, Gitleaks and GitGuardian scan files with no agent semantics and no notion of an agent config artifact.
v1_ref: Agent wrote a secret to disk (tracked vs ignored) / Workspace trust and repo-controlled permission exposure
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: agent_config_with_dependency: the Keyv-worm shape, joined to the install ledger
description: Fire when a repo_artifacts row of kind claude_settings, claude_hook, mcp_json, vscode_settings or git_hook first appears in a root inside the window of a package-execution row for that same root, and the root's lockfile sha changed across the same boundary — the exact shape of the Keyv npm worm, which planted Claude Code and VS Code hooks in 353-868 poisoned packages that execute once a workspace is trusted. The lockfile is added to the manifest as a hash-only artifact kind (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, Cargo.lock, uv.lock: name, bytes, mtime and sha256, never contents). Rule key is (root_id, artifact_kind, artifact_sha256, install_event_key), deterministic and free of now(), and the rule is hard-gated on repo_scan_state.last_scan_at IS NOT NULL for that root so a first-ever sweep — where every artifact is trivially 'new' — can never fire it.
desktop_surface: An incident card on the Behaviour feed reading 'a .claude/settings.json first appeared in <root> during npm install at <ts>; package-lock.json sha changed in the same window', with jumps to the install row in the package-execution ledger and to the artifact row in the Repos band.
data_source: repo_artifacts.first_seen and sha256 per root; the covered package-execution ledger's install rows and their cwd; <root>/{package-lock.json,pnpm-lock.yaml,yarn.lock,Cargo.lock,uv.lock} sha256
honest_limit: first_seen is Vole's first observation, not the file's creation, which is why the prior-clean-pass gate exists and why the incident text says 'first observed', never 'created'. mtime is writer-controlled and can be back-dated, so it is corroboration and never proof. Any dependency installed before Vole watched that root is entirely invisible, and an install performed inside a container or a devcontainer leaves no local install row to join to.
competitive_note: Sysdig flags new agent installs and credential access at the kernel but does not join an agent-config first-seen to a lockfile change. Legit and Cycode see the lockfile change in CI and never see the hook that landed beside it on the laptop. No vendor in the matrix correlates package execution with agent-config appearance.
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: Root tombstones: the clone that is gone and the hash that can never be re-verified
description: When a known root stops resolving on disk, set work_roots.exists_now=0 and disappeared_at, freeze every repo_artifacts row for it with verifiable=0 and a preserved last_verified_at, and fire root_not_present keyed (root_id, disappeared_at_day) at info severity so it lands once per root instead of once per poll. Without this a vanished root simply returns nothing and drops silently out of every posture figure, which is the single most likely way a repo-artifact claim becomes a lie: on this machine 34 of 58 known roots are already gone, including <redacted-local-path> with 4,398 events and <redacted-local-path> with 987, and two of the four repos named in ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths and two of the seven Codex project_roots no longer exist. Every evidence-bundle sentence about repo artifacts then carries this denominator instead of an unqualified 'no findings'.
desktop_surface: Gone roots render in the Repos band greyed with a 'not present since <date>' chip and a 'last verified <date>' line on each of their frozen artifact rows; the evidence-bundle preview shows the tombstone count inline with any repo-artifact claim.
data_source: work_roots.root_path existence probe (a single stat per root on the discovery cadence); repo_artifacts.last_seen; measured: 34 of 58 cwds absent, including 2 of 4 githubRepoPaths entries and 2 of 7 Codex project_roots
honest_limit: Gone is not deleted. An unmounted external volume, a renamed directory, a container-only path (/private/tmp/claude-501/... harness scratchpads and the Claude Desktop scratch-workspace roots seen here) and a real rm -rf are indistinguishable from a stat, so the state is 'not_present' and the row never says deleted. A root that reappears is re-probed and un-frozen, but the gap between disappeared_at and its return is an evidence gap, not a clean interval.
competitive_note: SCM-side tools (Legit, Cycode) never lose the repo because they watch the server, so they have no analogue and no reason to build one; endpoint DLP never had a repo registry to lose. Nothing in the 62-vendor matrix reports 'this evidence can no longer be re-verified'.
gap_area: The repo registry: enumerating repo-local agent artifacts at all

name: MCP registered-vs-observed call and spend join
description: The half of MCP visibility no scanner has: cross-join posture_mcp_servers.mcp_identity to observed `mcp__<server>__<tool>` calls in usage_events.tools (and the Tier-1 tool_calls ledger once it lands) to produce, per registered server, calls, sessions, tokens, cost_usd where priced, and the set of registrations with no observed call. Every inventory row gains a used/dormant chip and the dashboard gains a by-MCP-server grouping. This is the join that turns a config inventory into a security answer - which approved server is actually being called, by whom, and at what cost - and it is the one column the 62-vendor matrix has no row for, because it needs per-call token attribution rather than a request proxy.
desktop_surface: Dashboard > Breakdown gains a 'by MCP server' grouping (calls, sessions, tokens, cost, unpriced-call count); each Supply Chain > MCP row shows a used/dormant chip and a calls-per-day sparkline, and clicking it filters the tool ledger to that server's calls.
data_source: posture_mcp_servers.mcp_identity joined to usage_events.tools LIKE 'mcp__%' (and tool_calls.name once the Tier-1 ledger exists); usage_events token columns and cost_usd for the spend side.
honest_limit: Entirely dependent on the tools column, which is NULL on 7,108 rows whose stop_reason is tool_use, so every count is a floor until the tools-union fix lands, and six of the seven collectors do not record tool names at all. The chip must therefore read 'no call observed in range on this machine', never 'unused' - absence of a call is not absence of use. cost_usd is NULL for Codex, Grok and rerouted models, so every spend total carries an unpriced-call count beside it rather than a silently short sum.
competitive_note: v1 bundles config scanning, npx pin checks and codesign hashing with the usage join; the scanning half is commoditised (Snyk agent-scan is free and covers Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode and Antigravity; Cisco ships an OSS MCP scanner; Cyberhaven, Zenity, Nightfall and Lasso all ship MCP inventories) while the server-to-exact-tokens-and-dollars join exists nowhere in the matrix. Building the scanner spends effort on a commodity; keep codesign for agent binaries, where it returns a real answer, not for npx packages where it is NULL.
v1_ref: MCP server inventory, trust posture, usage diff and pin/sign rules
field_verified: Numbers verified against ~/.vole/vole.db (29,596 live rows). `SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE tools LIKE '%mcp__%'` = 1,066 — playwright dominates (browser_take_screenshot 232, browser_evaluate 210, browser_navigate 196, browser_run_code_unsafe 147), searxng 53, github and context7 in single digits (context7 = 9). `WHERE tools IS NULL AND stop_reason='tool_use'` = 7,115 (feature said 7,108; the store has grown). TWO CLAIMS IN THE HONEST LIMIT ARE FALSE: 'six of the seven collectors do not record tool names at all' — `SELECT tool, sum(tools IS NOT NULL), count(*) GROUP BY tool` returns opencode 9,658/10,885, grok 586/1,758, codex 29/83, claude_code 8,078/16,669; only devin (0/204), cursor and antigravity record none. What is true is narrower: only claude_code emits `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names — opencode rows read 'bash', 'read,read,read', grok 'list_dir,run_terminal_command', so the join is Claude-Code-only, not seven-tool.
constraint: C2 is the blocker the feature does not name. The upsert rewrites a stored row only when `excluded.total_tokens` is STRICTLY greater, and the SET list does include `tools` — so those 7,115 NULL-tools rows can never be back-filled by a re-scan, because a re-read produces an equal, not greater, total. The 'tools-union fix' is therefore a deliberate widening of the upsert WHERE/SET, which per C2 must be explicit and which changes rewrite semantics for every collector at once. Until then every count is a floor and the chip must read 'no call observed in range on this machine'. C5: cost_usd is NULL for Codex, Grok and rerouted models, so every spend total carries its unpriced-call count beside it.

name: Agent and AI-app binary signing ledger (TeamID, CDHash, ad-hoc)
description: For every executable behind a collected agent and every AI app in the surface registry, resolve the real binary (`which` + readlink for CLIs, Contents/Info.plist CFBundleExecutable for .app bundles) and run one read-only `codesign -dv --verbose=4`, parsing Identifier, TeamIdentifier, the first Authority line, CDHash, hardened-runtime and the adhoc/linker-signed flags into posture_binaries(source, kind, tool, path, version, signing_id, team_id, authority, cdhash, hardened_runtime, signature_kind, first_seen, last_seen), cached on (path, size, mtime) so codesign only re-runs when the file actually changes. Verified live on this machine: /Applications/ChatGPT.app resolves to Identifier=com.openai.codex, Authority=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2); /Applications/Claude.app to com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, Anthropic PBC (Q6L2SF6YDW); Homebrew opencode to /opt/homebrew/Cellar/opencode/1.18.15/libexec/.../opencode.exe with Identifier=a.out, flags=0x20002 (adhoc, linker-signed) and no TeamIdentifier at all. Three rules keyed on the surface, none containing now(): agent_binary_unsigned, agent_binary_team_changed (the trojanised-replacement or sideloaded-rebuild shape, quoting both TeamIdentifiers and both dates) and agent_binary_cdhash_changed_without_version_change.
desktop_surface: Supply Chain > Binaries: one row per resolved executable with a signature chip (Developer ID / ad-hoc / not applicable / unknown), Team ID, authority string, short CDHash, resolved path and version; the AI Surfaces grid gains a 'Signed by' column reading the same row with a red shield glyph on unsigned and ad-hoc entries; team-id and CDHash changes render as incident cards showing the old and new value side by side with their timestamps.
data_source: `which <agent>` plus readlink resolution; .app Contents/Info.plist CFBundleExecutable; `codesign -dv --verbose=4 <path>` stderr (Identifier / TeamIdentifier / Authority / CDHash / flags); ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ (2.1.234, 2.1.251, 2.1.263 retained here), ~/.grok/version.json, ~/.codex/config.toml CODEX_CLI_PATH = /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex; cache key (path, size, mtime).
honest_limit: codesign is a subprocess, not a file read - the first external tool Vole shells out to - so it needs its own consent entry, a slow cadence, and must degrade to signature_kind='unknown', never 'unsigned', when the tool is absent or exits non-zero. npm-installed JS CLIs run under an unsigned interpreter and are recorded signature_kind='not_applicable'; ad-hoc is normal for Homebrew builds, so the row states the fact and leaves the verdict to policy. A valid Developer ID proves only that Apple issued that team a certificate, never that the code is safe, and notarisation says no more. The binary on PATH today is not necessarily the binary that produced a historical row: the transcript `version` field is authoritative for the past, the signature is a statement about now.
competitive_note: v1 runs codesign only against MCP server binaries - where it is NULL for the npx packages that make up most registrations - and never against the agents themselves; its agent SBOM records version and path but no signing identity. Santa, Jamf Protect and Kolide do TeamID binary authorisation with no AI semantics: they cannot say which signed binary is an LLM agent. No vendor in the 62-row matrix reports the Team ID of the coding agent.
v1_ref: MCP server inventory, trust posture, usage diff and pin/sign rules (mcp_unsigned_binary); Agent runtime inventory (agent SBOM)
field_verified: Verified stronger than claimed. `codesign -dv --verbose=4 /Applications/ChatGPT.app` -> `Identifier=com.openai.codex`, `CDHash=e2f41d8f6362b87345d4e5a9336d0dc36ec199fe`, `Authority=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)`, `flags=0x10000(runtime)`, `Notarization Ticket=stapled`. Claude.app -> `Identifier=com.anthropic.claudefordesktop`, `TeamIdentifier=Q6L2SF6YDW`. TeamIdentifier IS emitted as its own line (`TeamIdentifier=Q6L2SF6YDW` on the claude CLI), not only inside the Authority parenthesis. The CLIs the feature did not test also resolve: `<redacted-local-path> -> <redacted-local-path>` = `Identifier=com.anthropic.claude-code`, `Authority=Developer ID Application: Anthropic PBC (Q6L2SF6YDW)`; `<redacted-local-path>` = `Identifier=xai-grok-pager`, `Authority=Developer ID Application: X.AI Corporation (5Y6N3AJ54S)`; `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex` = `Identifier=codex`, OpenAI 2DC432GLL2. opencode confirmed exactly as claimed: `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode -> /opt/homebrew/Cellar/opencode/1.18.15/libexec/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe`, `Identifier=a.out`, `flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)`, no TeamIdentifier. `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` holds 2.1.234, 2.1.251, 2.1.263; `~/.grok/version.json` = `{"version":"0.2.103"}`; `~/.codex/config.toml` line 114 `CODEX_CLI_PATH = "/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex"`.
constraint: C8 (third-party stores opened read-only; Vole writes only under ~/.vole) and C17 (no silent network) — codesign is the first subprocess Vole spawns, a new capability class neither constraint anticipated. The sharp edge the feature misses: `codesign -d` (display) is offline, but `codesign --verify` and `spctl -a` perform revocation/notarisation checks that hit the network. Reconciliation: hard-code display-only (`codesign -dv --verbose=4`), never --verify/--deep/spctl, gate on a consent entry, and make the no-egress switch also disable the pass. C14 (SEA, node: builtins only) is satisfied — node:child_process is a builtin. C5: absent/failed codesign must yield signature_kind='unknown', never 'unsigned'. The 5s poll loop cannot run codesign over a 310MB binary; the (path,size,mtime) cache plus a slow cadence is mandatory, not optional.

name: Shipped offline advisory floor table (version-vs-CVE, no network)
description: Ship a dated data/advisories.json alongside data/pricing.json - {tool, cve, fixed_in[], affects_range, title, url, published, class} - frozen into the SEA at build time exactly as pricing.json is, and join it to the version already stamped on every row. Claude Code writes `version` on every transcript line (15 distinct versions here, 2.1.215 through 2.1.263, with 2.1.234 / 2.1.251 / 2.1.263 retained under ~/.local/share/claude/versions/); ~/.claude/.last-update-result.json records {version_from: 2.1.251, version_to: 2.1.263, outcome: success}; Codex writes cli_version in session_meta; Grok has version.json; Cursor has argv.json. The rule agent_version_below_advisory_floor fires per session, quoting the session's version, the advisory id, the fixed_in floor, the advisory's publication date and the table's own build date beside it.
desktop_surface: Supply Chain > Versions: a bar per agent showing sessions by version in range with versions below a floor shaded red; each advisory row shows CVE id, fixed-in floor, sessions affected, and the footer reads 'advisory data as of <date>, from <file>'.
data_source: data/advisories.json shipped in the build, overridable by ~/.vole/advisories.json exactly as pricing.json is; ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl `version`; ~/.claude/.last-update-result.json; ~/.codex session_meta.cli_version; ~/.grok/version.json; ~/.cursor/argv.json.
honest_limit: The table is only as current as the Vole build: it can never claim a version is safe, only that no shipped advisory names it, and the UI must read 'no advisory data' rather than 'clean'. Vole makes no network call to refresh it; an org wanting fresher data supplies ~/.vole/advisories.json the way it supplies pricing.json, and every row names which file it used. Version ranges are the vendor's own wording, and an entry whose fixed_in floor is ambiguous is marked unverified and never fires. The rule reports the version the session recorded, which is not evidence the vulnerable code path was reached.
competitive_note: v1 explicitly gives up here - 'no local file knows the latest release' - wording its rule as 'ran 2.1.233 while 2.1.263 was installed here' and pushing advisories into an opt-in fetched bundle. A shipped, dated, no-network table is the same trust model as pricing.json and violates no principle, and it would have flagged Gemini CLI <0.1.14 (README hijack), Cursor <1.3.9 (MCPoison), Cursor <3.0 (DuneSlide CVE-2026-50548, CVSS 9.8) and Claude Code below 1.0.93 / 1.0.105 / 1.0.111 ($IFS bypass, CVE-2025-66032) - all four of which appear in sessions on machines like this one.
v1_ref: Agent runtime inventory (agent SBOM) and runtime_behind_local_max
field_verified: The mechanism is verified precisely; the advisory content is not sourced. Precedent confirmed in the repo: `packages/core/src/data/pricing.json` is imported into pricing.ts (`const BUILTIN = builtin as PricingFile`) and build-sea.mjs states `esbuild bundles src/cli/collect.ts (all local imports + pricing.json) into one`, with the override at `paths.pricingOverride() = process.env.VOLE_PRICING ?? ~/.vole/pricing.json` — so a dated advisories.json in the same shape is exactly feasible. Version stamps verified: 15 distinct Claude Code versions across transcripts, 2.1.215 through 2.1.263; `~/.claude/.last-update-result.json` = `{"version_from":"2.1.251","version_to":"2.1.263","outcome":"success"}`; Codex `cli_version` present in session_meta (0.135.0-alpha.1, 0.144.6 x9, 0.153.4 x7); `~/.grok/version.json` = 0.2.103. BUT THE FLOORS ARE NOT IN THE RESEARCH: market.md sources all four motivating incidents (Gemini CLI README hijack 2025-07-28, Cursor MCPoison CVE-2025-54136, Cursor DuneSlide CVE-2026-50548, Claude Code $IFS CVE-2025-66032) and names NONE of the fixed_in versions — '0.1.14', '1.3.9', '3.0', '1.0.93/1.0.105/1.0.111' and 'CVSS 9.8' return zero hits.
constraint: C14 — the SEA is specified as doing 'no runtime file reads except pricing override and sources'; a second override file is a real widening and must be named in the constraint, not slipped in by analogy. C17 is satisfied and must stay satisfied: the table can never self-refresh, so a stale build is silently stale — which is why the footer naming the data date and the source file is load-bearing, not decoration. Principle 1: 'no advisory data' and 'no advisory names this version' are different statements from 'safe', and the card must print whichever one is true.

name: Version residency: the exposure interval an advisory's affected range actually intersects
description: Five of the 27 dated incidents are version-bounded (Gemini CLI <0.1.14, Cursor <1.3.9 and <3.0, Amazon Q 1.84.0, Claude Code fixed in 1.0.93/1.0.105/1.0.111), and every one of them is answered by an interval, not by today's version. Claude Code stamps `version` on every JSONL line (12 distinct versions, 2.1.229 → 2.1.263, in a sample of 80 transcripts on this machine); Codex carries `session_meta.payload.cli_version`, OpenCode `session.version`, and IDE extension versions come from the editor's own Settings Sync backups. Folding consecutive same-version lines gives `agent_versions(tool, version, first_ts, last_ts, sessions, events, evidence_rows)`; an advisory's affected range intersects those intervals into exposure windows, joined to autonomy_intervals so the answer reads "1.0.104 ran here 3–19 Jul across 412 sessions, 38 of them with permissions bypassed". Rule `vulnerable_version_window` fires backdated at the interval start, with the fix date corroborated offline from the agent's own bundled changelog rather than from any network.
desktop_surface: A version lane on the annotated timeline — one band per agent version, advisory-affected bands tinted, click for the session list and the bypass count inside the band. Also a row on the Posture screen: "you have been on 12 Claude Code versions in the answerable window".
data_source: version field on every ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl line; ~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl session_meta.payload.cli_version; OpenCode session.version; VS Code/Cursor Settings Sync extension backups; ~/.claude/cache/changelog.md for fix dating
honest_limit: An interval is bounded by answerable_from: a version that ran before the oldest retained transcript is invisible, and the first retained line reports first-observed, not first-run — rendered as a left-open band, never as a start date. Sessions with no telemetry-bearing line contribute no version at all.
competitive_note: The shipped floor table answers "are you patched now"; nobody answers "were you vulnerable then, and for how long". Vendor-native telemetry cannot: Copilot's usage metrics lag ~2 days and its audit log excludes local prompts, and Anthropic's Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, personal accounts and Cursor/Codex entirely (market.md L137, L139).
v1_ref: Shipped offline advisory floor table (version-vs-CVE, no network)
gap_area: Indicator retro-hunt: 'an advisory just named X — were we exposed, when, and what happened next'

name: Agent reach: the key, the host policy and the forwarded agent that got it out
description: Once an agent can cross to an unmonitored context, the question is what authority it carried across. Three exact reads, no new instrumentation. From `~/.ssh/config`: per-Host `IdentityFile`, `ForwardAgent`, `StrictHostKeyChecking` and `ProxyJump` (this machine sets `StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new` on three of four hosts, meaning any new host is trusted silently). From the command-shape pass: `-i <path>` arguments handed to ssh/scp/rsync by the agent (147 occurrences of `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` here), `-A` agent-forwarding flags, and `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no`. From `~/.ssh/known_hosts`: the line count as a reach denominator (34 here), never the host keys themselves. Adds `context_authority(context_id, key_path_hmac, key_class, forward_agent, host_key_policy, evidence_kind, first_seen, last_seen, source)` and the rule `agent_reach_exceeds_monitoring`: an agent used a private-key path or a forwarded agent to reach a context with monitored=0, scored critical when ForwardAgent is on (the agent's authority then extends to everything that key can reach, transitively, and Vole monitors none of it) and when the host policy accepts new hosts without prompting.
desktop_surface: Posture screen gains a Reach row per context: key class, forwarding state, host-key policy, all three as the observed-versus-hardened pairs the vendor lever cards already use. The incident card states the reach in one line — 'this agent used <key class> to reach <label>, agent forwarding on, host policy accept-new; Vole has no data from that context' — with the config file and line as the evidence path.
data_source: ~/.ssh/config (Host, IdentityFile, ForwardAgent, StrictHostKeyChecking, ProxyJump, Include), ~/.ssh/known_hosts (line count only), and `-i` / `-A` / `-o StrictHostKeyChecking` arguments extracted in the collector's command-shape pass from Claude Code Bash input.command, Codex local_shell_call and OpenCode tool parts
honest_limit: An `-i <path>` argument proves what was typed, not that the key existed, was accepted, or was even the key used — ssh may fall back to the agent or to a default identity, and Vole never opens the key file to check. Agent forwarding can be enabled by an `Include`d config Vole does not follow, by a per-host default in /etc/ssh/ssh_config, or by the parent shell's environment, none of which the collector reads, so `forward_agent` has a genuine unknown state that renders as an em dash rather than 'off'. The key path is stored as an HMAC and a class; the path text and the key are never stored. Reach is counted, never resolved: Vole cannot enumerate what the forwarded agent could actually open on the far side.
competitive_note: Token/Oasis (Cyera, ~$1B) and Entra Agent ID / Okta for AI Agents cover non-human identity, but only for agents that authenticate through the IdP; an agent using a developer's own SSH private key to reach a GPU box is outside every one of those inventories. The sensitive-path work in the existing roadmap records reads of ~/.ssh; this records the key being handed to a transport as an argument, which is a different act with a different blast radius.
v1_ref: Sensitive-file access ledger and protected_path_access rule
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: Retroactive config history replayed from the agents' own rotating backups
description: Claude Code writes timestamped copies of its own config that Vole can replay to reconstruct posture history from before Vole was ever installed. A one-shot pass parses ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.<epoch_ms> (5 rotating, 78,466 bytes each, all five written within seven hours today) plus ~/.claude/settings.json.bak-pre-ccr, settings.json.ccr-original, two settings.json.ccr-backup-<iso> and settings.json.reset-backup-<iso> - six recoverable historical settings states on this machine - oldest first, computing the same mcp_identity, hook, permission, marketplace and env signatures as the live scan, and writing one posture_snapshots row per (kind, identity, sha256, observed_at) with provenance='backup'. Verified live: settings.json.ccr-original still carries env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://195.242.30.141:30000 with a literal ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and model qwen3.8-27b-fp8 - a cleartext raw-IP model endpoint absent from the current settings that no running collector could ever have observed.
desktop_surface: Supply Chain > History: a timeline of config states per file with 'reconstructed from backup' provenance chips, each entry expandable to the field-level diff; a first-run banner reading 'N historical states recovered from the tools' own backups'; recovered provider endpoints flow into the existing provider and egress panels tagged provenance='backup'.
data_source: ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.<epoch_ms>; ~/.claude/settings.json.{bak-pre-ccr, ccr-original, ccr-backup-<iso>, reset-backup-<iso>}; ~/.claude/.claude.json.ccr-original-missing; ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json.bak.
honest_limit: Backups are a rotating window (5 here, all inside one day) - anything older is gone, so the history is bounded and must be labelled 'earliest recovered state', never 'first ever state'. The filename is the only timestamp, and a backup written by a third-party tool such as ccr carries that tool's clock, not the agent's. Codex, OpenCode, Grok and Cursor keep no equivalent rotation, so their history starts when Vole starts and the coverage table says so per tool. A credential recovered from a backup is never stored: only the host, the key name and a shape class. observed_at is the backup's own epoch, never now(), so re-running the pass over the same files is a no-op.
competitive_note: v1 reads ccr backups only to fill provider_configs; no roadmap entry treats vendor backups as a general history source for MCP, hooks, permissions and marketplaces. No vendor in the 62-row matrix offers pre-install retroactive posture - every endpoint sensor (Cyberhaven, Nightfall, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) sees only what happens after deployment, which is exactly why the raw-IP endpoint on this machine would be invisible to all of them.
v1_ref: Provider endpoint snapshots (time-versioned, keys never read)
field_verified: The headline finding is real and better than described; the mechanism is much weaker than described. `~/.claude/settings.json.ccr-original` contains verbatim `"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://195.242.30.141:30000"`, `"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "m5ORTaDqHtk6ccewOzXCUBtjqJqCaLlhYeYbo8Qy7MM"`, `"ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "qwen3.8-27b-fp8"` — a cleartext raw-IP model endpoint with a literal token, absent from the live settings. I also found two states the write-up did not: `settings.json.bak-pre-ccr` and `settings.json.reset-backup-2026-08-29T06-40-00Z` both carry a claude-code-router gateway (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:3456`, `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID: ccr-local`). BUT THE ROTATION CLAIM IS WRONG: `ls -la ~/.claude/backups/` shows 5 files all 78,466 bytes, timestamped 09:34, 09:38, 09:40, 09:41, 09:42 — an EIGHT-MINUTE window, not 'seven hours'. And `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json.bak` does not exist (`no matches found`).
constraint: C1/C6 are satisfied by the design (observed_at = the backup's own epoch, never now(), so re-running is a genuine no-op, and rows need the source column). The real tension is Principle 1: a backup written by claude-code-router carries ccr's clock and ccr's idea of what the file was, so 'the configuration was X at time T' is an inference about a third-party tool's behaviour, not an observation of the agent. Reconciliation: store provenance='backup' plus the writing tool inferred from the filename, and label the timeline 'earliest recovered state', never 'first ever state' — which the write-up already says and must keep in the UI, not just the roadmap.

name: Blanket-approval inventory: what each wildcard grant actually authorised
description: Parse every reachable allow-list - ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow (9 entries here), ~/.claude/settings.local.json, each repo's .claude/settings.local.json, ~/.claude.json projects[*].allowedTools (21 of 23 projects carry one here) and the per-turn attachment.type='command_permissions'.allowedTools snapshots (130 occurrences across 622 transcripts here) - and classify each entry as exact, prefix_wildcard, tool_wildcard or mcp_server_wildcard. Then count, per entry, how many calls in the tool_calls ledger that entry authorised, so the panel answers the only question a security review cares about: how much did this one rule let through. On this machine `Bash(gh api *)` authorises arbitrary GitHub API calls and `Bash(python3 -)` authorises arbitrary code from stdin - two entries that between them make most of the permission system decorative.
desktop_surface: Supply Chain > Standing permissions: a sortable table of entry text (masked where it carries a path or URL), class, scope (user / project / per-turn), calls authorised and a destructive-class count, with a summary line reading 'N calls authorised by M wildcard rules'; clicking a row filters the tool ledger to the calls attributed to it.
data_source: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow; ~/.claude/settings.local.json; <repo>/.claude/settings.local.json; ~/.claude.json projects[*].allowedTools; ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl attachment.type='command_permissions'.allowedTools; the Tier-1 tool_calls ledger for the attribution side.
honest_limit: Attribution is Vole's own re-implementation of the vendor's matcher and can disagree with what the vendor actually matched, so the panel prints the matcher version and attributes a call matched by no entry to posture rather than to a rule. It cannot count anything until the Tier-1 tool_calls ledger exists; until then the classification half stands alone with a 'calls authorised: not evaluable' column. Entries whose text contains a path or a URL are masked to a class before storage, so the table shows the shape of the grant, not always its literal text.
competitive_note: v1 classifies each rule against a taxonomy and quotes the literal text, but stops at presence: counting what each entry actually let through is the part that changes a security review, and it is only possible because the tool ledger and the allow-list live on the same machine. Gateway vendors see only routed calls and no vendor console exposes the local allow-list at all.
v1_ref: Permission allowlist and managed-settings posture
field_verified: The literal entries are verified; the volume claim is not. `~/.claude/settings.json` permissions.allow is exactly 9 entries and does contain `"Bash(gh api *)"` and `"Bash(python3 -)"` as claimed (the rest are pinned curl and hf download lines). `~/.claude/settings.local.json` = `{"permissions":{"allow":["Skill(update-config)"]}}` — 1 entry. THE PROJECT LAYER IS EMPTY: the write-up says '21 of 23 projects carry one here', but the key is present on 21 while the array is `[]` on all 21 — zero project-scope entries exist on this machine. Per-turn snapshots are real but fewer and thinner than claimed: 43 `attachment.type='command_permissions'` (not 130), and the shape is `{"type":"command_permissions","allowedTools":["Read"]}` — a single exact tool, not a wildcard. Total inventory on this machine: 10 entries, 2 of them wildcards.
constraint: Principle 1 and Principle 3. 'This entry authorised N calls' is Vole's own matcher output presented as a figure about the vendor's behaviour — the feature admits the matcher can disagree, which makes the headline number an invention under principle 1 unless it is labelled as a Vole-computed match with the matcher version printed on the row, and unmatched calls attributed to posture rather than to a rule. The masking proposal also fights the codebase: C7 explicitly permits cwd and file paths in the DB and usage_events.project already stores raw cwds in cleartext, so hashing the rule text here makes the panel unjoinable to everything else while protecting nothing new. Reconciliation: store literal text as v1 does, and mask only in exported or synced rows. Hard dependency: the counting half cannot exist before the Tier-1 tool_calls ledger.

name: Dependency key-set delta from the pre- and post-image the transcript already holds
description: For a write classified `dependency`, the collector reconstructs both file images in memory — `toolUseResult.originalFile` is the pre-image and applying `oldString`→`newString` (or `content` for a create) yields the post-image — parses each as the manifest it is, and stores only the key-set delta in a new `dependency_deltas` table: ecosystem, manifest path, package name, old spec, new spec, section (dependencies / devDependencies / peer / optional) and verb. No regex over diff lines, so the result is exact rather than best-effort; run against this machine it recovers `devDependencies + {esbuild, postject}` and `dependencies − {better-sqlite3}` from single Edit rows. Rules: `dependency_added_by_agent` (info alone, warn when the same session's package-execution ledger then ran an install, critical when the added name is a typo-neighbour of a name already present in the shipped package pack) and `manifest_lockfile_desync` (manifest changed, no lockfile write anywhere in the session).
desktop_surface: A 'dependencies this agent added' table on the repo half of Blast Radius: name, section, spec, the session that added it, and a second column showing whether an install actually ran, so an unresolved manifest edit reads differently from an executed one.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl `toolUseResult.{originalFile, oldString, newString, replaceAll, content, filePath}` on package.json, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile and their lockfiles; joined to round 2's package execution ledger.
honest_limit: Only Claude Code carries a pre-image, so OpenCode `patch` parts give the path and nothing else and Codex/Grok manifest edits arrive as shell heredocs with no parseable delta — those rows keep the path class and every name column stays NULL. If either image fails to parse the row records `parse_failed` and no name is guessed. A typo-neighbour is a lexical claim about a string, never a claim that the package is malicious, and the shipped neighbour list is an offline floor, not a registry mirror.
competitive_note: Snyk and Dependabot read the manifest as it stands and cannot say an agent wrote the line; ASPM starts at the PR; none of the 62 vendors in the matrix ties a dependency addition back to the session, posture and principal that produced it, which is the only fact that distinguishes a reviewed upgrade from an agent improvising under bypass.
gap_area: Agent-authored change risk: writes that widen the security envelope, not writes that destroy

name: install_hook_added: the lifecycle script the agent planted
description: The same pre/post images, restricted to the keys that execute at install time rather than at run time: package.json `scripts.{preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepublish, prepack}`, pyproject `[build-system]` and build-hook tables, Cargo `build`/`build.rs`, a Makefile default target, and Gradle/Maven plugin blocks. The row stores the key name, a sha256 of the command string and round 2's command-shape skeleton id — never the command text. `install_hook_added` is critical by default, because this is the exact rung the Nx s1ngularity postinstall and the Malware-Slop package used, and because the entry then runs on every teammate's `npm install` without anyone opening the file. The extraction is proven here: the `scripts + {build:sea}` delta comes back exactly from one Edit row.
desktop_surface: Pinned to the top of the repo half of 'what the agent left behind', showing the key name, the command skeleton and the hash, with a copy-as-evidence action that emits the incident bundle row rather than a screenshot.
data_source: The same `toolUseResult.{originalFile, oldString, newString, content}` images used by the dependency delta, keyed on install-time script paths within the parsed manifest.
honest_limit: Benign build wiring dominates — `build:sea` here was entirely legitimate — so the rule states that an install-time entry point was added and by whom, never that it is malicious. It cannot see a script added by the editor, by `npm pkg set`, or shipped inside a dependency's own tarball; it sees only what an agent wrote through a ledgered tool. Agents with no pre-image contribute no key delta and are absent, not clean.
competitive_note: Round 2's package execution ledger catches the install that runs; nothing catches the install that will run on someone else's machine next week. Secret scanners and SCA both read the file's current state, and Sysdig's 'safeguard-weakening flags' watch agent CLI flags, not manifest keys.
gap_area: Agent-authored change risk: writes that widen the security envelope, not writes that destroy

name: Devcontainer and compose manifest reader: the agent the image installs, the home it mounts, the bypass it declares
description: Under consented repo roots only, read `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `.devcontainer/*/devcontainer.json` and a root `devcontainer.json` (JSONC — comments and trailing commas tolerated by a hand-written stripper, no new dependency), and line-scan `compose.yaml`/`docker-compose*.yml` for `image:`, `volumes:` and `command:` blocks. Extract exactly four things and store no other text: agent installs (`features` keys or `image`/`postCreateCommand` naming claude-code, @anthropic-ai/claude-code, codex, @openai/codex, gemini-cli, opencode, aider, goose, amp), provider key names appearing in `remoteEnv`/`containerEnv`/`build.args` (names only, values never read), host bind mounts classified by target (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gcloud`, `$HOME`, `/var/run/docker.sock`), and declared autonomy flags in any command string (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--yolo`, `--approval-mode yolo`, `--sandbox danger-full-access`, `IS_SANDBOX=1`). Adds `context_manifests(context_id, manifest_path, manifest_kind, agent_installs, env_key_names, mount_class, declared_bypass, content_hash, first_seen, last_seen, source)` and three rules: `agent_in_unmonitored_context` (a manifest installs an agent and no Vole row carries that context_id), `home_mounted_into_container` (a bind mount of an agent home or a credential dir — a credential-exposure finding in its own right, and the mechanical explanation for why some container runs do show up in the local store), and `unmonitored_context_declares_bypass` (the manifest hard-codes an autonomy flag for a context nobody observes). `content_hash` gives change detection so a mount added later fires again.
desktop_surface: Posture screen gains a Contexts section: one row per manifest with three-state chips (agent installed / home mounted / bypass declared), the evidence path and a diff badge when content_hash changes. Findings of class `home_mounted_into_container` also surface on the Leak Ledger with the mount target spelled out, since a mounted ~/.aws is a credential exposure regardless of what the agent does. Incidents carry the manifest path and the exact declared flag as their figures.
data_source: <repo>/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json and .devcontainer/*/devcontainer.json (`features`, `image`, `remoteEnv`, `containerEnv`, `mounts`, `postCreateCommand`, `runArgs`); <repo>/compose.yaml, docker-compose*.yml (`image:`, `volumes:`, `command:`); repo roots taken from the existing consented-scope policy, not from a filesystem walk
honest_limit: This reads declarations, never runtime. A `postCreateCommand` that curls an installer, a `--build-arg` override, a Codespaces prebuild, an image whose Dockerfile installs an agent no `features` entry names, or a `docker run` typed by hand all defeat it — Vole reports what the manifest says and never claims the container matched it. Compose files are line-scanned rather than YAML-parsed (the SEA collector must stay dependency-free), so anchors, multi-document files and folded scalars degrade to a declared-partial state with a lower coverage claim instead of a silent miss. Env key *names* are read; values are never opened, so a mounted secrets file is invisible.
competitive_note: Snyk agent-scan and Pillar scan rules files, MCP configs and skills; neither reads devcontainer.json or compose for agent installs, credential mounts or hard-coded bypass flags. Docker's own AI Governance (Docker Business, $24/user/mo) has full visibility but only into runs inside Docker's own sandboxes, and reports nothing about a devcontainer built by another runtime.
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: IDE agent posture as a dated interval, from the editor's settings backups
description: The bypass switches for IDE-resident agents live in the editor's settings, and the editor keeps a dated history of them. Two readers. (1) Effective posture: <App Support>/<Editor>/User/settings.json plus each workspace's .vscode/settings.json, for the editor's own agent keys (chat.agent.maxRequests, chat.agent.autoApprove, chat.agent.sandbox.enabled, chat.editing.confirmEditRequests, chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove*, security.workspace.trust.*, security.promptForLocalFileProtocolHandling) AND for every posture key an installed extension DECLARES in contributes.configuration.properties — so the watched-key list is derived from feature 3's scan, not hardcoded, and a new agent extension is covered the day it installs. Verified here: claudeCode.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions is true, chat.agent.maxRequests is 1000000000000, and the two dismissed-warning flags chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove.warningAccepted and chat.permissions.autoApprove.dontShowWarningAgain are both true in globalState. Also read <App Support>/<Editor>/User/globalStorage/agent-host-config.json: permissions.allow/deny, telemetryLevel, byokModelsEnabled, githubMcpServerEnabled, systemProxyEnabled, githubEnterpriseUri, defaultShell. (2) The history: replay sync/settings/<UTC>.json, which on this machine shows chat.agent.autoApprove:true AND chat.editing.confirmEditRequests:"never" appearing together at 2026-05-01T14:33:21 and both absent by 2026-05-07T15:37:16 — a six-day full-autonomy window that no snapshot, and no vendor console, can ever show. ide_agent_posture rows carry (root, setting_key, value, observed_from, observed_to); rule ide_agent_bypass_enabled is keyed on (root, setting_key, value_hash) so it ages by interval rather than refiring daily, and its severity is posture-weighted like every other behaviour rule.
desktop_surface: Posture screen gains an IDE band: one card per editor root, three-state controls showing observed value beside the hardened value, each with a provenance line naming the exact file; clicking a control opens the dated lane of that key's history with the windows in which it was permissive shaded.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/settings.json (claudeCode.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions:true, chat.agent.maxRequests:1000000000000, chat.agent.sandbox.enabled:'on'); .../User/sync/settings/{20260429T132155,20260501T143321,20260507T153716,...}.json; .../User/globalStorage/agent-host-config.json; .../User/sync/globalState/*.json for the dismissed-warning flags
honest_limit: settings.json is the user layer only: the effective value also depends on workspace, folder and managed-policy layers, so a row without all layers read is labelled 'user layer, precedence incomplete' rather than presented as effective. The dated history exists only where Settings Sync is on — absent for Cursor, Kiro and Antigravity here — so those roots show a snapshot with no interval. Backups are written when sync runs, not when a setting changes, so an interval is an outer bound: a switch flipped on and off between two syncs leaves no trace and is counted in unobserved_window. A permissive setting is a capability, not an act; it must never be rendered as 'the agent did X'. And these are the SYNCED settings, so a bypass may have been enabled on another device and roamed onto this one — an important finding in its own right, recorded as posture_arrived_by_sync with the syncData.machineId, not as a local action.
competitive_note: Cursor's audit events expose privacy_mode and mcp_server_config for Cursor only and Enterprise only; Copilot's audit log 'excludes local prompts' and carries no client settings; nobody exports a dated history of a client-side autonomy switch. market.md's white-space point 2 — consoles are single-tool and blind to other vendors' agents — is exactly what a settings-history reader crosses, since one file here versions both Anthropic's and Microsoft's agent posture.
v1_ref: Vendor lever cards: each tool's own permission config, observed value beside the hardened one
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Retroactive extension-version history from the editor's own Settings Sync backups
description: A snapshot cannot answer 'did this machine ever run the vulnerable version', and polling only samples forward from install day. VS Code already keeps the answer: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/extensions/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>.json, each a {version, content} envelope whose content is a JSON string of [{identifier.id, version, preRelease, pinned}]. The UTC timestamp is IN THE FILENAME, so event_key = sha256(root|filename|extension_id|version) is deterministic and contains no now() — it satisfies the anomaly-key constraint by construction. Verified on this machine: github.copilot-chat 0.45.1 (2026-04-28T19:59:20) -> 0.48.0 (2026-05-14T09:33:39) -> 0.61.0 (2026-08-13T19:24:17); anthropic.claude-code absent -> 2.1.141 -> 2.1.229 -> 2.1.263 today; ollama.ollama first appears 2026-08-13. extension_versions rows are appended per (root, extension_id, version) with observed_first_ts and observed_last_ts widened from the backup set, so known_vulnerable_extension_version fires over an INTERVAL ('ran Amazon Q 1.84.0 between 2025-07-19 and 2025-07-26') rather than over today's snapshot — which is the only shape in which CVE-2025-8217 is detectable at all, since the fix ships as a silent auto-update. Corroborate with <App Support>/<Editor>/CachedExtensionVSIXs, which holds github.copilot-chat-0.48.1 here: a downloaded VSIX for a version that is neither installed nor current.
desktop_surface: Clicking any Extensions-band row opens a version lane: a horizontal timeline of observed versions with advisory-floor bands shaded, each segment labelled with its two bounding observation timestamps and a 'sampled, not continuous' watermark; the incident card renders the interval, the floor version and the advisory id.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/extensions/{20260428T195920,20260514T093339,20260813T192417,lastSyncextensions}.json; ~/Library/Application Support/Code/CachedExtensionVSIXs/
honest_limit: This directory exists ONLY when Settings Sync is signed in — verified absent for Cursor, Kiro and Antigravity IDE on this machine, which have no sync/ dir at all, so those roots degrade to forward-only polling and the lane renders 'history unavailable, snapshot only'. The sync list has a different denominator from extensions.json: it includes built-ins (vscode.bat, ms-vscode.js-debug) that extensions.json omits, so counts from the two readers must never be subtracted from each other. It is the SYNCED set, so a version may have been installed on another machine and roamed here — the row carries syncData.machineId and is labelled 'observed in sync set' not 'ran locally' unless feature 4 or 7 corroborates. The editor rotates these backups, so the earliest observation is a floor on knowledge, not on behaviour, and a version installed and removed entirely between two backups is invisible and counted in an explicit unobserved_window figure.
competitive_note: That v1 feature replays the CLI agents' own backups (~/.claude, ~/.codex); this is a different artifact family with a real UTC timestamp in the filename rather than an mtime. No vendor in the matrix ships version-over-time for IDE extensions: Copilot metrics are ~2 days late and carry no extension version; Cursor's Admin API is Cursor-only and has 'no backfill'; Fleet/osquery gives a snapshot per collection interval.
v1_ref: Retroactive config history replayed from the agents' own rotating backups
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: extension_version_history: the permission that arrived in an auto-update
description: Chrome retains more than one unpacked version per extension id — verified here, bgnkhhnnamicmpeenaelnjfhikgbkllg holds both 5.5.2.19_0 and 5.5.2.20_0, each with its own manifest.json — which makes the on-disk profile an offline record of what an auto-update changed. Read every <ver>_0 directory under Extensions/<id>/, hash each version's permissions, host_permissions and content_scripts.matches, and date the switch from Secure Preferences last_update_time (AdGuard: 13433252744864122 = 2026-09-07T11:05:44Z) against first_install_time. granted_permissions records what the user then accepted. Adds extension_versions(ext_id, version, dir_mtime, permissions_hash, host_permissions_hash, first_seen) plus a computed set-difference between adjacent retained versions, and extension_grant_events from the two timestamps. Rule extension_permission_escalated fires when a version bump adds <all_urls>, cookies, clipboardRead, nativeMessaging, debugger, userScripts or webRequest, or widens content_scripts.matches; anomaly_key = ext_perm:<ext_id>:<from_version>:<to_version>, deterministic and free of now(), so re-scans are idempotent and the escalation channel carries any severity change.
desktop_surface: Posture screen, Browser band drill-down: the two permission lists rendered side by side with added entries marked, the update date, and — when no predecessor survives on disk — the words 'no prior version on disk' in place of a diff.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/<Chromium root>/<Profile>/Extensions/<id>/<version>_0/manifest.json (permissions, host_permissions, optional_permissions, optional_host_permissions, content_scripts.matches); Secure Preferences extensions.settings.<id>.{first_install_time, last_update_time, granted_permissions}
honest_limit: Only versions still on disk are comparable. Chrome deletes older version directories on its own schedule, so the first observation of an extension has no predecessor and the rule yields baseline NULL, printed as 'no prior version on disk' — never as 'no change'. Vole cannot see the CRX signature chain, cannot tell whether the publisher changed hands, and cannot reconstruct a permission that was added and removed between two scans.
competitive_note: Extension-risk vendors diff versions server-side from the store catalogue, which means they see the published lineage but not which two versions this laptop actually holds; nobody in the matrix computes the escalation from the directories the browser itself left behind, offline.
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: extension_store_state: Chrome's own store verdict, read from disk with zero network
description: Chrome caches the Web Store's safety verdict for every installed extension in Secure Preferences -> extensions.settings.<id>.cws-info {is-live, is-present, last-updated-time-millis, no-privacy-practice, unpublished-long-ago, violation-type}, verified present on all six store extensions here (AdGuard: last-updated-time-millis 1788678000000 = 2026-09-06). Alongside it sit .allowlist (Safe Browsing extension allowlist state, 1 here), .disable_reasons (verified [1] on three ids) and .location. Vole reads the verdict the browser already fetched; principle 5 forbids the network call that would refresh it, so the reader stamps verdict_observed_at from the pref file mtime and stores verdict_age_days as a column that every render must print. Adds these as columns on browser_extensions plus rules extension_unpublished_still_installed (is-live false or unpublished-long-ago true while the extension is enabled), extension_policy_violation (violation-type != 0), extension_sideloaded_unpacked (location = 4 UNPACKED, or from_webstore false outside a component/policy install — an extension nobody reviewed) and extension_no_privacy_practice (no-privacy-practice true on an all-urls extension).
desktop_surface: Posture screen, Browser band: each extension row carries a verdict chip reading "Chrome's verdict, N days old" — attributed to Chrome, never to Vole — and an 'unknown' bucket counting the ids that carry no verdict at all.
data_source: ~/Library/Application Support/<Chromium root>/<Profile>/Secure Preferences -> extensions.settings.<id>.{cws-info, allowlist, disable_reasons, location, lastpingday}, plus the file's own mtime
honest_limit: This is Chrome's verdict, not Vole's, and it is exactly as fresh as Chrome's last store ping (lastpingday) — a browser that has not launched in weeks yields a stale verdict, which is printed as an age and never refreshed. Five ids on this machine exist only as a lastpingday stub with no cws-info at all; they land in a counted unknown bucket rather than a clean verdict. Firefox and Safari have no equivalent cached verdict and stay NULL.
competitive_note: Chrome Enterprise Core surfaces extension risk in the admin console only for enrolled browsers — Local State.management.platform.enterprise_mdm_mac is 0 here, which is precisely the enrolment hole. Vole reads the same cws-info from the profile whether or not the browser was ever enrolled, and Secure-Annex-style extension-risk vendors get it by calling the store from their cloud.
gap_area: The non-developer AI surface: browser extensions with declared reach, agentic browsers, and OS-level intelligence

name: Fork drift: the same extension at two versions, and the fork the patch cycle forgot
description: A three-line join over feature 1 that produces a number nobody currently has. Group ai_extensions by extension_id across roots and compare versions. Measured on this machine: ms-python.vscode-python-envs is 1.36.0 in ~/.vscode and 1.20.1 in ~/.antigravity-ide — sixteen minor versions of drift for the identical extension id, because the fork has its own update cadence and its own gallery. Two rules. extension_version_drift_across_forks fires when an id sits BELOW the shipped advisory floor in one root and above it in another: the shape of 'IT pushed the patched build to VS Code and nobody owns the fork', which is how a vulnerable Amazon Q or Cline build survives a remediation sweep. ai_extension_in_non_default_fork fires when an id on the admin blocklist is absent from the primary root but present in a secondary one — a banned assistant reappearing inside Cursor after removal from VS Code. Both rules carry the two versions, the two roots and the floor as their explainability figures, and the anomaly key is (extension_id, root_a, root_b, floor_version) so it never embeds now().
desktop_surface: A drift strip at the top of the Extensions band: one row per drifting extension id showing each root's version side by side with the floor marked, sorted by distance below the floor; Posture screen gets a per-fork 'behind primary root by N extensions' figure.
data_source: the ai_extensions table from feature 1, over ~/.vscode, ~/.vscode-insiders, ~/.cursor, ~/.windsurf, ~/.kiro, ~/.antigravity-ide and each fork's app bundle; advisory floors from the shipped offline content pack
honest_limit: Forks pin their own marketplace — product.json.extensionsGallery.serviceUrl differs per fork and some point at OpenVSX or a private gallery — so 'behind' is not always 'patchable', and a row whose gallery differs from the primary root's is labelled version_incomparable rather than flagged as unpatched. Version strings are compared with a strict semver parser; anything unparseable (a fork's date-stamped or platform-suffixed build) yields no comparison at all rather than a lexicographic guess. A fork with no Settings Sync has only a snapshot, so drift is observable but its onset date is not. And the join says two roots disagree; it cannot say which one the developer actually opens, which is why the drift strip links straight to feature 7's activation counts.
competitive_note: Vendor consoles are per-tool by construction (market.md white-space 2), so no console can compare an extension's version across two editors, and JetBrains Console explicitly excludes what it did not provision. Fleet/osquery could express this join but ships no AI extension table and no advisory floor; Snyk agent-scan reads configs, not versions.
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Editor-synced agent plugins and skills: instruction packs that arrive over the wire with no install event
description: Instructions now reach IDE agents through a channel with no marketplace row, no extension id and no install prompt: Settings Sync. Verified on this machine: ~/.vscode/agent-plugins/cache.json plus ~/.vscode/agent-plugins/vscode-synced-customization-agent-host-claude/1066553724/skills/{pylance-docs,pylance-python-profiling,pylance-refactoring,python-fact-grounded-coding}/SKILL.md — four skill files delivered into the Claude agent host by sync, not by an install; ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/*/SKILL.md holds eighteen more, including shell, automate, create-hook and update-cursor-settings; ~/.kiro/powers/registries is the same shape for Kiro. And sync/profiles/lastSyncprofiles.json declares a profile named 'Agents' with useDefaultFlags.mcp, .languageModels and .extensions all true — a profile that roams MCP servers and model configurations between machines. ide_agent_packs rows are keyed (root, pack_dir, file_path, sha256) with first_seen, reusing the existing hook/plugin first-seen ledger and the instruction-file hidden-Unicode scan verbatim rather than adding new machinery. Rules: synced_agent_pack_first_seen (an instruction pack appeared with no local install), and synced_pack_grants_shell for a pack whose front-matter declares shell or command tools.
desktop_surface: A Synced packs row inside the Posture screen's IDE band: pack directory, file count, the agent host it targets, first-seen date and a hidden-Unicode verdict; the Policy screen shows whether roaming of mcp and languageModels is enabled per profile.
data_source: ~/.vscode/agent-plugins/cache.json and .../vscode-synced-customization-<agent>/<id>/skills/*/SKILL.md; ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/*/SKILL.md; ~/.cursor/plugins/local/; ~/.kiro/powers/registries/; ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/sync/profiles/lastSyncprofiles.json (useDefaultFlags.{mcp,languageModels,extensions})
honest_limit: cache.json carries a numeric sync id, not a publisher, a signature or a source URL, so provenance stops at 'arrived via Settings Sync under this account' — the customer trust anchor cannot be applied and the pack is classed unsigned by construction, never inferred as vendor-signed. SKILL.md content is hashed and scanned in the collector loop and never stored, so the Unicode verdict is a boolean and a count, not a quotable line. Presence of a skill file proves delivery, not that any agent ever loaded it: the tie to actual use exists only where feature 7 shows chat.customModes.claude-code or chat.customModes.agent-host-claude in a workspace (three and two workspaces here respectively). A pack removed upstream disappears locally on the next sync, so the ledger's first_seen is durable but its absence is not evidence of removal by anyone in particular.
competitive_note: That v1 entry enumerates installed_plugins.json and known_marketplaces.json for CLI agents, where an install event exists to observe. The sync channel has none: no vendor in the matrix — including Snyk agent-scan, which does scan skills — treats Settings Sync as a delivery path for agent instructions, and Cursor's Enterprise controls govern accounts, not what roams into the agent's context.
v1_ref: Plugin, skill and marketplace supply-chain inventory
gap_area: Editor-extension inventory and the version-over-time ledger (the IDE-resident AI surface)

name: Admin control resolved vs behaviour observed: autonomousAgentsDisabled while Autopilot ran
description: One line per launch carries the vendor's admin policy exactly as it landed on this device: [GovernanceService] Resolved {'enterprise':true,'provider':'Enterprise','profileArn':'arn:aws:codewhisperer:us-east-1:<acct>:profile/<id>','controlPlaneEndpoint':'https://management.us-east-1.kiro.dev','mcpDisabled':false,'mcpReason':'admin_disabled','webToolsDisabled':false,'autonomousAgentsDisabled':true,'disabledReason':'admin_disabled','registryUrl':'','catalogSize':0}. The same log then shows agent_controller.triggered {autonomyMode:'Autopilot'} and session.json shows autopilot:true. Adds vendor_admin_policy(tool, root_id, resolved_at, control_name, control_value, reason, tenant_ref_hash, control_plane_host, source) and the rule admin_control_unenforced, keyed (tool, control_name, session_id, bucket), whose explainable figures are: control=autonomousAgentsDisabled, admin value=true, observed autonomyMode=Autopilot, executions=N, first at <ts>.
