Adds view v_evidence_gaps and rule unmonitored_interval, which fires only when witness count > 0; observed = witness count, baseline = NULL (no baseline exists for a gap), threshold = the gap-length cutoff in ms. anomaly_key is gap:<epoch_id>:<floor(gap_start/3600000)> so it is stable on re-derivation and never contains now(); a still-open gap escalates through the separate escalation channel rather than minting a second key.
desktop_surface: Coverage strip gains a second figure — 'monitored 96.2% of the last 30 days; 3 gaps, 1 with activity' — clicking opens a Gaps list (interval, length, witness counts broken out by artifact, and what was running). Every incident detail and evidence bundle whose window overlaps a gap carries an inline gap chip.
data_source: collector_runs (v1 Tier 1); ~/.claude/history.jsonl {timestamp, sessionId, project}; ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json {pid, sessionId, startedAt, entrypoint}; ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl {id, updated_at}; ~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite logs{ts, thread_id, process_uuid}; collector_state.last_mtime; usage_events.ts
honest_limit: A gap with no witness stays silent and renders as 'unobserved, no activity witness' — a closed laptop is not tampering and must never be scored as such. Before collector_runs has its first row there is no run record at all, so the entire pre-install past is 'no run record', not 'monitored'. Every witness listed lives in the same user-writable home as the transcripts: an admin who deletes collector_runs rows and the witnesses leaves nothing behind. Detection is retrospective only — it cannot stop the gap, only name it afterwards.
competitive_note: CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne and Jamf buy tamper-resistance with an ES-level sensor the user cannot unload; Vole cannot and must therefore publish coverage instead. No row in the 62-vendor matrix states an observed-fraction-of-window figure, and CrowdStrike's retention is 'not stated'; Fleet/osquery answers point-in-time queries with no gap accounting at all.
v1_ref: Collector self-health: collector_runs, vole doctor, coverage matrix, freshness attestation
gap_area: Evidence integrity when the monitored user is the local admin: gaps, source mutability, store lineage, clock

name: Pack inventory on the wire: the only signal that a rollout missed a laptop
description: Because Vole never fetches, telemetry is the sole way an admin learns that 200 machines missed a pack, so the existing heartbeat export emits one record per content_pack — kind, version, built_at, age_days, ring, load_state, trust, sha256 — and every exported finding, incident and tool-call row carries its `content_rev`. Resource attributes `vole.content.<kind>.version` and `vole.content.<kind>.age_days` ride every OTLP batch so a SIEM groups by version without a join, and the field registry gains those keys explicitly (the export is deny-by-default). The rollout queries ship with the Sigma/SPL pack: distinct devices per content version, and devices whose advisory_floor version trails the fleet mode — because the fleet answer is a SIEM query and one laptop cannot compute it.
desktop_surface: No new screen: the Content table already lists exactly what is exported, and the Privacy Center's live export-payload inspector shows the pack records verbatim as they leave, which is where a DPO checks that a pack row carries no personal data.
data_source: content_packs rows; the existing export outbox, heartbeat export and export_seq cursor.
honest_limit: A laptop that is both stale and not exporting is invisible in both places — the dead-man's switch detects absent heartbeats, not absent content. Ring membership is whatever the admin's MDM wrote locally, so Vole can report which ring this machine claims but cannot verify that the canary ring is the twenty machines the admin intended.
competitive_note: Falcon and SentinelOne consoles show sensor content version per endpoint as a first-class fleet column. Vole has no console, so the same column has to be reconstructed in the customer's SIEM — the "be the source, not the console" position already taken with the osquery table pack.
gap_area: Detection-content lifecycle: how packs, CVE floors and allowlists reach the fleet offline, age, and re-score history

name: MCP inventory export in server.json shape
description: Emit `vole export --mcp --format=server-json`, mapping posture_mcp_servers onto the MCP registry's server.json object shape (name, description, version, packages[] with registryType/identifier/version/runtimeHint, remotes[] with type/url) plus an x-vole extension block carrying mcp_identity, first_seen, last_seen, observed_call_count, config_path and instruction_block_sha256. One file per host, deterministic ordering, no timestamps in the body, so two runs against an unchanged machine diff to nothing and an org can compare its real observed MCP estate against a curated internal registry with plain `diff`. Writing the file is local; shipping it anywhere is a separate opt-in.
desktop_surface: Supply Chain → MCP toolbar gains an Export button that writes the file and reveals it in Finder; Settings shows the last export path and row count. No network path is added.
data_source: posture_mcp_servers joined to observed mcp__<server>__ call counts in tool_calls and posture_injected_text hashes; ~/.claude.json mcpServers, .mcp.json, ~/.codex/config.toml.
honest_limit: server.json describes a package or registry entry, and Vole can fill only the fields a local registration actually contains: description, publisher and canonical version are NULL for a locally registered `npx -y <pkg>` entry, and the export omits NULL rather than inventing a placeholder. The x-vole block is a documented extension, not part of the upstream schema, and that schema is still moving, so the export pins the snapshot version it was written against. It inventories what is registered and observed on this machine, never what an org approved.
competitive_note: v1's export work (vole.event.v1, OTLP, SIEM forwarder) covers usage and incidents; no entry exports posture in an ecosystem-native shape. Snyk agent-scan and Cisco's MCP Scanner emit their own proprietary formats and Zenity keeps its MCP inventory in a SaaS console; a registry-comparable file is the artefact an org actually needs to answer 'which of these are approved'.
field_verified: Sources confirmed, one dependency dissolved. ~/.claude.json carries global `mcpServers: ['searxng','playwright','context7','github']` plus one per-project block (<redacted-local-path> → {"ui-skills":{"type":"http","url":"https://www.ui-skills.com/mcp"}} — a remote, exactly the remotes[] case). ~/.codex/config.toml has `[mcp_servers.node_repl]`, `[mcp_servers.node_repl.env]` and `[mcp_servers.computer-use]`. `posture_mcp_servers`, `posture_injected_text` and `tool_calls` do NOT exist — but observed_call_count does not need them: the existing usage_events.tools column already holds the MCP names, verified by scanning all 18,389 non-null values — mcp__playwright__browser_evaluate 210, mcp__playwright__browser_navigate 196, mcp__searxng__web_url_read 43, mcp__github__search_code 6, etc.
constraint: Constraint 8 (third-party stores read-only) is respected — this only reads configs. Constraint 14 if the server.json snapshot schema is vendored as a data file: like pricing.json it must be inlined at build time, not read at runtime. Nothing else strains; the export writes under the user's chosen path and adds no network, which is what principle 7 asks.

name: Fleet / osquery ATC table pack
description: The cheapest enterprise distribution is not a second agent: osquery's Automatic Table Construction reads SQLite files directly, so ship docs/fleet/vole-atc.conf declaring vole_usage_events, vole_anomalies and vole_sources over ~/.vole/vole.db plus a query pack of saved queries (agents seen per host, sessions in bypass mode, incidents in the last 24 h, tokens by model, unpriced call share). Fleet then reports Vole's evidence on the schedule it already runs, with no new daemon, no new port and no export path. Generate the ATC column list from the redaction manifest that declares which columns may leave (packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts) rather than from types.ts, so an osquery column can never expose a field the exporter is forbidden to send — the raw proposal named a fields.ts registry that does not exist.
desktop_surface: Settings → Export gains a 'Fleet / osquery' section with a Copy button for the generated ATC config, the exact DB path it points at, and the column list it exposes.
data_source: ~/.vole/vole.db (usage_events, anomalies, collector_state); packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts for the allowed column list; osquery ATC configuration format
honest_limit: ATC takes a fixed path and Vole's store lives under a user home, so a shared or multi-account Mac needs one ATC entry per home or a world-readable derived copy under /Library, which is a new artifact with its own privacy question. osquery runs as root and reads the raw file, bypassing every filter Vole applies in its own exporter, so the generated column list is the only control and the docs must say so. It also needs the busy_timeout fix first: db.ts:60 sets none (node:sqlite default 0), so a scheduled osquery read against a WAL store can abort a collector pass.
competitive_note: Fleet already advertises inventory of MCP servers, agents and skills for Claude, OpenAI, Cursor and Windsurf with undocumented depth at $7/host/month; being the table Fleet queries is coexistence rather than competition with the incumbent already on the endpoint. v1 ships SIEM, OTLP and Prometheus exporters but no osquery path, which is the one that requires no network at all.
v1_ref: SIEM forwarder (Splunk HEC / Elastic bulk / Datadog Logs)
field_verified: FAILS its own correction. `ls packages/core/src/sync/` → 'No such file or directory'; there is no sync directory anywhere in packages/core/src (full listing: cli/, collectors/, detect/, util/, db.ts, digest.ts, index.ts, paths.ts, pricing.ts, queries.ts, schema.ts, sqlite.ts, types.ts). The feature replaces the raw proposal's non-existent fields.ts with an equally non-existent manifest.ts — which is in fact an unbuilt v1 Tier-1 roadmap item, roadmap-v1.md:43: 'Redaction manifest and verify --content ... packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts declares exactly which columns may leave'. Everything else CONFIRMED: db.ts:60-61 sets only `journal_mode = WAL` and `synchronous = NORMAL`, no busy_timeout; market.md:121 'Fleet / osquery | ... | $0 / $7 host/mo'; market.md:184 'Fleet/osquery integration rather than a second agent: expose Vole tables'.
constraint: Constraint 7 (the DB holds paths and raw_ref pointers) — an osquery column exposing raw_ref hands a root-run agent a map into ~/.claude transcripts; v1's own sync rule is 'usage_events minus raw_ref' and the ATC column list must match it explicitly, not by reference to a module that does not exist. Constraint 13 for the Settings → Export section (no such section today). Reconciliation, and the lazy one: drop the generator entirely, ship a static docs/fleet/vole-atc.conf with a hand-written column list and one test asserting it stays a subset of an allow-set; when manifest.ts eventually lands, point the test at it. That version is genuinely S and exact_from_local_data.

name: Export sink volume and cardinality measured from real serialized bytes
description: Every SIEM and observability contract meters something — Splunk and Sentinel by GB, Datadog by custom metric series and spans, Elastic by field count — so the question after 'can you export' is always 'what will this cost me'. Before a sink is enabled, serialize the last seven days of real rows through that sink's exact encoder in memory and report measured bytes/day, events/day, spans/day and distinct metric series (the true cardinality of tool × model × confidence × project present in the data), plus the same figures projected over 30 days and labelled as a projection with its window. Nothing is derived from a per-row guess: the numbers come from encoding real rows and counting the resulting bytes, and the sample is discarded rather than written anywhere.
desktop_surface: Settings → Export: each sink card shows 'measured: 41 MB/day, 128k events/day, 312 series (7-day sample)' with a link to the exact range measured, rendered above the Enable switch rather than after it.
data_source: usage_events and anomalies for the selected range; the per-sink encoder in packages/core/src/export/sinks/*.
honest_limit: A seven-day sample is a sample — a busy sprint or a new agent rollout changes the figure, which is why it is labelled with its window rather than presented as a rate. It measures the payload Vole produces, not what the customer's pipeline stores after their own enrichment, retention tier or index-time transforms, so it is a floor for their bill and never a quote.
competitive_note: Datadog bills roughly $160/mo per 100k spans plus overage and Langfuse meters per 100k units; publishing the exact byte and cardinality volume before the switch is flipped is the concrete form of Vole's flat, no-per-span-meter positioning, and no competitor tells a buyer what their own export will cost them.
v1_ref: vole export with versioned public schema (vole.event.v1)
field_verified: The named data source does not exist. `ls packages/core/src/export` → **No such file or directory**; packages/core/src/cli/ contains collect, digest, mcp, pr, seed, statusline, top, verify and nothing else; package.json scripts have no `export` entry. So `packages/core/src/export/sinks/*` — 'the per-sink encoder' this feature measures — is a path to code that has not been written, and roadmap-v1's 'vole export with versioned public schema (vole.event.v1)' is itself unbuilt. What DOES verify is the row side: 29,430 live usage_events and 249 anomalies are available to encode, and the cardinality dimensions are real columns (tool, model, confidence, project — 58 distinct project values, 1 distinct user, 1 distinct machine, so the true series count on a single host is far lower than a fleet's). The one competitive figure I could source is real: market.md:115 'Datadog Agent Observability | … | $160/mo per 100k spans +$3.50-5/10k'.
constraint: No constraint conflict — measuring bytes from real rows through a real encoder and discarding the sample is principle 1 executed properly, and 'labelled as a projection with its window' satisfies principle 2. The problem is ordering, not compliance: constraint 13 (read-model parity) and the whole export subsystem must exist first. A cardinality figure measured on this host (1 user × 1 machine × 58 projects) is also not predictive of a fleet's series count, which is the number a Datadog bill actually turns on — the entry should say the measurement is per-host and multiplies with enrolment.

name: Detection content pack: Sigma, SPL and EQL generated from the rule registry
description: A new log source is worthless until someone writes detections over it, so ship them. Generate docs/siem/sigma/*.yml plus Splunk SPL and Elastic EQL equivalents from the same rule registry the detectors use, covering the exported fields: a session running in bypassPermissions, a secret_finding row, a shadow account class, a burn-rate incident above threshold, a missing heartbeat, and an unmanaged telemetry endpoint. Because field names come from packages/core/src/export/fields.ts and rule ids from packages/core/src/detect/index.ts, a rename in code regenerates the content and a test fails if a shipped rule references a field the exporter cannot emit.
desktop_surface: Settings → Export → 'Detection content' listing the generated rules with a Reveal in Finder action and the rule ids they correspond to; no runtime behaviour is added to the app.
data_source: packages/core/src/detect/index.ts rule list and per-rule thresholds (with the RuleConfig DEFAULTS once they exist); packages/core/src/export/fields.ts wire names.
honest_limit: Sigma has no product/service taxonomy for AI agents, so the pack uses a custom `product: vole` that no backend recognises out of the box and every customer must convert with sigma-cli themselves. Detections that need a baseline (burn rate, tool loop) are computed by Vole and cannot be re-derived in Sigma, so most shipped rules match on Vole's verdicts rather than independently re-detecting — which means they inherit Vole's thresholds and go stale if the customer retunes policy.json without regenerating.
competitive_note: Anthropic hands anomaly detection to the SIEM and ships no content to do it with, and no vendor in the matrix publishes detection rules for coding-agent telemetry. Shipping detections alongside the source is what makes the CISO ask — 'SIEM-native events, not a new console' — actually land instead of becoming a six-week content-engineering project.
field_verified: The registry is thinner than the pack assumes. detect/index.ts exports exactly five rules — detectBurnRate, detectLoops, detectErrorStorms, detectRateLimitPressure, detectContextPressure — and thresholds are module constants, not a registry: burn-rate.ts:4-7 `const WINDOW_MS = 10*60*1000; const MIN_TOKENS_IN_WINDOW = 20_000; const SPIKE_MULTIPLE = 3`. Of the six detections the description promises, only 'a burn-rate incident above threshold' maps to something that exists today; bypassPermissions sessions, secret_finding rows, shadow account class and unmanaged telemetry endpoints have neither a rule nor a table (sqlite_master: three tables). The 'missing heartbeat' one depends on feature 18.
constraint: Constraint 3 is the trap: shipped detections that match on Vole's verdicts inherit Vole's frozen-at-first-sight severity (db.ts:130 INSERT OR IGNORE), so a Sigma rule keyed on severity='critical' silently never fires for an incident that escalated after its first sighting. Constraint 6: any generated query must carry `source='live'` or a customer's SIEM lights up on `pnpm seed` demo data. The honest_limit's own point — that baseline-dependent rules cannot be re-derived in Sigma — is correct and unusually candid.

name: RFC 5424 syslog and CEF sinks for the SIEMs that predate JSON
description: QRadar, ArcSight and most on-prem log estates still ingest syslog and cannot take OTLP, so add two thin sinks over the same field registry: RFC 5424 with a structured-data element [vole@<PEN> event_key="..." tool="..." confidence="..." observed="..."] over TCP+TLS, and ArcSight CEF (CEF:0|Vole|vole|<version>|<rule>|<title>|<sev>| plus mapped extensions) for incidents only. Both build their payload by iterating packages/core/src/export/fields.ts, so a column that cannot leave over OTLP cannot leave over syslog either, and neither carries a free-text message body beyond the rule name.
desktop_surface: Settings → Export sink picker gains 'Syslog (RFC 5424)' and 'CEF' entries with host, port and TLS fields plus a live one-line preview of the exact framed message that would be sent.
data_source: packages/core/src/export/fields.ts; anomalies.{rule,severity,observed,baseline,threshold}; usage_events.{tool,model,session_id}; an IANA PEN for the SD-ID.
honest_limit: Syslog has no acknowledgement and no document id: over UDP messages are lost silently, and over TCP a relay may still truncate at 1024 or 2048 bytes so long attribute sets are cut mid-field. CEF has no place for the cache-write 5m/1h split or the subagent roll-up, so those fields simply do not travel on this sink — Vole must state which sinks are lossy rather than implying parity — and a truncated syslog line looks like a complete one to the receiver.
competitive_note: None of the AI-specific vendors in the matrix (Zenity, Harmonic, Nightfall, Prompt Security/SentinelOne) advertises syslog or CEF output; they all assume a SaaS console or a modern JSON sink. It is table stakes for the on-prem security teams who hold the 'AI Usage Control' budget market.md identifies as the one Vole should sell into.
field_verified: Inputs exist; the sinks do not. anomalies.{rule,severity,observed,baseline,threshold} and usage_events.{tool,model,session_id} are all in schema.ts and populated (live rules: burn_rate_spike 190, loop_suspected 38, context_pressure 10, error_storm 10, rate_limit_pressure 1). No packages/core/src/export/ exists. The IANA PEN is genuinely a forge item — an external registration Vole does not hold, so the SD-ID cannot be written correctly today; feasibility 'needs_network_or_forge' is right for two independent reasons (the socket and the PEN).
constraint: Constraint 14 is satisfied — node:net and node:tls are builtins, so a TLS syslog client needs no dependency, unlike a protobuf or Azure SDK path. Constraint 17: every byte here crosses the network line, so it inherits the opt-in, disclosure and no-egress-switch requirements, and the CEF field loss must be visible in the UI rather than implied as parity.

name: Microsoft Sentinel connector generated from the field registry
description: Sentinel ingest for a custom source is a fixed shape: a Data Collection Endpoint, a Data Collection Rule declaring a column schema, and a *_CL custom table. Generate docs/siem/sentinel/ — the ARM template, the DCR transform KQL, and the VoleAgentEvents_CL and VoleIncidents_CL table schemas — directly from packages/core/src/export/fields.ts, so adding a column regenerates the DCR and schema drift between Vole and the table is structurally impossible. The sink posts to the Logs Ingestion API using the same export_seq cursor and outbox as every other sink, with a client credential held in the Keychain and never in the DB.
desktop_surface: Settings → Export sink card 'Microsoft Sentinel' showing the DCE URI, DCR immutable id and stream name, with a 'Download ARM template' action and the projected monthly GB before the sink can be enabled.
data_source: packages/core/src/export/fields.ts as the schema generator input; usage_events and anomalies rows; Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API.
honest_limit: Purview is the request buyers actually voice and it is the one Vole should decline: Purview DSPM for AI ingests from its own browser extension and device onboarding with no public ingestion API for third-party AI events, so the only honest answer is Sentinel plus a note explaining why Purview is not possible rather than a half-working connector. Sentinel ingest is billed per GB by Microsoft, so the volume forecast must be shown before enabling. A column type change on an existing _CL table requires a new table, not an edit, so schema evolution costs the customer a migration.
competitive_note: Microsoft Purview's own coverage of coding agents is a domain wildcard list of browser sites, and Copilot's usage metrics are credits with a two-day lag; a Sentinel table carrying exact per-session CLI-agent tokens and explainable incidents fills a gap Microsoft's own stack does not, inside the console the customer already pays for.
v1_ref: SIEM forwarder (Splunk HEC / Elastic bulk / Datadog Logs)
field_verified: Generator input confirmed (schema.ts column list, anomalies and usage_events rows, 29,511 live events here); everything downstream is greenfield — no docs/siem/, no export/fields.ts, no Keychain use anywhere in packages/core (grep for Keychain/security-framework returns nothing; the collector is a Node SEA with no macOS API access, so the credential must be reached through the Swift app or a shelled-out `security` call, which the description does not address).
constraint: Constraint 14 twice: the credential cannot be read by the SEA collector without a runtime file read or a subprocess, and the Logs Ingestion API's auth flow must not pull in an Azure SDK — it has to be a hand-rolled OAuth2 client-credentials POST over node:https. Constraint 17: this is the largest single egress surface in the shard and needs the volume forecast BEFORE enablement, which the desktop_surface correctly puts on the card.

name: Loopback OTLP receiver with parser-fidelity reconciliation
description: Claude Code's own opt-in telemetry emits things the JSONL never records: claude_code.lines_of_code.count, claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision (accept/reject), and the events tool_decision with its source (config / hook / user_permanent / user_temporary), permission_mode_changed, mcp_server_connection, plugin_installed, hook_* and auth. Add `vole collect --otel-listen` binding 127.0.0.1:4318 only and refusing any other bind, accepting http/protobuf and http/json, writing to a separate agent_telemetry(id, tool, session_id, event_name, ts, attrs_json, source) table — never into usage_events, because these numbers are tool-reported rather than parsed and must keep a different provenance badge; fields produced only under OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT or raw API bodies are dropped at parse, before storage. On top of it, a native_telemetry_gap rule compares per session and hour the claude_code.token.usage totals in agent_telemetry against the summed usage_events rows for the same session and fires warn with observed = parsed tokens, baseline = tool-reported tokens, threshold = the tolerated delta — and fires in reverse when the receiver saw a session id with no parsed rows at all, meaning the walker missed a transcript. That reconciliation is the answer to the single biggest risk in the product: Anthropic states transcripts are internal and change between versions, so a silent parser regression would quietly hollow out every downstream feature.
desktop_surface: A new Monitor → 'Agent-reported' pane listing permission-mode changes, tool decisions and MCP connections with a 'tool-reported' badge visibly distinct from the parsed rows everywhere else in the app; the gap incident appears in the normal Incidents feed naming the session, both figures and the delta; Settings → Export shows a 'parser fidelity' line with the last reconciliation result and its sample size.
data_source: OTLP/HTTP on 127.0.0.1:4318 from Claude Code with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1; [otel] in ~/.codex/config.toml (exporter none by default); usage_events for the same session_id; packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts reconciliation pattern.
honest_limit: This only covers sessions where someone turned telemetry on, which is not the default, so both the pane and the reconciliation are a spot check on a subset and must be shown as such rather than as zero or as fleet-wide assurance. OTLP records carry no natural id, so idempotency needs a synthetic key over (session, event name, timestamp, attributes) and a clock change can duplicate. Claude does not pass OTEL_* into Bash, hooks or MCP subprocesses and collapses MCP tool names to 'custom'/'mcp_tool', so this stream is coarser than the transcript for tool identity. The two sources count different things at the edges — the receiver may report a turn the transcript records as two coalesced copies — so the tolerated delta is a tuning constant that must be printed in the incident, not hidden. It is also a listening socket: off by default, loopback only, disclosed in SECURITY.md.
competitive_note: Zenity ingests native hooks plus OTel as a SaaS; doing the same on loopback with no cloud is the works-council-safe version, and it fills the exact gaps (lines of code, edit accept/reject) that make Vole comparable to Copilot's cohort metrics. No vendor cross-checks its own parser against the tool's own telemetry, which is the concrete answer to the 'your parsers are a maintenance liability' objection market.md raises against the whole approach.
v1_ref: OTEL receiver collector for tools that only telemeter
field_verified: Every named field verified against the shipped binary. `strings` over <redacted-local-path> (Mach-O arm64, 199 MB, installed 2026-09-06) returns hits for claude_code.token.usage (2), claude_code.lines_of_code.count (2), code_edit_tool.decision (2), permission_mode_changed (2), mcp_server_connection (8), tool_decision (5), user_permanent (7), OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS (6), CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY (9). So the stream exists and the gating env var is real. ~/.codex/config.toml has no [otel] section, consistent with 'exporter none by default'. usage_events is available for the same session_id join; cli/verify.ts is the reconciliation precedent (539 lines, top-level await, independent RATES copy).
constraint: Constraint 14 blocks half the wire format: 'accepting http/protobuf' needs a protobuf decoder, and the SEA must stay zero-runtime-dependency with node: builtins only. Reconciliation: ship http/json only (which roadmap-v1's own OTEL-receiver item already scopes to), or hand-roll the handful of varint reads. Constraint 17: a listening socket is not egress but is new attack surface — off by default, 127.0.0.1 only, refuse any other bind, disclosed in SECURITY.md, which the description already commits to. Constraint 5/1: OTLP records carry no natural id, so the synthetic key over (session, event name, timestamp, attributes) must be stable under a clock change or re-runs double-count. Constraint 3: the gap rule's anomaly_key must be (session, hour) with no now().

name: Console-blind spend and the shadow_account_spend rule
description: A local session is console-blind when its exact tokens map to no vendor row for its day, model and identity. Three classes are already detectable from stored rows: an agent talking to a non-vendor model (2,661 `claude_code` calls and 559.1M tokens here carry `qwen3.8-27b-fp8`, `glm-5.2`, `anthropic/claude-ccr-<hex>`, `fable-fusion-27b`, `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha` — Anthropic's console will never show one of them); a vendor entitlement consumed through a third party (3,336 OpenCode messages with `providerID='github-copilot'`); and an account mismatch, where `bridge-session.ownerOrganizationUuid` or OpenCode `account_state.active_org_id` differs from the org the reconcile ran against. Rule `shadow_account_spend` fires per (identity, day, class) with `anomaly_key='reconcile:shadow:<identity_hmac>:<day>:<class>'` — deterministic, no `now()`, per the anomalies constraint — populating `observed` (local tokens), `baseline` (vendor tokens for the same cell) and `threshold`.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen right pane 'Console never saw this', plus a dedicated incident card listing the model set and the token total; the Breakdown gains a 'console-blind' badge on any model absent from the reconciled vendor's model list.
data_source: usage_events (tool, model, cost_usd IS NULL, session_id) joined to vendor_ledger and vendor_identities; ~/.claude-code-router/ and settings `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` as corroborating evidence.
honest_limit: 'Console never saw it' is provable only for a window and identity the reconcile actually pulled; without a successful pull the rule must not fire at all, and under a subscription plan it can never fire for Anthropic. A model name Vole does not recognise is evidence of routing, not proof of it — a renamed first-party model looks identical, which is why the incident quotes the model string rather than asserting a destination. The rule needs a vendor-side pull, so it is the one feature in this category that is not purely local.
competitive_note: market.md white-space finding 4 names shadow accounts and shadow agents as Vole's genuine differentiator because the detection is auth-path and plan agnostic. Gateways see only what routes through them; Copilot-via-OpenCode routes through nothing they control.
field_verified: Local halves verified, network half verified absent. Class 1: 2,549 claude_code rows / 559,145,144 tokens on non-Anthropic model ids (feature says 2,661 calls — count off by 112; the 559.1M token figure is exact). Class 2 verified verbatim: `SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE source='live' AND model LIKE 'github-copilot/%'` -> 3,336, matching the claimed 3,336 OpenCode messages with providerID='github-copilot'. Class 3 (account mismatch) cannot be evaluated: `.tables` on ~/.vole/vole.db returns `anomalies  collector_state  usage_events` — vendor_ledger and vendor_identities DO NOT EXIST, no reconcile has ever run, and the feature's own gate ('without a successful pull the rule must not fire at all') means it fires never, today.
constraint: Constraint 3, first half: `anomaly_key='reconcile:shadow:<identity_hmac>:<day>:<class>'` is deterministic and now()-free — compliant, and correctly avoids the antigravity.ts:63 anti-pattern. Constraint 3, second half is unaddressed: anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE (db.ts:137), so once a (identity, day, class) cell fires, a later pull that grows the gap can never update observed/baseline — the incident freezes at its first, smallest figure. This feature needs the upsert-on-greater-observed change (code-map bug 9) as an explicit prerequisite. Constraint 17 (keep it local, no silent network): a vendor pull is egress and must ship behind the same disclosed opt-in and no-egress switch that UpdateChecker.swift:27 currently violates — otherwise this feature makes an existing principle-7 breach worse.

name: cost_basis stamped at insert, with unpriced counters in every aggregate
description: `cost_usd` today mixes three incompatible definitions with no marker: Anthropic list-equivalent for claude_code via computeCost, OpenCode's own provider bill for opencode rows (opencode.ts:143), and genuine zero for free models — and getSummary runs a bare `SUM(cost_usd)` that adds $1,778.48 of list-equivalent value to $580.26 of provider-reported dollars and calls the result one KPI. Worse, that SUM silently drops 4,723 of 29,284 live rows (16%) whose cost is NULL, including 3,550 exact-confidence rows (claude_code 2,678, codex 83, grok 789) representing real tokens whose model has no rate. Add a `cost_basis` TEXT column written at insert (`'anthropic_list' | 'provider_reported' | 'self_hosted_uncosted' | 'contract:<name>'`) as an add-nullable-column migration, and add `unpricedCalls` and `unpricedTokens` fields to Summary, ToolSummary, LiveSession and SessionDetail so every aggregate either groups by basis or returns `mixedBasis: true` beside the figure. v1 defers rate_source to a Tier 4 FinOps item, but every dollar-denominated thing above it — budgets, budget_exceeded, showback, cost per PR, policy budget clauses, the evidence pack — is wrong without it.
desktop_surface: Every cost figure in MenuPanel, the Dashboard KPI tile and Breakdown gains a basis chip; a mixed roll-up renders 'mixed basis' with a tap-through split, and the unpriced count sits beside the total as '$1,778.48 · 2,678 calls unpriced' instead of an unqualified dollar figure.
data_source: packages/core/src/queries.ts:56,79,294,459,615 SUM(cost_usd); pricing.ts computeCost and unpricedReason; collectors/opencode.ts:143; live vole.db counts above.
honest_limit: Existing rows have no basis and must migrate as NULL rather than be guessed, and since the upsert only rewrites a row when total_tokens strictly grows, backfilling basis on historical rows needs an explicit one-shot widening UPDATE keyed on event_key, not the normal collect loop. A row whose model has no published rate stays NULL forever — never estimated — so a USD aggregate over a scope containing Codex or Grok is not evaluable and must refuse rather than under-report. A single session that switched models mid-thread can legitimately carry two bases. Provider-reported cost is the vendor's number, which Vole cannot verify.
competitive_note: v1's rate_source introduces 'list | contract:<name> | opencode' for contract pricing but does not treat OpenCode's provider-reported dollar as a different definition from Anthropic list value, so the headline KPI stays wrong and every Tier 4 dollar feature inherits it. Cursor calls its own cost 'best-effort'; no competitor exposes cost basis at all, and exact-or-NULL with a visible definition is the whole FinOps pitch.
v1_ref: Contract rate cards, rate_source labelling and seat-price comparison
field_verified: Every figure verified, and I found the enum is wrong. Verified: 29,430 live rows, 4,723 NULL cost_usd (16.05%); exact-confidence unpriced = claude_code 2,678 + codex 83 + grok 789 = 3,550 ✓ to the row. Basis mixing verified: claude_code SUM(cost_usd) = **$1,798.52** (Anthropic list-equivalent via computeCost) added to opencode **$580.26** (provider-reported, opencode.ts:143 `cost_usd: typeof d.cost === 'number' ? d.cost : null` with the comment 'OpenCode's own figure. A real 0 (free local model) is kept') by a bare `SUM(cost_usd)` at queries.ts:56, 79, 196, 294, 569, 615 and DB.swift:161. (Feature cites line 459 — no SUM there; the real lines are 196 and 569.) DB.swift:161-163 confirmed: `COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tf THEN total_tokens END),0), SUM(cost_usd), …`. **NEW FINDING that breaks the proposed enum**: `select … where tool='claude_code' and cost_usd is null and confidence='exact'` and counting Anthropic-named models returns **0 of 2,678**. Every unpriced Claude Code row is a foreign model routed through the Claude Code binary — qwen3.8-27b-fp8 (1,492), glm-5.2 (564), `anthropic/claude-ccr-h7177656e2f7177656e332e382d3237622d667038` (456, a hex-encoded claude-code-router alias for qwen3.8-27b-fp8), `<synthetic>` (129), fable-fusion-27b, openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha, gemini-3.7-flash, lfm2.5:latest.
constraint: Constraint 2 (upsert rewrites only when total_tokens strictly grows, so backfilling basis needs an explicit one-shot widening UPDATE keyed on event_key) — named correctly ✓. Constraint 12 (add-nullable-column only via migrate()'s PRAGMA probing) — satisfied ✓. TWO it does not name: constraint 11 (node:sqlite named binding is strict — a new column requires matching edits to the INSERT column list, the @params object, the UsageEvent type, schema.ts and migrate(), or the whole batch throws) and constraint 13 (read-model parity: unpricedCalls/unpricedTokens on Summary, ToolSummary, LiveSession and SessionDetail must be written twice, queries.ts and DB.swift, or the app cannot show them). Reconciliation on the enum: `'anthropic_list' | 'provider_reported' | 'self_hosted_uncosted' | 'contract:<name>'` has no home for the 2,678 rows above — they are neither Anthropic list, nor provider-reported, nor knowably self-hosted. Add a fifth value (`routed_foreign` / `unknown_route`) stamped when the tool is claude_code but the model resolves to no Anthropic rate, and surface it: 2,678 calls of foreign-model traffic through the corporate coding agent is a shadow-AI finding wearing a FinOps costume.

name: DSAR export that answers Art. 15(1)(h): the logic, not just the rows
description: v1's 'vole dsar export' ships the subject's rows plus the manifest and policy; Art. 15 also requires categories, recipients, the retention period and, for anything resembling automated evaluation, meaningful information about the logic involved. Extend the bundle so each incident about the subject carries its rule id, the effective thresholds in force at detection time, and the observed/baseline/threshold figures already stored at schema.ts:42-64 but selected by no reader today (queries.ts:230 omits them, DB.swift:227 likewise), rendered in plain language: 'this fired because 36,751 tokens in 10 minutes exceeded 3x the 12,149-token median'. Recipients come from the export_sinks ledger and the retention period from the per-class retention table.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Export my data' producing the bundle with a preview listing its sections; every row in the existing Incidents feed gains a 'Why this fired' disclosure showing the same three figures — the same disclosure a security lead wants for triage.
data_source: anomalies.observed/.baseline/.threshold/.rule/.window_start/.window_end (stored, never read); rule thresholds today hard-coded as module constants at burn-rate.ts:4-7, loop.ts:4-8, error-storm.ts:4-6, rate-limit.ts:4-5, context-pressure.ts:5-7; the export_sinks ledger; the per-class retention table.
honest_limit: Incidents detected before rule-version stamping existed can only cite today's thresholds and must be labelled 'thresholds not recorded at detection time'. INSERT OR IGNORE at db.ts:137 freezes the first verdict, so observed is the value at first sight rather than the worst value in the window, and the export has to say which.
competitive_note: v1 has the export but not the logic disclosure, and the figures needed already sit unread in the schema, which makes this cheap. No competitor ships a subject-facing explanation of why a detection fired.
v1_ref: Data-subject access and erasure: vole dsar export and vole forget
field_verified: The columns exist and are unread, exactly as claimed. schema.ts:54-56 declares `observed REAL NOT NULL, baseline REAL, threshold REAL` inside the anomalies block; queries.ts:225-235 getAnomalies selects `id, rule, severity, tool, session_id, model, window_start, window_end, title, detail, confidence, source` -- all three figures omitted. Every threshold constant is at the cited line: burn-rate.ts:4/6/7, loop.ts:4/5/6/8, error-storm.ts:4/5/6, rate-limit.ts:4/5, context-pressure.ts:5/6/7. And the plain-language sentence is ALREADY WRITTEN: `select detail from anomalies limit 1` -> 'Burned 36,751 tokens in 10 min (3,675/min) across 2 calls — 3.0x this model's typical 12,149-token window. Session 019e5765.'
constraint: C3 respected and reinforced -- the feature exists because principle 3 currently leaks (the figures are stored and never selected). Its own honest limit about INSERT OR IGNORE freezing the first verdict is correct (db.ts INSERT_ANOMALY is INSERT OR IGNORE), so `observed` is the value at first sight, never the worst in the window, and the export must say which. C12 parity for the 'Why this fired' disclosure.

name: Enterprise demo story: seed --story, an unmissable demo bar and a guided tour
description: cli/seed.ts produces one implicit user, one project and four rule firings — nothing a security buyer wants to see. Add `pnpm seed --story=enterprise`, still writing only source='seed', generating twelve pseudonymous employees across three machines, an unsanctioned Grok CLI on two hosts, three secret findings at different lifecycle states, a bypassPermissions session with a destructive command and a quota-exhausted day: enough to populate every screen. The app gains a demo-mode bar that is impossible to miss, extending the existing 'Demo Data' toolbar item (DashboardView.swift:325), plus a scripted six-stop tour, and every export path refuses seed rows so a demo can never become evidence.
desktop_surface: A persistent striped bar across the top of the window whenever any visible row is seed, with a 'Purge demo data' button; Cmd-Shift-D starts the tour, which walks Overview → Shadow AI → Data Exposure → Live Sessions → Incidents → Evidence bundle with a caption per stop.
data_source: cli/seed.ts source='seed' rows and purgeSeed in db.ts; the seedClause appended by every production query; DashboardView.swift:325 'Demo Data' toolbar item.
honest_limit: Seed data is fiction and must never appear in an evidence bundle, a posture coverage ratio or an exported metric — the only guard is the source column, and getSessionDetail (queries.ts:399) has no source clause today, so drill-downs leak seed rows until that is fixed. Re-running seed is not idempotent (seed.ts:173), so the bar must offer purge rather than assuming a clean re-seed, and a story is a story: it proves the screens render, never that the buyer's fleet looks like this.
competitive_note: Every enterprise competitor demos a cloud console with a canned tenant; a prospect running Vole on their own laptop sees their own agents in ninety seconds, and the seed story exists only to fill the screens their laptop cannot yet fill — a design-partner motion rather than a sales-engineer motion.
v1_ref: vole.computer static site with docs, downloads, changelog, signed appcast, demo page and status monitor
field_verified: All premises confirmed. seed.ts:41 `const NOW = Date.now()` with :61 `event_key: \`seed:${over.tool}:${seq++}\`` — keys stable, timestamps shift each run, and db.ts:102's `WHERE excluded.total_tokens > usage_events.total_tokens` means a re-run leaves stale ts on every row whose tokens do not grow: 'not idempotent' verified. seed.ts:9-10 states it 'deliberately exercises all four rules'; :180 `detectBySource(all, { seed: seedRateLimits }, NOW)` runs the real detectors. DashboardView.swift:313-316 is the `Label("Demo Data", systemImage: "testtube.2")` toolbar item (feature says :325). queries.ts:396-399 getSessionDetail is `SELECT * FROM usage_events WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY ts, id` — no source clause, so drill-downs do leak seed rows, exactly as claimed. UNNAMED BLOCKER: db.ts:129 is `stmt.run({ ...r, ...ORIGIN })` — ORIGIN is spread LAST and overwrites any user/machine the caller sets, and UsageEvent carries no identity fields at all. Twelve pseudonymous employees cannot be seeded through insertEvents today.
constraint: Constraint 6 is the entire feature and it is respected in design (source='seed' only, detection partitioned, purge by source). But the twelve-employee story collides with the ORIGIN spread above: seeding distinct principals requires either bypassing insertEvents — breaking the single-write-path invariant — or changing db.ts's spread order so an explicitly-set user/machine survives, plus adding those fields to UsageEvent. Prefer the second; it is three lines and it is also what fleet ingest will eventually need. Constraint 6 also demands fixing queries.ts:399 before any drill-down ships, or a demo contaminates an evidence path.

name: Per-active-agent-host meter, computed and auditable offline
description: v1 prices per seat; the research supports per active agent host, flat, at roughly $7-10/month with a free tier at ten hosts, because that is what Fleet ($7/host) and the 'AI Usage Control' budget line (+73% to 2027) support, and because a seat count cannot be verified from a laptop while an active host can. Ship `vole hosts --range=30d`: COUNT(DISTINCT user || '@' || machine) over sessions with at least one live row, plus the underlying rows, so a customer audits their own invoice without contacting anyone — no activation call, no phone-home, the same figure on the invoice derivable from their own database. Per-token, per-event, per-incident and per-GB pricing stay excluded by design: a commercial incentive attached to the numbers Vole reports would corrode 'never invent a number' faster than any bug.
desktop_surface: Settings → Licence shows the 30-day active-host count with a 'show the rows' disclosure and the edition (Core / Enterprise / Fleet), and states in one line that collection, rules and every read model behave identically in all three.
data_source: usage_events.user and usage_events.machine — two columns db.ts:19-35 stamps on every row at insert and that no query in queries.ts or DB.swift has ever selected
honest_limit: A host that never runs the collector is never counted, so the meter is a floor and never an inventory; the MDM's own device list is the expected set to reconcile against. user@machine is an OS identity, not an SSO principal: two people sharing a laptop are one host, one person on three laptops is three. Hostnames routinely contain a person's name (this machine's does), so the count ships as a count and the underlying rows never leave the device.
competitive_note: The explicit contrast with Datadog ($160/mo per 100k spans plus overage), Langfuse ($6-8/100k units) and Braintrust: a flat per-host price is quotable in a first email and survives procurement, while a metered price on telemetry volume punishes the customer for adopting agents — the exact behaviour the buyer is trying to measure. It also undercuts per-user multi-year DLP contracts (Cyberhaven estimated $30-48K/yr) without a discount conversation.
v1_ref: docs/PACKAGING.md: three editions and per-seat pricing
field_verified: CONFIRMED precisely, including the negative. db.ts:19-35 is `function origin(): { user: string | null; machine: string | null }` using userInfo().username and hostname(), with `const ORIGIN = origin()` at module scope and @user/@machine in the INSERT column list — the two columns are stamped on every row exactly as claimed. The never-selected claim holds: grep for user/machine in queries.ts returns only a comment at line 188 ('`by` is a closed union, never user text'), and DB.swift returns only an unrelated comment at line 133 — neither reader has ever selected either column. Live data confirms the meter and its own honest limit in one row: `select user, machine, count(*) ... → shiva|Marys-MacBook-Pro.local|29469` — one host, and the hostname does contain the person's name. Pricing sourced verbatim at market.md:190: per 'active agent host' (>=1 session in last 30 days) at ~$7-10/host/month, Fleet $7/host, free <=10 hosts, 'Flat, no per-span/GB meter — the explicit contrast to Datadog/W&B/Braintrust'.
constraint: Constraint 6 (seed and live never mix) — the count must append AND source='live' or demo rows inflate a customer's invoice; the feature does say 'sessions with at least one live row', so this is handled but must stay explicit in the SQL. Constraint 13 (a DB.swift port for the Settings → Licence row, which does not exist today — settingsPane has General/Data/about sections only). The deeper tension is with principle 1: a commercial figure computed by the engine that must never invent a number. The 'show the rows' disclosure is the correct mitigation and must not be optional.

name: principal_lifecycle: a declared state, never an inferred one
description: An append-only principal_lifecycle(principal_id, state active|departing|departed|scope_changed|suspended, effective_from, effective_to, declared_by, basis, decl_hash, source, first_seen, last_seen) sourced from a new lifecycle[] block in ~/.vole/policy/identity.json (managed mode) or an explicit `vole lifecycle set` (personal mode); one row per declaration, never updated in place, so the state at any past instant is a query (latest effective_from <= t), not a mutable column. Nothing in the codebase may write this table from observation: silence means the collector was off, the tool's retention pruned the source, or the person was on leave — it never means departed. verify --lifecycle FAILs if any row carries declared_by='inferred', and the table takes the source column and seed/live partition every table needs (constraint 6). decl_hash is the sha256 of the declaring file so every downstream pack can cite which version of the declaration authorised it.
desktop_surface: People view gains a state chip beside each principal (Active / Departing since / Departed / Moved) whose popover shows declared_by, basis, effective_from and the decl_hash; a new Lifecycle screen lists declarations chronologically. Principals with no declaration render 'no declaration', never a guess.
data_source: ~/.vole/policy/identity.json (new lifecycle[] block); `vole lifecycle set` CLI; no agent artifact read
honest_limit: Vole cannot know anyone left a company. It records who said so, when, and on what basis. With no declaration every lifecycle feature reports 'no declaration' rather than inferring one from inactivity; HR/IdP sync would be network and is not proposed.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-vendor matrix ties a coding-agent record to an employment state — Cyberhaven, CrowdStrike Falcon AIDR and MintMCP scope by device and console identity, and the employment state lives in an HR system their console never sees.
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: Departure evidence pack: one principal, one window, a denominator on every figure
description: `vole pack --principal <id> --window 30d --basis <text>` is the existing incident-bundle and export machinery scoped to one principal and one window, writing a packs(pack_id, principal_id, window_start, window_end, basis, purpose, created_at, row_counts_json, chain_head) row and the checkpoint-chain head over what it emitted. Sections, each with its own denominator: surfaces used with account class, unsanctioned surfaces from the policy join, secret_sightings by class and direction, dlp_egress destinations, context_edges and agent_pushed_data_off_device, package and VCS actions, remote-execution hops, grant/override changes inside the window, and incidents with the observed/baseline/threshold columns that queries.ts:230 never selects today. Every figure carries three fractions: collector coverage over the window from collector_runs/evidence_gaps, source survival from evidence_freeze, and the pre_tenancy exclusion count. The header block refuses to render empty — it prints the lawful basis given at the command line, the declaration that triggered it (declared_by, basis, decl_hash), the purpose from the closed purpose union, and the custody sentence bounding what the pack claims.
desktop_surface: Lifecycle screen action 'Build departure pack', opening in the just-in-time evidence viewer with the existing pre-export field preview and re-identification scan, a coverage column per section, and the not-covered list rendered before the export button is enabled.
data_source: vole.db only — usage_events, tool_calls, secret_sightings, dlp_egress, context_edges, ai_surfaces, grants/overrides, anomalies, collector_runs, evidence_freeze; no new disk read
honest_limit: It proves what the agents recorded while the collector ran, not what the human did — browser chat, phone, personal laptop and any tool with no collector are absent by construction and are named in a 'not covered' section. A window whose source was pruned reads 'source deleted', never 'no activity'. Re-scanning a leaver is a new processing purpose: the pack prints the basis it was handed and will not run without one, because a departed person cannot consent to a fresh scan.
competitive_note: MintMCP, Cyberhaven and CrowdStrike can print a per-user report, but from a console already holding prompt text under vendor retention; Anthropic's Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry and personal accounts, so the shadow-account half of a leaver's story is missing there by construction.
v1_ref: Compliance evidence pack export

name: Credential residency and liveness sweep: the rotation worklist at exit
description: At a departing or departed declaration, enumerate where provider credentials still live on this device — names and metadata only, never a value. Reads ~/.codex/auth.json auth_mode ('chatgpt' here), last_refresh (2026-09-07T05:08:23Z here), presence booleans for OPENAI_API_KEY and tokens.account_id; Keychain service names from `security dump-keychain` attributes, which on this machine list Claude Code-credentials, Cursor Safe Storage, Grok Bot Safe Storage, com.anthropic.operon-cli and com.local.gemini-gateway-for-claude; export names in ~/.zshrc and ~/.zprofile; env blocks in ~/.claude/settings.json and its rotating .ccr/.bak backups; LaunchAgent EnvironmentVariables keys; and .env paths under known project roots. Adds credential_residency(principal_id, store_kind keychain|file|env|launchd|config, locator, key_name, provider, present, last_refresh_ts, last_observed_use_ts, first_seen, last_seen) plus a departure view ordered by still-live-and-still-used, joining each credential to the last session that used the matching provider — a rotation list rather than a hunch.
desktop_surface: Lifecycle panel section 'Rotate on exit': one copyable row per credential with a state chip (live OAuth, refreshed <date> / key name present / no use observed) and a link to the sessions that used that provider.
data_source: ~/.codex/auth.json (auth_mode, last_refresh, key presence); security dump-keychain attribute names; ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile; ~/.claude/settings.json + backups env blocks; ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist EnvironmentVariables; .env paths
honest_limit: A name is not a valid credential and absence is not proof one was never there. A locked keychain or a missing Full Disk Access grant yields NULL, not zero. Vole never reads the secret, so two keys sharing a name are indistinguishable, and a key that only ever lived on a server is invisible here. last_refresh proves the session was alive at that instant and says nothing about now.
competitive_note: NHI vendors (Token Security, Astrix/Cisco, Oasis-Cyera) enumerate keys from cloud provider APIs and never see the laptop copy; TruffleHog and GitGuardian find keys in repos, not in Keychain, a LaunchAgent env block or a settings.json backup.
v1_ref: key_residency: naming where else this key lives, so a spend gap stops being a mystery

name: Departure delta against the principal's own baseline, purpose-gated
description: Inside the pack only, and only for a principal whose declared state is departing or departed: a table comparing the last N days against that same principal's prior 90-day median in exposure-relevant counts alone — secret_sightings by class, dlp_egress destinations, off-device pushes from context_edges and agent_pushed_data_off_device, repositories first touched in the window, package installs, VCS pushes to non-corporate remotes, and unsanctioned surfaces first seen. No composite score, no cross-person ranking, no output or productivity axis; the inalienable exclusion floor stays in force and the table refuses to render when either window's coverage fraction is below the pack's floor. Adds one member to the closed purpose union, 'offboarding_review', so the purpose-bound query layer refuses this view in every other context and the access log records each render with the pack_id that authorised it.
desktop_surface: A section inside the departure-pack preview, deliberately unreachable from the People view or any live screen, with both windows' coverage fractions printed beside every pair of figures.
data_source: secret_sightings, dlp_egress, context_edges, tool_calls, VCS/package action ledgers, usage_events.project — all existing rows, no new read
honest_limit: A change in counts is not intent. A quiet baseline can mean the collector was off or the tool's retention pruned the window, and the same delta appears when someone simply finished a project and started another. The view emits no incident, produces no score, and prints the coverage fraction of both windows next to every figure.
competitive_note: Insider-risk and UAM products build a person-level risk score out of content; this deliberately produces none, which is what makes it defensible to a works council under GDPR Art. 88 and BetrVG §87(1) Nr. 6 — there is no score to contest, only counted rows with their denominators.
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: Costs screen and `vole showback` with the coverage fraction attached to every total
description: The app's cost KPI is `SUM(cost_usd)` in DB.swift:161, which silently drops the 16% of rows with no price, so the headline understates and nobody can tell. Give Costs its own screen where every total reads 'across N of M calls; P unpriced (<reason>)' using pricing.ts unpricedReason, with breakdown dimensions that already exist as columns but have never been grouped: `user` and `machine` (stamped on all 29,284 rows since day one and selected by no query), project/repo, agent, model, tool and confidence. The same read model backs `vole showback --by=user,team,repo,model --range=30d --format=table|csv|json`, where team comes from an opt-in `~/.vole/attribution.json` and repo comes from the normalised git origin rather than cwd, and every output row carries five numbers rather than three — calls, tokens, priced cost, unpriced calls, activity_only calls — so a team running everything through a local model shows as high-usage-and-uncosted rather than as cheap. The screen states its definition once in the header rather than hiding it.
desktop_surface: A Costs screen with a totals header carrying the coverage fraction inline, a stacked bar with a dimension picker (user/machine/repo/agent/model), and a table whose unpriced rows render an em dash and a reason chip instead of $0.00; a Showback pivot in the Dashboard sidebar with basis chips per cell, gated behind the governance tier's per-person policy switch.
data_source: usage_events.{user, machine, project, model, tool, agent_id, cost_usd, cost_basis, confidence}; pricing.ts unpricedReason and data/pricing.json; <cwd>/.git/config remote and ~/.claude.json githubRepoPaths for repo identity; ~/.vole/attribution.json.
honest_limit: This is equivalent API value, not an invoice: subscription seats, Bedrock/Vertex routing and non-Anthropic list rates are not modelled, and cost is not date-aware because pricing.json's effective_from is never read. On one laptop `user` has exactly one value, so real showback is a fleet feature needing opt-in sync and the single-host view must be labelled 'this machine' rather than presented as an org report. `project` is a filesystem path containing a username until repo identity resolves it, and worktrees, monorepos and cloned forks collapse or split incorrectly without git-origin normalisation. Per-person cost views carry works-council and GDPR Art. 88 exposure and must be off by default.
competitive_note: v1 derives the repo identity keys but the showback report itself is absent from all 143 features. Claude Code Analytics is daily, per-user and excludes Bedrock, Vertex and every other vendor's agent; Cursor's is Enterprise-only and Cursor-only; ccusage is local and free but has no security surface. Exact per-session, per-repo, per-person cost with a visible coverage fraction is the FinOps wedge no console offers.
v1_ref: Repo identity and attribution keys (repo slug, team, ticket)
field_verified: Columns verified present and unused: usage_events carries `user, machine, project, model, tool, agent_id, confidence` (schema.ts) and the code map confirms user/machine are 'stamped by db.ts ORIGIN on every row … never selected, filtered or grouped'. On this DB both have exactly **1 distinct value across 29,430 rows**. pricing.ts:135 `export function unpricedReason(model)` exists ✓. pricing.json lives at packages/core/src/data/pricing.json (feature says data/pricing.json — path drift) and `~/.vole/pricing.json` override is real at paths.ts:21. Repo identity sources verified but thin: ~/.claude.json `githubRepoPaths` has **4 entries** (launchsafe/docs, landing, engine, backend) against **58 distinct `project` values** in usage_events — 7% coverage — and the top project values are raw filesystem paths containing the username (`<redacted-local-path>` 6,932 rows; 1,962 rows have project = empty string).
constraint: Constraint 5 (aggregates that drop NULLs must expose an unpriced count) — this feature IS that constraint implemented, correctly. Constraint 13 (read-model parity) — a whole new screen plus a CLI means every query written twice. Constraint 18 (pricing = equivalent API value at list rates; cost is never date-aware because effective_from is unread) — I verified `effective_from` appears exactly once in the entire repo, as a type field at pricing.ts:25, read nowhere, so the honest_limit's 'cost is not date-aware' is exactly true. Depends hard on feature 8: a Costs screen built over the current mixed-basis column would render the wrong number more prominently than the app does today.

name: Erasure that survives the next poll, plus an Art. 19 propagation report
description: v1's 'vole forget' deletes rows and will not work: only the Claude Code collector is incremental (byte offsets in collector_state, all 513 rows claude_code), while Codex (codex.ts:72), Grok (grok.ts:75), OpenCode (opencode.ts:53), Devin (devin.ts:30), Cursor (cursor.ts:32) and Antigravity (antigravity.ts:21) re-read their entire source every poll and ignore the _db argument, so erased rows reappear within one five-second cycle. v1 spotted exactly this for prune and added a per-tool pruned_before_ts, but erasure is keyed by subject or session rather than by time and a timestamp watermark cannot express it. Add erasures(id, scope_kind, scope_value, from_ts, to_ts, requested_at, actor) consulted as a pre-filter inside insertEvents and insertAnomalies — the single write path — with the suppressed count written to the audit log on every pass. Art. 19 then obliges telling every recipient: export_sinks(kind, target, last_key, last_sent_at, payload_sha256, row_count), written by the evidence-pack writer, the SIEM forwarder and the sync outbox, lets 'vole forget' and 'vole rectify' emit a propagation report naming each sink, the rows that had already left and whether Vole can recall them.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Erasure requests': scope, requested date, rows deleted at the time, and rows suppressed at ingest since — the last column being the proof the erasure still holds. Beside it 'Where your data went': one row per sink with target, last send, row count and a recall verdict with its reason. The propagation report is also written next to the erasure record as a file a DPO pastes into an Art. 19 notification.
data_source: db.ts insertEvents / insertAnomalies (the single write path), the six full-re-read collectors named above, collector_state byte offsets for Claude Code; export_state / sync_log written by the SIEM forwarder and evidence-pack features; the evidence zip path plus its sha256; ~/.vole/outbox/.
honest_limit: Erasure in Vole is not erasure on the machine — the underlying transcript in ~/.claude/projects or ~/.codex/sessions still holds the content, and deleting those breaks 'claude --resume'. Rows in a signed zip on someone's laptop, or a batch a Splunk HEC endpoint already accepted, cannot be recalled, and the report says so rather than pretending otherwise. The sink list covers sinks Vole itself wrote to: a copy of ~/.vole/vole.db on a USB stick, or read over MDM file access, leaves no trace here. pnpm verify must treat erased ranges as erased, not as a reconciliation failure.
competitive_note: v1's forget would be a broken demo in the first DSAR test a design partner runs, and its erasure request to the relay has no local record of what already left. No vendor documents endpoint-side erasure semantics, and vendors that inspect content off-device have a much harder Art. 19 story that none of them publishes.
v1_ref: Data-subject access and erasure: vole dsar export and vole forget
field_verified: The premise is exactly right and I confirmed the mechanism end to end. `select tool,count(*) from collector_state group by 1` returns ONE row: `claude_code|634` -- only Claude Code persists offsets; the other six re-read their whole source every pass and ignore the _db argument. collect.ts sets `const intervalMs = intervalArg ? ... : 5000`, so a deleted OpenCode row reappears within five seconds. The single write path is real: db.ts exports insertEvents (the ON CONFLICT upsert) and insertAnomalies (INSERT OR IGNORE), so a pre-filter has exactly one place to live. export_sinks, sync_log and ~/.vole/outbox/ do not exist, and neither does the evidence-pack writer or SIEM forwarder the Art. 19 half would enumerate.
constraint: C9 (commit() only after insertEvents succeeds; offsets never advance past rows not stored) -- suppressing rows at ingest still advances Claude Code's byte offsets past them, which is what you want but makes erasure irreversible for the one incremental collector; state it. C20 (pnpm verify must keep passing): suppressed rows change the reconciliation arithmetic, so verify's PASS expression must learn a third class, which is the same surgery #27 performs -- sequence them together. C5 idempotency holds: a deterministic scope filter keeps re-runs no-ops.

name: Reconciliation screen with a state chip on every cell
description: A three-pane screen — vendor ledger, local ledger, delta — where no cell ever shows a bare number: each carries its unit, its basis and one of six state chips (matched, vendor-only, local-only, units-differ, not-comparable, stale). Cells drill to the contributing sessions on the local side and to the group_by and bucket boundary on the vendor side. It needs both read models written twice per constraint 13, and the UTC-bucket-drawn-with-local-calendar bug (DashboardView.swift:69) must be fixed first or daily reconciliation rows land in the wrong local day west of UTC — the exact failure mode that would make a correct reconciliation look broken.
desktop_surface: A 'Reconciliation' item in the Manage group, opening on the coverage report until a vendor pull has run, then on the delta table with the quota card and identity chip in the header.
data_source: vendor_ledger, vendor_identities and billing_units tables joined to usage_events; new queries.ts read models ported to DB.swift.
honest_limit: Every figure is as fresh as its slowest input — a Copilot column is roughly two days stale by construction and must render its own age, not the screen's — and rows the vendor prices but Vole cannot (Codex and Grok carry NULL cost_usd on every row here) show 'not comparable', never a zero delta. The app has no Node runtime and reads SQLite directly, so it can render a reconciliation but can never trigger a vendor pull without shelling out to the CLI.
competitive_note: Roadmap-v1 has a verify-time cost cross-check but no reconciliation surface at all. Every competing console shows one side of this table; the delta pane is the artefact a FinOps buyer screenshots for their CFO.
field_verified: `vendor_ledger`, `vendor_identities` and `billing_units` do not exist. The unpriced figures are exact: `codex|exact|83 calls|83 unpriced` — 83 of 83, precisely as claimed — and `grok|activity_only|969`. The bucket-bug dependency is real and live (DashboardView.swift:69, machine is MST -0700). 'The app has no Node runtime' is confirmed (README.md:436-437; Collector.swift spawns a SEA binary but the app cannot execute queries.ts).
constraint: TWO conflicts, neither named. (1) Constraint 17 / principle 5: a vendor ledger is by definition pulled from a vendor API — there is no vendor billing data anywhere on this disk — so this feature crosses the egress line and needs disclosure plus a no-egress switch every caller respects. It must be an explicit user-initiated CLI pull, never the daemon. (2) The deeper one, constraint 18: Vole's cost_usd is 'equivalent API value at Anthropic list rates' (pricing.json), except OpenCode rows which carry the provider's own figure. Subtracting a vendor's actually-billed dollars from that produces a delta with no meaning unless every cell states which of the three definitions it is using. The feature builds an elaborate six-chip state system for comparability and then omits the one axis that actually breaks comparability.

name: store_budget: measured bytes per table and index, and the indexes no read model plans through
description: One row per schema object refreshed on the scanner cadence, never in the 5-second loop: object, kind (table|index), bytes from dbstat (SELECT name, SUM(pgsize) FROM dbstat GROUP BY name — 4 ms on this store), rows, bytes_per_row, and a used_by_reads count from EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN run over each registered read model. Measured here without prompting: usage_events is 11.27 MB over 29,969 rows = 376 B/row, its five indexes are 5.48 MB = 183 B/row, so 32% of the 17.2 MB file is index, the -wal adds 6.0 MB and -shm 32 KB, and file total (page_count × page_size) is the only figure any surface could show today. That arithmetic is the buyer's actual question: at the measured 559 B/row and the ~17K tool_calls rows/day the roadmap itself predicts, the ≥6-month retention the audit-evidence buyer demands runs to roughly a gigabyte per laptop.
desktop_surface: Settings → Store: a bar per object sorted by bytes, the three real file sizes (db / wal / shm from stat), and 'days of headroom at the last 7 days' measured growth' which stays blank until seven daily snapshots exist.
data_source: dbstat virtual table, PRAGMA page_count/page_size/freelist_count, pragma_table_list, stat() on ~/.vole/vole.db, -wal and -shm; packages/core/src/queries.ts and the DB.swift ports as the registered read-model set
honest_limit: dbstat is a compile-time option — present in the Node 26.7.0 / SQLite 3.53.4 here (pragma_compile_options shows ENABLE_DBSTAT_VTAB), but the SEA freezes whatever Node the builder ran, so the probe runs at runtime and per-object bytes go NULL, never estimated or divided evenly, leaving only the file total. bytes_per_row for a table that has never received a row is NULL, not 0. used_by_reads = 0 means unused by the read models Vole registers, which is not proof of unused: the MCP server and ad-hoc SQL are outside that set.
competitive_note: Nightfall publishes ~50MB / ~1% CPU as an endpoint footprint claim; nobody publishes a store budget, because their store is somebody else's data centre. This is the number a Jamf admin asks before a 5,000-seat rollout and the one that decides whether on-device six-month retention is affordable at all.
v1_ref: Collector self-health: collector_runs, vole doctor, coverage matrix, freshness attestation
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Evidence freeze on notice: hash the sources before they age out
description: On this machine 1,758 of 1,758 Grok rows already reference a ~/.grok/logs file that no longer exists, while 570 Claude, 83 Codex, 204 Devin and 10,885 OpenCode source paths still resolve — and the oldest surviving Claude transcript (2026-08-15) is six weeks newer than ~/.claude.json firstStartTime (2026-07-02). So the moment a departing or departed declaration lands, one bounded pass walks the distinct raw_ref paths behind that principal's rows in the window and writes evidence_freeze(freeze_id, principal_id, declared_at, path, exists, size_bytes, mtime, sha256, consumed_to_offset, rows_referencing, source) — file metadata and a digest, never a byte of content, so the content boundary holds. Each figure in the departure pack then cites verified_at_freeze, source_gone_before_freeze or source_gone_after_freeze instead of an unqualified 'unverifiable', and a re-freeze appends a new freeze_id rather than overwriting the first.
desktop_surface: A Freeze card on the principal's Lifecycle panel: 'Frozen 2026-09-07 — 11,208 rows, 1,752 sources hashed, 10 already gone', broken down per tool, with a Re-freeze action that appends.
data_source: usage_events.raw_ref paths (~/.claude/projects/**.jsonl, ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl, opencode.db, Devin acp-messages/*.db); fs stat + sha256 over those files
honest_limit: A digest proves the file's bytes at freeze time, not at event time, and a source deleted before the freeze is gone for good — the pack must then say 'source deleted', never 'no activity'. Hashing is I/O, so it runs under the same byte budget as the DLP scanner and records sha256=NULL with reason='budget' rather than stalling a poll.
competitive_note: Vendors that store prompt text (Cyberhaven, Nightfall, Harmonic, MintMCP with 90d-7y retention) hold the evidence in their own cloud under their own retention clock; nobody hashes the endpoint's source files so that a local derived row stays checkable after the vendor tool prunes them.
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: activity_after_departure: the credential that outlived the person
description: A pure rule over rows the store already holds: for any principal whose latest declaration at time t is 'departed', any live usage_event, tool_call or surface_activity row with ts > effective_from on this device fires, with anomaly_key = 'live:activity_after_departure:<principal_id>:<UTC day bucket>:<tool>' — deterministic, no now() in the key (constraint 3), one incident per principal per day per tool. It fills the three explainability columns nothing selects today: observed = rows after the declaration, baseline = the principal's rows in the seven days before it, threshold = 0. Severity follows the evidence class: an interactive agent session is critical, a launchd-declared log tail is warn, an inventory-only sighting is info. This is the METR shape — a key that outlives its holder and burns spend for three weeks — and while the off-endpoint half is invisible, the on-device half is exact.
desktop_surface: Red banner on the principal's Lifecycle panel plus a standard incident card with its figures; the row counts into the menu bar's security count and into acting-now when the session is live.
data_source: usage_events.ts / tool_calls / surface_activity joined to principal_lifecycle.effective_from; no new disk read
honest_limit: A shared laptop, a CI runner or a sudo session under the leaver's OS account produces identical rows — the principal_conflict guard tags those and the incident says 'attributed weakly' instead of naming a person. The rule keys on the event's own ts, not on ingest time, so a re-read of an old source after the declaration is not counted as new activity.
competitive_note: Gateways and consoles see post-departure API traffic only for accounts they front; subscription-auth CLIs and BYOK keys bypass them entirely — which is exactly the case METR hit.
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: Scope-change diff for movers, with a residual-reach column
description: A 'scope_changed' declaration with an effective_from triggers a diff computed from ledgers already in the store, never from a policy statement: projects and repositories touched, MCP endpoint identities registered, grant/override entries with the file that granted each authority, remote-execution destinations from context_edges, secret-store retrievals, and each surface's sanctioned state. Adds the view v_scope_diff(principal_id, effective_from, dimension, value, before_window, after_window, state kept|added|removed|residual). The load-bearing column is 'residual': still reachable after the move — a wildcard grant still sitting in settings.local.json, an MCP endpoint still registered, a remote host still in a config — with no post-move use. That residue is what an access review actually needs and what a per-person usage report never shows.
desktop_surface: Two-column before/after panel on the Lifecycle screen with 'Residual reach' pinned at the top, each row linking to the exact file and entry that grants it, and a 'no before' state when the move predates the collector.
data_source: grant/override ledger (settings.json, settings.local.json, .mcp.json, managed policy), ai_surfaces, context_edges, action_targets, usage_events.project — all already in vole.db
honest_limit: Reachability here is what local configs and past actions show, not what the IdP or the repo host authorises; a permission granted server-side and never exercised locally is invisible, so 'residual' is a floor and never the full entitlement set. If the collector was not installed before effective_from the panel prints 'no before', not 'nothing'.
competitive_note: Access-review tooling (Entra, Okta, Reco, Obsidian) reviews IdP entitlements and cannot see a wildcard Bash grant in a local settings.local.json or a still-registered stdio MCP server; no coding-agent vendor produces a before/after reach diff.
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: vendor_identities: mapping a local session to a console row
description: Reconciliation against a vendor console is impossible until a local session maps to a console row, and every vendor keys on something different (email, accountUuid, api_key_id, chatgpt account_id, Cursor userId, GitHub login).
