Add `vendor_identities(vendor, local_key_kind, local_key, vendor_id_kind, vendor_id_hmac, plan, org_id_hmac, auth_path, first_seen, last_seen, evidence_artifact)`, filled from disk only: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{accountUuid, organizationUuid, organizationType, billingType, organizationRole}; transcript type:'bridge-session'.{ownerAccountUuid, ownerOrganizationUuid}; ~/.codex/auth.json auth_mode plus the presence of tokens.account_id; ~/.grok/auth.json principal_id and team_id; OpenCode account_state.active_org_id. Ids are stored as HMAC-SHA256 under a per-install Keychain key by default with a policy flag for cleartext, and — correcting the tempting shortcut — the Codex id_token is never decoded, because decoding a credential is reading a credential.
desktop_surface: Settings → Identity: one row per detected account showing vendor, plan, auth path, org role and the sentence 'this is how your sessions map to the console', with a copy-hash action for support; the same chip appears in the Reconciliation screen header.
data_source: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount (all fields confirmed present); ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl type:'bridge-session' (18 files here); ~/.codex/auth.json auth_mode and tokens.account_id presence; ~/.grok/auth.json principal_id/team_id; ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db account_state.active_org_id.
honest_limit: An HMAC over a few hundred known employee emails or account ids is reversible by whoever holds the key, so the hash is a join key and not a privacy control — pseudonymity comes from not storing the value at all. The mapping is per-machine: it proves this laptop's sessions belong to an account, never that an account has no other laptops, and a user who reauthenticates under a different account leaves two rows with only last_seen to disambiguate. OpenCode's arm is declared and unverified here (account, account_state and control_account are all 0 rows), and access_token, refresh_token, credential.value and session_share.secret sit in those same tables, so the collector reads named columns and never SELECT *.
competitive_note: v1's identity binding populates user/machine/org for shadow-account detection; this adds the vendor-side half of the join and the plan/auth_path fields that decide whether a vendor API can be queried at all. Cursor blocks personal logins only via MDM Allowed Team IDs, and nothing in the 62-vendor matrix maps a local session to a console identity from disk.
v1_ref: Identity binding: user, org, seat and device (shadow_account)
field_verified: Every named field exists. ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{accountUuid len 36, organizationUuid len 36, organizationType='claude_max', billingType='stripe_subscription', organizationRole='admin'} — confirmed. bridge-session ownerAccountUuid/ownerOrganizationUuid in 18 files / 575 lines — confirmed, resolving to 1 account and 1 org. ~/.codex/auth.json auth_mode='chatgpt' with tokens.account_id len 36 present — confirmed, and the never-decode-the-id_token rule is well aimed: that JWT is 1,820 characters sitting in the same object. ~/.grok/auth.json principal_id and team_id — confirmed. OpenCode arm declared and dead: account_state has the active_org_id COLUMN but 0 rows; account and control_account also 0, and their columns really do include email/access_token/refresh_token, so the never-SELECT-* rule is warranted.
constraint: C7 — reading named columns rather than SELECT * on OpenCode's credential-bearing tables is the correct reconciliation and the feature states it. C6 — needs a source column and purge participation like every other table. DUPLICATION: roadmap-v1's 'Session exposure and remote-control surface' already says verbatim 'Claude bridge-session entries (575 here) with owner uuids compared to the local oauthAccount' — same artifact, same count, same comparison; and feature 1's session_identity already carries account_id, org_id, plan and source. Three tables over five reads. Reconciliation: fold this into session_identity plus one small accounts dimension rather than a parallel ledger.

name: Cache economics with the 5m-versus-1h split, and the burn-rate rule that ignores multipliers
description: Cache is the largest single cost lever and Vole mishandles it in three places today: getLiveSessions computes rewarm_cost as always ×write5m (queries.ts:340) even for 1h writes billed at 2.0×; the burn-rate rule scores raw `total_tokens` including 0.1×-priced cache reads, which is why 188 of 244 live incidents fire on windows that are ~99% cache reads; and no view separates the three multipliers at all. Add a cache economics read model reporting, per model and window, fresh input versus 5m write versus 1h write versus cache read tokens with their 0.1 / 1.25 / 2.0 multipliers applied separately, the read-to-fresh ratio, and a re-warm total computed with the write class that actually occurred — then weight the burn-rate rule's score by the same multipliers so a cache-read-heavy window stops being an incident. Because Anthropic's usage_report/messages returns `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` as separate fields, this is the one cost lever the console can independently confirm.
desktop_surface: A Cache economics card on the Breakdown and Reconciliation screens: four token-class bars with their multipliers, the read/fresh ratio, re-warm cost split by TTL class, and a vendor-confirmed tick on the 5m/1h split once a pull has run.
data_source: usage_events.{input_tokens, cache_write_5m_tokens, cache_write_1h_tokens, cache_read_tokens}; data/pricing.json cache_multipliers {read 0.1, write5m 1.25, write1h 2.0} and the per-model flat cache_read override; detect/burn-rate.ts:29; queries.ts:340; Anthropic usage_report cache_creation fields.
honest_limit: Only Claude Code splits the two TTL classes on disk: Codex reports cache_write_input_tokens as a single field (and codex.ts:204 hard-codes it to 0 today), OpenCode reports one cache.write number, and Grok reports only cached_prompt_tokens — so the 5m/1h split is NULL for three of the four token-bearing tools and no vendor confirmation is possible there. At least one model prices cache reads at a flat per-MTok rate rather than a multiple of input, so any multiplier-based presentation must special-case it or be wrong. TTL refreshes on every hit, so re-warm must be classified per session gap rather than per write, and the re-written prefix always includes new content that is not re-warm.
competitive_note: v1 covers the re-warm incident and a TTL premium audit but keeps the always-×write5m computation, leaves the burn-rate rule scoring unweighted tokens, and does not connect the split to the vendor's separately reported cache_creation fields. No console and no gateway exposes cache economics per session at all.
v1_ref: Cache re-warm incident and 1h-vs-5m TTL premium audit
field_verified: All three defects confirmed in code; one supporting statistic is overstated. queries.ts:340 verified verbatim: `rewarm_cost: rate && ctx > 0 ? (ctx * rate.input * CACHE_MULTIPLIERS.write5m) / 1e6 : null` — always write5m, never write1h ✓. burn-rate.ts:29 verified: `const tokens = evs.reduce((s, e) => s + (e.total_tokens ?? 0), 0)` — raw totals including 0.1×-priced cache reads ✓. The flat-rate special case the honest_limit warns about ALREADY exists in code: pricing.ts:127 `read * (rate.cache_read ?? rate.input * CACHE_MULTIPLIERS.read)` ✓. Claude Code's TTL split is real: claude-code.ts:143-146 reads `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` with a documented fallback. Codex's zero is hard-coded as claimed (`cache_write_5m_tokens: 0, cache_write_1h_tokens: 0` with the comment 'Codex has no cache-write concept: 0 here is structural') — though the rollouts DO carry `usage.cache_write_input_tokens` (0 in every sample), so 'no concept' is now wrong. **Statistic corrected**: not '188 of 244'. Live DB has **249 anomalies, of which 190 are burn_rate_spike**; joining each fired window to its events, **152 of 190 are >90% cache_read and 102 of 190 are >99%** — not '188 fire on windows that are ~99% cache reads'. The code map's own phrasing (median fired window is 99% cache_read) is the accurate one.
constraint: Constraint 3, and this is the conflict the feature misses entirely. Re-weighting burn-rate's score changes the verdict for windows already stored, but anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key (db.ts:137) — the 190 existing burn_rate_spike incidents were computed on the unweighted score and are frozen. A re-scored rule produces neither an update nor a retraction: the feed keeps showing 102 cache-read incidents forever while the new logic silently agrees they should never have fired. Reconciliation: version the rule in the key (`burn_rate_spike/v2:…`, still deterministic and free of now()) and either retract or leave v1 keys visibly labelled — do not quietly change scoring behind a stable key. Constraint 19 (UTC bucketing) unaffected.

name: Retention split by data class, with the AI Act floor shown against the minimisation ceiling
description: v1 has one 'vole prune --keep=90d'. Privacy needs classes whose pressures point in opposite directions: behavioural rows (usage_events) minimise downward; incident evidence (anomalies, findings) has an upward floor wherever the org has declared itself a deployer under EU AI Act Art. 26(6), which requires logs kept at least six months; access and audit logs outlive both; collector_runs at roughly 17,000 rows a day is operational and measured in days. Render the effective table with the reason attached to each number, and raise a conflict when a declared obligation exceeds the configured retention — 'policy keeps incidents 30 days; the profile declares an Art. 26(6) obligation of 180'. The value is showing the tension rather than resolving it silently in either direction.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Retention' table: class, days, reason, oldest row held, next prune; a red row when a declared floor exceeds the configured value.
data_source: usage_events, anomalies, collector_state, plus the audit/access/collector_runs tables; ~/.vole/policy.json retention block; the declared obligations from the lawful-basis record.
honest_limit: Vole does not know whether the org is a deployer of a high-risk AI system, and whether a deterministic rule engine even falls under Annex III 4(b) is unsettled — Annex III obligations were deferred to 2027-12-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The floor is a value the profile declares; Vole only checks internal consistency and must never assert the classification itself.
competitive_note: v1's prune is one flag with one number, one retention for every table and no reason column. Vendors ship a single retention slider tied to their cloud tier; none surfaces the AI Act logging floor against the minimisation duty, and handing a DPO and a CISO their argument pre-drawn shortens the review.
v1_ref: Historical rollups, retention prune, bounded detection window and legal hold
field_verified: usage_events, anomalies and collector_state exist and 'oldest row held' is measurable now (`select datetime(min(ts)/1000,'unixepoch'), datetime(max(ts)/1000,'unixepoch') from usage_events` -> 2026-05-24 to 2026-09-07). findings, collector_runs and any audit/access table do NOT exist, so three of the four named classes have no table. The '~17,000 rows a day' collector_runs figure is a projection from the 5s default interval (17,280/day), not a measurement -- it is presented as fact. The legal frame is fully sourced at market.md L49: Art. 26(6) logs >=6 months, Annex III 4(b) covers systems that 'monitor and evaluate the performance and behaviour' of workers, deferred to 2027-12-02 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. ~/.vole/policy.json does not exist.
constraint: C1 satisfied -- 'oldest row held' is measured, the floor is a value the profile declares, and the feature explicitly refuses to classify the org as a deployer. That refusal is the correct reading of the constraint and of the unsettled Annex III question. No prune implementation exists at all (roadmap-v1 L166 proposes it), so 'next prune' has nothing to report on day one.

name: Measured reclaim: VACUUM INTO a scratch copy is the measurement, the in-place VACUUM is the decision
description: The obvious gate is freelist_count, and on this store it is wrong: freelist_count reads 0 yet a full VACUUM still took the file from 4,198 to 4,036 pages — 663 KB reclaimed by defragmentation alone, in 60 ms. So the honest sequence is: check free disk ≥ file size, VACUUM INTO a scratch path (28 ms / 16.5 MB measured here), compare stat sizes, delete the scratch, and run the in-place VACUUM only if the measured delta clears a threshold — the reclaimed figure reported is the one observed on this machine's own data, never a rule of thumb. Idle is defined by evidence rather than a timer: k consecutive polls that inserted zero rows, read from collector_state.last_scanned_at (648 rows here) or collector_runs once it exists. PRAGMA optimize runs on clean close regardless — one line, SQLite decides — and wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) handles the 6.0 MB -wal that no screen counts today.
desktop_surface: Settings → Store → Maintenance: last run, bytes actually reclaimed, next eligibility, and an explicit 'not measured — 17.2 MB required, 4 MB free' state rather than a skipped run reported as success.
data_source: PRAGMA freelist_count / page_count / page_size, VACUUM INTO, PRAGMA optimize, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint, statfs for free disk, collector_state.last_scanned_at
honest_limit: VACUUM takes an exclusive lock. At 30K rows that is 60 ms and invisible; at the tool_calls volumes the roadmap predicts it will exceed the app's 2-second busy_timeout, and the app's current response to a busy store is a screen of zeros — so the pass must publish a state row the app reads before it takes the lock, and must never run while a --once collect or an export is in flight. VACUUM INTO needs as much free disk as the store, so on a full laptop the correct output is 'not measured', not 'nothing to reclaim'.
competitive_note: No comparator: osquery's RocksDB is compacted by its engine and Fleet publishes no reclaim figure. This is principle 1 (never invent a number) applied to Vole's own housekeeping, where every other product guesses.
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Art. 30 record and the Art. 15(1)(c) recipients answer, both with an unknown denominator
description: Two exports off `v_processing_register`, both refusing to drop the unknowns. `vole register --art30` emits an org-level record of processing activities: recipient, legal entity, contract_scope, third-country transfer yes/no/unknown, safeguard cited by the pack, categories of data evidenced (from the dlp_egress data-class column, not from prose), retention default, evidence count and first/last seen — with a mandatory header line counting the surfaces whose recipient could not be resolved and the egress rows with no in-force terms entry. `vole dsar --recipients <principal>` answers Art. 15(1)(c) for one subject: the companies that received that person's data, which surfaces carried it, and the same unknown counts, purpose-gated through the existing closed purpose union and written to the access log. Both go through the deny-by-default export field registry and the NULL-omitting encoder, so an unresolved recipient is an absent field, never an empty string that reads as 'none'.
desktop_surface: An 'Export register' button on the Processing Register with the pre-export field preview and re-identification scan already used by evidence bundles; on the People view, a per-person 'Recipients' tab rendering the same rows the DSAR export would contain, gated by the existing per-person view gate and subject notice.
data_source: v_processing_register (processing_terms pack × terms_basis × recipient_state × dlp_egress data classes), export field registry, ~/.vole/policy/identity.json for the principal
honest_limit: An Art. 30 record is the controller's document; this is a machine-generated draft of the recipients section from endpoint evidence and cannot state purposes, lawful bases or the controller's own retention decisions. It covers only what this device saw — a colleague's laptop, a hosted agent and a browser chat are outside it, and the header must say so. A recipient absent from the record may simply be a surface Vole cannot read.
competitive_note: Vendor consoles are single-tool and identity-fragmented — Anthropic's Compliance API excludes Bedrock/Vertex, API-key and personal accounts, Copilot's audit log excludes local prompts — so no console can produce a cross-vendor recipients list for one employee; the SASE vendors could, but only for traffic they proxy and only inside their own cloud.
v1_ref: DSAR export that answers Art. 15(1)(h): the logic, not just the rows
gap_area: AI-vendor processing register: where the data landed, under whose law, and on what default terms

name: Quota ledger: the real cachedUsageUtilization shape, a scoped rule key, and the percent-to-money bridge
description: v1 describes `~/.claude.json cachedUsageUtilization` as `{fetchedAtMs, five_hour, seven_day, limits[].{percent, resets_at}}`; the real shape on disk is `cachedUsageUtilization.{fetchedAtMs, accountUuid, utilization:{five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_cowork, nimbus_quill, …}}` where each window is `{utilization, resets_at, limit_dollars, used_dollars, remaining_dollars, locked_reason}`, plus `utilization.limits[]` entries of `{kind, group, percent, severity, resets_at, scope.model.display_name, is_active}` and `utilization.extra_usage.{is_enabled, monthly_limit, used_credits, spend_limit_reached}` and `utilization.spend.used.amount_minor` — a collector written to v1's path reads undefined and emits NULL forever. Two further corrections: the reading is account-global rather than per session, so RateLimitObservation.session_id must be NULL, which makes rate-limit.ts:25 key on `rate_limit_pressure:claude_code:none:<hour>` and puts Claude's account-wide window and Codex's per-session window under one rule with two different meanings — the key and the detail need a scope field. On top of the corrected ledger, render one explicitly derived line for subscription plans that have no billing API: 'weekly Fable limit 61% used · Vole observed N tokens / $X list value in this window · implied full-window value ≈ $X/0.61', with all three inputs, the window boundaries and the snapshot's age printed beside it, suppressed below 20% for division noise and never fed into cost_usd or any aggregate.
desktop_surface: MenuPanel gains a headroom line ('7-day 42%, resets 9 Sep 10:00 UTC, read 3 h ago'); a 'Quota & headroom' card on the Reconciliation screen lists one row per limit window (session, weekly_all, weekly_scoped per model, Codex primary/secondary) with percent, resets_at, reading age, in-window tokens and the implied value with its formula inline; Incidents can finally fire rate_limit_pressure for Claude Code, not only Codex.
data_source: ~/.claude.json cachedUsageUtilization — verified live here: fetchedAtMs 1788763107042, utilization.seven_day.utilization 42 resets_at 2026-09-09T10:00:00Z, limits[] session 0% / weekly_all 42% / weekly_scoped 61% scope.model.display_name 'Fable' is_active true, all *_dollars null, extra_usage.is_enabled false, spend.used.amount_minor 0; ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl payload.rate_limits.{primary,secondary,credits,plan_type}; packages/core/src/detect/rate-limit.ts:25.
honest_limit: The percent covers the whole account across every surface — claude.ai web, Cowork, Claude Desktop, other machines — so the implied full-window value is an upper bound on what Vole's share explains and degrades to nonsense the moment the account is used elsewhere. The snapshot refreshes only while Claude Code is running, so the reading can be hours stale; its age must be rendered and the derived line suppressed past a staleness bound. limit_dollars, used_dollars and remaining_dollars are null on this subscription, so the dollar path is unavailable for exactly the population that has no invoice to reconcile against. Read only cachedUsageUtilization, never the adjacent oauthAccount emailAddress/fullName/organizationName.
competitive_note: v1's Tier 1 field path does not exist on disk and its Tier 4 quota panel never crosses percent with observed tokens, so the only reconciliation available to subscription accounts — which market research puts at a majority of Claude usage — is missing. market.md notes Codex is wrongly documented as the only tool that self-reports quota; no vendor console exposes subscription headroom to the endpoint, which is why FinOps buyers cannot see a seat about to throttle.
v1_ref: Claude subscription quota tracker (5-hour / 7-day windows)
field_verified: The strongest field verification in the shard — I reproduced the entire object and roadmap-v1's documented path is definitively wrong. Live ~/.claude.json: `cachedUsageUtilization: {fetchedAtMs: 1788763107042, accountUuid: '909a1169-…', utilization: {five_hour: {utilization: 0, resets_at: null, limit_dollars: null, used_dollars: null, remaining_dollars: null, locked_reason: null}, seven_day: {utilization: 42, resets_at: '2026-09-09T10:00:00.066479+00:00', limit_dollars: null, …}, seven_day_opus: null, seven_day_sonnet: null, seven_day_cowork: null, nimbus_quill: {utilization: 0, …}, extra_usage: {is_enabled: false, monthly_limit: null, used_credits: null, spend_limit_reached: false, credits_ever_enabled: true}, limits: [{kind:'session', group:'session', percent:0, is_active:false}, {kind:'weekly_all', group:'weekly', percent:42, resets_at:'2026-09-09T10:00:00Z', is_active:false}, {kind:'weekly_scoped', group:'weekly', percent:61, scope:{model:{id:null, display_name:'Fable'}}, is_active:true}], spend: {used: {amount_minor: 0, currency:'USD', exponent:2}, limit: null, enabled: false}}}`. Every window nests under `utilization`; **v1's `{fetchedAtMs, five_hour, seven_day, limits[]}` reads undefined and would emit NULL forever** ✓. All *_dollars null ✓. rate-limit.ts:25 verified verbatim: `const key = \`rate_limit_pressure:${o.tool}:${o.session_id ?? 'none'}:${bucket}\`` and the file's own header comment says 'Codex is the only tool here that reports its own remaining quota' — the live DB has exactly **1 rate_limit_pressure anomaly**, from Codex.
constraint: Constraint 3 (deterministic keys, no now()) — satisfied, and the proposed scope field is the right fix: without it, Claude's account-global reading and Codex's per-session reading collapse into one key shape carrying two different meanings. Constraint 4 (confidence is exactly two values) — a percent read from a cached snapshot with a fetchedAtMs is 'exact' as an observation of the cache, not of the account now; render the reading age rather than inventing a third tier. Principle 1 on the derived line: 'implied full-window value ≈ $X/0.61' is a computed number, and the guards offered (all three inputs printed, window boundaries, snapshot age, suppressed below 20%, never fed into cost_usd or any aggregate) are the minimum acceptable — I would additionally keep it out of the MenuPanel headline, because a number that good-looking will be quoted without its formula.

name: vole import --context and the devcontainer feature: rows from a container arrive as rows, never as estimates
description: The deployment answer to a gap that cannot be closed by reading harder. Ship three things: `docs/COVERAGE-TOPOLOGY.md`, one page stating plainly which contexts Vole reads and which it counts-but-cannot-read; a published devcontainer feature and container image layer that installs the collector inside the image and points it at a spool directory the container already mounts, so a devcontainer run writes `~/.vole/contexts/<context_id>/events-*.ndjson` in the normalised UsageEvent shape with its own declared context and origin; and `vole import --context <id> [--dry-run]`, an opt-in local file read (no network, no container exec) that inserts those rows through the same `insertEvents` path with the origin override from the previous feature. Idempotency comes free from the existing UNIQUE event_key: if a container's home was also bind-mounted, its rows are already present from the local file scan and the import is a no-op rather than a double count — but only for sources whose keys are content-derived, so the Codex `codex:<session>:<line index>` collision must be fixed before Codex import is enabled, and the CLI refuses that source until it is. Import writes a `context_imports(context_id, spool_path, rows_offered, rows_inserted, rows_deduped, collector_version, imported_at)` audit row, and a context flips `monitored=1` only when an import has actually landed rows.
desktop_surface: Topology card rows gain a state chip: unmonitored / spool present, not imported / imported <n> rows at <time>. Settings gains an Import Contexts pane listing discovered spool directories with row counts and a dry-run preview before anything is written. The Coverage strip's `contexts_unmonitored` figure drops only when an import lands, so the number can never be improved by configuration alone.
data_source: ~/.vole/contexts/<context_id>/*.ndjson written by the collector running inside the container; the feature manifest published for devcontainer `features`; execution_contexts.context_id as the join key; existing db.ts insertEvents and event_key UNIQUE for dedupe
honest_limit: This only helps images the organisation actually rebuilds and mounts a spool into — a container already running, a Codespace, a CI runner nobody controls, and every SSH remote get nothing, and for SSH remotes the honest answer stated in the doc is 'install Vole there too'. Vole still never exec's into a running container; that would be a new capability and a new trust boundary, and the NON-GOALS charter should say so. An imported row is trusted as far as the spool is trusted: the container is inside the organisation's own image, and the import records collector_version so a drifted parser is visible rather than silent. Contexts with no import stay at monitored=0 and their usage stays unknown, never zero, never estimated.
competitive_note: Anthropic's client OTel and Codex's [otel] block do work inside a container if enabled there — both opt-in, Codex's exporter defaulting to none and its metrics defaulting to OpenAI statsig — so the honest framing is that Vole's answer is the same as the vendors' answer, 'install it where the agent runs', except stated in a shipped topology doc and backed by a measured unmonitored count instead of left implicit. Fleet/osquery integration (fleetdm.com/endpoint-governance) is the fleet-scale variant: the execution_contexts table exports into the existing ATC pack so a container census can be queried without a second agent.
v1_ref: Headless CI mode (GitHub Action / container step)
gap_area: Where agents actually run: devcontainers, Docker, SSH remotes, VMs and CI runners as declared blind spots

name: Retention with a receipt, gated on what can still be rebuilt
description: The v1 prune item treats deletion as free — roll up, delete the live rows, move on — and the reason it is not free is in this repo: docs/EXTENDING.md still calls the store 'disposable — it rebuilds from source logs', which stopped being true the moment a row outlived its source. Add store_prunes(id, ran_at, trigger, data_class, table_name, rows_deleted, oldest_deleted_ts, newest_deleted_ts, bytes_before, bytes_after, policy_clause): one row per data class per pass, counts taken from the statement's own .changes and bytes from store_budget, with trigger being 'policy' (retention_days) or 'budget' (a store_budget threshold). Before deleting, resolve raw_ref for the oldest rows in the class: where the source file is already gone the Vole row is the only remaining record, so the pass refuses that class, downgrades to a warning naming the count, and prunes only what is still reconstructable. Pairs with v1's own P4 note — the six full-re-read collectors would re-insert pruned rows within 5 seconds unless a per-tool pruned_before_ts filters them.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → Retention: one row per pass showing class, rows deleted, the exact date range destroyed and bytes reclaimed, plus a 'refused' section listing classes held back because their source is gone.
data_source: usage_events.raw_ref existence on disk, ~/.claude/.last-cleanup, cleanupPeriodDays, store_budget bytes, ~/.vole/policy retention clause
honest_limit: A receipt proves what was destroyed, not what it said: after a class is pruned the only honest DSAR answer for that window is 'deleted on <date>, N rows, class X', and it must be worded as one. A legal hold protects Vole's own rows only — it cannot stop Claude Code's cleanup deleting the transcript underneath, so a held range can still lose its evidence.
competitive_note: MintMCP advertises 90-day-to-7-year retention of prompts and tool arguments in its cloud; a counted, local, per-class deletion receipt is something a prompt-storing SaaS cannot put in front of a works council.
v1_ref: Historical rollups, retention prune, bounded detection window and legal hold
gap_area: The store's own lifecycle: schema migration, column widening, growth budget, downgrade, support bundle

name: Uncosted rows: local and free-tier providers render an em dash, never $0.00
description: Eleven of the thirteen providers behind OpenCode on this machine report cost exactly 0.0 — opencode Zen (2,803 messages), qwen38-fp8 (2,802), openrouter free-tier (724), qwen38-heretic (590), qwen38-base (268), ollama (184), fable-fusion (84), qwen-h200 (57), qwen, unsloth-studio, qwen12 — 7,521 assistant messages in total. Storing 0.0 and rendering '$0.00' invents a number in the direction nobody checks: an H200 running a 27B model has a real hourly cost the provider never bills, and a free-tier row is a rate-limited entitlement rather than free compute. Classify these as `cost_basis='self_hosted_uncosted'` at insert when the provider resolves to local/loopback or when a provider-reported cost is exactly 0 while tokens are non-zero, render them as an em dash with a separate 'uncosted calls' count, and let `~/.vole/units.json` carry an optional usd_per_1m_tokens or usd_per_gpu_hour declaration so an admin can price them under a labelled basis.
desktop_surface: Breakdown and Costs screens gain a distinct 'uncosted' section listing local and free-tier providers with token totals and an em dash for cost, plus a one-line 'declare a rate in units.json to price these' affordance that deep-links to Settings → Units.
data_source: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db `message.data.providerID` and `data.cost` (13 providers, 7,521 zero-cost assistant rows here versus 3,364 priced); local runtime evidence from loopback provider ids ollama / unsloth-studio / qwen-h200 and their listening ports.
honest_limit: A provider-reported 0.0 is ambiguous between 'genuinely free', 'not yet computed by the provider' and 'self-hosted', so the classifier only distinguishes local/loopback providers with confidence and marks the rest as uncosted-unknown rather than guessing. Vole cannot see GPU hours, electricity or cloud instance cost, so any declared self-hosted rate is an allocation the admin owns and it is labelled as such wherever it appears.
competitive_note: Every FinOps and observability tool in the matrix reports local-model usage as $0 or omits it entirely. market.md flags local-LLM port detection as a cheap shadow-AI adjunct; nobody connects it to the cost story, and a team that shifted work to an H200 currently looks like a team that stopped spending.
field_verified: Reproduced exactly against ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (507 MB). Assistant messages by providerID with summed cost: github-copilot 3,336/$575.19, **opencode 2,803/$0.00, qwen38-fp8 2,802/$0.00, openrouter 724/$0.00, qwen38-heretic 590/$0.00, qwen38-base 268/$0.00, ollama 184/$0.00, fable-fusion 84/$0.00, qwen-h200 57/$0.00, qwen 7/$0.00, unsloth-studio 1/$0.00, qwen12 1/$0.00**, anthropic 28/$5.07. That is 13 providers, 11 reporting exactly zero, **7,521 zero-cost assistant messages against 3,364 priced** — the feature's counts to the row. The storage behaviour it objects to is confirmed in code: opencode.ts:143 `cost_usd: typeof d.cost === 'number' ? d.cost : null` under the comment 'OpenCode's own figure. A real 0 (free local model) is kept; only a missing field becomes null.'
constraint: Principle 1 read in the direction nobody checks — storing a true 0 is defensible (it is the provider's own figure) but rendering '$0.00' asserts a measurement about an H200 that Vole never made. Constraint 18 (a cost roll-up must not mix definitions silently) is the same constraint feature 8 addresses; this is one enum value of that feature (`self_hosted_uncosted`), not an independent change. Reconciliation: ship it as part of feature 8's classifier and counters rather than as a separate table, and keep the classifier honest — loopback/local provider ids (ollama, unsloth-studio, qwen-h200) classify with confidence, everything else is uncosted-unknown, never guessed.

name: Purpose-bound query layer with a closed purpose union
description: The code map already asks for a where({from, includeSeed, user, machine, tool, project}) builder to replace the seedClause hand-spliced at 8 sites in queries.ts and TOKEN_FILTER at 6. Give that builder a required purpose argument from a closed union — security_incident | cost_allocation | capacity | self_view | dsar — and attach to each purpose the columns it may select and whether it may group by subject. A purposes.test.ts walks every exported read model and fails the build if one omits a purpose, or if a query whose purpose is not security_incident, self_view or dsar selects subject_id. That turns v1's purpose-limitation policy — a role table in a JSON file with nothing enforcing it — into a compile-and-test-time property of the codebase, which is what an auditor can check, and the builder is also the single place access_log rows get written.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Purposes' table listing each purpose, the columns it may read and the count of queries bound to it, generated from the test's own fixture so the screen cannot drift from the code.
data_source: queries.ts (all read models, seedClause at 8 sites, TOKEN_FILTER at 6), cli/mcp.ts TOOLS array, DB.swift read-model ports.
honest_limit: On a single-user machine the reader is the subject, so purpose binding is bookkeeping rather than access control; it becomes a real control only where the reader is not the subject — a fleet relay or a shared machine. It binds Vole's own code paths only: anyone with the SQLite file bypasses it entirely and FileVault is the only thing in the way. It also doubles read-model work, since read-model parity means every query must be ported to DB.swift carrying the same purpose.
competitive_note: v1 has the policy block but no enforcement seam, and defers it to a relay that does not exist. No competitor documents per-purpose column restrictions; Cyberhaven notably lacks even SCIM, so role plumbing is thin across the whole category.
v1_ref: Purpose limitation policy: role query rights, per-table retention, sealed-until-incident
field_verified: The duplication is real and WORSE than the code map states: `grep -c seedClause packages/core/src/queries.ts` -> 18 occurrences (not 8) and `grep -c TOKEN_FILTER` -> 10 (not 6). queries.ts:165 confirms `export type BreakdownBy = 'model' | 'project' | 'branch'`. cli/mcp.ts TOOLS is the seven-entry array at :20-83 as cited.
constraint: C12 (read-model parity) is the decisive conflict and the feature concedes it: 'it doubles read-model work, since read-model parity means every query must be ported to DB.swift carrying the same purpose.' Reconcile: bind purposes in TypeScript only and expose purpose-scoped SQL VIEWS that DB.swift consumes read-only, so the Swift side inherits the binding without re-implementing the builder. Without that reconciliation this is the most expensive item in the shard for the least day-one control.

name: billing_units: a declared bridge for credits, seats and premium requests, or an em dash
description: The four vendors bill in four incompatible units — Anthropic in tokens and USD, OpenAI in tokens and USD for API but ChatGPT seats for Codex, Cursor in requestsCosts and totalCents, Copilot in premium requests and seats — and every dashboard that shows a single number has invented the conversion. Rather than invent one, add `~/.vole/units.json` following the pattern pricing.json already establishes for overrides, where an admin declares `{vendor, unit, usd_per_unit, effective_from, note, author}`, plus a `billing_units` table recording which declaration priced which row. Absent a declaration every cross-unit cell renders an em dash and the reconciliation reports `state='units_differ'` with the two raw figures side by side and neither converted; when a declaration exists the converted value is always shown beside the raw unit and labelled with the declaration name and its effective_from, so a policy number can never be mistaken for an observed one.
desktop_surface: Settings → Units: an editable list of each declared rate with who declared it and when, and a staleness flag; every converted dollar figure anywhere in the app carries a small superscript linking back to the declaration that produced it.
data_source: ~/.vole/units.json (new); vendor_ledger.unit; observed plan fields ~/.claude.json oauthAccount.{organizationType, organizationRateLimitTier, seatTier}, Codex rate_limits.plan_type, Copilot seat plan from the billing endpoint.
honest_limit: A seat price divided across a month is an allocation choice, not a measurement — the tool can carry it but must never present it as spend or sum it into a spend total. Premium-request-to-dollar rates change with GitHub's published multipliers and are not fetched, so a stale declaration silently mis-prices; effective_from is therefore mandatory and stale declarations are flagged rather than applied. A declared rate is only ever as good as the admin who typed it, and the provenance link exists so a reader can dispute it.
competitive_note: Windsurf, JetBrains Console and Copilot all report credits with no token or dollar equivalent (market.md §4, competitor matrix rows 110/144); every FinOps dashboard that shows one anyway has invented it. Refusing to convert without a declaration is a position no competitor takes.
field_verified: The override-file pattern it copies is real and verified: paths.ts:21 `pricingOverride: () => process.env.VOLE_PRICING ?? join(home(), '.vole', 'pricing.json')`, merged over the built-in table at pricing.ts:45 (`cache_multipliers: {...BUILTIN.cache_multipliers, ...(o.cache_multipliers ?? {})}`) — so `~/.vole/units.json` follows an established, working precedent rather than inventing a config mechanism. The observed plan fields it keys on verify: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount `organizationType 'claude_max'`, `organizationRateLimitTier 'default_claude_max_20x'`, `billingType 'stripe_subscription'` present; **`seatTier` is null and `userRateLimitTier` is null** on this account, so two of the named inputs are em dashes here. Codex `plan_type` verified in rollouts: 'team' 43, 'free' 4, null 21. Copilot seat plan is unverifiable locally (no endpoint, no local artifact).
constraint: Principle 1 and constraint 5, handled correctly and unusually well: an admin's declared usd_per_unit is a policy number, not an observation, and the design never lets one masquerade as the other — em dash absent a declaration, `state='units_differ'` with both raw figures unconverted, converted value always shown beside the raw unit with the declaration name and effective_from. This is the only place in the shard that solves the 'derived number' problem structurally rather than with a label. Note the irony worth fixing: units.json makes effective_from mandatory and flags staleness, while pricing.json's own effective_from is read nowhere in the repo (pricing.ts:25 only) — ship the staleness check for both or neither.

name: AI literacy and tool-usage record per subject
description: EU AI Act Art. 4 has been enforceable since 2026-08-02 and obliges deployers to ensure staff have sufficient AI literacy; the evidence an auditor asks for is a per-person record of which AI systems each employee actually uses, which Vole already holds and throws away. Add a literacy_record view — SELECT DISTINCT tool, model, MIN(ts), MAX(ts), COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) per subject over usage_events — plus a training(subject_id, course, completed_at, source_file) table populated only from a CSV the org imports, never inferred. The same view is the developer's own 'these are the AI tools you use' card, which is the friendlier half of the same artifact.
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Your AI tools' card: one row per tool and model with first seen, last seen and session count, plus imported training rows where present; the fleet view shows only the aggregate.
data_source: usage_events DISTINCT (tool, model) with MIN/MAX(ts) and COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) per subject; an org-supplied CSV for the training column.
honest_limit: It proves use, never competence — the record shows a person ran a model, not that they understood it, and the training column is imported rather than derived. Tools Vole has no collector for are absent from the record rather than zero, so the coverage screen must ship alongside it or the record reads as a false negative.
competitive_note: Named in the research's feature implications, present in no v1 tier and in no vendor in the 62-row matrix. A compliance artifact with a hard enforcement date, produced from rows already stored — unusually cheap leverage in a procurement conversation.
field_verified: Every column in the view exists and is populated: usage_events.tool, .model, .ts, .session_id all in schema.ts:9-14, and .user carries a value on every row (`select distinct user, machine` -> `shiva|Marys-MacBook-Pro.local`). The SELECT DISTINCT tool, model, MIN(ts), MAX(ts), COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) is writable today with no schema change. Art. 4 enforceability from 2026-08-02 is sourced at market.md L49 (EC AI-literacy FAQ, 2026-07-27).
constraint: None. C1 is respected in the right place -- the training column is imported from an org CSV and never inferred, which is the difference between a record and a fabrication. C12 parity for the card. It does depend on #3: tools Vole has no collector for are absent rather than zero, so without the coverage screen the record reads as a false negative.

name: Budget burn-down scoped by cost_basis, with a budget_indeterminate verdict
description: A dollar budget is meaningless over a column that mixes Anthropic list value, OpenCode's provider figure and 4,723 NULLs, so correct the budget design before it ships: `~/.vole/budgets.json` limits are declared per `(scope, cost_basis)` — a budget against anthropic_list for a repo, a token budget where no basis exists — and the pure detect/budget.ts rule computes burn only over rows matching that basis. When the unpriced or uncosted share of the scope exceeds a declared tolerance (default 10%), the rule fires `budget_indeterminate` rather than `budget_exceeded`, carrying the priced total, the unpriced call count and the tolerance in the observed/baseline/threshold columns so the incident explains itself. Burn-down projection is rendered only beside the budget, only on demand, with the formula and its inputs shown, and is never stored, summed or alerted on.
desktop_surface: A budget card per declared scope showing spent / limit / remaining with the window boundary, and — where the basis is impure — an amber 'indeterminate: 2,678 unpriced calls in scope' state in place of a percentage rather than a misleading bar.
data_source: ~/.vole/budgets.json (new); usage_events.{cost_usd, cost_basis, project, model, user, tool}; vendor_ledger for the vendor-anchored variant.
honest_limit: A budget can only bind on what has a price, and here 100% of Codex and Grok exact rows and 16% of Claude Code calls do not — refusing to show a percentage in that case is the feature, not a limitation to engineer around. On subscription accounts cost is list-equivalent value and nobody is billed it, so a USD cap enforces a number that does not exist and the card must say so. Projections assume the remaining window resembles the observed one, which is false around releases and incidents, so the projection stays on-demand and labelled.
competitive_note: v1 computes burn over a raw SUM(cost_usd) and would therefore alert on a silently mixed-basis number with a 16% hole; its own caveat says a USD cap over unpriced rows should be refused, but nothing in the design makes that a verdict the rule can emit. Datadog, Braintrust and the gateway vendors all meter a single basis because they only ever see their own path.
v1_ref: Budgets, budget_exceeded rule and labelled pace projection
field_verified: The premise verifies exactly: a USD budget over the current cost_usd column would bind on a number that mixes $1,798.52 of Anthropic list-equivalent with $580.26 of OpenCode provider dollars and drops 4,723 of 29,430 rows (16%). The unpriced share is not evenly spread — it is **100% of codex (83 of 83 exact rows NULL) and 100% of grok (789 of 789 exact rows NULL)** — so any scope containing either tool is unevaluable in USD outright, exactly as the feature says. `~/.vole/budgets.json` follows the verified paths.ts:21 override precedent. detect/budget.ts does not exist (detect/ holds burn-rate, context-pressure, error-storm, loop, rate-limit, util, index).
constraint: Constraint 3, unnamed and material: a `budget_indeterminate` verdict emitted early in a window is frozen by INSERT OR IGNORE, so a scope that later becomes evaluable (unpriced share drops below tolerance) keeps showing 'indeterminate' and a scope that later exceeds its cap never escalates — the same upsert-and-re-notify need as features 7 and 13, and all three should be one change. Constraint 5 respected: refusing a percentage is the feature. Depends entirely on feature 8 — a budget declared per (scope, cost_basis) cannot exist before the column does.

name: Device decommission: seal, attest, erase — and the hold that names its declarer
description: `vole decommission --principal <id> --out <path>` runs three gates that cannot be skipped or reordered. Seal: export that principal's rows through the deny-by-default field registry, plus the evidence_freeze manifest, plus the checkpoint chain, then hash what was written. Attest: recompute the chain over the archive and print the head beside the store's store_epoch, so the archive can be shown to be the store it came from. Erase: delete the principal's rows and set each tool's pruned_before_ts, because six collectors re-read their whole source every five seconds and would otherwise silently re-insert exactly what was just erased — the naive prune plan in v1 undoes itself on the next poll. A legal_hold(hold_id, scope principal|window|session, declared_by, basis, opened_at, expires_at, released_at, decl_hash) row blocks the erase gate and prints who declared it, on what basis and when it expires, with the conflict against the minimisation retention ceiling shown side by side rather than one silently winning.
desktop_surface: A Decommission sheet with the three gates as sequential steps, a hold banner naming the declarer and expiry when the erase gate is blocked, and a final receipt (rows erased per table, chain head, pruned_before_ts per tool, hold status) that is itself exportable.
data_source: vole.db tables only, plus the export field registry and legal_hold declarations from ~/.vole/policy; no agent artifact is modified
honest_limit: Erasing Vole's rows does not touch the agents' own transcripts under ~/.claude, ~/.codex, opencode.db or the Devin stores — the receipt says so and lists the paths that still hold source data, because deleting those is the vendor's data and breaks `claude --resume`. On a developer-writable SQLite with a developer-reachable key the chain is tamper-evident only after the head has left the box.
competitive_note: Cloud consoles cannot offer a device-decommission path at all — the data is already off the endpoint and their retention clock, not the customer's, decides when it dies; Fleet/osquery erases nothing because it stores nothing per person.
v1_ref: Data-subject access and erasure: vole dsar export and vole forget
gap_area: Employee lifecycle: leaver, mover, joiner — and the departure evidence pack

name: k-anonymity with complementary suppression for aggregate mode
description: Roadmap-v1's aggregate sync mode 'suppresses cells with fewer than k devices', but primary suppression alone leaks: if the row total and the org total ship unsuppressed, a single suppressed cell is recovered by subtraction, and a row with exactly one suppressed cell always is. Implement the standard two-pass rule — suppress primary cells with n<k, then suppress additional cells per row and per column until no suppressed value is derivable from published margins, and never publish a margin whose complement is one suppressed cell. Two further corrections to the v1 text: k must count distinct subjects, not devices, since one person with a laptop and a desktop currently counts as two; and suppressed cells stay blank, never zero and never estimated, per principle 1.
desktop_surface: Privacy section → 'Aggregate preview' renders the exact grid that would be published, with suppressed cells shown as '— (n<k)' and a footer stating k, the number of primary suppressions and the number of complementary ones, so a DPO can inspect the published artefact before it exists.
data_source: Daily rollups over usage_events GROUP BY (day, tool, model, project-slug) with COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) resolved through the principals binding; k from ~/.vole/policy.json.
honest_limit: Suppression is computed per publication, so an adversary differencing successive daily publications with shifting cell sets can still reconstruct a suppressed cell; the only sound answer is a fixed publication schedule with a stable cell set, which the docs must state as a deployment requirement rather than a nice-to-have. Adding noise is not available — principle 1 forbids inventing a number, so Vole cannot offer differential privacy and must say so. Counting distinct subjects is only possible where identity binding is proven; ambient bindings must be counted as separate subjects or the k is overstated.
competitive_note: No vendor in the matrix publishes a suppression rule at all, and Cursor's and Copilot's admin analytics are per-user by design. Complementary suppression is standard statistical-disclosure practice and is the specific thing a European DPO or works council will test the aggregate mode against, which is where Vole's GDPR-88/BetrVG positioning either survives or dies.
v1_ref: Identity pseudonymisation modes at sync (cleartext / HMAC-org-key / aggregate-only k)
field_verified: The v1 text it corrects is verbatim in roadmap-v1.md:257 — 'the relay suppresses cells with fewer than k devices as suppressed (n<k)' — so both the primary-suppression-only flaw and the counts-devices-not-people flaw are real as quoted. The inputs are not there: ~/.vole/policy.json does not exist, `principals` does not exist, and COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) has no subject_id to count — the only identity columns populated are user/machine ('shiva' / 'Marys-MacBook-Pro.local'), one pair across the whole store, which is precisely the single-device case that makes k meaningless without the binding.
constraint: Constraint 5 / principle 1, and the feature handles it correctly rather than violating it: noise-based disclosure control is unavailable because Vole may not invent a number, so differential privacy is off the table and suppressed cells stay blank, never zero. The unavoidable consequence — that Vole can offer suppression but not DP — should be stated as a product limit, not buried. Constraint 6 also applies: a daily rollup must exclude seed rows or k is computed over synthetic devices.

name: Vendor rate cards read from disk, in the vendor's own unit, with the real context ceiling
description: debug-logs/<id>/models.json carries the vendor's full billing table per model: billing.token_prices.{default,long_context}.{input_price, output_price, cache_price, cache_write_price, context_max}, billing.restricted_to (pro_plus, business, enterprise, max) and capabilities.limits.{max_context_window_tokens, max_output_tokens, max_non_streaming_output_tokens}. The chat store keeps a per-session copy in inputState.selectedModel.metadata: pricing 'In: 1000 · Out: 5000 AICs/1M tokens', inputCost, outputCost, cacheCost, cacheWriteCost, priceCategory, maxInputTokens 223790, auth.{providerLabel, accountLabel}. Adds vendor_rate_cards(tool, model, unit, tier, input_price, output_price, cache_price, cache_write_price, context_max, observed_at, root_id, source) and gives contextWindow() a measured window per model per tier instead of the hardcoded 1M/200K guesses in data/pricing.json — the same model reads 200,000 on default and 936,000 on long_context, a split Vole's single-number window cannot express, so context_pressure divides by the wrong denominator for every row from this surface today. restricted_to gives the plan classes entitled to each model, so use of an enterprise-only model is seat-class evidence without a console call.
desktop_surface: Costs prints an AIC subtotal on its own line with an em dash in the USD column until an admin supplies a conversion in policy; the Models table shows the vendor's declared ceiling beside the observed peak, and a tier chip where two ceilings exist.
data_source: <editor root>/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/debug-logs/<sessionId>/models.json; chatSessions/*.jsonl inputState.selectedModel.metadata
honest_limit: Prices are AICs per 1M tokens, not dollars: they are stored with unit='AIC' and never converted, because the AIC rate is not on this machine. models.json only exists once someone has opened the Copilot debug log — 22 files across 11 sessions here — so coverage is opportunistic and each card carries observed_at rather than pretending to be current. These are the prices this client was told, which may differ from the invoice; reconciliation must treat them as a vendor figure, not as truth. accountLabel is a binding-evidence row for the identity ledger and is hashed like every other identifier.
competitive_note: Market finding 130: vendor consoles are identity- and unit-fragmented, each blind to the others. No competitor reads the price card the client already holds, so nobody else can show a per-model rate and a real context ceiling for an editor agent with zero network calls; Copilot's own console reports premium requests, not per-model prices.
v1_ref: billing_units: a declared bridge for credits, seats and premium requests, or an em dash
gap_area: Editor-embedded agent task stores (Cline, Roo/Kilo, Kiro, Zed, JetBrains) across every VS Code fork root

name: Server-tool billing line (web_search_requests, web_fetch_requests)
description: Anthropic bills server-side tools per request rather than per token, and `message.usage.server_tool_use.{web_search_requests, web_fetch_requests}` appears on 29,114 assistant lines in this machine's transcripts — every one of them discarded at claude-code.ts:138-146. `~/.claude.json projects[].lastTotalWebSearchRequests` and each cost-state `modelUsage[model].webSearchRequests` confirm the vendor counts them as a separate line item. Until they are stored and priced, every reconciliation against Anthropic's cost_report carries a permanent unexplained delta that reads as shadow spend. Add two nullable INTEGER columns with an explicit backfill pass, a `server_tools` rate class in pricing.json with `unit:'requests'`, and include the line in computeCost under its own basis so it can be broken out — and because usage_report/messages returns `server_tool_use.web_search_requests` per bucket, this is the one line item that reconciles exactly on both sides.
desktop_surface: Breakdown gains a 'server tools' row under each model with the request count and its own cost line; the Reconciliation delta table shows web searches as a first-class row alongside the five token classes.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl `message.usage.server_tool_use.{web_search_requests, web_fetch_requests}` (29,114 occurrences here); ~/.claude.json `projects[].lastTotalWebSearchRequests`; Anthropic usage_report `server_tool_use`.
honest_limit: Every occurrence on this machine is zero, so the columns will be all-zero until someone runs web search — the feature is proven by field presence, not by a live figure, and the view must not imply otherwise. No other tool in the set reports server tools at all, so this line exists for Claude Code only and is NULL elsewhere. Rates for web search and web fetch differ and are not in pricing.json today; until an admin adds them the count is shown and the cost is an em dash. New nullable columns need an explicit backfill UPDATE because the upsert only rewrites rows when total_tokens strictly grows.
competitive_note: v1 lists server_tool_use among attribution metadata rather than as a priced line item that reconciliation depends on, which leaves a permanent unexplained delta in the Tier 4 cost story. Cursor's OTel export and Copilot metrics have no equivalent concept at all.
v1_ref: Provider, service-tier and gateway attribution columns
field_verified: Field presence confirmed, value presence refuted. `grep -rho server_tool_use ~/.claude/projects --include=*.jsonl | wc -l` → **30,026 occurrences**; but `grep -rho '"web_search_requests":[0-9]*' | sort | uniq -c` → **29,685 × `"web_search_requests":0` and nothing else**, and identically **29,685 × `"web_fetch_requests":0`**. Not one non-zero value exists anywhere on this machine. `projects[].lastTotalWebSearchRequests` is present on all 6 projects that have it — and is **0 in all 6**. The discard is confirmed: `grep -rn 'server_tool_use|web_search_requests'` across packages/ and apps/ returns **zero hits** — claude-code.ts:132-183 toEvent never reads it, matching the code map's fields_available_but_ignored entry. pricing.json has no `server_tools` rate class.
constraint: Constraint 2 (the upsert rewrites only when total_tokens strictly grows, so two new nullable INTEGER columns need an explicit backfill UPDATE keyed on event_key rather than the normal collect loop) — named correctly ✓. Constraint 11 not named: two new columns require matching edits to the INSERT column list, the @params object, the UsageEvent type, schema.ts and migrate(), and a stray undefined throws and aborts the whole batch. Constraint 5: with no published web-search/web-fetch rate in pricing.json, the count is shown and the cost stays an em dash — correct, and the feature says so.

name: Checkpoint chain over exported rows, witnessed by the sink the buyer already configured
description: Every export batch appends one export_checkpoints row: (epoch_id, seq_from, seq_to, row_count, rows_sha256, prev_checkpoint_sha256, checkpoint_sha256, sink_id, acked_at), where rows_sha256 covers the exact bytes the deny-by-default field-registry encoder emitted in export_seq order, so it is reproducible from the store at any later time. Checkpoints ship as ordinary rows through the same sink, so there is no new network path and no addition to the declared egress inventory. `vole verify --chain` recomputes from the live store and prints one of three states: intact, broken at seq N, or unverifiable — rows pruned under retention, that third state being the one every hash-chain design omits because it assumes retention never deletes. This corrects the v1 entry on its own terms: v1 already concedes that a chain in a developer-writable SQLite with a developer-readable key is not tamper-evident against the seat owner, and chaining exported rows moves the head off the box by construction while needing no per-device signing key for the subject to steal.
desktop_surface: Settings > Evidence carries a chain state chip (intact / broken at seq N / unverifiable — pruned), the last checkpoint seq and time, and which sink holds it. Each evidence bundle embeds the checkpoint covering its window plus the sink's ack timestamp.
data_source: export_seq change cursor and the durable export outbox; the field-registry encoder's serialized bytes; new export_checkpoints table
honest_limit: It proves only that rows which reached the sink were not altered afterwards. It cannot prove a row was ever created — an event deleted before its batch was encoded is invisible to the chain, which is what evidence_gaps and witness-orphans exist for. A buyer who never enabled export has no witness and the chain degrades to a local checksum, which the screen must state. Retention pruning legitimately breaks recomputation, so 'unverifiable' is a pass state and must be labelled one or the alert becomes noise auditors learn to ignore.
competitive_note: Buyer need #13 asks for tamper-evident export and >=6-month retention against NIST 800-53 AU-9 and ISO 42001 A.6.2.8. Every sink Vole already speaks — Sentinel, RFC 5424 syslog/CEF, OTLP — is itself the off-box witness, so Vole ships the auditor's control without becoming a cloud vendor, which is the one thing the local-first wedge cannot afford to trade away.
v1_ref: Tamper-evident audit log (hash chain + signed checkpoints)
gap_area: Evidence integrity when the monitored user is the local admin: gaps, source mutability, store lineage, clock

name: Reconciliation coverage report: what share of spend is even checkable
description: Classify every local row on three axes for a range and print the share of list value in each bucket: priced versus unpriced (2,661 of 15,933 Claude Code calls here carry NULL cost); exact versus activity_only (Cursor, Antigravity, Devin and 969 failed Grok calls can never be reconciled on tokens); and reconcilable auth path versus not (Console API key = reconcilable; Max/Pro subscription, ChatGPT seat, Bedrock, Vertex or a routed base URL = structurally invisible to the vendor's own API). The output is one sentence with real numbers — 'N% of observed list value is reconcilable against Anthropic; M% is subscription-auth; K% went to non-Anthropic models through a router' — plus the per-bucket table. It ships as 'vole reconcile --coverage', needs no network, and runs before anyone buys a vendor-pull feature.
desktop_surface: The Reconciliation screen opens on this report when no vendor pull has ever run; afterwards it stays as a permanent header strip so no delta table is ever read without its denominator.
data_source: usage_events.{confidence, cost_usd, model, tool}; vendor_identities.{auth_path, plan}; ~/.claude/settings.json env (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, apiKeyHelper); presence of ~/.claude-code-router/.
honest_limit: Coverage is computed over rows Vole holds, so it cannot account for agents Vole does not collect or for machines it is not installed on — it is a statement about this endpoint and says so in its first line. Auth path is inferred from configuration and model naming, never observed on the wire, and a session that switched auth mid-flight is classified by its first evidence.
competitive_note: market.md's stated white space is that nobody is out-of-path, exact and prompt-free at once; publishing the denominator is how that claim survives a security questionnaire. Every competing FinOps dashboard shows a total with no statement of what it could not see, and Anthropic's own Compliance API excludes API-key, Bedrock/Vertex and personal accounts without saying so in the console.
field_verified: Re-measured today: claude_code 16,702 rows with 2,678 NULL cost_usd; codex 83/83 NULL; devin 204/204 NULL; grok 1,758/1,758 NULL, split 789 exact + 969 activity_only -- the feature's '969 failed Grok calls' is EXACT; opencode 0 NULL of 10,885 (OpenCode supplies its own figure). The router signal is live: `ls -d ~/.claude-code-router` -> exists. But the auth-path source is absent here: ~/.claude/settings.json has NO `env` block (keys are permissions, enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, effortLevel, remoteControlAtStartup, agentPushNotifEnabled, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt), so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and apiKeyHelper are all unset. vendor_identities does not exist as a table.
constraint: C18 (pricing = equivalent API value at Anthropic list rates; cost is never date-aware): '% of observed list value is reconcilable' must say list-rate-equivalent, not billed, or it silently mixes definitions -- which is the exact failure C18 forbids. C1 is satisfied and is the point.

name: Works-council pack: DPIA pre-filled with measured facts, plus BV and CSE skeletons
description: v1 generates DPIA sections from the manifest, which is a statement of intent; a works council argues proportionality with numbers. Fill the necessity, proportionality and risk tables from the running install: rows per table, which columns are non-NULL and at what rate (2,008 of 28,948 rows here have no model and 12,930 no branch), how many manifest fields are personal data, the k achieved for each aggregate, the count of content-reading scanners enabled, and the collector's measured CPU and wall time from collector_runs. Ship alongside it a German Betriebsvereinbarung skeleton naming the § 87(1) Nr. 6 trigger and a French CSE information-consultation note naming L.2312-38, with every legal conclusion left as [ORG TO COMPLETE].
desktop_surface: Privacy Center → 'Generate works-council pack' button; the resulting document's fact table is previewed in-app so the developer sees the same numbers the council will.
data_source: PRAGMA table_info plus COUNT and non-NULL scans over the live DB, packages/core/src/sync/manifest.ts, ~/.vole/policy.json, collector_runs duration rows, the lawful-basis record.
honest_limit: Templates, not legal advice, and the measured figures describe one machine — fleet-wide numbers do not exist until sync is on, so the pack must label them 'one endpoint, <date range>'. It cites the co-determination trigger; it cannot tell an employer whether their specific deployment crosses it.
competitive_note: v1's pack has the DPIA sections, the employee notice and per-jurisdiction notes but no measured proportionality table and no BV or CSE skeletons. Vendors ship marketing-grade DPIA templates with no install-specific numbers; grounding the proportionality table in measured non-NULL rates is the difference between a document a council reads and one it approves.
v1_ref: Compliance documentation pack generated from the manifest (docs/compliance/)
field_verified: The measured facts are the most accurate numbers in the shard and I reproduced them: 2,008 of 29,632 rows have NULL model (the feature's numerator 2,008 is EXACT; its denominator 28,948 is three days stale) and 12,930 have NULL git_branch (EXACT). PRAGMA table_info works, COUNT and non-NULL scans work. BUT collector_runs does not exist, so 'the collector's measured CPU and wall time' has no source -- though collect.ts already computes it and throws it away (`const ms = Date.now() - started;` printed as `(${ms}ms)`), so one table would persist a datum that already exists. sync/manifest.ts does not exist, so 'how many manifest fields are personal data' has no source. No k-anonymity machinery exists anywhere in the codebase. BetrVG §87(1) Nr. 6 and CNIL/CSE consultation are sourced at market.md L50; L.2312-38 specifically is not cited in the research file.
constraint: None -- it is a read-only generator over the live store. C12 only for the in-app fact-table preview.

name: vendor_ledger: the vendor's own billing figures, read from disk with zero network
description: Every vendor Vole covers already writes its own billing figure to local disk, so reconciliation can start before any API key exists. Add one table `vendor_ledger(vendor, scope_kind, scope_id, metric, value, unit, window_start, window_end, observed_at, artifact_path, origin, source)` — `origin='local_cache'` now, `origin='api'` when an adapter runs — populated from Claude Code `type:'cost-state'` lines (`totalCostUSD`, `modelUsage[model].{costUSD,inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheReadInputTokens,cacheCreationInputTokens,webSearchRequests}`, `hasUnknownModelCost`), `~/.claude.json projects[].{lastCost,lastModelUsage,lastSessionId,lastTotalInputTokens,lastTotalOutputTokens,lastTotalCacheReadInputTokens,lastTotalCacheCreationInputTokens,lastTotalWebSearchRequests}`, `cachedUsageUtilization.spend.used.amount_minor`, Codex `payload.rate_limits.{primary,secondary}.used_percent` and `credits.{has_credits,unlimited,balance}`, and OpenCode `message.data.cost`. Rows are INSERT OR IGNORE on `(vendor, scope_kind, scope_id, metric, window_start)` so re-collection is a no-op, the key embeds no poll-time value, and the table carries the mandatory `source` column with the same live/seed partition and purge as usage_events. Every diff view, rule and verify leg downstream reads this one shape whether the row came from a JSONL tail or an admin API.
desktop_surface: New Reconciliation screen, left pane 'Vendor says': one row per vendor figure with unit, window boundaries, artifact path and observed_at beside it; the session detail drill-down gains a 'Vendor $0.2025 / Vole $0.2019' line, and a per-project line anchored on lastCost.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl `type:'cost-state'` (present on this machine); ~/.claude.json `projects[].lastCost` (6 of 23 non-null: <redacted-local-path> 0.39005, .../landing 2.02543, one exactly 0) and `cachedUsageUtilization.spend.used.amount_minor` (0 here); ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl `payload.rate_limits`; ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db `message.data.cost`.
honest_limit: cost-state is written at session end, so an interrupted or crashed session has no vendor figure at all — NULL, never zero. `hasUnknownModelCost:true` means the vendor's own number is itself incomplete, so the row is stored with that flag and is never treated as ground truth. cachedUsageUtilization is an account-wide cached snapshot with its own fetchedAtMs covering claude.ai web, Cowork and Desktop, not just Claude Code. Codex `credits.balance` was null in every rollout here and `limit_dollars`/`used_dollars`/`remaining_dollars` are null under this subscription — those cells stay em dashes permanently.
competitive_note: v1 puts cost-state into session_meta for `pnpm verify` only; this generalises it into a queryable four-vendor table the API adapters later write into. No competitor reads the vendor's own cost figure off the endpoint: Cyberhaven, Nightfall and Harmonic see the traffic but not the bill, and Anthropic's own Analytics API is daily and server-side (market.md §4).
v1_ref: Claude Code cost-state cross-check in pnpm verify
field_verified: Mixed. cost-state EXISTS verbatim — `{"type":"cost-state","sessionId":"d6eccf70…","totalCostUSD":0.20247400000000002,"modelUsage":{"claude-opus-5[1m]":{"inputTokens":508,"outputTokens":170,"cacheReadInputTokens":107314,"cacheCreationInputTokens":14109,"webSearchRequests":0,"costUSD":0.20153700000000002}},"hasUnknownModelCost":false}` — but coverage is catastrophic and the feature does not say so: parsing every line of all 628 transcripts yields **6 cost-state records across 3 distinct sessions**, and 2 of the 6 carry hasUnknownModelCost:true. (`grep -rl cost-state` hits 73 files, but 70 of those are agents *writing about* cost-state in message content — the real record count is 6.) lastCost verified exactly: 6 of 23 projects non-null, <redacted-local-path> 0.3900484999999999, LaunchSafe/landing 2.0254337, LaunchSafe/docs exactly 0. cachedUsageUtilization.spend.used.amount_minor = 0 ✓. Codex rate_limits verified across 66 rollouts: 68 objects, 45 with non-null primary (`{"used_percent":3.0,"window_minutes":10080,"resets_at":1780856692}`), credits `{has_credits:false, unlimited:false, balance:null}` in every one ✓. OpenCode: better than described — `session` is a real table with typed columns `parent_id, cost REAL NOT NULL, tokens_input/output/reasoning/cache_read/cache_write, share_url`, so the session-level vendor figure is a column read, not a JSON extract. Repo grep for `cost-state|totalCostUSD|lastCost` returns zero hits — nothing of this is built.
constraint: Constraint 1 (idempotency) and constraint 3's spirit. The proposed INSERT OR IGNORE on (vendor, scope_kind, scope_id, metric, window_start) is wrong for the primary source: Claude Code rewrites cost-state repeatedly within one session with a growing totalCostUSD (I observed session d6eccf70 written twice, same cost, totalDuration 24553 then 24559). INSERT OR IGNORE freezes the FIRST, smallest reading and silently discards the session's final bill — the same defect class as the usage_events upsert in constraint 2. Reconciliation: the ledger needs `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE WHERE excluded.value > value` for monotonic metrics, explicitly declared per metric, plus the mandatory `source` column, live/seed partition and purge from constraint 6 (feature already carries these).

name: Reconciliation delta view with a not_comparable state that refuses to invent a gap
description: A view over `vendor_ledger` LEFT JOIN a same-shaped local aggregate, keyed on (vendor, UTC day, model, identity), producing `vendor_value`, `local_value`, `delta`, `delta_pct` and a `state` enum of `matched | vendor_only | local_only | units_differ | not_comparable`. The arithmetic obeys principle 1 absolutely: when the local side contains any activity_only row or any row with NULL cost_usd for that cell, `delta` is NULL and `state` is `not_comparable` — a missing local number is never read as zero, which is the single most common way FinOps tools manufacture a fake gap. Two findings fall out and both are load-bearing: `vendor_only` rows are console spend no monitored host accounts for (hosted runners, cloud agents, laptops without Vole), and `local_only` rows are endpoint activity the console never saw (personal accounts, raw API keys, a competitor's agent). Every cell carries `local_unpriced_calls` and `local_activity_only_calls` beside it so the reader sees exactly why a comparison was refused, and each run is stamped into `reconcile_runs(vendor, day, vendor_total, local_total, unpriced_local_rows, state, fetched_at, source)`.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen centre pane: the delta table sorted by absolute vendor_only value, each row expanding to the contributing local sessions and the vendor-side group_by that produced it; the Coverage screen gains a 'Reconcile' tab with the same rows per day and a persistent 'this data required network calls to <hosts>' banner rendered from the egress allowlist.
data_source: vendor_ledger; usage_events (source='live') grouped by CAST(ts/86400000) day, model and identity; reconcile_runs.
honest_limit: On a single laptop most vendor_only spend is simply other employees' machines, so the view must label single-host mode explicitly and scope the vendor query to this identity or the number is meaningless. Bucket boundaries differ (Anthropic buckets are UTC-anchored, Cursor timestamps are epoch ms, Copilot lags roughly two days), so single-day deltas at window edges are noise, not signal. Claude Code transcripts are cleaned up on the tool's own schedule, so any window older than the local retention horizon shows vendor_only for a reason that is not shadow spend. It can never attribute a console-side excess to a cause: 'hosted agent' and 'unmonitored laptop' are indistinguishable from here.
competitive_note: No vendor in the 62-row matrix produces this diff because none has out-of-path endpoint evidence to diff against — each console reconciles only against itself, and Datadog/Langfuse/Helicone reconcile only what an SDK sent them. This is the concrete form of market.md white-space finding 2, 'vendor consoles are single-tool and identity-fragmented'.
field_verified: Local side verified exactly: 29,430 live rows, 4,723 with NULL cost_usd (16.05%), of which 3,550 are confidence='exact' (claude_code 2,678 / codex 83 / grok 789) — the feature's own figures reproduce to the row. `usage_events.user` and `machine` have exactly 1 distinct value each across all 29,430 rows, confirming the single-host caveat is not hypothetical. The vendor side it joins against is the ledger above, which on this machine holds 3 Claude Code sessions — so the delta table renders `vendor_only` for ~99.5% of days for a reason that is not shadow spend. The 'Coverage screen' the desktop_surface extends does not exist in the app (DashboardView.swift has Dashboard/Breakdown/Settings only).
constraint: Constraint 19 (UTC epoch-anchored integer bucketing) — the view keys on `CAST(ts/86400000)` which is correct, but the vendor side's buckets are the vendor's own day boundaries; joining two differently-anchored days is the exact 'window edge noise' the honest_limit admits. Constraint 13 (read-model parity): the view must be written twice, queries.ts and DB.swift. Otherwise clean: refusing to read a missing local number as zero is principle 1 executed correctly, and `local_unpriced_calls`/`local_activity_only_calls` beside every cell satisfies constraint 5's 'aggregates that drop NULLs must expose an unpriced count'.

name: `pnpm verify --reconcile`: cost arithmetic checked against the vendor's own local figure
description: verify.ts today reconciles Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex rows against their own source logs (Grok is never reconciled at all, and it PASSes on an empty DB). Add a third leg comparing Vole's computed per-session sums against the vendor's own local figure: cost-state `totalCostUSD` and `modelUsage[model].costUSD` per session, and `~/.claude.json projects[].{lastCost, lastTotalInputTokens, lastTotalOutputTokens, lastTotalCacheReadInputTokens, lastTotalCacheCreationInputTokens}` per project, failing with the exact delta and the session id when they diverge beyond a token-rounding tolerance. This is where principle 1 becomes checkable rather than asserted, and it doubles as a regression test for pricing.json rate changes — verify.ts's RATES is a deliberate independent copy that must be mirrored by hand on every rate change, and this leg is what catches a missed mirror.
desktop_surface: Settings replaces the hard-coded 'Verification: Every stored row reconciled' string with the last verify result, its timestamp, the covered fraction and per-leg pass/fail — including the vendor-figure leg and the honest 'Grok: not reconciled'.
data_source: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl type:'cost-state' (e.g. totalCostUSD 0.20247400000000002 with a two-model modelUsage breakdown); ~/.claude.json projects[].lastCost (6 of 23 non-null here); packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts.
honest_limit: cost-state exists only for sessions that ended cleanly and lastCost holds only the most recent session per project, so this leg covers a sample and must report the covered fraction rather than a bare PASS. `hasUnknownModelCost:true` means the vendor's figure is itself untrusted — report 'vendor figure unknown', never a mismatch — and a model absent from pricing.json produces NULL on Vole's side so the comparison is skipped rather than failed. The '[1m]' model-name suffix must be stripped before comparing, and the comparison is total-versus-total per session, not per message.
