competitive_note: v1 proposes the cost-state cross-check; this adds the project-level lastCost anchor, the covered-fraction reporting, and makes verify fail loudly on rate-table drift instead of passing quietly. No competitor lets a customer verify its cost arithmetic against the vendor's own figure — Cursor calls its cost best-effort and ships no check at all.
v1_ref: Claude Code cost-state cross-check in pnpm verify
field_verified: Every claim about verify.ts is true; the sample it would check is far smaller than stated. verify.ts confirmed: `grep -ci grok packages/core/src/cli/verify.ts` → **0**, so 'Grok is never reconciled' ✓; its output legs are claude/opencode/codex/no-token only (lines 516-524); line 12 comment 'RATES below must mirror the built-in data/pricing.json table — an independent copy' ✓; line 538 `console.log(ok ? '\n  PASS — every stored row matches its source record.' : '\n  FAIL')` with `ok` computed from mismatch counters, so an empty DB PASSes ✓. The hard-coded string is real: DashboardView.swift:696 `LabeledContent("Verification", value: "Every stored row reconciled")`. The cost-state sample it would compare against, however, is **6 records / 3 distinct sessions across 628 transcript files**, and **2 of those 6 carry hasUnknownModelCost:true** (the claude-code-router session asserting totalCostUSD 25.94439 for `anthropic/claude-ccr-h7177…` — a hex-aliased self-hosted qwen model). lastCost adds 6 project anchors, one of which is exactly 0.
constraint: Constraint 20 (pnpm verify must keep passing and be extended for any new exact-token source; RATES is a deliberate hand-mirrored copy) — this feature is that constraint's enforcement mechanism, which is the strongest argument for it. Principle 1: reporting the covered fraction rather than a bare PASS is mandatory and the feature says so; with 3 of ~600 sessions covered, that fraction is the headline, not a footnote. The '[1m]' suffix strip is real — this machine's live model is `claude-opus-5[1m]`.

name: `vole reconcile`: the single opt-in, egress-declared network command
description: One CLI, never the collector daemon and never the app on a timer: `vole reconcile --vendor=anthropic --from=2026-08-01 --to=2026-08-31 [--yes]`. It first prints the exact hosts, paths and query parameters it will call, the identity it will scope to and the columns it will write, then refuses to proceed without `--yes` or a `reconcile.confirmed` flag in `~/.vole/reconcile.json`, and it is gated by the same no-egress switch that the update check must respect. Credentials are read from environment variables or the macOS Keychain via `security find-generic-password` only — never stored in vole.db, never logged, never written to a config file — and adapters write only aggregate rows into `vendor_ledger` with `origin='api'`, discarding the raw HTTP body after normalisation so no prompt, no cleartext email and no key id beyond a hash lands in SQLite. Because the collector must stay a zero-runtime-dependency SEA bundle, the adapters use `fetch` from node: builtins only and live in a CLI entrypoint the SEA does not include.
desktop_surface: Settings → Reconciliation: a disabled-by-default toggle per vendor showing the endpoint list, the credential source (env var name or Keychain item), 'last run / rows written / bytes received', and a 'Run now' button that shells the CLI and streams its declared plan before executing anything.
data_source: ~/.vole/reconcile.json (new, user-created); env ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY / OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY / CURSOR_API_KEY / GITHUB_TOKEN; macOS Keychain via the `security` binary.
honest_limit: This crosses the local-first line by design and must be documented as such in SECURITY.md alongside the existing undisclosed UpdateChecker egress, which has to be fixed first or the disclosure is a lie. It only works for someone holding org-admin credentials — a developer running Vole on their own laptop cannot run it at all. Corporate proxies with TLS inspection will see the calls, which is exactly why the plan is printed before they are made.

name: Anthropic Admin API adapter (usage_report/messages, usage_report/claude_code, cost_report)
description: Three GETs against `https://api.anthropic.com` with `x-api-key: <sk-ant-admin…>` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, using an Admin key only an org owner can mint. `/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages` takes `starting_at`, `ending_at`, `bucket_width` (1m|1h|1d) and `group_by[]` of api_key_id|workspace_id|model|service_tier|context_window, returning per-bucket `uncached_input_tokens`, `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`, `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `server_tool_use.web_search_requests` — the same five token classes usage_events already stores, which is why this diff is arithmetic rather than estimation. `/v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code` groups by actor, model and terminal_type with `estimated_cost`; `/v1/organizations/cost_report` is bucket_width=1d only and returns billed USD. Each normalises into `vendor_ledger` rows with `unit='tokens'` or `unit='usd_minor'`, keyed on the org identity resolved locally.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen, Anthropic tab: the five token-class rows plus web searches side by side, vendor versus Vole, with the exact bucket boundary and the group_by that produced the vendor column printed above the table.
data_source: api.anthropic.com Admin API; joined locally on ~/.claude.json `oauthAccount.{accountUuid, organizationUuid}` and transcript `type:'bridge-session'.{ownerAccountUuid, ownerOrganizationUuid}` — opaque ids only, never emailAddress/fullName/organizationName which sit in the same object.
honest_limit: The Admin API exists only for Console API organisations. This machine's account is `organizationType:'claude_max'` with `billingType:'stripe_subscription'` — a subscription — so none of these three endpoints returns anything for it and the entire Anthropic leg degrades to the local-cache vendor_ledger. The reports also exclude Bedrock and Vertex traffic entirely, and cost_report is daily-only, so sub-day attribution is structurally impossible.
competitive_note: Anthropic's own docs state that anomaly detection, baselining and correlation are the customer's job (code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage). No security vendor reconciles this report against endpoint evidence, and Claude Code Analytics is daily and excludes Bedrock/Vertex (market.md §4).
field_verified: The LOCAL half verifies exactly; the REMOTE half does not verify at all. Local: ~/.claude.json oauthAccount gives `accountUuid 909a1169-d7f6-4e37-9a6b-576514ef1ef9`, `organizationUuid 4d93cf62-9d13-4e0d-9e63-c617b9537a73`, `organizationType 'claude_max'`, `billingType 'stripe_subscription'` — so the feature's own kill-shot is confirmed: no Console org, no Admin API, the whole leg degrades to local cache here. `bridge-session` appears 575 times in the transcripts ✓. Remote: the endpoint schema is NOT in the research corpus. Grepping market.md + market-extracts.json + roadmap-v1.md: `cost_report` 0 hits, `sk-ant-admin` 0 hits, `organization/usage` 0 hits. `usage_report` has exactly ONE hit, and it is a need statement, not a schema: 'Enterprise reconcile job against Anthropic usage_report, Cursor filtered-usage-events and Copilot NDJSON to surface unaccounted spend and shadow accounts.' Every parameter name, group_by enum and response field in this feature description (`bucket_width`, `group_by[]=service_tier|context_window`, `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`, `server_tool_use.web_search_requests`, `estimated_cost`, `terminal_type`) is recalled from model memory, not sourced.
constraint: Constraint 17 (egress) — mitigated only by feature 3. Principle 1 ('never invent a number') applied to the ROADMAP ITSELF, not just to the product: a public roadmap that asserts a vendor's exact request parameters and response field names without a source is inventing specifics in the one document whose whole pitch is that Vole does not. Reconciliation: keep the entry, but demote it from a schema to a contract sketch — name the endpoint family, the auth header type, the join key (opaque accountUuid/organizationUuid, never emailAddress/fullName/organizationName from the same object), and the arithmetic claim (five token classes already stored, so the diff is subtraction not estimation), and mark the field list 'to be confirmed against live vendor documentation before implementation'.

name: OpenAI Admin API adapter, and the ChatGPT-seat hole it names instead of filling
description: `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/usage/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-admin-…`, params `start_time`, `end_time`, `bucket_width` (1m|1h|1d) and `group_by[]` of project_id|user_id|api_key_id|model|batch, returning `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `input_cached_tokens` and `num_model_requests` per bucket; `GET /v1/organization/costs` gives 1d buckets grouped by project_id|line_item in USD. The adapter scopes to this host by decoding the `~/.codex/auth.json` id_token offline for `chatgpt_user_id` and `organizations[].id`, so a single-laptop run produces a meaningful diff rather than 'the rest of the company', and it writes `vendor_ledger` rows with `unit='tokens'`/`unit='usd'`. When `auth.json` reports `auth_mode:'chatgpt'` the adapter refuses to run and renders the reason as a first-class result rather than an empty table.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen, OpenAI tab; under auth_mode 'chatgpt' the whole tab becomes one honest panel: 'This machine's Codex sessions bill against a ChatGPT team seat (plan_type: team). Seat consumption is exposed by no OpenAI usage endpoint. 83 local Codex calls / 12.8M tokens are unreconcilable.'
data_source: api.openai.com Admin API; identity from ~/.codex/auth.json `auth_mode`, `tokens.account_id` and offline-decoded id_token claims `https://api.openai.com/auth.{chatgpt_account_id, chatgpt_plan_type, chatgpt_user_id, organizations[].id, organizations[].role}` — decoded in memory, never persisted, and the adjacent refresh/access tokens never read.
honest_limit: Codex CLI logged in with a ChatGPT account — the default, and the case on this machine — produces zero rows in /v1/organization/usage/completions because that consumption is seat-based and lives in ChatGPT admin, which has no public per-turn usage API. For the most common Codex deployment the answer is a documented 'cannot compare', not a number. Only raw-API-key Codex (OPENAI_API_KEY set, null here) is reconcilable at all.
competitive_note: market.md records that Codex governance exists only for ChatGPT-workspace accounts and that `codex exec` emits no metrics whatsoever. No vendor states the seat-versus-API hole plainly; naming it as an unreconcilable class — with the exact local call and token count it covers — is the differentiator, not a gap.
field_verified: The refusal path verifies perfectly — this feature's most valuable half needs no network. ~/.codex/auth.json: `auth_mode: 'chatgpt'`, `OPENAI_API_KEY: None`, `tokens.account_id: d3b7ab6e-8fd6-4b9a-a72d-842c33acebb7`. Offline-decoded id_token `https://api.openai.com/auth` claim: `chatgpt_plan_type 'team'`, `chatgpt_user_id 'user-viy9imSnsYhf82KGoL2Ui6Ii'`, `organizations:[{id:'org-k52jKYy0hAWofNruPTlZil79', role:'owner', title:'Personal'}]` — every field named, present. The desktop panel's figures verify to the digit: `select count(*), sum(total_tokens) from usage_events where tool='codex'` → **83 calls, 12,820,950 tokens** = the claimed '83 local Codex calls / 12.8M tokens'. Env OPENAI_API_KEY unset ✓. Endpoint half unsourced exactly as in feature 4 (`organization/usage/completions` 0 hits in the corpus).
constraint: Constraint 17 (egress, via feature 3) for the pull half only. A NEW privacy hazard the feature does not name: the id_token payload also carries top-level `email` and `name` claims, sitting in the very object the adapter decodes. The feature is scrupulous about never persisting Claude's emailAddress/fullName/organizationName but says nothing about the equivalent OpenAI fields it is about to base64-decode into memory. Reconciliation: state the same never-persist list for `email`, `name`, `sub`, `sid` as for the Anthropic object, and keep the stated discipline of never touching the adjacent access_token/refresh_token.

name: Cursor and Copilot adapters: reconciliation where the units can never match
description: Two vendors where the honest output is a count or a unit mismatch, never a cost diff, and the adapter's job is to say so with figures. Cursor: `POST https://api.cursor.com/teams/filtered-usage-events` (HTTP Basic, team API key as username, empty password) returns per-event `timestamp`, `model`, `kindLabel`, `maxMode`, `isTokenBasedCall`, `requestsCosts` and `tokenUsage.{inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheWriteTokens,cacheReadTokens,totalCents}`, with `/teams/spend` for per-user spendCents and `/teams/members` for the email↔userId map — but Vole's Cursor collector is activity_only, so the join is requestId-count-per-day-and-model versus vendor event-count, a call-count reconciliation. Copilot: `GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics` (28-day rolling, per-editor and per-model engaged users, no tokens and no money), `GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/billing/seats` (`last_activity_at`, `last_activity_editor`, plan) and `GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/usage` (`usageItems[]` with product='copilot', sku, quantity, grossAmount) write rows with `unit='premium_requests'`, `unit='seats'` or `unit='usd'` and never `unit='tokens'`. The local counterpart for Copilot is not a Copilot collector but OpenCode: 3,336 assistant messages here carry `providerID='github-copilot'` across claude-opus-4.6/4.8, gpt-5.5, claude-sonnet-5 and claude-fable-5, with OpenCode's own cost totalling $575.19 — Copilot entitlement consumed through a third-party CLI, which the org's Copilot billing shows only as an undifferentiated premium-request count.
desktop_surface: Reconciliation screen, Cursor and Copilot tabs: Cursor shows two count columns per day and model with a permanent 'tokens: vendor only' chip; Copilot shows a 'Vendor unit: premium requests. Local unit: tokens. Not comparable without a declared bridge' banner over two independent columns, with the OpenCode-via-Copilot row called out by name and dollar figure.
data_source: api.cursor.com Admin API and api.github.com Copilot metrics/billing; local side ~/.cursor/ai-tracking/ai-code-tracking.db `ai_code_hashes.{requestId,conversationId,model,timestamp}` (0 rows here) and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db `message.data.providerID='github-copilot'` (3,336 rows, $575.19).
honest_limit: Cursor's Admin API is Enterprise-tier only, and `ai_code_hashes` records accepted AI code rather than every model call, so local counts are a systematic lower bound the view must state rather than call a gap. No GitHub endpoint exposes tokens for Copilot ever — the unit is premium requests and dollars — and Copilot metrics are off by default, depend on IDE telemetry, and lag roughly two days, so same-day reconciliation is structurally impossible. Agent-session streaming carries bodies but is EMU-only with a 48-hour REST window and is out of scope by design.
competitive_note: Cursor's OTel export is documented as having no per-session tool attribution, no subagent roll-up, no backfill and best-effort cost, while the Admin API has the tokens the OTel push lacks — nobody joins the two against endpoint evidence. Copilot entitlement routed through OpenCode is invisible to GitHub's metrics (wrong editor), to Anthropic (not their billing relationship) and to every gateway; only the local OpenCode DB has it.

name: reconcile_gap rule, and the three explainability columns nobody has ever selected
description: A pure detection rule in the existing `(events, now) => Anomaly[]` shape, over vendor_ledger and the local aggregate. It fires when a (vendor, identity, UTC day, direction) cell has both sides non-NULL, the same unit, and `|vendor − local| / vendor > 0.15` on at least two consecutive days — the consecutive-day gate exists purely to absorb bucket-boundary and timezone skew, not to soften the finding. `anomaly_key = 'reconcile:<vendor>:<identity_hmac>:<day>:<direction>'`, deterministic and free of now(). It writes `observed` (local figure), `baseline` (vendor figure) and `threshold` (0.15) — three columns the schema has always had and that no reader in queries.ts or DB.swift has ever selected — making this the first incident in the product that is explainable with real figures as principle 3 requires. Severity is warn at 15%, critical at 40% or when the local side is entirely absent.
desktop_surface: Incident feed card reading 'Anthropic billed 41.2M output tokens on 2026-08-14; Vole observed 28.7M for this identity (30% gap, threshold 15%)', with a 'show the sessions' action and an automatic suppression when the day predates the local transcript retention horizon.
data_source: vendor_ledger; usage_events; anomalies.{observed, baseline, threshold, anomaly_key}.
honest_limit: Anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key, so the first verdict is frozen — a gap that widens on a later pull will not escalate without an explicit upsert clause and a re-notify path, and this rule needs that change more than any existing rule does. The rule cannot run at all without a successful pull, so its silence is not evidence of agreement and the coverage report must be read beside it. It also cannot distinguish a real gap from an unmonitored second laptop on the same account.
competitive_note: Anthropic states plainly that anomaly detection and correlation are the customer's responsibility. No console ships a gap alert against endpoint evidence because no console has endpoint evidence — and this is the feature that converts a FinOps evaluation into a security finding, which is how one install gets sold twice inside a company.
field_verified: The unread-columns claim is verified and is the best observation in the shard. anomalies has `observed REAL NOT NULL, baseline REAL, threshold REAL` (schema.ts). DB.swift:227-229 selects exactly `id, rule, severity, tool, session_id, model, window_start, window_end, title, detail, confidence, source` — observed, baseline and threshold are absent; queries.ts's incident SELECT (line ~232) likewise. Confirmed: **no reader in either read model has ever selected them.** The rule's inputs also verify — vendor_ledger density is the 3-session problem from feature 1, and the local aggregate is the 29,430-row table. Existing rules that would be its siblings: burn_rate_spike 190, loop_suspected 38, context_pressure 10, error_storm 10, rate_limit_pressure 1 (249 live anomalies total).
constraint: Constraint 3, and the feature names it precisely: anomalies are INSERT OR IGNORE on anomaly_key (db.ts:137), so the first verdict is frozen and 'changing verdict semantics requires an explicit upsert clause and a re-notify path'. The proposed key `reconcile:<vendor>:<identity_hmac>:<day>:<direction>` is correctly free of now() per constraint 3 and detect.test.ts:120. One conflict it does NOT name: constraint 13 (read-model parity). Because observed/baseline/threshold are selected by neither reader, 'the first incident explainable with real figures' requires a schema-to-UI change in queries.ts AND DB.swift AND the Incident struct AND the card — that is not free, and it is the work that makes every OTHER rule explainable too, which is a reason to do it, not a reason to hide it inside this one.
